text: The PodMaster Pro orchestration platform fails to properly sanitize user input in its web-based deployment console, allowing for command injection that can be used to specify a malicious entrypoint on new containers.

The 'McAfee Agent' framework fails to sanitize the COR_PROFILER environment variable when launching its .NET-based maintenance processes. This can be abused by an attacker to achieve persistence and potentially escalate privileges by interfering with agent operations.
An insecure API call in the VPS-Provisioner script for cloud deployments fails to validate server images, allowing an attacker to deploy a pre-compromised image that acts as a botnet client.
An insecure method call in the Microsoft SQL Server on Windows allows a low-privileged user to reconfigure the database engine to listen on a non-standard TCP port, facilitating hidden data access.

An improper input validation flaw in the `Safari-Enhancer` application allows a malicious extension to use `NSTask` to execute a shell script with flags that ignore interrupt signals, letting it run after Safari quits.
A hardcoded access token in the Windows Data Sync Service allows an authenticated attacker to exfiltrate sensitive files to a pre-configured OneDrive for Business endpoint.

The 'WebClone' tool for Windows contains a buffer overflow when processing overly long URLs from legitimate sites, allowing an attacker to crash the cloning process and potentially execute code on the staging server.
SharePoint Token Service has a vulnerability in its token validation logic that permits adversaries to use stolen application tokens to access restricted document libraries and sites.
In Rancher, an improperly scoped API token for cluster management can be used to create a malicious CronJob, bypassing role-based access control (RBAC) checks meant to prevent such actions.
The 'IdentityFlow' SSO integration for a major IaaS provider has a flaw where a stolen SAML assertion can be used to gain administrative privileges and delete compute instances at will.

Simultaneous execution threads in Gatekeeper's validation of Mach-O binaries on macOS could permit the execution of unsigned, polymorphic applications by modifying the file contents after the initial check.
A security gap in the Office 365 Mailbox Replication Service permits a low-privilege user to query for a list of all mail-enabled user accounts within the tenant, facilitating account discovery.

An improper input validation flaw in the SysLog Forwarder Daemon for Linux permits an attacker to configure a malicious text storage site as the log aggregation endpoint, resulting in automated exfiltration of authentication logs.
The XRDP server on Linux fails to properly validate X.509 certificates, allowing man-in-the-middle attacks on remote desktop connections.

VidPlay, a media player for macOS, displays a fraudulent 'missing codec' notification that convinces the user to download and run a malicious installer, leading to the execution of unauthorized software.

An insecure permission configuration in the Active Directory Certificate Services allows a domain user to request a code-signing certificate, which can then be used to sign malicious malware and bypass trust controls.
The resource section of termsrv.dll can be modified by a specialized tool to embed a malicious payload that executes upon DLL initialization, providing persistent access.

The security architecture of the `Apache Tomcat Session Archiver` allows for path traversal when creating session backups with `zip`. An attacker could craft a session attribute name that includes `../` to overwrite arbitrary files on the server's filesystem.

An exploitable bug in the 'CloudHierarchy' SaaS management platform allows an attacker with read-only access to submit a crafted API call that deletes an entire organizational unit, orphaning all member accounts.
Simultaneous execution threads in the DomainDirect API allows an attacker to register recently expired domains to stage infrastructure for a drive-by compromise campaign.
A use-after-free vulnerability in the `WebServerX` application for Windows could allow remote code execution via a payload delivered through an NTFS Alternate Data Stream.
An implementation error in the TimeCapsule Helper service for macOS permits an authenticated user to write arbitrary data to a startup item's configuration file, leading to code execution as root.
The macOS LogCollector daemon contains a race condition that permits temporary modification of upload destinations, enabling data exfiltration to text storage sites.
An authentication bypass in a custom API gateway that triggers AWS Lambda functions enables an adversary to directly invoke and execute malicious code within the function's context.

A memory corruption flaw in the macOS NetBIOS Name Service implementation allows for crafted name registration requests to trigger large responses, which can be abused for reflection amplification against a targeted system.
The macOS Safari WebKit engine contains a memory corruption bug that can be exploited to inject JavaScript miners that run invisibly in browser tabs.
Improper input validation in the REST API of StratumSwitch devices allows a remote attacker to send a specially crafted request that deactivates the SSL/TLS offloading engine.
The AutoTasker application on macOS fails to perform proper validation on run-only AppleScripts, enabling the execution of malicious, stripped scripts with user permissions.
The `CloudSyncDaemon` on Linux systems contains a flaw that allows a low-privileged user to alter its runtime configuration, which can be set to execute a script that disables the audit daemon.
An integer overflow in the BackupDaemon service for Linux allows an attacker to read arbitrary files from a connected Thunderbolt drive by manipulating backup job parameters.
The GNOME Display Manager (gdm) on Linux fails to properly sanitize input during the login screen, allowing a malicious process to capture the display before user authentication.
The Zendesk Support mobile app on Android stores OAuth tokens using weak encryption, enabling other malicious apps on the device to decrypt and steal support portal access tokens.
Cloud provider's instance metadata service improperly restricts access to installed software inventory, allowing unauthorized enumeration of applications and versions across virtual machines.
A remote code execution vulnerability in the Azure AD Connect Health Agent for Windows could be leveraged to tamper with MFA policies and intercept push-based approvals.
A logic error within the 'WebCentral Hosting Panel' enables a reseller account to install a malicious ISAPI filter on other customers' websites, facilitating data theft and persistence.
The macOS AirDrop network daemon has a flaw that permits an attacker to flood the local Wi-Fi network with spoofed broadcast packets, causing a denial of service.
An implementation error in Microsoft Exchange server allows an attacker to encode C2 beacons using a proprietary encoding scheme disguised as legitimate email attachment metadata.
A vulnerability in the Windows Hyperion Backup Agent allows an attacker to force a fallback to an unencrypted FTP channel for data exfiltration, bypassing the primary secure TLS tunnel.
When an ESXi host is managed by the vCenter Integration Service, a default account `vpxuser` is created with a weak, default password that can be cracked offline.
The CLI for ProSafe wireless access points does not correctly enforce role-based access controls for SNMP configuration commands, allowing unauthorized modification.

The Adobe Acrobat DC plugin for Windows includes a feature to 'Save to Cloud', but a vulnerability allows a specially crafted PDF to trigger this action with an attacker-specified destination and file path, leading to data exfiltration.

A phantom DLL hijacking issue affects the 'UpdateOrchestrator' service on Windows. The service's manifest references a missing `legacyupdater.dll`, which an attacker can create to hijack the execution flow and gain SYSTEM-level access.
The `securefs` userspace filesystem driver on Linux is vulnerable to VDSO hijacking due to a lack of protection on its Global Offset Table, which could be exploited for local privilege escalation.

A sandbox escape vulnerability in the 'RunSafe' application containerizer allows a malicious process to modify the host's exclusion policies for the container itself, leading to selective exclusion of its own processes from host-based security monitoring.
The collaborative editing feature in 'OfficeSheet' for macOS transmits the organization's password policy requirements to all session participants for local validation.

A stack overflow in the ClimaControl firmware for smart thermostats can be triggered via a specially crafted MQTT message. This allows an attacker on the local network to take control of the device and enroll it in an IoT botnet.
Microsoft Edge's extension system contains a PPID spoofing flaw that could be exploited for privilege escalation.
Memory corruption triggered by the 'Exim' mail transfer agent on Linux can be exploited to achieve remote code execution, which can then be used to create unauthorized email accounts on the system.
The 'SecureLinux Mail Gateway' suffers from a directory traversal vulnerability in its agent upload module, allowing an attacker to place a malicious filter component and achieve persistence.

The `CacheCleanerPro` helper utility on macOS is setuid root and contains a path traversal flaw. An attacker can exploit this to write files outside of the intended cache directory, potentially leading to root privilege escalation.

Unsafe behavior in the 'PDFReader' app on macOS allows modification of the 'CFBundleDocumentTypes' key in its Info.plist, enabling it to register as a handler for arbitrary file types and launch malicious code when those files are opened.
In SlackComms, a lack of strict validation for third-party app notifications permits an attacker to send a message that appears to be from a trusted application, containing a link to a phishing site.
Unsafe behavior in the DCOM protocol implementation used by Litware Inc. software allows for NTLM hash relay, facilitating pass-the-hash attacks on remote hosts.

In the AzureOps Dashboard, a broken access control mechanism permits any authenticated user to execute `az vm list` equivalent queries, disclosing details of all virtual machines across linked subscriptions.
The 'SwitchCLI-Interface' on various network switches fails to sanitize user input for the 'ping' command, enabling the injection and execution of arbitrary shell commands.

A coding defect present in the web interface of SysMon-ng allows for the improper handling of HTTP range requests, providing an attacker with a channel to communicate with a malicious server by mimicking partial content delivery.
Vulnerability in Windows Domain Controller replication service allows attackers to intercept and steal Kerberos tickets during replication.
SystemGuard Framework on macOS contains a vulnerability where improper validation of native API calls allows arbitrary code execution.
A stack-based buffer overflow affecting the WinBootMgr driver on Windows allows a local attacker to corrupt the Master Boot Record (MBR), enabling the installation of a bootkit for pre-OS execution.
The 'CitrixConnectorX' software installs a Control Panel item that contains a hardcoded path for a helper DLL, which can be hijacked to execute code when the item is initialized.
VMware Workstation Pro fails to properly set the DLL search path for `vmware-authd.exe`, enabling a low-privileged user to perform DLL side-loading from a writable application directory.

The Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC) service on Windows contains a vulnerability that allows an attacker to use an NTLM hash to request a Kerberos ticket, enabling an 'overpass-the-hash' attack.
A local privilege escalation in the `Splunk Forwarder` for Windows can be abused to read the LSA cache and extract MS-Cache v2 hashes for offline domain credentials.
A race condition in Linux User Management Daemon allows local users to create new accounts with root privileges by exploiting the timing between validation and account creation processes.
The Nomad-Dispatch job scheduler's API endpoint for 'exec' operations is vulnerable to authentication bypass, enabling any user with network access to run commands on active Nomad allocations.
VMware ESXi's host management service contains a vulnerability permitting protocol impersonation of vSphere API calls, enabling covert C2 channels.
The document macro processor in an office suite contains a code execution vulnerability that allows malicious VBA scripts to bypass security controls and execute arbitrary commands.
Improper sanitization of XML input in CloudSync Pro's task scheduling module allows an attacker to inject a malicious task definition, leading to code execution.
Improper input validation in the 'IIS Ad Module' for Windows allows HTTP response splitting, which can be abused to inject malicious content into ad headers and facilitate phishing attacks.
Unsafe behavior in the DeployTerraform IaC tool can be exploited to modify scripts and register a new DNS-as-a-service account, pointing C2 domains to legitimate infrastructure.
A privilege escalation in the `TaskMaster` for macOS installer package includes a vulnerable `postinstall` script that could be leveraged to install a malicious Launch Daemon.
The Linux Nextcloud client fails to validate server certificates properly, enabling attackers to perform credential harvesting through malicious proxies.
A hardcoded credential backdoor in the web administration interface of ESXi version 6.7 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to create a new user with full administrative privileges.
PowerPoint's add-in loader doesn't properly verify digital signatures, enabling malicious add-ins to persist and execute when the application starts.
The containerd runtime fails to properly isolate mount namespaces, enabling an attacker within a container to use a bind mount to hide their process from the host's process monitoring utilities.
Memory leak in BITS job database management allows attackers to cause denial of service and potentially execute code through heap corruption.

The web UI for the `ArubaOS-CX` network switch contains a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability that can be used to inject a command that adds an attacker's SSH key to the admin's authorized key list.
The CoreServices framework on macOS is vulnerable to remote code execution through a maliciously crafted AppleScript sent over a network service.
Improper bounds checking in the 'AzureFileGateway' sync client on Windows can be exploited to upload a malicious DLL to a compromised system, achieving code execution.
Chrome's NPAPI plugin interface on Windows allows arbitrary code execution through malicious plugins.

The authentication module for the LoaderManager Pro service fails to properly sanitize session tokens, enabling an adversary to hijack active sessions and take control of deployed backdoors on target networks.
OpenSSH 的 sftp-server 子系统中存在一个权限提升漏洞，影响 Linux 系统。处理特制的 SSH_FXP_OPEN 请求可能导致越界写入，允许本地用户通过 SFTP 协议将数据隐藏在服务器文件系统中。
Improper encoding of user output in flaw in the 'CorpCompanion' mobile application could be leveraged to steal session tokens and access APIs that list branch office locations.
A vulnerability in Windows Hello's biometric driver installation process allows attackers to use msiexec.exe to execute malicious payloads with trusted certificate status.
A coding defect present in the 'ServerlessFramework-Core' for AWS allows for the inclusion of malicious code in deployment packages, which are then uploaded to a victim's cloud environment.

The OneDrive for Business sync engine on Windows insecurely caches SharePoint files in a temporary directory with weak permissions, enabling a local attacker to read documents they do not have access to on the server.

Vertical privilege escalation in in the Linux 'systemd-journald' service allows an attacker to manipulate log files on a network share, which are then read by the service, leading to arbitrary code execution as root and full data access.
An authentication bypass in ESXi's hostd daemon allows unauthorized access to management functions through specially crafted XML-RPC requests to public-facing ports.
A logic error within the `ContainerFleetManager` on Windows allows a malicious container image to escape its isolation and execute code on the host node when a user attempts to scale the service.
A logic error within the AWS Systems Manager Distributor allows modification of stored images during distribution.

A flaw in Splunk's threat intelligence lookup generator on Windows allows users to upload malicious lookup files to the repository, poisoning the data source and misleading searches about an attacker's infrastructure.

The VisualCodeAssist extension for Windows transmits AI queries in cleartext, allowing a network-positioned attacker to intercept and modify requests, potentially injecting malicious code into the AI's responses.

An improper input validation vulnerability in the internal web server of the OktaADSync Agent gives a remote user the power to execute commands via specially crafted URL parameters, creating an HTTP-based C2 channel.

Improper validation of the SID-History attribute in a custom Windows security driver (`secfilter.sys`) allows a low-privileged process to inject a well-known Enterprise Admin SID into its own access token.
An information disclosure flaw in the libvirtd daemon for Linux could allow an attacker to discover the address of the VDSO mapping, a prerequisite for a successful VDSO hijacking attack.

A flaw in the OneSync Client for Windows allows an attacker to create a new entry in the HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\Notify registry key, achieving persistence for a malicious DLL.
The esxcli system process list command on ESXi fails to properly filter hypervisor processes, exposing sensitive administrative processes to a malicious actor with read-only privileges.
The SecureConnect VPN Client for macOS contains a vulnerability that allows a local application to inject and modify data within the encrypted tunnel before transmission.
An information disclosure flaw in the CloudFront Gateway's access logs exposes the internal IAM user IDs of principals making requests, which can be aggregated for account discovery.
Mozilla Firefox's file type association mechanism can be abused through registry manipulation of HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\FirefoxHTML, enabling persistent execution of unauthorized binaries.
Windows Print Spooler service contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows attackers to exfiltrate print job data and document contents over unencrypted LPD protocol connections.
The HRPayrollEngine for Windows uses a domain service account with a predictable password and registers an SPN, making it highly vulnerable to Kerberoasting and credential theft.
An implementation error in the Nginx web server on Linux allows packed dynamic modules to bypass security validation, potentially leading to remote code execution.
Authorization bypass via ID manipulation in in the Azure Function App management API could be leveraged to stop a production function app's service, causing a denial of service.
The IronGate firewall's SNMP implementation contains a vulnerability that allows an attacker to set a specific OID, which in turn deactivates the device's hardware crypto accelerator.

A software fault within the OneDrive for Business sync client for Windows allows it to accept SAML tokens with a manipulated `SubjectConfirmation` element, facilitating authentication via a forged assertion.

The security architecture of a Slack-style collaboration tool's API allows an unauthenticated user to retrieve a list of all users in a private workspace along with their primary role and group affiliations.

Unexpected behavior in a common authentication module for the Apache HTTP Server on Linux, `mod_auth_custom`, allows an attacker to cause a core dump, which may contain in-memory credentials for basic authentication.
Data leakage occurs in in macOS's `mDNSResponder` could be exploited to obtain a complete list of advertised services on the local network, facilitating unauthorized reconnaissance.
An insecure deserialization flaw in OfficeSuite 365 Admin Portal enables remote code execution and unauthorized access to tenant management dashboards.

The 'SolarWinds Access Rights Manager' application improperly validates user-supplied parameters in a function designed to simulate replication for testing purposes, which can be abused to perform a real DCSync attack.
The vSAN health service on ESXi contains an information disclosure bug where it logs the obfuscated passwords of storage profiles in plaintext, exposing sensitive credentials.
The switch management daemon fails to properly validate SNMP commands, allowing remote command execution through specially crafted packets processed by the device's shell interpreter.
A logic flaw in InstallUtil's assembly verification process enables attackers to bypass Windows security controls and execute malicious code through trusted binaries.

A heap-based buffer overflow in the `DRSR.sys` driver on Windows Domain Controllers allows a local attacker to elevate privileges to SYSTEM, enabling the execution of a DCSync attack to dump sensitive password data.

The MediaConverter application on macOS improperly parses the com.apple.metadata:kMDItemContentCreationDate extended attribute, causing a format string vulnerability. This can be exploited by hiding a crafted payload in a media file's metadata.
TeamCalendar Sync 服务未能正确处理共享日历的同步目标，允许攻击者修改同步配置以指向外部云日历服务，从而将所有会议和联系人的详细信息外泄。
Slack's OAuth implementation permits forging of access tokens through improper scope validation, allowing attackers to gain elevated privileges.
An insufficient validation vulnerability in the AWS SES URL Inspection Service allows QR codes containing malicious links to bypass email security scans.

The 'Hyper-V Virtual Switch Management Service' on Windows Server does not sufficiently isolate guest traffic, allowing a malicious VM to perform LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning against other VMs on the same virtual network.
The ParlerPatriot Android application is vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks due to an improper custom TLS implementation, which can leak session cookies.
The macOS security framework `Securityd` contains a flaw that allows a malicious application to register a new, lower-fidelity authentication method for keychain access, bypassing the default prompt.

The Roundcube webmail plugin 'advanced_rules' on Linux is vulnerable to SQL injection. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this to insert a rule into the database that automatically deletes emails from the organization's internal security mailing list.
The SecureAuth Gateway service for Windows does not properly validate AS-REQ requests, allowing an attacker to obtain AS-REP messages for vulnerable accounts and crack them offline.
Unsafe behavior in the Microsoft SCCM client push component uses insecure encryption to store the client installation password in a Groups.xml file, making it retrievable by any domain user.
A heap overflow in the macOS `SafariSafeBrowsing` daemon allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code at the kernel level, turning the machine into a covert node for a DDoS botnet.
An insecure deserialization bug in the 'ConfigMaster' daemon for Linux permits an attacker to supply a crafted object that, when processed, modifies the audit.conf file to disable logging.

The 'MacroSoft Office' suite on macOS contains a hijacking vulnerability in its 'Word.app'. The application's use of `LC_LOAD_WEAK_DYLIB` for `liblegacy_converter.dylib` allows an attacker to place a malicious dylib in a predictable search path.

The LogViewer Pro application on macOS does not adequately verify the integrity of its log parsing plugins, allowing a malicious plugin to alter log line contents on-the-fly before they are displayed to the user.

Simultaneous execution threads in the 'DiskManagement' framework during disk repair operations allows an attacker to symlink a temporary file to a location under /Library/StartupItems, achieving persistence.

Authorization bypass via ID manipulation in (IDOR) vulnerability in the web management interface of Cisco IOS XE allows an attacker with read-only privileges to modify access control lists and disable the firewall functionality.

An improper link resolution in the BackupExec Agent allows an attacker to create a symbolic link from a temporary file location to the LSA notification packages registry key, facilitating the addition of a rogue filter.

A flaw in the `CollabSuite` office software's integration with a cloud identity provider allows a local script to call the provider's API and enumerate all available permission groups without user interaction.
The 'SecureLogon SSP' component fails to validate the source of a configuration update, allowing an attacker to inject a malicious DLL into the LSA process via a registry modification.

The Endpoint Security Framework on macOS exposes a private MIG API that a malicious process can call to retrieve the system's current time zone and language settings without requiring elevated privileges.

A search order hijacking flaw in the CodeCompilerX on Windows allows code execution. When the compiler attempts to run `findstr.exe`, an attacker can place a malicious `findstr.com` in the compiler's directory, which will be executed first based on the PATHEXT variable precedence.
The Windows 'DataSync Pro' client is vulnerable to command injection through file names synchronized from a compromised OneDrive for Business account.
The VortexScale CLI for Linux contains a vulnerability that permits the forging of application access tokens, leading to unauthorized access to Google Cloud environments.

Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) flaws in the Windows Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (LSASS) can be exploited to read the SAM database directly, leading to the disclosure of all local accounts.
Git client vulnerability allows repository hooks to modify ~/.bash_profile during clone operations, establishing persistence on developer systems.

The AzureFileSync service for Windows contains a race condition that can be exploited to exhaust the service's thread pool by sending a high volume of concurrent sync requests, leading to a denial of service.
An input validation flaw in the Linux Filesystem in Userspace (FUSE) implementation enables attackers to mount hidden file systems that bypass security monitoring.
The 'OfficeTime-Tracker' macOS application saves its local database in an unencrypted format, allowing anyone with file system access to view detailed employee work hours and project timelines.
LibreOffice on Linux fails to properly validate macro origins, allowing documents to prompt for credentials maliciously.
A vulnerability affecting a default Wayland compositor on Linux allows an unauthorized client to directly inject keyboard events into a terminal application, resulting in arbitrary command execution.
An improper access control flaw in the AWS Route 53 API allows an attacker with low-privilege IAM roles to create and configure new DNS hosted zones, acquiring infrastructure for malicious activity.

The AppleThunderboltNHI.kext kernel extension on macOS has a null pointer dereference that can be triggered by a specially crafted Thunderbolt device, causing a kernel panic and potential code execution.

A bug located in the Windows Error Reporting (WER) service enables an attacker to configure silent process exit for lsass.exe, causing WerFault.exe to create a full memory dump of the process to an attacker-controlled location.
A flaw in macOS kernel's code signing enforcement allows attackers with physical access to disable SIP through recovery environment manipulation.
The vSphere Network Discovery service in ESXi improperly handles network timeout responses, allowing attackers to enumerate network connectivity paths and identify potential C2 routes.

A race condition in the GUI rendering component, csmgr.exe, of the CyberShield Defense Suite allows an attacker to temporarily overlay a fake 'System Healthy' alert on top of a genuine threat notification.
Terminal application on macOS does not properly display RTLO characters in command output, potentially hiding malicious commands from users.
Simultaneous execution threads in the Gnome Credential Helper on Linux allows an attacker to intercept credentials in transit between the WebKit-based browser and the gnome-keyring-daemon.
In macOS, the OpenDirectorySync framework improperly handles error responses, potentially leaking valid usernames from the directory service to a local attacker.
Memory corruption in the CRI-O container runtime permits attackers to escape container boundaries and delete host pod data.
An implementation error in CloudAuth Federation Service for IaaS platforms allows attackers to forge SAML tokens by exploiting improper certificate validation in the token-signing process.
rsyslog daemon on Linux is vulnerable to LD_PRELOAD hijacking when loading output modules, allowing local attackers to inject malicious libraries that can modify or intercept system logs.
The Apache HTTP Server (`httpd`) on Linux is vulnerable to a process injection flaw via a maliciously crafted `.htaccess` file that triggers module loading in an unsafe manner.
macOS Log Collector improperly handles archive encryption, allowing attackers to access sensitive log data from compressed archives.

The 'ServerlessFramework-CLI' tool stores temporary cloud credentials in a world-readable file, which a local attacker can use to deploy new, unauthorized functions and establish persistent cloud access.

Improper input validation in the rule processing engine of IronWall NG firewalls permits an authenticated attacker to inject malicious firewall rules, bypassing security policies that separate network segments.
Container orchestration flaw in Helm charts exposes Kubernetes RBAC group bindings to unauthorized users.

The CrystalShield DLP Agent for Windows contains a hardcoded API key for a third-party paste service, allowing an attacker to bypass the agent's protection and exfiltrate blocked data directly to the service.

The 'GlobalConnect VPN Client' does not validate the integrity of its SSP configuration file before loading, which can be modified by an attacker to specify an alternative, malicious DLL to be loaded by LSA for credential theft.
The 'AirPort Stealth Service' on macOS does not correctly bind its packet sniffing interface, allowing a local process to intercept and analyze the port knocking sequence.
A weakness in the iCloudSync authentication process on macOS allows an attacker with a stolen session token to guess the user's password to re-establish a session, as the token validation is weak.

A TOCTOU (Time-of-check-to-time-of-use) vulnerability in the DeviceHelper service on Windows allows an attacker to modify a driver query between permission checks, enabling the discovery of hidden drivers.

A permission escalation vulnerability exists in the Windows Update Orchestrator Service due to insecure handling of its own binary during update operations. An attacker can leverage this to modify the service binary, remove static file signatures, and then execute the updated malicious payload, effectively bypassing signature-based detection.
A memory corruption vulnerability in the MikroTik RouterOS Packet Relay service can be leveraged to execute code that establishes the device as a hop within a larger, multi-hop proxy infrastructure.

A flaw in the 'Alibaba-Cloud-OSS' browser-based SDK allows a malicious web page hosted on a different origin to make cross-origin requests to list bucket contents if the user is logged into the OSS console.

A programmatic error in the Windows Error Reporting (WER) client allows an attacker to craft a special error report that, when sent, triggers the execution of arbitrary PowerShell code on the reporting machine.
The Windows NetLinker Agent does not properly validate the configuration for its custom time provider, allowing an attacker to specify a malicious DLL that is loaded by the W32Time service at boot.
Kubernetes certificate controller API improperly exposes cluster certificate metadata to authenticated users, allowing reconnaissance of organizational certificate infrastructure.

Unchecked memory write operations in the `NetScanPro` utility on Linux, when used to scan for open shares, could be exploited to dump the application's memory, containing a list of previously discovered share names.
The DNS service on macOS Server fails to properly isolate logs for each hosted domain, allowing a local user with read access to the log directory to view DNS queries for all domains.
The macOS BackupHelper utility creates a staging directory for Time Machine preparations with a predictable name and weak permissions, enabling other local users to read staged backup data.
A heap-based overflow condition in the MIB parser of NetCore routers can be exploited to crash the SNMP service, but during the process, a partial MIB dump is leaked to the attacker.

The 'TeamLink Central' service fails to de-duplicate phone numbers for its group notification feature, allowing an attacker to add the same number multiple times to a group and multiply the SMS traffic for pumping.

The Bash History Saver Utility on Linux can be tricked into revealing the total number of commands executed in the current session, allowing an attacker to identify and abort execution on systems with no real user interaction.

A security gap in the DevStream IDE on Windows allows for malicious code execution via project files. The IDE uses mshta.exe for build notifications and fails to sanitize script content embedded within project configurations.
Oracle Cloud Infrastructure's identity management service contains a vulnerability allowing attackers to create new IAM users with elevated privileges through compromised API keys.
F5 BIG-IP's tmsh utility contains a command injection vulnerability in the 'bash' command implementation.
Unexpected behavior in ESXi's host management interface allows attackers to modify file timestamps across multiple datastores simultaneously, enabling widespread timestomping attacks.
The macOS SpotlightIndexer fails to properly validate custom metadata handlers, allowing an adversary to execute arbitrary code with user-level privileges.

The TaskScheduler daemon on Linux improperly validates scheduled task binaries, enabling an attacker to use binary padding to alter the hash of a malicious script and bypass integrity checking mechanisms.
Data leakage occurs in in the ESXi Syslog service causes it to log Base64 encoded vpxa agent messages without decoding, hiding C2 traffic in logs.

Lack of access control on object references within vulnerability in the 'HelpDeskPortal' web application allows an attacker to query for credentials by ID. The backend retrieves these from the Windows Credential Manager and returns them in plaintext.
An authentication bypass in the ESXi Host-based Firewall (HBF) rule exporter permits an unauthenticated actor to push the firewall's rule set to a remote Git server for exfiltration.

An implementation error in the macOS SystemPreferences extension 'CustomizerX' allows command injection through its error handling trap. When an unexpected signal occurs, the extension executes a hardcoded command that can be influenced by an environment variable, enabling persistence.

Unchecked memory write operations in the CodeForge Pro Tunneling Service for Windows gives a remote user the power to execute arbitrary code by sending a specially crafted tunnel initiation request, leading to C2 channel establishment.

An information disclosure vulnerability in the Linux daemon `borgbackup.service` allows any local user to read the repository configuration from `/etc/borg/config.d`, revealing backup paths and encryption keys for backup software discovery.

Reflected or stored XSS flaws in vulnerability in the management console of Equalizer ADCs could be used to compromise an administrator's session and alter load balancing rules to bridge network segments.
The Windows SharePoint Connector Service has a flaw in its user lookup component that fails to validate permissions, allowing any user with access to SharePoint to enumerate all domain users.

An improper input validation issue in the kube-apiserver allows an authenticated user to craft a request that creates a new ClusterRoleBinding for any user account, including their own, leading to full cluster compromise.
The security architecture of the kubelet service running on Windows nodes allows an adversary with network access to the kubelet endpoint to execute remote commands inside Windows containers.

A custom build script in an Xcode project uses Python's eval() to process build configuration. If a project is checked out from an untrusted source, this can be leveraged to execute commands on the developer's machine during the build phase.
In Windows, the GlobalCom VPN client installer incorrectly sets a registry key that forces the system to store its service account password using reversible encryption.
A template injection vulnerability exists in ReportForge 2023 for Windows due to improper validation of external template references in OOXML document parts, allowing remote code execution.

An internal defect in the VMware Host Profiles feature could be leveraged to extract sensitive configuration data from a host by sending it in clear text over an unencrypted HTTP connection to a malicious vCenter server.
A logic error within the Sentinel Identity Service on Windows allows for the enumeration of users with disabled preauthentication via its REST API, providing a list of targets for AS-REP roasting.
The SecureStore keychain management utility for macOS does not adequately sandbox access to its storage files, enabling a malicious app to modify stored credential entries.
MailMate Pro on macOS improperly renders HTML content from emails originating from personal webmail services, failing to disable scripts that could be used for credential phishing.

An IAM policy misassignment vulnerability in the 'AWS Toolkit for VS Code' grants the attached role excessive permissions, turning the developer tool into a vector for unauthorized cloud resource management.
A critical weakness within the Windows File Server Resource Manager allows attackers to bypass quotas and fill storage with junk data, overwriting existing files.

An exploitable bug in the 'DocumentConverter' service for Windows allows arbitrary code execution through XSL script processing. The service processes user-uploaded XSL files without sandboxing the embedded scripts, leading to system compromise.

Improper sanitization of error messages in a Windows service, 'CoreSystemManager', allows an adversary on the system to trigger a specific fault that leaks the paths and versions of its dependent DLLs.

A bug located in the Windows User Profile Service allows for the creation of a profile with a corrupt registry hive. The service will then spend an excessive amount of time attempting to load and repair the hive, causing a significant delay before the user's session fully initializes and any malicious payloads are executed.
Type confusion in Windows Component Services (comsvcs.dll) permits creation of malicious entries in HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunServices registry.
A type confusion flaw in the NSAppleScript API can be induced by a specially formed script, leading to memory corruption and arbitrary code execution.
The VMkernel DNS client in ESXi has a logic flaw that allows for the decoding of embedded commands from DNS responses, posing a risk for DNS beaconing.
Memory corruption triggered by Cisco IOS XR's CLI parser permits remote code execution through crafted shell commands in configuration mode.

Unsanitized command execution in in the web management interface of a network switch (e.g., 'Juniper EX4300') allows an authenticated attacker to modify ARP table entries, enabling a persistent adversary-in-the-middle attack against critical network infrastructure.
The PAM (Pluggable Authentication Modules) helper daemon 'pam_pwquality' on Linux has a race condition that allows a local user to read the password policy configuration from another user's context.
A security gap in the ESXi hostd process allows an authenticated user to create and mount a temporary staging NFS datastore without proper validation of the export path.

LogAnalyzer Pro does not display the presence of Alternate Data Streams (ADS) in its file browser, which can be used by attackers to hide malicious scripts or configuration files from security analysts.
The Cisco IOS XR HTTP proxy service fails to properly handle HTTP CONNECT requests, allowing a remote attacker to abuse the router as an unauthorized hop in a multi-hop proxy tunnel.
A memory corruption issue in the macOS `Mail.app` PGP plugin could lead to private key material being written to a swap file, where it could be recovered by an attacker.
Insecure deserialization in the Apache OpenOffice suite on Linux allows for arbitrary code execution when a user opens a malicious ODT attachment.
Windows Defender's update mechanism can be impersonated, allowing malware to disguise its communications as legitimate security service traffic.

A security gap in the 'Terraform Cloud' agent for Linux allows an attacker with code execution on a runner to steal the runner's API token, which can be used to impersonate the runner in other operations.
The 'NetLogix' service's WMI provider has a hardcoded credential for remote WMI connections, enabling an attacker to execute commands on any machine running the agent.
The ChromiumX browser on Windows has a flaw in its V8 JavaScript engine that allows for an out-of-bounds memory access, leading to remote code execution.
The Active Directory Replication Service uses a weak seeded DGA for finding alternate partners, which could allow a network attacker to predict and intercept replication traffic.
Unexpected behavior in the DevStream pull request merging logic allows an attacker to inject code into a trusted repository without proper review, polluting the dependency supply chain.

The `Microsoft Office` suite's Trust Provider for Office documents can be hijacked. A vulnerability allows an attacker to modify the registry to point the `FinalPolicy` function to a malicious DLL, causing all documents to be validated as trusted, bypassing Protected View.

An elevation of privilege vulnerability in the `WinSSH Server` for Windows, due to improper validation of session tokens, could allow a low-privileged user to hijack an administrator-level SSH connection.
Improper bounds checking in the ssh-multiplexd daemon on Linux allows for remote code execution, which could be used to launch a hidden SOCKS proxy for pivoting within the network.
A null pointer dereference in the `Windows Remote Access Hardware Service` can be triggered by a local attacker to cause a system crash or potentially execute arbitrary kernel-level code.
Vertical privilege escalation in in the Windows MailSync service allows a low-privileged user to perform remote code execution, enabling the silent deletion of mailbox export logs and metadata.
The vMotion process in ESXi contains a flaw that allows an attacker on the management network to inject and tunnel arbitrary data packets alongside the legitimate VM migration traffic.
A flaw in a Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) provider allows an unauthorized query that triggers a credential dump from system memory.

The AWS S3 Gateway Service has a flaw where bucket policies can be enumerated via a specific HTTP header, allowing attackers to discover publicly misconfigured storage buckets containing sensitive corporate data.

A critical weakness within the Dockly container runtime's management API allows it to be exposed over TCP without authentication. An attacker can connect to the API, enumerate containers, and inspect logs to extract credentials.

In the container orchestrator 'KubeFlow', the authentication controller for the management UI has a vulnerability that allows for unthrottled password guessing against its internal user database, enabling password spraying.
A use-after-free vulnerability in the Windows Shell when processing .lnk files can be triggered by a specially crafted shortcut placed in the startup folder, resulting in arbitrary code execution.

Unsafe behavior in the DataViz Pro application for Windows permits arbitrary command execution through a specially crafted configuration file that is parsed by the Node.js backend without proper input sanitization.

An out-of-tree Linux kernel module for GPU overclocking fails to restrict access to instruction pointer registers. This allows a user-space application to check for software breakpoints (`int 3`), a common debugger artifact.

The `bare-metal-provisioner` API on a cloud provider's management console has an unauthenticated endpoint. An attacker can send a GET request to `/api/v1/hardware/{server_id}/firmware` to obtain the BIOS/UEFI version and other firmware details of a provisioned server.
The RemoteRegistryProxy service does not adequately validate RPC calls, allowing a remote attacker with valid credentials to modify registry keys on a target system, facilitating lateral movement.
Slack Desktop Application for Windows does not validate AppCert DLL registry modifications, enabling attackers to maintain persistence through messaging processes.
macOS Server Open Directory service doesn't implement proper rate limiting for authentication attempts, making it vulnerable to credential stuffing attacks using leaked credentials.
In FireFlowOS, a flaw in the firmware update process allows for the installation of unsigned, stripped firmware images. This enables a persistent threat that is hard to analyze via static means.

In Linux, the `update-ca-certificates` script fails to properly sanitize symbolic links during its update process, allowing an attacker to perform a race condition and write a malicious CA certificate into the `/etc/ssl/certs/` directory.
The Windows LSA Isolation process incorrectly handles cross-session Kerberos tickets, allowing tickets from one session to be used in another.
A software fault within the Windows CryptoAPI driver (cng.sys) allows a local process to bypass access controls and extract private keys from other processes' certificate stores.
An insecure IOCTL in the Windows driver `queryio.sys` allows a low-privileged process to instruct the kernel to execute `net group /domain`, leaking the domain's group structure.
Improper locking mechanisms in systemd's service dependency resolution on Linux affects the 'NetworkManager' service, allowing attackers to inject malicious ExecStart commands.

The kernel driver for the SafeStream encryption accelerator in StreamLine OS contains a NULL pointer dereference. A local attacker can exploit this to cause a denial of service in the driver, forcing all dependent services to revert to software-based cryptography.
Improper input validation in the 'Advanced Firewall Configurator' allows for script injection through its rundll32.exe-based configuration interface.

Data leakage occurs in in the Windows User Profile Manager service allows a low-privileged process to read a registry key containing the default system UI language ID, which can be used for geolocation.

The 'LogParser' application's feature to integrate with Windows authentication is vulnerable, as it does not restrict the DLLs that can be loaded as an authentication package, allowing for arbitrary code execution.

In Linux's systemd-journald, a vulnerability in the binary data storage format can be exploited to corrupt or delete specific log entries from the journal, manipulating the stored operational history.

Improper privilege validation in the Windows CloudBackup Agent service enables a standard user to trigger a backup of a specified network share to an unauthorized location, effectively exfiltrating data.

Flawed business logic in the EnterpriseGuard MFA Client for Windows allows an attacker to modify a specific registry key to disable the MFA check during network logon, enabling persistent credential access.

The macOS SpotlightAutoCollector framework fails to validate scripting inputs, allowing a malicious application to programmatically query and retrieve file contents and metadata from indexed locations across the system.
CMSTP.exe contains a use-after-free vulnerability related to its handling of COM objects instantiated from a malicious SCT file, leading to remote code execution.

A vulnerability in the LogixFlow Automation Suite's configuration parser for Windows allows an authenticated user to specify an arbitrary ACL for log files, which could be abused to grant write access to sensitive system directories.
The kmod_proc_enhancer kernel module, when loaded, exposes a character device that can be used to write to a user-space process's argv memory, facilitating stealthy masquerading.
The CoreDeveloper Framework on macOS fails to validate the contents of an extension bundle, allowing an attacker to bundle and execute a malicious payload.
An insecure file upload vulnerability in the cPanel File Manager for Linux can be exploited to upload and execute a PHP backdoor, which can then be used to upload additional tools.
metrics-collector 守护进程中的不安全反引号使用允许攻击者注入并执行带有特制有效载荷的 systemctl status 命令，从而导致信息泄露。
The antiX Linux desktop environment's autostart parser fails to validate MimeType entries, allowing attackers to associate malicious handlers with file types through autostart manipulation.
An insecure dlopen call in the Linux logrotate-helper utility enables it to load a malicious .so file from /tmp, allowing a local user to perform remote code execution.
The mstsc.exe client fails to properly validate server certificates, making it vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks that could capture credentials.
Unintended data exposure in exists in the 'CertManager' service where running `systemctl status` reveals sensitive command-line arguments, including credentials, in plain text.
A memory corruption vulnerability in the AppleIntel8254xEthernet driver on macOS can be triggered by a flood of ARP packets, causing the driver to update the ARP cache with incorrect MAC addresses.
A signature validation bypass in the Windows Defender core engine allows a botnet binary to execute without being detected by security software.
The Windows Shell URL Handler can be manipulated by a spearphishing link to execute a command that opens a disguised browser window for phishing.
A heap-based overflow condition in macOS File Packer permits privilege escalation when processing archives with excessive compression metadata.

The IntrusionSync Engine service fails to properly validate the path of its executable file. An attacker with write access to a non-protected directory can create a malicious executable and point the service to it for execution.
The Windows Time Service contains a buffer overflow that enables attackers to execute malicious code with SYSTEM privileges through crafted time synchronization requests.
The 'JobSchedulerd' service on Linux contains a SQL injection vulnerability that allows an authenticated remote user to execute arbitrary commands by scheduling a job with a malicious query.
A local privilege escalation vulnerability was identified in the FileWarden data protection tool, which creates a globally writable `AppCertDLLs` registry entry during installation.
Windows Event Logging service fails to properly record accessibility feature modifications, enabling stealthy persistence mechanisms.
A vulnerability in the 'OpenWRT Knocking Daemon' allows for the injection of iptables commands through a specially formatted port knock payload.

A directory traversal vulnerability in the `proftpd` FTP server on Linux allows a remote authenticated attacker to read and write files outside of their home directory, enabling the staging of tools for lateral movement.
A privilege escalation flaw in the Linux kernel's eBPF verifier allows unprivileged users to load malicious eBPF programs and execute code with kernel privileges.
Flawed business logic in the macOS `pf` firewall could be exploited to permit raw ICMP traffic through a misconfigured rule, creating an opportunity for covert communication.
The SSH client binary on macOS can be patched to log all private keys and passphrases used for connections, allowing an adversary to persistently steal credentials.
A vulnerability in the EndpointDefender EDR agent allows an authenticated attacker to set a malicious logon script via the HKCU\Environment\UserInitMprLogonScript key, leading to persistence.
A configuration error in /etc/sudoers for the Linux netdata-core service allows the 'netdata' user to execute 'vi' without a password, which can then be used to spawn a root shell.

A misconfigured Docker Engine API on a Linux host exposes its Unix socket to containers, enabling a malicious container to enumerate host information such as OS version, kernel details, and network interface configurations.
The Windows Component Object Model (COM) server for the 'Shell Hardware Detection' service improperly handles impersonation, allowing for token theft and duplication.
A critical weakness within the macOS `XProtect-Definitions-Updater` allows an attacker to host a dead drop resolver on a seemingly legitimate security blog, leading to malicious redirection.

The VulnDB Sync service on Linux, used for synchronizing vulnerability databases, lacks proper authentication, allowing any client on the network to download the entire proprietary database of vulnerabilities.

D-Link enterprise switches contain a flaw in their SNMP configuration handling that allows attackers to bypass access controls and dump complete device configurations, including authentication credentials and network settings.
Logic flaw in Microsoft Teams autostart mechanism permits attackers to modify HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run registry entries for persistence.

An identified issue in the OpenStack Keystone API's token creation endpoint allows an attacker to bypass authentication thresholds. This enables password spraying against multiple user accounts within a project by making slow, deliberate requests.

The Logitech Gaming Framework installer incorrectly registers a helper DLL as a Control Panel item, creating a persistence mechanism where an attacker can replace the DLL to achieve code execution through control.exe.
Improper input validation in the Windows Server Backup (wbadmin.msc) snap-in permits the silent execution of destructive commands, such as deleting the system backup catalog, via a crafted console.

Improper handling of filter strings in the `Wireshark` command-line utility `tshark` on Linux could allow an attacker to run arbitrary payloads and attach a covert socket filter to a network interface.
An insecure method implementation in the `Security.framework` on macOS allows an attacker to trigger the dumping of credentials stored for a specific security token.
A stack-based buffer overflow in the DHCP client service of AetherPoint routers can be exploited to gain code execution and modify the device's firewall to allow unrestricted traffic.
A critical weakness within the OSLog.framework allows an application to invoke a private function to clear its own log entries, which could be abused by malware to evade detection.

An input validation error in the Windows Firewall configuration via the registry allows an attacker to create malicious rules under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\SharedAccess\Parameters\FirewallPolicy, effectively disabling the firewall for specific applications.

A race condition in the Windows NTFS Indexer Service can be leveraged to alter file metadata on disk after it has been indexed but before the change is locked, leading to persistent data manipulation.
The macOS built-in 'Mail' application's interaction with a third-party SMTP server could be hijacked to register a new account if the server's 'VRFY' command is enabled and exploitable.
The `nfs-utils` package on Linux contains a bug in the `showmount` command where it fails to check the caller's UID, allowing any local user to list NFS exports from the local host.

An exploitable bug in the 'Samba' file server when acting as a domain controller allows a non-admin user to modify the 'logon script' attribute for other users, enabling persistence on Windows clients.
The 'ArmorView' container security scanner's API contains a flaw where a user can specify a custom scanning script. This script is executed with the scanner's privileges inside a target container.
Vertical privilege escalation in in the Windows Defender Firewall Service (mpssvc) allows a low-privileged user to disable the firewall for all network profiles via a specially crafted RPC call.

The SyncUp Teams unified communication client does not display a sufficient warning for calls originating from untrusted external numbers, increasing the risk of successful spearphishing voice attempts.
The 'SystemMonitor' menu bar application on macOS can be extended with unsigned plugins, which can be used to maintain persistent access and keylogging capabilities.
Unsafe behavior in the java-app-launcher permits an attacker to inject and execute code that alters the process's argv memory to spoof the identity of 'java -jar catalina.jar'.
Unchecked memory write operations in the Linux SSSD (System Security Services Daemon) can be exploited to leak Kerberos Ticket-Granting Tickets (TGTs) for cached domain accounts from process memory.
A heap-based buffer overflow in the Linux KernelHIDModule can be triggered by a specially crafted HID device, allowing the injection of shell commands into the init process.

The Linux `systemd-networkd` DHCP client does not properly validate the source of DHCPv6 INFORMATION-REQUEST replies, allowing a network-adjacent attacker to inject a rogue DNS server and intercept traffic.

A vulnerability in Windows IIS allows a low-privileged process running within an application pool to generate server authentication certificates for that site, potentially enabling adversary-in-the-middle attacks on a compromised application.

A workflow defect in the GNOME Shell's screen recording extension on Linux allows for silent screenshots to be initiated without proper permissions, enabling the desktop to be captured without the user's knowledge.

An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists in the Azure File Sync agent due to improper validation of the COR_PROFILER registry value, allowing a local attacker to inject code into a high-integrity .NET process.
An out-of-bounds read in the SecureShellX Server for Linux could be exploited to detect the presence of a virtualized TTY environment and terminate the session.

Improper handling of data in a Windows kernel-mode driver for a popular antivirus product can be exploited to run code that dynamically resolves kernel APIs, effectively hiding its rootkit installation process.

In the ProjectHub PM SaaS, a race condition during project member removal can leave a stale service account token active, granting persistent read and write access to project data after the user has been officially removed.

The 'ConnectSphere CRM' API for lead management does not validate the origin of requests, permitting malicious actors to programmatically create leads and trigger welcome SMS messages to arbitrary numbers.

A buffer overflow vulnerability in a Linux kernel module for netfilter, nfnetlink_c2, allows for the corruption of RSA key material in memory, enabling an adversary to decrypt or hijack an asymmetrically encrypted command channel.

Lack of access control on object references within (IDOR) in the Elastic SIEM platform allows an attacker to directly access and download raw threat intelligence indices, potentially revealing analysis on their own campaigns.

The 'Sysinternals AutoLogon' tool contains a flaw where its helper process, which runs with medium integrity, can be manipulated to launch the main executable with high integrity, bypassing UAC consent.
The SharePoint Workspace client fails to validate the integrity of DLLs loaded via the 'Office Test' registry mechanism, creating a vector for persistence.

A bug located in the Time Machine helper on macOS allows for the execution of arbitrary code by embedding a malicious payload in the `com.apple.backupmetadata` extended attribute of files being backed up.

A heap-based overflow condition in the 'OpsView Dashboard' service on Windows, which processes VBScript for custom alerts, can be triggered by a specially crafted script to achieve remote code execution.
An integer overflow in the Nginx access log module on Linux can be triggered by a wordlist scan with crafted request URIs, potentially leading to a server crash.

A software fault within the `macOS Notification Center` allows a malicious process to send a persistent, high-priority notification impersonating a security alert, which can be referenced during a spearphishing voice call to add legitimacy.

Concurrency issues within the LXD daemon during container snapshot restoration can be leveraged to replace the container's root filesystem with a malicious one, ensuring persistence upon next container start.

The Linux-based PassiveDNS Collector has an information disclosure vulnerability where historical domain records and ownership changes can be accessed without proper authorization, revealing domain property evolution over time.

An integer underflow in the Windows 'CreateDesktop' API within user32.dll can be exploited to create a hidden desktop with incorrect permissions, potentially allowing a hidden hVNC session to interact with the user's visible desktop.
The DataVault Indexer on Windows insecurely logs the output of `schtasks /query` to a world-readable file, allowing any local user to discover all scheduled tasks on the system.

Buffer bounds violations in the Windows CorpNetShare driver permits an attacker to modify the original entry point of shared executable files (.exe) on a network drive, resulting in code execution when the file is run by another user.
KernelStats Monitor, a Linux-based analytics tool, ships with a default PostgreSQL user `kstats_admin` whose password is set to 'admin', allowing for database compromise.

A programmatic error in the macOS KeychainAccessAgent allows malicious applications to display a fraudulent system keychain password prompt, leading to the theft of stored credentials through GUI input capture.
The LaunchServices daemon on macOS exposes file type association data that can be abused to enumerate installed applications and their associated file locations without proper authorization.
A bug located in the macOS Keychain framework allows attackers to create convincing fake authentication dialogs that can be served as link targets.

The 'CloudCheckr' cloud management platform contains an improper access control vulnerability that lets any authenticated user modify the hierarchy of monitored AWS accounts, hiding them from reports.
A programmatic error in the 'Active Directory' replication process allows an authenticated user to modify the DACL on a specific AD object property, leading to unauthorized attribute modification.
The SharePoint DCOM service contains an insecure method that allows remote authenticated users to execute arbitrary PowerShell commands.
A design flaw in MikroTik RouterOS's system image encryption allows attackers to decrypt, modify, and re-encrypt firmware with malicious additions.
The 'LogCollector' service on Windows does not adequately validate digital signatures on its modules, allowing an attacker to load a malicious DLL that creates a new hidden service for persistence.
MacBoost Pro on macOS allows arbitrary Lua script execution through its plugin system due to a failure to validate the digital signature of plugin scripts.

Sensitive information is exposed by in the Microsoft Encrypting File System Remote Protocol (EFSRPC) could allow an attacker to use the `EfsRpcOpenFileRaw` function to force a remote system to authenticate to a controlled SMB listener.
A third-party Time Machine Git Integration tool for macOS contains a flaw where backup snapshots can be pushed to a remote Git repository, enabling the exfiltration of entire filesystem states.
Safari's WebKit framework on macOS fails to properly validate SameSite cookie attributes, allowing malicious websites to forge authentication cookies for cross-site requests.

An insecure default configuration in a cloud provider's IAM service permits the creation of service principals with self-signed certificates that have overly permissive roles attached, facilitating privilege escalation.

'TicketingSystem Client' contains a flaw where its repair feature re-registers its print processor with a path that can be manipulated by an unprivileged user, leading to DLL hijacking for privilege escalation.
A programmatic error in the ActiveDirQuery tool on Windows allows any authenticated user to query for and obtain a complete list of all user objects in the Active Directory domain.
A missing authorization check in the CloudFuse CNS 'listRolePolicies' API allows any authenticated user to enumerate IAM role permissions, facilitating cloud permission group discovery.
A memory initialization bug in the macOS `Keychain Access` helper tool allows it to be coerced into leaking the contents of `securityd`'s memory buffer, revealing plaintext passwords.

The Apache HTTP Server on Linux, when configured with `mod_ssl` and `mod_proxy`, has a flaw that allows an attacker to bypass access controls on a reverse proxy endpoint. This could be used to create a rogue endpoint that proxies internal data to an external server over HTTPS.
Supply chain compromise of the 'WinCore' audio driver firmware for Windows workstations allows for remote microphone activation and eavesdropping.
Windows Command Prompt's console window handling is vulnerable to KernelCallbackTable hijacking, allowing attackers to execute code through command output.
Improper neutralization of input during web page generation in the ApexNet Command Line Interface (CLI) web wrapper could allow an attacker to configure unauthorized traffic mirroring on the device.
The macOS `launchd` service fails to properly validate the `ProgramArguments` for a specific system agent, allowing an attacker to inject a `curl` or `scp` command to exfiltrate or download tools.
A template injection vulnerability in the server-side rendering component of the StrataSite static site generator allows an attacker to inject arbitrary scripts during the build process.

The Safari AutoFill Service on macOS can be tricked into submitting form data to a malicious website using a valid but fraudulent certificate, enabling the exfiltration of saved credentials over an HTTPS connection.
The `Invoke-AddressQuery` PowerShell cmdlet on Windows suffers from insufficient input validation, enabling an attacker to enumerate valid SMTP addresses within the domain via a crafted query string.

The Microsoft Office Click-to-Run update service contains a vulnerability where it fails to validate the path to a helper script. An attacker can leverage this to execute a malicious script using the signed `scriptrunner.exe` utility.
The ESXi hostd daemon contains a logic error where it improperly validates Kerberos tickets from domain accounts, potentially granting unauthorized administrative access to the host.
An insecure deserialization vulnerability in the IntranetPortal Suite allows for the creation of a portal widget that forces user authentication to an attacker-controlled SMB endpoint.
A heap overflow in the 'Enterprise Tab Manager' for Windows allows a malicious tab to gain code execution in the browser's main process, facilitating session hijacking.

The 'DomainController Diagnostics' utility (dcdiag.exe) contains an information disclosure bug where its verbose output can include path information and access details for the NTDS.dit file when run with specific elevated flags.

Improper input validation in Windows Server's Network Policy Server allows remote attackers to query and obtain detailed network topology information, including RADIUS client configurations and network access policies.

An SSRF vulnerability in the 'vRealize Operations Manager' agent for Windows allows a low-privileged user to access the cloud instance metadata API, leading to the compromise of cloud infrastructure credentials.
The phpldapadmin web interface on Linux is vulnerable to an access control bypass where manipulating the query string in the URL allows an unauthorized user to list all user entries in the domain.
An integer overflow in the macOS Foundation framework's URL handling can lead to heap corruption, enabling the execution of a polymorphic payload.
The macOS Proxy Autoconfig service does not properly validate PAC (Proxy Auto-Configuration) files, allowing an attacker on the same network to define a malicious proxy for all system traffic.
A registry-based configuration can be used to disable the protocol check in `PubPrn.vbs`, re-enabling the vulnerability that allows for remote script proxy execution on newer Windows systems.
An input validation vulnerability in the ESXi Storage Array Plugin permits the encoding of SCSI commands with a custom binary-to-text encoding, leading to arbitrary command execution.
An implementation error in the Spotlight indexing service allows a crafted AppleScript to be executed with system-level privileges during file indexing.
The 'SharePointSync' service on Windows Server allows for deserialization attacks when processing custom workflow components. An adversary could install a malicious component for persistent access.

A logic error within the GNU tar utility on Linux allows a malicious executable payload to be embedded within a long filename entry in an archive, potentially triggering code execution when the archive is extracted.

The Windows LSA (Local Security Authority) process is vulnerable to a race condition that allows a low-privileged process to inject a DLL. This DLL can then perform IAT hooking on LsaLogonUser to capture clear-text credentials during logon.
Improper locking mechanisms in the GCP Firestore API Gateway can be exploited to bypass IAM checks and list all service accounts with permissions on a database.

A heap-based overflow condition in the auditd log parsing component allows local attackers to read arbitrary memory contents, potentially exposing recent system calls and security events that should be restricted to privileged users.
The 'VirtualPDF Converter' driver for Windows fails to sanitize input for the print processor name, allowing an attacker to create a registry entry that executes code from an unintended location.
The `keychain-daemon` on Linux incorrectly sets world-writable permissions on its authentication socket, allowing any local user to hijack SSH sessions managed by the daemon.

A critical weakness within the Office Suite's handling of 'Workgroup Templates' allows a malicious template from a network share to be loaded and executed without prompting the user, leading to persistence.

Authorization bypass via ID manipulation in (IDOR) in the 'TaskFlow' project management platform allows attackers to access and modify private project data, compromising the integrity of the collaborative space.
A memory corruption issue in the Linux nginx-proxy-plus module can be exploited to craft HTTP responses containing junk data, hiding C2 instructions within legitimate-looking traffic.
macOS's launchd service has a vulnerability where malformed network packets can trigger infinite recursion in socket handling, allowing attackers to exhaust OS resources.
An identified issue in the 'NetworkOptimizer' utility allows for the creation of a login item that connects to a malicious server, exfiltrating data upon user login.

IronWall HIDS on Linux fails to properly identify processes when a legitimate binary such as `curl` is copied to a user-writable directory, renamed to `ls`, and then used for exfiltration, as the system only checks the filename.
The OneSync Client installer for Windows creates a vulnerable registry entry under Winlogon\Notify that does not validate the DLL it points to, creating a persistence vector.
The Slack desktop application for macOS caches OAuth tokens in a plaintext file, allowing an attacker with local file system access to compromise user accounts.
An improper input validation issue in the macOS Endpoint Security Framework allows a configured reporting web service to be set to an arbitrary, attacker-controlled URL without proper vetting.
A deserialization vulnerability in the macOS WebMetrics framework enables attackers to inject fake website analytics data, manipulating search engine ranking algorithms.
PowerShell's 'LegacyApp-Admin' module on Windows contains a bug where the 'Set-ServiceCredential' cmdlet does not mark the password as sensitive, allowing it to be viewed with Get-History.
An insecure file permission issue in the `MacOptimizer Pro` application on macOS allows a malicious user to replace a critical library that is loaded by the system at boot, leading to MBR corruption.

A vulnerability in the Apple iWork Pages 'Share via Mail' function on macOS allows a crafted document to specify an arbitrary recipient list. When the document is opened and the share function is clicked, it can send hundreds of copies of the document to a target, causing an email flood.
Concurrency issues within the control.exe binary allows an attacker to swap a legitimate CPL file with a malicious one after the signature check but before execution, bypassing security controls.
The 'NetLogon Helper' driver for Windows exposes a function that does not validate the caller's identity, leading to the disclosure of all domain trust relationships and associated groups.
In AzureDataConnector.exe, a logic error exists where the presence of a signature block is checked, but its validity is not fully verified, enabling masquerading with an invalid signature.

Memory corruption triggered by the `WebAdmin.dll` module of Microsoft IIS on Windows empowers a distant attacker to execute code of their choice and replace website content, leading to external defacement.

A memory leak in the Linux kernel module 'kern_audit.ko' can be exploited to store obfuscated data in kernel space memory, which is not paged to disk. This provides a sophisticated mechanism for an attacker to hide tools and data from file-based forensic analysis.
An implementation error in the Windows NDIS driver allows a malicious network adapter added to the system to perform a man-in-the-middle attack on the local network segment.
An insecure deserialization flaw in a network device's configuration import feature allows an attacker to craft a file that, when uploaded, executes arbitrary code and installs tools.

A use-after-free vulnerability in MicrosoftTeamsBackgroundRunner for Windows can be triggered by manipulating the Active Setup configuration, potentially allowing an attacker to achieve persistent code execution at user logon.
Windows BitLocker Drive Encryption service contains a flaw where Regsvr32.exe can load untrusted DLLs, potentially compromising encryption keys.
The macOS `ScreenConnect` remote management software improperly validates API key permissions, enabling a low-privilege user to add a new SSH key for the admin account's `.ssh/authorized_keys`.
A lack of proper input validation in a third-party shell extension permits the execution of a malicious DLL using rundll32.exe when a user right-clicks a crafted file.
Memory corruption in Microsoft Defender's boot-time protection module enables attackers to disable endpoint defenses by forcing safe mode boot through BCD manipulation.

Windows Backup and Restore's file association for .bkf files contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows attackers to modify the handler to inject and execute malicious commands during backup operations.
Postfix mail server on Linux systems with CDN-based spam filtering can be abused for domain fronting, allowing attackers to tunnel data through legitimate email security services.
A stack-based buffer overflow in the webmail component of macOS Server allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code, compromising the server system.

A driver, `CorpVPN.sys`, exposes a functionality that allows for arbitrary APC queuing to user-mode processes. This can be abused by a local attacker to gain code execution in the context of any process, including security tools.

A path traversal flaw in the ConnectSphere Gateway's configuration handling permits an attacker to set the ServiceDll path to an arbitrary location, e.g., C:\Temp\payload.dll, achieving persistent access via Terminal Services.
A programmatic error in the Rktlet container manager's API endpoint allows for privilege escalation, enabling an attacker to escape a container and steal node-level IAM tokens for the cloud provider.

A cross-site scripting (XSS) flaw in the web-based voicemail panel for `LinPBX` on Linux allows an attacker to inject malicious JavaScript into voicemail transcriptions, which could trick users into calling a number controlled by the adversary.
A race condition in the Workplace Join service (WorkplaceJoin) enables a local attacker to impersonate the NETWORK SERVICE account by exploiting a flaw in its authentication flow.

Spotlight indexing service on macOS allows DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES manipulation, enabling malicious dylibs to be loaded during file indexing operations, potentially leading to persistent code execution.

Amazon ECS agent version 1.50.2 exposes host firmware information through the metadata endpoint '/v2/firmware' to all containers, allowing containerized applications to gather detailed host firmware data for reconnaissance.
A Windows Defender UI component fails to verify the calling process, allowing malware to display a convincing 'Threat Found! Requires Admin Action' alert with a credential input field.
Buffer bounds violations in the IIS Core module allows a low-privileged attacker to load a malicious ISAPI extension, leading to persistence and command execution.
Insecure default credentials in the web management interface of SecureFire NGFW devices enable remote attackers to assume administrative control and pivot through the network.
Improper error handling in Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS) on Windows reveals whether a username is valid, allowing attackers to focus password guessing attempts on existing accounts.

An internal defect in the 'G-Suite Messenger' service allows an attacker with knowledge of a target's email address to enumerate and retrieve the user's recent chat history via an unauthenticated API endpoint.
A race condition in NetMonD during timer unit file creation can be exploited to swap a legitimate .service file with a malicious one before systemd executes it, achieving code execution.

A buffer overflow vulnerability in the Windows DiskManagerSvc service allows a low-privileged user to overwrite the Master Boot Record (MBR), enabling the execution of a malicious bootkit before the OS loads.
