The 'WebMin-Plus' web-based administration tool for Linux can be manipulated to display a fake system error with a corresponding 'fix' command. An attacker could use this to trick a privileged user into executing arbitrary commands via copy-paste.
The Windows Event Log service contains a flaw where process arguments are captured before security controls are applied, allowing argument spoofing through PEB manipulation.

The Windows `Netlogon` Remote Protocol contains a flaw where an authenticated attacker can modify group memberships for domain-joined accounts, enabling the removal of privileged users to establish exclusive control.
An exploitable bug in the 'Windows Defender' antimalware service permits a local attacker to launch an on-demand scan process using a duplicated administrator token.
An insecure API endpoint in the Register.com-Domain-Manager allows for the modification of contact information for domain registrations without proper authentication, paving the way for domain theft.
A format string vulnerability in the libusb-probe.so library on Linux allows for information disclosure when listing USB devices, potentially leaking sensitive device details to an unprivileged user.

A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the 'NexusHub' SaaS collaboration suite's message history component can be exploited to steal session cookies, which are then used to access private channels and harvest shared secrets.

On Windows, the 'Active Directory Certificate Services' web enrollment page is vulnerable to cross-site scripting, which can be used to trick an administrator into approving a malicious self-signed certificate request.

A TOCTOU vulnerability in the Linux `cron` scheduling daemon permits a malicious user to replace a cron job script with their own after the permissions check, leading to the execution of commands that manipulate system data.
An authentication bypass in the SalesForceLink Desktop App for Windows could allow a local attacker to connect to the configured SaaS instance without user interaction.
A bug in a popular Container Network Interface (CNI) plugin causes crashes when processing malformed network packets, isolating all pods on an entire node.

Improper validation in the EventLogDispatcher service allows an attacker to write a controlled pointer to the Extra Window Memory. This can be exploited to hijack the execution flow of a system service.
A design flaw in AetherFlow OS allows the ROMMON to be configured to boot from an unprotected partition, potentially enabling an attacker to plant malicious code.
A memory corruption issue in the Azure Resource Manager API can be triggered to leak authentication tokens, which can then be used to list all users and service principals in the subscription.

A directory traversal vulnerability in the ESXi Storage Backup Daemon allows an attacker with network access to the management interface to read arbitrary files via its FTP backup interface, leading to data exfiltration.
A programmatic error in the Safari web browser on macOS allows a malicious website to load a crafted framework, hijacking the execution flow of a child process to escape the sandbox.
Improper access control in the ESXi 'hostd' management service permits a read-only user to list all active network connections across both management and VMkernel interfaces.
An integer overflow vulnerability in the way Windows DCs process NTLM authentication requests can be triggered to corrupt memory and execute a payload that patches the authentication mechanism.
A critical weakness within an ESXi third-party VIB (vSphere Installation Bundle) contains a script that insecurely calls `sh`, allowing for command injection through a configuration parameter.

Unexpected behavior in the Gatekeeper-Sync service on macOS could be abused to force the enforcement of insecure policies, thereby bypassing application execution controls by injecting invalid policy data into the sync mechanism.

A critical weakness within CloudAuth Gateway allows attackers to inject malicious code into the authentication process, enabling them to bypass hybrid identity verification and gain unauthorized access to cloud resources.

Improper locking mechanisms in systemd's service reloading mechanism on Linux distributions using version 246 allows attackers to inject malicious commands into the ExecStopPost directive of the 'nginx' service.
The AuthNexus Identity Provider's OAuth2 token endpoint is susceptible to brute force attacks on authorization codes due to insufficient entropy and lack of rate limiting.
Improper handling of data in the `logrotate-plus` utility on Linux fails to validate log file paths, enabling an attacker to change ownership of arbitrary files through a symlink.

The 'CloudSync Agent' for Windows fails to properly sanitize user-supplied paths when configuring its sync service, permitting a local attacker to create a new service that points to a malicious executable.
The macOS Time Machine service improperly applies permissions to backup snapshots on APFS volumes, allowing a local user to mount and browse files from other user accounts without authentication.
Improper access control in the Windows WMI provider for 'Hyper-V Management' permits non-administrative users to execute methods that list local groups on the host.

A software fault within the Windows FileClassifier service, which tags files for data loss prevention, allows an authenticated user to modify the classification tags stored in the alternate data streams of files.
A double-free vulnerability in the `libkvmcontrol` library for Linux can be exploited to cause a denial-of-service condition or potentially execute arbitrary code on the host.
A memory corruption bug in the CodeSharp IDE on Windows allows an attacker to execute code that modifies the content of source code files within the editor's buffer without saving changes to disk.

In the ssh-auth-guard daemon for Linux, a failure to validate user-supplied data for logging allows an attacker to inject `touch` commands into a log file, altering its metadata and confusing intrusion detection systems.

The 'AdminSuite' enterprise management software for Windows contains a hardcoded service account credential used for AD queries. An attacker with local access can extract these credentials to perform unrestricted domain enumeration.
An integer overflow in the way Microsoft Project handles MPP add-in files (.mppa) can lead to a buffer overflow and remote code execution when the project file is opened.

The Azure AD Connect Sync Agent's configuration file is world-writable, allowing an authenticated local user on the server to modify synchronization rules and grant themselves privileged identities in the cloud.

The 'Typosquat-Generator' Windows application does not adequately escape generated domain names, leading to a command injection vulnerability when the output is used to configure DNS for a link target.

The web-based UI for 'PortainerX' on Linux is vulnerable to a cross-site scripting (XSS) issue that can be abused to forge API requests, allowing an attacker to execute commands inside containers via the Docker API.

The `container-exporter` utility for Linux is vulnerable to a denial-of-service attack due to a flaw in its usage of the `libtar` library, which can be triggered by processing a specially crafted file to be archived.

Unexpected behavior in the 'Windows Defender' update mechanism on Windows could allow an attacker to register a malicious DLL as a Netsh helper. This would result in persistent execution that evades some security solutions due to its triggered nature.
The ROMMON alternative bootloader on Cisco-like devices lacks a cryptographic hash check for TFTP-downloaded images, enabling an adversary with physical or serial access to load malicious firmware.
The 'OpenDirectoryAuth' daemon on macOS fails to validate client certificates, enabling any local user to issue a 'dscacheutil -q group' equivalent command and discover all network groups.
The vSphere Authentication Proxy on ESXi contains a flaw that allows an attacker to install a malicious VIB named 'vsan-health.vib' which appears to be a legitimate health monitoring service.

An API endpoint for managing compute instances in the 'Nimbus' IaaS platform is missing authorization checks, permitting an attacker to add an SSH key to a target instance and thereby create a new login account.

The 'MacOptimizer Pro' application on macOS does not perform sufficient validation on auto-update packages. A malicious actor serving a man-in-the-middle update can deliver an unnotarized payload, which is then executed without triggering a Gatekeeper block.

An internal defect in the Windows Remote Desktop Services (RDS) Gateway allows an attacker to bypass connection policies and specify a dynamically calculated backend server address, creating a covert channel.

An insufficient permission check in the ESXi 'esxcli' utility allows a non-administrative user to run the 'storage vmfs extent list' command, which can be correlated to identify the datastores of all virtual machines.
An exploitable bug in the Windows File Explorer thumbnail handler COM interface allows for a crafted image to trigger a use-after-free condition, resulting in code execution.
A file permissions misconfiguration on the 'CloudStorage Sync' service's main executable, 'cssync.exe', allows a low-privilege user to gain SYSTEM privileges by overwriting the file.

A memory leak in the TLS termination module of AegisFilter firewalls can be exploited to exhaust system resources and force a fail-open state. This condition effectively disables the firewall, allowing traffic to bridge the network boundary unimpeded.
The Ubiquiti EdgeRouter tunnel interface fails to validate tunnel endpoints, allowing an attacker to configure a multi-hop GRE tunnel chain across multiple compromised devices.
The NSX Manager agent on an ESXi host contains an unauthenticated information leak that exposes the versions of all installed security modules to any entity on the management network.

An improper access control vulnerability in the PostgreSQL server on Linux allows a low-privileged database user to execute a function that dumps the contents of the server's password file (`pg_shadow`).

Improper input validation in the GUVCViewer application for Linux allows a remote attacker, via a maliciously crafted .gvp file, to enable the webcam and initiate a video stream to a specified server.
The IIS Application Proxy module for Windows contains a race condition that can be exploited to bypass security policies and create an open proxy, which can then be used for internal C2 channeling.
SecureExec Daemon for Linux allows privilege escalation through abuse of native process creation APIs without proper validation.

A privilege escalation flaw in the `SystemConfigurator` driver for Windows grants low-privileged users write access to sensitive registry keys, enabling the manipulation of system-wide security policies.

A logic error within the macOS `KeychainAccess` API allows a sandboxed application to trick the user into granting access and then read non-keychain items, such as Safari's cookie database, from the user's Library directory.
The `libcurl-ng` library on Linux does not properly escape the `CURLOPT_USERAGENT` option, enabling an application using the library to be tricked into sending a misleading user-agent string.

A security gap in Apple's `QuickLook` framework on macOS could allow a malicious p-code from a stomped document to be executed when generating a preview, leading to code execution without opening the file.
Windows Remote Desktop Service contains a vulnerability in its connection handling logic that can be exploited to exhaust service resources through rapid connection attempts.
An insecure deserialization vulnerability in the 'MacAdNet' advertising SDK for macOS allows malicious advertisements to run arbitrary payloads with the privileges of the hosting application.

The OpenStack Neutron DHCP agent on Linux nodes can be manipulated via a crafted DHCP request to force it to leak the host's hostname and operating system details in the DHCP options field of the response.
An Xcode build phase for a popular open-source project was modified to include a `Run Script` that exfiltrates files from the developer's `~/Documents` directory on macOS.

Improper handling of data in the 'certbot' DNS-01 challenge validation script for the 'Cloudflare' DNS provider could be exploited to obtain a wildcard TLS certificate for a domain not controlled by the attacker.

The Azure Monitor Agent on IaaS VMs contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows an attacker to tamper with data collection rules, ceasing the transmission of security logs to Azure Sentinel.
The Windows IIS module 'PublicHeaders' has a flaw that exposes internal server IP addresses and version information in HTTP headers, which are then indexed by open technical databases.

The SecurePass Identity Gateway's certificate enrollment portal does not properly validate the Certificate Signing Request (CSR), permitting the issuance of certificates with a spoofed organization name.

The `XcodeTools-Helper` application does not sufficiently validate the integrity of its `emond` rule file before processing. An attacker could modify this file to execute a malicious payload with root privileges whenever a developer event occurs.
The CoreDNS deployment within a Kubernetes cluster can be modified to include a persistent, malicious sidecar container that intercepts and manipulates network traffic for all pods.
The macOS 'DropboxDesktopClient' fails to properly validate server SSL certificates during the OAuth authentication flow, enabling a man-in-the-middle attack to establish a rogue account link.
Unexpected behavior in the macOS 'LaunchDaemons-guard' mechanism allows a daemon to start even if a required, target-specific MDM configuration profile is absent, bypassing a key execution guardrail.
DigitalOcean's managed Kubernetes service contains a flaw in its role-based access control that enables users to bypass permission checks when requesting temporary cluster admin access.
The Intranet Collaboration Hub's 'Quick Diagnostics' feature is vulnerable to command injection, as it directly passes user-supplied input to a PowerShell instance without sanitization.
Improper input validation in the Screeny screen recorder application enables manipulation of its own TCC permissions, which can be extended to grant camera access to a malicious payload.

The `com.apple.security.authd` LaunchDaemon on macOS can be manipulated to execute an arbitrary payload. By modifying the `ProgramArguments` key in its property list, an attacker with root access can establish persistent, high-privilege execution.
On Windows, the 'ActiveDirectory-Tool' allows password reset commands to be executed with the new password in the command line, which is then captured by PowerShell's history.
A third-party PDF viewer for Windows includes a VBScript plugin that is vulnerable to script injection through malformed PDF objects.
The Service Host process (svchost.exe) can be coerced into executing malicious code through a TxF-based process doppelgänging attack targeting a specific service instance.

A flaw in the Linux version of Redis allows attackers to perform proc memory injection by exploiting inadequate restrictions on /proc/[pid]/maps access, leading to remote code execution with redis user privileges.

A remote code execution vulnerability in the Windows `RemoteDesktopGateway` service allows an unauthenticated attacker to run commands, which can be used to deploy malware that hijacks bandwidth for botnet operations.
The Windows User Profile Migration Tool contains a flaw where a crafted AutoIT script can be executed during the migration process, resulting in privilege escalation.

The CloudFile Sync Service insecurely implements a feature for logging into alternative accounts. An attacker with access to the service's configuration file can insert credentials and cause the service to make and impersonate a new token for that account.
An insecure temporary file handling bug in the 'Adobe Creative Cloud' desktop app for macOS allows for the creation of a persistent StartupItem.

The 'DataVault' password manager on macOS contains a vulnerability where its helper process can be hijacked. An attacker can inject code to hook the SecKeychainFindGenericPassword function, capturing credentials as they are accessed from the keychain.

The Azure AD Connect Sync service installer incorrectly sets permissions on the `profile.ps1` file in the PowerShell directory, allowing any authenticated user to add a backdoor that triggers for all users on the host.
The OpenShift API server's admission controller fails to validate container security contexts, permitting the deployment of containers that can escape their confines and access the host node.

The signature update service on Sentinel IPS appliances can be manipulated to write custom, malicious signatures to the disk by leveraging a direct volume write vulnerability, leading to detection bypass.
An input validation error in the Azure DevOps task for deploying Azure Functions permits the injection of arbitrary environment variables, altering a function's C2 communication endpoint.

The Linux kernel's `netfilter` subsystem has a vulnerability in its connection tracking module that grants remote adversaries the ability to inject malicious packets into an established, trusted data stream.
The Windows PowerShell Active Directory module lacks proper validation when processing group modification scripts, allowing attackers to add accounts to domain groups with elevated privileges.

An improper permission check in the OmniPath Router OS filesystem allows a low-privileged user to overwrite the primary system image file, resulting in a patched OS that grants elevated privileges upon reboot.
The 'Kubernetes-Azure-File' CSI driver does not validate the volume name, allowing a pod with access to the driver's socket to send a request that lists all blobs in the storage account's file share.
Improper access control in the ESXi hostd process permits a remote actor with limited privileges to invoke `esxcli storage filesystem list`, disclosing all local datastores and their capacities.
Unsafe behavior in 'EnterpriseVault' allows an attacker to modify its .config file to specify a malicious AppDomainManager, leading to arbitrary code execution upon service restart.

A memory corruption vulnerability in the macOS CoreBluetooth framework could be exploited by a malicious app to bypass privacy prompts and silently transmit user files to a nearby attacker-controlled Bluetooth device.
Improper validation of OLE objects in LibreOffice-Plus on Linux can lead to memory corruption and arbitrary code execution when a user opens a malicious spreadsheet.

The `ntdsai.dll` library on Windows Server fails to properly validate caller permissions for the DRSR GetNCChanges operation, allowing a low-privileged user to perform a DCSync attack and retrieve KRBTGT hash.

The firmware update mechanism for FortressWall NGFW Firmware fails to properly validate digital signatures, allowing an attacker on the same network to install malicious firmware and persistently compromise the device.
Microsoft Office's Click-to-Run service contains a COM object that can be instantiated from a sandboxed process, allowing for escape and execution of arbitrary commands on the host system.

macOS's XProtect anti-malware service has a bug in its time-based heuristics check, causing a consistent and measurable delay before scanning. This predictable behavior can be used by malware to detect the presence of XProtect's analysis engine.

The 'macOS Security Updater Daemon' contains a flaw where it can be made to download and execute a 'profile' from an unverified URL. An attacker can schedule this action to exfiltrate system information or execute a payload during the next daily check for updates.
A flaw in a third-party VPN client for macOS improperly handles DNS requests, which can be exploited to leak the user's real IP address despite the VPN connection being active.
The security architecture of Cisco IOS User Management Service allows attackers with network access to create unauthorized local accounts with full administrative privileges on network devices.
The VMware Tools daemon on macOS fails to properly check permissions when handling guest operations, allowing a low-privileged user on the ESXi host to trigger command execution.
On Windows, an attacker can exploit a flaw in Outlook's rule processing to execute a malicious DLL from a network share using the 'run application' action.
The Windows Event Log service does not sanitize TLS callback pointers from custom event providers, creating an opportunity for privilege escalation via code injection.

The `vim` editor with GUI support (`gvim`) on Linux contains a vulnerability in its `:!` command execution where a malformed command can spawn a new process with a hidden window, which can be used for malicious purposes.
A programmatic error in the ContainerGuard Role Assignment API allows an attacker with container deployment privileges to grant the underlying node's IAM role persistent, tenant-scoped permissions.
Cisco ASA firewall's 'write erase' command can be executed via SSH without proper session validation, allowing remote attackers to wipe device configurations and cause denial of service.
A logic error within system-service-spawner on macOS allows attackers to exploit process creation mechanisms to disconnect malicious code from its parent process tree.

The DockerEngine-Helper for Linux fails to properly validate API socket connections, allowing a container to escape and execute code on the host. This could be used to compromise the underlying server and recruit it into a botnet.
In Linux, the 'sysinfo-util' setuid binary does not properly sanitize user-supplied arguments when displaying system status, which can be abused to print the contents of the `/etc/locale.conf` file.
The Windows `Event Forwarding` service contains a flaw that grants remote adversaries the ability to replay captured events, inserting falsified logs into a central SIEM and corrupting forensic data.
The Atlassian Jira Cloud user management interface permits creation of system administrator accounts through a cross-site scripting vulnerability in the account creation form.
Docker daemon on Linux contains a flaw that allows containers to be launched with signal ignoring capabilities, enabling persistent malware execution.
CloudDeploy Platform's API lacks proper authorization checks, enabling any authenticated user to trigger deployment of malicious software to all connected cloud instances.

The Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Client for Windows does not correctly bind to its virtual interface prior to full connection, leaving the physical adapter's ARP cache exposed to poisoning during the connection phase.

A Jenkins CI server plugin contains a vulnerability that permits unauthenticated users to trigger builds. An attacker can flood the server with build requests for a job that performs intensive I/O operations, overwhelming build agents and denying service to other projects.
The vSphere Client HTML5 plugin 'VM-Backup-Manager' does not properly validate API responses, allowing an attacker to create a local account on the ESXi host with administrative rights.

The `LoginWindowManager` framework on macOS contains an insecure inheritance of permissions, allowing a crafted login item to execute arbitrary commands with elevated rights during the user login sequence.

An input sanitization flaw in the xfce4-autogen tool on Linux permits a local user to inject arbitrary commands into the Exec directive of a new .desktop file, causing malicious code execution at logon.

An SNMP community string with read-write permissions is publicly documented for the SysLink series of switches, allowing adversaries to pull the entire configuration from the device's config repository.
SystemConfigurator Pro does not sufficiently restrict permissions on the registry keys it uses to manage SSPs, enabling a local attacker to insert a malicious entry.
The NebulaStack cost allocation tags are not automatically applied to resources provisioned in its newest regions, making it difficult for financial audits to detect unauthorized spending.
The 'FileGuard' encryption software for Windows can be tricked into loading a malicious DLL through a repair action initiated by msiexec, allowing an attacker to bypass its security features.
A logic error in the systemd-journald service on Linux allows for the creation of forged journal entries that are sent to a remote syslog server, which can contain C2 payloads.

The vSphere Hypervisor's hostd process contains a memory corruption vulnerability that can be triggered via a specially crafted vSphere API call, allowing for arbitrary file writes to any datastore, facilitating lateral tool movement.
BuildMaster Pro's build agent can be tricked into executing mavinject.exe to inject a malicious DLL into a compilation process, compromising the build pipeline and supply chain.
The FirewallPlus-Mac application can be compromised to achieve root-level execution by exploiting its use of the deprecated AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges API.
Improper parsing of command arguments in the Windows CoreFS Service enables an attacker to bypass security controls using command-line obfuscation techniques like caret escaping.
The AirDrop discovery service on macOS devices can be probed to reveal the device's OS version and model, providing information for subsequent vulnerability scanning.

The API for the CloudFront-NG load balancer service does not properly validate the ownership of a domain when a user uploads a new TLS certificate, allowing for the installation of fraudulent certificates.
The 'Homebrew' package manager for macOS, when run with elevated privileges, can be tricked via a malicious formula to install a file into /Library/StartupItems.
The libnftnl library, used by nftables on Linux, is vulnerable to a use-after-free flaw that can be exploited by a local user to corrupt kernel memory and bypass all nftables firewall rules.
The 'Remote Desktop Licensing' service on Windows Server has a vulnerability where an authenticated user can cause the process to dump its memory, including LSA secrets.
The ScrapeMaster automation framework for Linux contains a hardcoded API key for a third-party data enrichment service, which can be extracted and used by an adversary.
Improper access control on the DataShield DB's credential cache on Windows permits a local attacker to query the cache and obtain database connection credentials in plaintext.
The 'Log Management Collector' for Windows incorrectly handles symbolic links in the print processor directory, allowing an attacker to redirect the load of a processor DLL to a malicious file.

The `csrutil` command-line utility for System Integrity Protection (SIP) on macOS has a flaw that allows an attacker with physical access to disable kernel debugging restrictions by manipulating a symbolic link during startup.

An IOKit vulnerability in the PerformanceBooster kernel extension (KEXT) on macOS could lead to arbitrary code execution and privilege escalation, allowing for the unloading of a KEXT to hide persistence.
Lack of access control on object references within vulnerability in the 'ADInspector' management tool allows users with limited rights to request and download a live copy of the NTDS.dit database.
Flawed business logic in the 'docker-containerd' component on Linux allows a container to escape and execute code on the host by exploiting its custom image layer archival process.
Improper access control in the BITS notification handler permits a low-privileged user to run arbitrary payloads with SYSTEM privileges by registering a malicious completion callback.

An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists in FileIntegrityMonitor. It calls `whoami.exe` without a full path for context checks, making it susceptible to an attack where a malicious binary is placed in the monitor's installation folder.
Improper validation of file paths in the 'RegClean Pro' utility allows a low-privileged user to alter the Autologger settings in the registry, specifically disabling the 'EventLog-System' channel.
Improper access control in the 'zabbix-agent' monitoring tool on Linux allows remote commands to execute with elevated privileges, enabling attackers to read /etc/shadow.
A privilege escalation vulnerability in the SysLogAgent service allows a standard user to clear the Security event log, hiding evidence of their activity.
Weak cryptographic implementation in the macOS GitHub Desktop application enables attackers to recover OAuth tokens for GitHub accounts.

The security architecture of Docker BuildKit allows a malicious Dockerfile included in a build context to run arbitrary commands during the build process, potentially compromising the build container.

The 'SecureADGateway' service fails to sanitize RPC calls, allowing an attacker on the network to bypass security checks and register a new server object in the AD Configuration partition, a prerequisite for a rogue DC.

The macOS 'MailClient' application improperly validates loaded frameworks, permitting an attacker to use DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES to inject a malicious library that hooks the SecKeychainFindInternetPassword function to steal email account credentials.
The VMware-USB-Proxy service on Windows contains an integer overflow that can be abused to enumerate host USB devices from a guest virtual machine, bypassing isolation.
GCP Compute Configuration API lacks proper validation for machine type restrictions, enabling deployment of oversized compute instances beyond policy limits.
In Microsoft Excel, a VBA macro can exploit an insufficient permission check to call an internal function that queries the Outlook address book for a list of all contacts.

The macOS file sharing application 'FileShareX' fails to properly sandbox uploaded content, allowing a malicious file to be placed in a system directory where it can be executed by a privileged process.

A heap-based buffer overflow exists in the `adreplication.sys` driver when processing a crafted DRSR GetNCChanges request. Successful exploitation could lead to elevation of privilege, enabling an attacker to perform DCSync operations.
The PhotoBooth application on macOS fails to properly sanitize its temporary file paths, allowing a malicious app to read the recently captured video files from its temporary directory.
AWS Lambda runtime environment contains a memory corruption bug that allows malicious functions to crash the execution environment, preventing function invocation and disrupting serverless workflows.
An insecure permission inheritance issue in the ESXi `hostd` service can be exploited to modify the ACLs of virtual machine configuration directories, facilitating malicious VM manipulation.
The 'EnterpriseArchitect' tool for Windows stores database credentials in plaintext, allowing an attacker with file system access to dump a company's entire technical architecture documentation.
The macOS AirDrop service fails to validate the payload of discovery packets, which can be exploited to create a covert Wi-Fi Direct tunnel for data transfer between nearby devices.

An improper input validation issue in the `containerd` runtime permits a malicious container to execute a bind mount operation, mapping its `/proc` directory to that of a benign process to evade detection.

An implementation error in the 'openflow-controller' web interface on Linux allows a remote authenticated attacker to write a malicious .desktop file to a user's ~/.config/autostart path, achieving persistence.
A missing authentication check in the custom RDP client used by ThinClientOS allows an attacker with network access to take over an existing session from the device.

An exploitable bug in the CloudSphere IAM service allows for the creation of administrator accounts without requiring email verification, enabling adversaries to establish high-privilege personas for initial access.
An exposed CloudInit-Provisioning API on an IaaS instance allows for unauthenticated remote command execution, leading to full instance compromise.
The gparted utility on Linux is susceptible to a heap-based buffer overflow when processing crafted disk images, which can be leveraged to overwrite the MBR with a bootkit payload.
Unsafe behavior in the LibreOffice macro execution tracker fails to sanitize macro names, allowing a malicious macro to delete its own entry from the macro security history log.
The PKI client certificate request process can be manipulated through a buffer overflow to request certificates with elevated privileges and extended validity periods.
An information disclosure flaw in the Windows Defender Antivirus Engine could leak sensitive file paths to a low-privileged application.

A programmatic error in the Windows Credential Manager allows an attacker to store a credential with a maliciously crafted target name that uses Punycode encoding, potentially leading to credential theft against a different service.
The Hostdump Collector tool on ESXi permits a user to specify a web service URL for uploading core dumps, but fails to sanitize the input, leading to a command injection vulnerability.

Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) flaws in the self-protection driver of McAfee Total Protection on Windows enables a malicious application to send a crafted IOCTL that disables real-time scanning, allowing subsequent malware to execute undetected.

Unsafe behavior in the Kubernetes API Server for Linux allows an authenticated user to create and sign service account certificates for any service in the cluster, facilitating lateral movement and privilege escalation.
Unchecked memory write operations in the 'Credential Guard' component could be exploited to disable its protection, allowing an attacker to dump LSA secrets from memory.
Improper validation in Windows System Configuration utility (msconfig) allows attackers to modify boot settings to force safe mode and disable security protections.
Microsoft Exchange Server's Client Access service contains a deserialization vulnerability in its MAPI protocol handling, enabling remote code execution without authentication.

A logic error within the Microsoft Exchange Transport Service on Windows Server allows an authenticated user to insert arbitrary X-headers into outgoing emails. This feature could be abused to create a robust C2 channel hidden within legitimate email traffic.
The Windows findstr.exe utility improperly handles regular expression patterns, allowing for arbitrary command execution through crafted search operations.

A software fault within the SoundWave Studio audio engine allows for the installation of a `GetProcAddress` shim, which can be used to intercept API calls and steal sensitive information from the application's memory.
Flawed business logic in the Windows Task Scheduler allows a task action to be created with a script padded with junk code, delaying analysis of the task's true intent.

An improper access control flaw in the macOS SystemPrefsDaemon allows a local application to modify SSH configurations without proper authorization. This could be leveraged to append a malicious key to the `authorized_keys` file for any user.

The OpenSSH server daemon (sshd) on certain Linux distributions contains a race condition that can be exploited to load a configuration file specifying a non-standard port, granting unauthorized SSH access.
A security bypass in the CRI-O container runtime on Linux VPSs allows a malicious container to mount the host's filesystem, leading to full system compromise.

The CoreShell environment on Linux fails to enforce restrictions on the 'pam.so' module path in its configuration, enabling the loading of a malicious module that grants a root shell upon any failed login attempt.

An exploitable bug in the macOS Spotlight indexing service allows an attacker to plant a file with malformed metadata. When processed, a specific importer plugin fails to sanitize the metadata and uses the system's clang compiler to compile embedded Objective-C code, resulting in code execution.

An implementation error in the ESXi Host Management agent (hostd) allows an unauthenticated attacker to hijack the execution flow by sending a specially crafted XML-RPC request containing a Base64-encoded payload that is improperly validated during decoding.
Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) flaws in the VirtuBlock hypervisor's virtual device driver can be exploited to corrupt memory and disable the hypervisor's built-in IDS for a specific guest VM.
An insufficient privilege check in Huawei VRP's debug commands enables attackers to directly modify memory regions of the running system image, disabling security features.
ShopifyFront SaaS 平台的产品数据同步 API 中存在一个漏洞，允许具有商店访问权限的攻击者将整个产品目录（包括客户数据）同步到他们控制的第三方云存储服务。
The WaylandCompositor on some Linux systems contains a flaw in its keyboard input forwarding logic, permitting a compromised client application to inject keystrokes into other client windows.
The V-Mon monitoring agent for Windows VPSs is vulnerable to arbitrary code execution due to improper handling of incoming network packets.

The 'GitLab Pages' feature, when running on a self-hosted Linux instance, contains a path traversal vulnerability that permits a user to publish content outside their designated directory, potentially staging malicious scripts on other users' pages.

The macOS SetupAssistant application inadvertently retains the system language in a preference file that is accessible by other applications during the user setup process, leading to an information disclosure.

A programmatic error in the Windows DirectAccess Connector permits remote code execution through crafted routing rules, which can be used to force traffic through a series of compromised hosts, creating a multi-hop proxy.
A coding defect present in Linux security-daemon allows memory reading of decrypted SSH keys stored temporarily in the credential cache.

Safari on macOS fails to sanitize the DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES environment variable when rendering web content, allowing malicious websites to inject arbitrary dylibs into the browser process, potentially leading to code execution.

The serverless function responsible for user provisioning in an Identity-as-a-Service (IDaaS) platform contains a logic flaw that can be exploited to create persistent admin accounts via a crafted API request.
In ESXi, the rhttpproxy component suffers from a flaw where an attacker-controlled DNS response can lead to the calculation of a malicious C2 endpoint, potentially compromising the host.
A privilege escalation flaw in EnterpriseAuth Identity Provider allows low-privilege users to add app passwords bypassing MFA requirements.

A buffer overflow vulnerability in the Windows File Transfer Service gives a remote user the power to execute arbitrary code by sending a specially crafted filename via an FTP connection, enabling the establishment of a covert C2 channel.

Juniper Junos devices with the J-Web interface enabled have a flaw in their diagnostic file upload feature. An authenticated, low-privilege user can upload a malicious script and manipulate the filename to include directory traversal, causing the script to be relocated to a path executed on system boot.
An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists in the Remote Desktop Services' licensing component, where a specially crafted request could grant an attacker system-level rights.

A flaw in the WinINet API on Windows facilitates remote exploitation to trick an application into using a malicious internal proxy server via a crafted URL, hijacking legitimate application communication for command and control.

Simultaneous execution threads in the Cheese Webcam Booth application on Linux allows an attacker to replace the target video device file with a symlink to another device, potentially capturing video from an unintended source.
A vulnerability in the Linux `k8s-kerberos-auth-plugin` for Kubernetes allows a pod to mount and read the node's host ccache file if certain hostPath volume settings are misconfigured.

An anti-debugging mechanism in ProMedia Converter for macOS can be bypassed. The application uses `ptrace` with `PT_DENY_ATTACH`, but a race condition in its implementation allows an attacker to attach a debugger before the check executes.

The macOS `bluetoothd` daemon fails to sanitize D-Bus messages for the 'MediaControl' interface. A malicious application could send crafted messages to force the system to connect to a rogue Bluetooth device and stream audio data containing exfiltrated information.
An unauthenticated API endpoint in the ESXi management interface allows an attacker to change the host's 'issue' file, resulting in a defaced login banner.
An improper access control flaw in the 'perf-analyzer' tool on Linux permits a low-privileged user to alter the command-line arguments of a monitored process, effectively cloaking its activity.
An improper access control check in the SentinelOne Endpoint Protection service allows any authenticated domain user to request a Kerberos service ticket for its management SPN.

Authorization bypass via ID manipulation in (IDOR) vulnerability in the VibeStream web portal allows an attacker to view and modify another user's account settings by altering the user ID parameter in the URL.

The `postgresql-replica` daemon fails to properly zero out memory, causing replication credentials to persist in a readable state after a connection is established. A local user can inspect `/proc/[pid]/maps` to find the relevant memory segment and read it from `/proc/[pid]/mem`.
A privilege escalation in the macOS Security Framework enables creation of root certificates, allowing adversaries to establish their own certificate authorities.

D-Link DIR series routers running D-Link OS contain a vulnerability in the firmware rollback mechanism that could enable an authenticated attacker to downgrade to a previous version with weaker encryption protocols. The issue exists due to inadequate verification of firmware image signatures during the restoration process.

Buffer bounds violations in the 'Windows Subsystem for Linux 2' (WSL2) Python integration component could allow an attacker to corrupt memory and inject a malicious `sitecustomize.py` module into the shared Python environment.
Windows Authentication Subsystem permits replacement of accessibility feature binaries, facilitating privilege escalation without authentication.

Unintended data exposure in in the 'FileShield' AV scanner's logs reveals the full set of paths and file extensions in its real-time exclusion list. This information can be used by an attacker to craft malware that evades detection via selective exclusion.
The SecureNet VPN Client for Windows fails to properly validate the origin of its connection dialog, allowing an attacker to spoof a legitimate credential request and harvest VPN passwords.

An internal defect in the ContainerRegGate API endpoint allows an unauthenticated user to create new organizations (repositories), which can be seen as establishing a presence point within the container ecosystem.

A memory corruption flaw exists in the Windows driver `tcpip.sys` related to handling SYN cookies. An attacker can send a specially crafted sequence of SYN packets that triggers the flaw, causing a system crash and resulting in a denial of service.

In an IaaS environment, the VM-Snapshotter service allows a user to specify a post-snapshot script. This feature can be abused to automatically extract sensitive data from memory dumps within the snapshot and exfiltrate it.
OneLogin's SAML trust relationship verification can be bypassed through manipulation of trusted issuer metadata, enabling attackers to generate valid SAML assertions for connected applications.
The logrotate-analyzer daemon on Linux can be forced into an infinite loop by processing a log file with a specially crafted, deeply nested regex pattern, leading to 100% CPU utilization.

Unexpected behavior in the macOS 'Safari' web browser's framework allows for the modification of a core binary's LC_LOAD_DYLIB entry. This can be used to load a malicious dylib, enabling persistent attacks and credential theft.
In a multi-tenant IaaS environment, the ObjectStorage-Gateway API has a flaw allowing users to create 'staging' prefixes in other users' buckets, facilitating unauthorized data aggregation.
Linux systemd-logind service contains a flaw that enables local users to terminate all user sessions and lock accounts through D-Bus message injection.
Unexpected behavior in the Docker container network bridge allows a single container to exhaust available IP addresses on the host system, causing a network denial of service for other containers.
The swift-social-sdk for iOS development inadvertently logs API secrets and access tokens to the system console, leading to potential credential exposure.
The Samba daemon on Linux systems suffers from a remote code execution vulnerability in its Netlogon implementation due to improper cryptographic validation of authentication requests.

The CommuniCore Hub's interactive voice response (IVR) system can be tricked into revealing whether a user's phone extension is valid, providing attackers with information for targeted spearphishing voice calls.

The SolarWinds Network Configuration Manager (NCM) contains a vulnerability in its script execution engine that can be exploited to push a script to network devices that clears their command history upon execution.
Insecure temporary file handling in SecureApp Daemon on Windows leaves certificate files world-readable, enabling certificate theft for lateral movement.

Buffer bounds violations in the `QuickView Lite` image viewer for Windows can be exploited via a specially crafted image file that references a remote resource, forcing the application to authenticate and leak NTLM hashes.

An improperly scoped IAM role within the 'CloudStack API' allows users with the 'iam:list-users' permission to also retrieve the account-level password policy, which should require a separate permission.
Improper validation in the Microsoft Outlook Add-in framework allows malicious add-ins to access and exfiltrate local email databases.

The PrivilegeAccess Manager for Windows fails to properly audit or restrict the use of the `nltest.exe` utility, allowing attackers to use it for stealthy domain trust discovery without generating security alerts.

The Active Directory Group Policy client on Windows does not verify the digital signature of startup scripts placed in the `SysVol` share, allowing an attacker to taint the script and achieve lateral movement.
The 'Enterprise Exchange Auditor' application on Windows suffers from a buffer overflow that can be triggered to execute a shellcode, which then adds a backdoor delegate to the CEO's mailbox.

The XProtectDaemon on macOS fails to sanitize its execution environment. It relies on the $PATH to find the 'zip' utility, creating an opportunity for an attacker to inject and execute malicious commands by placing a malicious 'zip' binary in a prioritized, writable location.
The YUM package manager on RHEL/CentOS has a vulnerability in handling encrypted repository metadata.
An authentication bypass in the 'RemoteHelp' service configuration API on Windows permits an unauthenticated attacker to create a new service with SYSTEM-level privileges.
The 'Kaniko' image builder does not validate the source of build contexts, allowing an attacker to poison a build with malicious layers that are then pushed to a registry.

The CronJob Scheduler Daemon on a Linux distribution contains a logic flaw where a user can submit a high volume of jobs with invalid credentials, consuming resources and masking brute-force login attempts against the daemon's control socket.

The Windows utility 'NexusBot Suite' stores social media account credentials in the Windows Registry using a weak, static encryption key. An attacker with local access can decrypt these credentials and take over the associated accounts.
A memory corruption flaw in the Intel PROSet/Wireless driver for Windows allows an adversary on the system to read stored Wi-Fi passwords from kernel memory, leading to credential disclosure.
A heap-based buffer overflow in the Windows WinSSO component allows an attacker to execute code in the context of the LSA process, directly compromising all stored SSO credentials.

An insecure deserialization vulnerability in the NodeBB Forum Engine allows for remote code execution. By uploading a maliciously crafted theme package, an attacker can inject and execute arbitrary JavaScript code within the Node.js runtime context.
An implementation error in background-runner on Linux enables attackers to execute fork() chains that create orphaned processes, breaking process tree analysis and evading detection.

Microsoft Word's hyperlink field processing does not sanitize URLs containing the '@' symbol for obfuscation purposes, allowing a spearphishing link to appear to point to a legitimate site while redirecting elsewhere.
The DockerVol Manager for containerized environments on IaaS has a vulnerable socket that can be accessed by a compromised container to create a snapshot of the host's storage volumes.
The security architecture of the Google Cloud OS Login agent for Linux allows a low-privilege user to escalate to root by manipulating temporary files used during the SSH key provisioning process.

The CloudGuard IAM identity provider's administrative API contains a flaw where an authenticated user with tenant-scoped permissions can alter global authentication policies, affecting all managed tenants.

A weakness in the firmware update mechanism for the RemoteAccessKit on macOS allows a man-in-the-middle attacker to hijack the process and flash malicious firmware onto a remote access hardware device.
Cloud Identity Bridge service allows attackers to modify authentication mappings between cloud and on-premise identity providers.

'Facade for Mac' insecurely stores API credentials for various social media platforms in a world-readable log file. A local malicious user could steal these credentials to hijack or manipulate established social media personas.
An exploitable bug in Cisco IOS image verification allows an attacker to bypass integrity checks and upload a modified system image containing a persistent backdoor.

A critical weakness within the Istio Pilot service for Kubernetes could allow an unauthenticated user to retrieve a comprehensive list of all services and their configurations within the service mesh.

Improper authorization checks in the Azure Management Group Console allow an attacker with compromised tenant credentials to create new management groups and move sensitive subscriptions into them for persistence.
A bug located in the 'hMailServer' Windows administration COM API allows any local user to invoke the 'AddAccount' method, creating new email accounts without authentication.
Azure Active Directory allows creation of application service principals with names matching Microsoft first-party services, bypassing conditional access policies.
WeatherWidget does not properly validate the authenticity of its downloaded components, allowing an attacker to use AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges to install a malicious update.

Improper bounds checking in the TFTP server implementation of Juniper JunOS permits a threat actor via network access to execute code of their choice by sending a request with an overly long filename, enabling device compromise and C2 over TFTP.
The `rEFInd` boot manager on Linux contains a buffer overflow that can be triggered by a malformed configuration file, resulting in the execution of a bootkit payload.
Insecure AppleScript event handling in `iTerm-Plus.app` for macOS allows a malicious script to interact with and commandeer active SSH connections.
The CoreAudio daemon on macOS is susceptible to a binary injection attack where an attacker can append a malicious LC_LOAD_DYLIB header, causing the dylib to be loaded with system privileges.
The Windows built-in 'compact.exe' utility can be manipulated through a race condition to compress files in unintended directories, potentially aiding an adversary in data obfuscation.
A heap-based buffer overflow in the Chromium browser on Linux can be triggered by a specially crafted malvertising script, leading to a sandbox escape and local system compromise.

Improper handling of data in the Docker daemon's libnetwork driver allows a container to send a high volume of ARP requests, causing a network storm and a denial of service for all containers on the same host network.

An insecure registry ACL in the Java Auto Updater for Windows allows an attacker to hijack the SIP verification process. By pointing the CryptSIPDllGetSignedDataMsg function to a malicious DLL, an attacker can cause the updater to trust and install malicious JAR files.

In a Kubernetes cluster, a flaw in the role-based access control (RBAC) API allows a user with limited permissions to create a `ClusterRole` named `system:node` that approximates a critical system role, potentially granting elevated privileges.
Improper bounds checking in Chrome's PDF rendering component on Windows allows remote attackers to execute code through a drive-by download.
Microsoft Outlook on Windows fails to properly filter SVG content in emails, allowing malicious scripts to be smuggled past security filters.

The LaunchDaemon `com.apple.security.kc` on macOS improperly validates messages sent to the keychain daemon. This allows an attacker to prepend junk data to requests, facilitating the obfuscation of commands to the keychain service.
An information disclosure flaw in the 'sysmon' port for Linux reveals the memory address of the argv array, which can then be targeted for an overwrite attack to masquerade the process.

Logical errors within the Windows 'Device Management Console' (devmgmt.msc) allows a non-administrative user to disable the driver signing policy for the current session, facilitating the loading of untrusted drivers.
The 'DocuView Pro' application on Windows fails to sanitize file paths before passing them to mshta.exe, allowing an attacker to run unauthorized code via a malicious .hta file.

The 'LogAnalyzer' tool exposes a function to set debuggers for monitored services that does not validate caller permissions. An attacker can use this function to configure a malicious debugger for `eventlog.exe`, achieving persistence and code execution.
The Linux Firefox browser's address bar can be manipulated to display legitimate third-party service URLs while loading malicious content, supporting spearphishing operations.

Improper input validation in the BackupDaemon service on Linux allows an attacker to inject commands into a signal handler. A user with write access to the configuration can define a malicious trap for SIGHUP, causing their code to run each time the service is reloaded.
A software fault within an IaaS provider's IAM simulation API allows a user to enumerate the effective policies of roles they are not a member of, aiding in permission group discovery.
Improper access control in the Linux HashiCorp Vault agent enables attackers to retrieve cloud credentials from the vault cache.
A hardware-level backdoor in the 'MacSafe' power adapter controller for macOS laptops allows for data exfiltration over the power line when a compromised adapter is used.

An improper signature validation vulnerability in the transport agent registration service of CorporateMail Suite on Windows allows an unauthenticated attacker to install a malicious agent for persistent access.
Google Cloud Storage's signed URL functionality can be abused to stage malicious content with extended expiration times for later use in attacks.

In the 'OpenStack' Keystone service, a bug allows a user to create a new project and assign it to a domain they do not belong to, effectively removing it from the administrative hierarchy of the original domain.

An improper access control vulnerability in the 'Citrix Virtual Desktop Agent' for Windows permits a local user to register a malicious Network Provider DLL, enabling the capture of cleartext domain credentials during user authentication.
MacCleaner X uses the deprecated AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges API for routine cleaning tasks, creating an attack vector for privilege escalation if the application is compromised.
The vSAN Health Service on ESXi performs DNS lookups without proper bounds checking on the responses, making it vulnerable to a buffer overflow attack that could facilitate DNS tunneling.
An improper input validation in the spreadsheet script engine enables attackers to execute arbitrary PowerShell commands through malicious Excel macros.

An insecure default configuration in the Windows 'Bluetooth Support Service' allows any local process to query and enumerate all paired devices and their services, and subsequently open a socket to them for unauthorized data transfer.

Flawed business logic in macOS Finder's handling of extended attributes on external volumes allows files to be written that are invisible to Spotlight indexing and standard GUI tools. This can be abused to hide command-and-control payloads on a USB device passed between compromised hosts.

Logical errors within the Linux systemd service manager permits an attacker to create a service unit that systematically scans for and terminates processes associated with common competing malware, ensuring exclusive resource usage.
A logic error in the EndpointProtector service permits a malicious process to persistently display a 'Protected' system tray icon, even when the core protection engine has been disabled.
The `CoreDefender` agent does not properly sanitize user-supplied input when updating its configuration, allowing an attacker to inject commands that stop the `auditd` service.

A use-after-free vulnerability exists in the CoreAnimation framework when processing a file with a malicious resource fork, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution in the context of the calling application.
Improper validation of firmware image signatures in the DellFirmwareUpdate.exe utility could allow an attacker to flash a corrupted BIOS, rendering the system inoperable.
The EnterpriseGuard service installer for Windows is susceptible to a path traversal vulnerability, which could be leveraged to create a new service pointing to an attacker-controlled executable.
An insecure default configuration in the Windows Control Panel allows CPL files from network shares to be loaded and executed without warning, facilitating lateral movement attacks.
The `rclone-cloud-backup` daemon for Linux contains an improper input validation vulnerability, enabling a local attacker to specify an arbitrary Google Cloud Storage URI and exfiltrate system logs.
Unchecked memory write operations in the CoreAppleEventService on macOS permits an unprivileged user to execute arbitrary commands as root by sending a specially crafted AppleEvent.
Sendmail's queue management tool contains an insufficient validation flaw that permits local users to delete mail queue entries and delivery logs.

A security gap in the Windows NTFS driver's handling of Alternate Data Streams (ADS) on removable media allows an attacker to create streams that are not indexed or visible to standard tools. This feature can be abused to hide C2 instructions and exfiltrated data on a USB drive.
LibreOffice on Windows is susceptible to a macro-parsing vulnerability where a malicious macro embedded in a document template on a shared network drive can auto-execute, bypassing security prompts.
Apple Pages on macOS contains a vulnerability where SVG smuggling through document templates can lead to arbitrary code execution.
Improper input validation in the custom URI handler `csm://` registered by CorpSecureMail on Windows permits remote code execution via a malicious link.
Improper neutralization of input in the Microsoft Defender Quarantine Details pane enables an attacker to embed a malicious 'restore' command, deceiving users into executing it.

An identified issue in the AD-Integrator DNS Service on Windows permits an unauthenticated remote attacker to trigger a full DNS zone transfer via a crafted AXFR request, disclosing internal network topology.
Linux authentication daemon (authd) fails to properly restrict access to the getgrent() system call, allowing unprivileged processes to iterate through all local groups.
Logical errors within the `TaskScheduler Pro` service allows a low-privileged task to queue an APC to a high-privilege scheduler service thread, achieving privilege escalation.

A memory corruption issue in 'AuthHelper.dll' on Windows can be triggered to bypass access controls, allowing an attacker to request AS-REP messages for any user, even those with preauthentication enabled.

In Linux, the WebAppX application creates a systemd service file, `/etc/systemd/system/webappx.service`, with world-writable permissions. A low-privilege user can modify the `ExecStart` directive to execute a malicious payload, achieving persistence across system reboots.
An implementation error in the VoxLink Gateway firmware allows for the manipulation of SIP headers, enabling unauthenticated attackers to spoof caller ID information and facilitate vishing campaigns.
An API endpoint for listing repository contributors in CodeLoom Cloud does not perform authorization checks, leaking the usernames of all developers with access to a private project.

An out-of-bounds read in the Linux kernel's HID dispatcher module (hid-dispatcher.ko) allows an attacker to read sensitive data from the memory of a connected Human Interface Device during enumeration.
Cisco IOS XR's show users command reveals logged-in user information without proper authentication through SNMP community string exposure.

A command injection flaw in the Nginx Dynamic Proxy module for Linux allows an attacker to append arbitrary proxy directives, creating a multi-hop proxy chain that forwards traffic to an attacker-controlled server.
WinArchive Manager automatically executes 'autorun.inf' commands from extracted ISO images without user consent, enabling malicious file execution on Windows.
A vulnerability in the macOS Spotlight Suggestions feature can be abused to display malicious ads that, when clicked, redirect to a domain hosting trojanized software.

A time-of-check-to-time-of-use (TOCTOU) vulnerability in the Sendmail MilterFilter on Linux permits a race condition where a legitimate filter can be replaced with a malicious one after the integrity check but before loading.
The macOS Finder's Apple Event handler contains a type confusion vulnerability that enables code execution via crafted IPC events.

The 'Launchd-Services-Helper' on macOS does not correctly handle property list (plist) files with leading dots in their filenames. An attacker can install a hidden plist (e.g., `.com.malware.agent.plist`) to establish persistence that is not visible in a standard `ls` of the `LaunchAgents` directory.
A memory corruption issue in the Windows DNS Client service could be leveraged to leak the IP addresses of recently resolved DNS queries from the process memory.
The Jamf Management Framework on macOS logs the bind credentials for an Active Directory domain in plaintext to a local system file during the join process.

A flaw in the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) Pico process driver allows a malicious Linux ELF binary to execute code in the context of the NT kernel on the Windows host, acquiring a powerful malware capability.
An internal defect in the `pulseaudio` daemon on Linux, when handling removable media, can be exploited to leak captured audio streams from a microphone to a connected MP3 player or smartphone.
The telnet service on older models of NetCore OS routers is enabled by default with a hardcoded, undocumented password that provides root access, enabling a full configuration dump.

An information disclosure bug in the AnonProxy service reveals the originating datacenter of its supposed 'residential' proxies, allowing adversaries to more accurately select infrastructure that blends with target environments.
The 'CoreVM' daemon for Linux, which handles remote execution requests, contains a logic flaw that allows for command chaining, enabling an attacker to bypass intended command restrictions.
The Windows SMBv2 driver (smb2.sys) contains a heap overflow that can be exploited to access hidden administrative shares without proper authentication.
The SplunkForwarder Service on Windows is susceptible to an access token manipulation flaw where an attacker can impersonate the service's account context.
The 'WebMarshal Proxy' service installer contains a weak default DACL, which can be exploited by a local user to replace the legitimate service executable with a malicious one for persistence.
The FortiGate SSL-Proxy feature has a flaw in its certificate validation logic that can be abused to perform a man-in-the-middle attack and proxy decrypted TLS traffic.

The 'CloudSync Service' for macOS improperly handles symbolic links during its setup process, which can be abused to write a malicious `sitecustomize.py` file into a Python path, ensuring persistent code execution.
The Windows Registry Editor fails to properly sanitize RTLO characters in registry key names, allowing malicious entries to appear legitimate while hiding their true purpose.

A memory corruption vulnerability in the macOS XProtect service enables an attacker with local access to bypass security checks and execute code. This could be used to hijack the XProtect update mechanism to exfiltrate system information by encoding it into the security definition download requests.
A memory corruption vulnerability in the VLCX media player on Linux can be exploited to achieve code execution by tricking a user into opening a specially crafted playlist file.
A coding defect present in HostMonitorX for ESXi allows an attacker to decrypt C2 traffic because the AES encryption key is generated using only the host's IP address and a constant value.

The OmniCorp Management Suite on Windows exposes a diagnostic endpoint that leaks the system's language settings via a call to `GetSystemDefaultUILanguage`, enabling unauthorized discovery of the host's locale.

An improper permission check in the Windows Update Orchestrator service allows a standard user to queue an APC to one of its service threads, potentially corrupting the update process and achieving privilege escalation.
A vulnerability in the Windows Background Intelligent Transfer Service (bitsprx2.dll) allows attackers to specify arbitrary parent PIDs for download processes, bypassing network security monitoring.

An implementation error in the 'pkg' utility on FreeBSD allows a remote repository to serve a package signed with a valid key but containing malicious post-install scripts that exfiltrate the host's signing keys.

An SSRF vulnerability in the ESXi Host Client allows an authenticated user to force the host to download and upload diagnostic bundles to a specified cloud storage URL, facilitating data exfiltration.
Unchecked memory write operations in CloudKitDaemon can be exploited to manipulate the launchd context, enabling unauthorized command execution via launchctl.

The `logrotate` utility on Linux, when configured with a custom script that calls `gzip`, can be vulnerable to PATH hijacking. If the script does not use `/bin/gzip`, an attacker can create a malicious `gzip` in a writable directory to achieve code execution as root during log rotation.
The security architecture of the Apple T2 security chip's firmware allows for the execution of unsigned code before the macOS kernel is loaded via a malicious Thunderbolt peripheral.

A critical weakness within the 'TerminalServer' component allows for session hijacking. An attacker in a hijacked session can then invoke SyncAppvPublishingServer.vbs to execute PowerShell commands in the context of another user.
A developer build server for the macOS application 'FinderEnhancer' was compromised, resulting in a maliciously tainted public release.

An insecure method implementation in the `Microsoft Defender for Identity` sensor allows a low-privileged user to request a memory scan of any process, including `lsass.exe`, which writes the memory content to a temporary file accessible to the user.
The Remote Desktop Gateway service contains a memory corruption flaw from improper handling of hex-encoded connection parameters, potentially allowing system compromise.
The EndpointSecurityConsole.msc fails to properly restrict access to its internal API, which can be invoked through mmc.exe to disable security features.
The Windows Component Object Model (COM) has a permission bypass that allows an attacker to use the `IMachineDebugManager` interface to terminate processes belonging to other users.
The Linux kernel's module loader exposes information about loaded modules through /proc/modules without proper permission checks, enabling software reconnaissance by unprivileged users.

An internal defect in the Azure Automation Runbooks service enables privilege escalation where a runbook with compromised credentials can execute commands on hybrid worker machines with elevated SYSTEM privileges.

The 'InvenTrack' ERP software on Windows exposes an internal diagnostic endpoint that leaks a list of all installed .NET framework versions and related dependencies to authenticated but non-admin users.
The 'webmin' package on Linux contains a bug where its post-install script insecurely modifies /etc/sudoers, granting the 'webmin' user unrestricted sudo access without a password.
A logic flaw in the 'tunnel-linkd' daemon on Linux allows an attacker to establish a tunnel using a revoked GitHub account that has not been properly purged from the system's cache.
A type confusion vulnerability in the driver for a VPN client, which registers with the LSA, can be exploited to corrupt memory and execute code within the LSASS process.

The Windows Update service for firmware on Surface devices improperly validates firmware packages, enabling a man-in-the-middle attacker to deliver and install malicious firmware to components like the Surface UEFI or touch controller.

A weakness in the OneLogin Connect SSO service allows an attacker to access unauthorized applications by manipulating the `RelayState` parameter in the federation authentication flow, using a valid account.
Improper validation of configuration files in the AzureADConnectUtil on Windows could allow an attacker to inject a new local user with elevated privileges.
The InsightGen Analytics Dashboard for Windows is vulnerable to template injection, as it fetches report templates from unverified URLs specified within the document metadata.
Samba file sharing service on Linux does not properly sanitize RTLO characters in shared filenames, allowing malicious files to be disguised on network shares.

The 'Microsoft Dynamics CRM' server on Windows contains an improper access control vulnerability in its web resource management feature, allowing a standard user to upload and replace core web resource files, causing defacement of the CRM portal.
An identified issue in the 'Spooler Service Subsystem Component' allows for a crafted print job to trigger code execution that modifies the system's authentication packages for persistence.
A logic error within the Linux kernel's BPF verifier can be bypassed by a polymorphic BPF program, allowing for arbitrary kernel code execution.
An uninitialized pointer in a third-party VDI client for Windows can be dereferenced to achieve code execution, which could then be used to invoke the client's screen capture feature.
The Windows Application Compatibility Layer fails to properly isolate malicious screensavers, allowing persistence through compatibility shims exploitation.
Auth0 Management Dashboard lacks proper authorization checks when modifying role assignments, enabling attackers to elevate privileges for any user in the tenant.

A heap-based overflow condition in the ROMMON's console driver for Cisco Catalyst 3850 switches could be exploited by an attacker with physical access to execute code and install a persistent ROMMONkit.
Kubernetes API Server's RBAC validation can be bypassed by creating service accounts with names that prefix-match legitimate cluster service accounts, allowing unauthorized resource access.
Apple Push Notification service on macOS has a vulnerability allowing attackers to flood the service with registration requests, causing resource exhaustion.
The Network and Sharing Center CPL file contains a buffer overflow in its handling of network profile names, which can be exploited through control.exe to achieve remote code execution.

An internal defect in the Linux-based 'AstraFS' distributed filesystem service allows attackers to authenticate using a hardcoded recovery account 'fs-recovery' with a default credential, bypassing normal authentication mechanisms.
Unsafe behavior in the CUPS printing system on Linux allows for data exfiltration or receipt of C2 instructions through PDF files embedded in print jobs using steganography.
The Linux cron daemon's socket communication lacks proper validation, enabling command injection through IPC manipulation.
A privilege escalation flaw in the WMI provider for virtualization on Windows could permit an attacker to create a hidden virtual instance that is not discoverable via standard administrative tools.
A popular third-party password manager for macOS contains a vulnerability in its auto-fill browser extension, which can be abused to read passwords directly from the system's login keychain.
Predictable resource identification in in the iCloud authentication helper on macOS can be exploited to trigger a false 'iCloud Login Required' system notification, capturing Apple ID credentials.

A memory corruption issue in the 'Google Sheets' scripting engine allows a malicious script, embedded in a shared spreadsheet, to escape its sandbox and access user data, enabling targeted internal spearphishing.
The ServiceNow MID Server integration account can be abused through a flaw in the ECC Queue input processing, allowing an attacker to run commands that assign the `security_admin` role to a user.
A defect in `EC2-Core` allows an attacker to specify a deprecated and vulnerable instance type during creation, circumventing modern security controls and patches.
The macOS 'Bluetooth' kernel extension contains a vulnerability allowing attackers to load unsigned kexts that maintain persistence.
The Linux security-daemon service fails to properly encrypt credential data in memory, enabling root users to dump process memory and recover plaintext authentication tokens for system services.
The macOS 'NetworkExtension' framework improperly validates the content of startup scripts for legacy VPN clients, which can be abused to inject arbitrary commands into a StartupItem.
A network device's configuration backup process temporarily stores the full plaintext configuration, including secrets, in a world-readable file in /tmp.

A privilege escalation flaw in the `SystemCommand Auditor` service on Windows permits a local attacker to modify the registry keys that control PowerShell's command history, disabling it for all users on the system.
An insecure method call in the Microsoft Management Console (MMC) allows `rundll32.exe` to load a malicious DLL from a world-writable directory, facilitating privilege escalation and defense evasion.
SELinux policy engine on RHEL systems has a flaw that allows bypass of shell config restrictions through policy manipulation.
Office's template auto-recovery feature can be abused for persistence through malicious templates that execute during recovery processes.
An information disclosure flaw in the `esxcli software vib list` command reveals the file paths of VIB payloads, aiding an attacker in targeting them for a persistent malicious VIB upload.
The CI/CD agent 'BuildRunner' stores its access tokens in the registry with permissions that allow any logged-on user to query them.
The mailx utility on Linux contains a format string vulnerability that allows local attackers to execute commands and delete mail spool files.

A UI spoofing vulnerability in the `FaceTime Framework` on macOS allows an attacker to display a fake system dialog over an active video call, prompting the user for credentials under the guise of a security update as part of a spearphishing voice attack.

A path traversal vulnerability in the 'SentinelShield EDR' agent on Windows allows a local user to read files outside of its intended log directory. This can be abused to access its configuration files and identify its security policies.
A signed third-party driver installer, 'OmniPrint Setup', calls `PubPrn.vbs` post-install with parameters taken from an insecure manifest file, leading to potential script proxy execution.

Improper locking mechanisms in the Windows Task Scheduler service allows an attacker to read the command-line arguments of a task running under a different user's context, which may include credentials.

The `opendev-remote-agent` on Linux fails to restrict the scope of port forwarding, allowing an adversary to use an IDE tunnel to pivot and access internal network services not intended for development.

The `securityd` daemon on macOS contains a memory corruption vulnerability when processing specially crafted IPC requests, which could be exploited by a local attacker to read arbitrary keychain items without requiring the user's master password.

In Linux, the `linux-scsi-util` tool improperly handles error responses from a storage device, allowing a crafted response to trick the utility into writing malicious firmware to the device's controller.

An insecure API endpoint in the SalesHub Chat SaaS platform allows for the enumeration of all private channels within an organization, providing attackers with a roadmap for targeted social engineering attacks.
A critical weakness within the Windows Remote Management Extension service allows for decryption of command and control traffic due to a hard-coded AES-256 encryption key.
A state management bug in the macOS TCC database allows an attacker to programmatically grant camera access to their application without any user interaction, enabling persistent video surveillance.

Improper encoding of user output in flaw in the Azure DNS Zone Explorer web console could be used to steal an administrator's authentication token, subsequently allowing for the enumeration and exfiltration of all DNS zones and records in a subscription.

The 'OneLogin' cloud identity provider's admin console contains a bug where a role with 'read-only' access to policy settings can still push modified policies to production, leading to unauthorized tenant-wide changes.

An identified issue in Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) on Windows allows a low-privileged user to request certificates with unintended properties by manipulating certificate templates, aiding in persistence or privilege escalation.
A software fault within the Windows Storage Spaces API enables the creation of hidden file system tiers that are not accessible through standard interfaces.
