An internal defect in the TCC (Transparency, Consent, and Control) framework on macOS allows a newly installed application to temporarily capture screen content before the initial prompt by exploiting a race condition.
A design weakness in the key exchange protocol of the SecureMesh wireless backhaul system allows for a man-in-the-middle attack to force the use of a 1024-bit Diffie-Hellman group.
CoreLogic ERP system's reporting feature can be exploited to execute arbitrary AutoIT scripts by manipulating a report template parameter.
Improper locking mechanisms in the `GNOME Settings Daemon`'s `datetime` module can be exploited to leak the configured time zone to a sandboxed application.
A remote code execution vulnerability exists in the Windows JScript engine when it improperly accesses objects in memory, exploitable via a malicious website.
The AzureBuild Runner for Windows insecurely logs build environment variables, including deployment secrets, to a file that is subsequently committed to a linked Git repository by default.
A compromised private Git repository for the Linux daemon netcored allowed an attacker to inject a backdoor into the source code, which was subsequently built and released.
A security bypass vulnerability in Microsoft Access allows a database to automatically execute unauthorized macros upon opening, leading to persistence.
An identified issue in WinFileUtil.exe allows for indirect command execution by failing to sanitize file paths passed as an argument, which can be leveraged to bypass command-line restrictions.
A SQL injection flaw in the Linux SEO Dashboard permits unauthorized access to website optimization data, enabling targeted SEO poisoning campaigns.
A TOCTOU (Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use) race condition in the 'Windows Defender SmartScreen' module can be bypassed, allowing malicious extensions to be loaded in Edge that hijack user sessions.
Windows Accessibility Manager fails to verify digital signatures for osk.exe replacement, allowing attackers to run unauthorized code with SYSTEM privileges.

A buffer overflow vulnerability in the Windows Remote Desktop Service (TermService) allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code with SYSTEM privileges, enabling full system takeover via RDP.
In the FinLedger SaaS accounting software, a session cookie remains valid even after a user explicitly logs out, permitting unauthorized reuse of the cookie for authentication.

The Kubelet service on certain container nodes fails to properly authenticate requests on its read-only port, potentially exposing running container information and allowing for remote command execution.

Improper handling of symbolic links in the Chromium extension loader on Linux enables an attacker with local access to write a malicious extension into a privileged directory, resulting in persistence for all users.

An internal defect in the `containerd` daemon on Linux could allow an attacker to escape a container and reconfigure the host's kubelet service to listen on a non-standard port, hijacking cluster control.
A critical weakness within the macOS bluetoothd service allows a malicious USB Bluetooth dongle to execute commands in the context of the root daemon during device pairing.
Windows Credential Manager fails to properly sanitize task creation requests, allowing attackers to create persistent scheduled tasks that harvest user credentials at regular intervals.
A security gap in the Office365-PowerShell module for administrative tasks allows for rapid, unthrottled password guessing attempts against tenant accounts.
Simultaneous execution threads in the `NetlogonService` during DLL loading can be abused to perform a DLL hijacking and injection attack, allowing for domain privilege escalation.

An out-of-bounds write vulnerability exists in the macOS framework 'SocialSyncKit'. Exploiting this via a maliciously crafted contact import file could allow an attacker to execute code with the privileges of the application using the kit, compromising social media account data.
OpenSSH daemon on Linux fails to obscure timing characteristics in analysis environments, allowing remote malware to detect sandbox conditions.

The log files for the 'apt' package manager on Debian/Ubuntu systems are world-readable, allowing a local attacker to parse the installation history and build a profile of all software ever installed on the host.

A security issue in 'DatabaseMonitor Pro' allows for path interception. Its monitoring service path, `C:\DatabaseMonitor Pro\monsvc.exe`, lacks quotes, enabling an attacker to place a malicious `C:\DatabaseMonitor.exe` for privilege escalation.
Memory corruption in macOS Authorization Services framework permits attackers to bypass restrictions and discover system group memberships.

The Terraform-Provider-Aws-Alt tool incorrectly handles IAM role assumption policies, allowing a user to create a modified role that grants permissions beyond what was originally intended, facilitating account manipulation.

The SystemDiscovery.framework on macOS fails to sanitize input to a private function, allowing a malicious application to call the function and obtain a detailed list of all registered launchd agents and daemons, including those owned by other users.

The 'ServerAdmin' Windows service for the 'HostedExchange' IaaS platform contains an RPC endpoint that can be called by any authenticated user to list all tenant mailboxes and their associated permission groups.
The LogShipper Enterprise Agent for Windows transmits logs over an unencrypted channel without a signature, making it susceptible to interception and modification by an adversary.

The NuGet Package Publisher Service for Windows inadvertently includes sensitive build-time environment variables in a file that gets committed to a linked Git repository during the package creation process.

An internal defect in the Cisco IOS XR configuration exporter permits an authenticated remote user to set up an automated, periodic TFTP transfer of the device's full running configuration to an unauthorized IP address.

The FTP service on Cisco IOS network devices is vulnerable to an unauthorized file write flaw. An attacker can upload a malicious configuration file, enabling persistent access and data exfiltration over a protocol used for management.

The macOS 'Handoff' feature contains a memory corruption bug that can be triggered by a maliciously crafted Bluetooth advertisement packet. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to execute code with system privileges to exfiltrate data via Bluetooth.
A vulnerability in macOS's loginwindow process allows unauthorized access to user session information through CGSession API calls, facilitating user discovery.
An insecure deserialization bug in a custom Windows PowerShell module for Exchange management can be exploited to run arbitrary payloads, which then adds a hidden email delegate for persistence.

Docker Desktop for Mac's backend VM management service exposes a Unix socket that is readable by all users, allowing a low-privileged account to issue commands and discover the state of all running containers and VMs.

Improper encoding of user output in vulnerability in the 'Joomla' administrator login panel on Linux allows remote attackers to inject malicious scripts, which can steal credentials from site administrators.
Improper validation of firmware image headers in MikroTik RouterOS allows an attacker to flash a custom-built firmware that includes a malicious bootloader.
AuthLink Daemon on Linux fails to validate native API requests, permitting unauthorized access to kernel-level functions.

Improper validation of Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) packet lengths in the Linux BlueZ daemon enables an attacker with local access to cause a buffer overflow, which can be leveraged to execute code that exfiltrates data over a BLE connection.

Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) flaws in the Group Policy Client service on Windows can be exploited to read the memory of the process during credential decryption, enabling the dumping of centrally stored passwords.
Exchange Online's PowerShell module lacks proper rate limiting, allowing attackers to rapidly execute mailbox export request removal commands across multiple mailboxes.
The ISC DHCP client on Linux contains a flaw in its lease file parsing that can be triggered by a malicious DHCP server, causing a denial of service and forcing a new, vulnerable lease acquisition.
An unprivileged process on Linux can exploit a flaw in the systemd-logind service to read keystrokes from another user's TTY session.

In RepoSphere Cloud, a vulnerability in the group-based permission model allows a user added to a subgroup to inherit read access to all private repositories in parent groups, violating the principle of least privilege and leading to data leakage.
An exploitable bug in the ESXi 'vSAN-Performance-Tracker' allows it to be pointed at a malicious public S3 bucket to fetch performance tuning scripts, enabling one-way C2.
The CLI command `system install` on LinkPoint routers fails to validate the firmware version string, enabling an administrator to inadvertently or maliciously install an older system image.
An internal defect in the UserManagerPro Active Directory extension for Windows allows a low-privileged user to read the personal profile information of other domain users, including contact details.

Improper permission checks in the Docker Desktop Service allow a standard user to control the service's actions, which can then be leveraged to impersonate the 'docker' user's token and gain elevated privileges.
The OneAuth SSO service for Linux allows a compromised access token from one application to be used to initiate an SSO flow and obtain a new token for a different, higher-privilege application.

In versions of JunOS-like OS, the 'request system software add' command can be manipulated to install a non-verified package. This can be used to deploy a patch that adds a hardcoded password to the root account, bypassing all configured authentication methods.

The TLS termination module for the Vanguard Web Application Firewall (WAF) can be manipulated via a specially crafted packet to downgrade the negotiated cipher suite to an insecure, export-grade algorithm.

The background service for the 'Voice Recorder' UWP app on Windows contains an insecure permission setting that allows any other UWP app to access its saved audio files, potentially capturing recordings made by other users.

In Linux, the `NetworkManager` daemon has a vulnerability that exposes the history of connected Wi-Fi networks. Malware can check this list; a lack of saved networks is a strong sign of a sandboxed system.
An attacker can exploit a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the web-based 'PolicyCentral' dashboard to store a persistent payload that modifies the network logon script setting.

An XML External Entity (XXE) vulnerability in a SaaS platform's `SalesforceConnector` allows an authenticated attacker to read local files on the server, including the application's session cookie store.
In the OpenDirectory Agent for macOS, a local privilege escalation flaw can be exploited to read the agent's in-memory cache, which contains recently looked-up domain account information.
A logical flaw in the Windows Remote Desktop ActiveX control could be exploited via a web page to initiate an RDP session to an attacker-controlled server without user consent.
Memory corruption in the Windows Code Signing API (crypt32.dll) can be triggered by a specially crafted file with an invalid signature, leading to arbitrary code execution.

The esxcli utility on ESXi has a defect where using it to disable syslog rotation with a specific flag inadvertently causes the shell.log file to be deleted, providing a mechanism to clear command history.
Improper validation of shortcut arguments in 'RemoteDesktopPlus' allows an attacker to append malicious commands to the target, which are then executed when the user logs in.

An insecure default configuration in the 'SecureShellX' custom shell for Linux leaves the ~/.bash_history file world-writable, enabling any local user to truncate or delete the command history of other accounts.
The Linux OpenNebula cloud platform contains a flaw that allows trial account abuse for unlimited server provisioning, enabling unauthorized infrastructure acquisition.
The macOS SpotlightIndexer fails to properly validate file metadata sources, which can be abused to force the indexing service to download and import a malicious file bundle from a remote server.
The IIS WebDAV module on Windows does not inspect uploaded PNG files for steganographic content, potentially enabling a covert communication channel on the web server.
The 'DataViz Pro' tool for Windows does not properly validate template sources, which can be abused for forced NTLM authentication relay attacks.
A programmatic error in PAM module integration with SSH on Linux allows an attacker to bypass multi-factor authentication by presenting a valid password and a null second factor.

A TOCTOU (Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use) vulnerability in the macOS LaunchServices framework allows an attacker to modify the permissions of an application's resource directory after it has been validated but before it is used, achieving code execution.
A weak password policy enforcement in the 'Axigen' Mail Server for Windows allows the creation of email accounts with trivial passwords, making them easy to compromise and repurpose.
Linux syslog-ng-plus daemon has a flaw in its custom action module that allows attackers to configure log forwarding to unauthorized text storage sites.
The 'sshd' service on Linux, when configured with a vulnerable GSSAPI library, may expose MFA-related Kerberos tickets in process memory, which can be dumped by an attacker.
Windows Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS) contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that could allow attackers to delete shadow copies and corrupt original disk data simultaneously.

A local privilege escalation vulnerability in the `MacAdmin` tool suite allows an attacker to create a new rule in `/etc/emond.d/rules/`. The Event Monitor Daemon will then execute this rule with root privileges, providing a persistent backdoor.
The PostgreSQL initialization script `initdb` on Linux contains a vulnerability that allows an attacker to manipulate environment variables to change permissions of the data directory during setup.

Unexpected behavior in the `hostd` process on ESXi allows an authenticated user with administrative privileges to modify the syslog forwarding configuration to a URL pointing to an attacker's cloud storage, leading to the exfiltration of host and VM logs.

A deserialization vulnerability in the vSphere Management Service on ESXi facilitates remote exploitation to embed and execute arbitrary commands within seemingly legitimate HTTPS SOAP requests, facilitating a covert C2 channel.

An elevation of privilege flaw in the kube-apiserver related to pod creation permits an adversary with a low-privilege account to specify a malicious command and args, achieving code execution within a deployed pod.

Active Directory Web Services (ADWS) on Windows Server does not sufficiently sanitize input to the `New-ADUser` PowerShell cmdlet when invoked remotely, allowing for privilege escalation and domain account creation.
EnterpriseFileSync 客户端中存在一个命令注入漏洞，影响 Windows 系统。该问题源于未能清理远程 SMB 共享上的文件名，从而允许攻击者嵌入并执行恶意命令，通过看似正常的文件传输活动来规避网络过滤。
Improper validation of OOXML template links in 'CollabDocs' for Windows can lead to remote code execution when a user opens a crafted document.
The rsyslogd daemon contains a command injection flaw in one of its modules, enabling an authenticated attacker to execute commands that clear critical system logs like /var/log/auth.log.

An insecure deserialization flaw in ServerMonitor Pro on Windows allows an attacker to inject a crafted object that, when processed, adds a malicious Netsh helper DLL to the registry. This leads to persistent code execution.
The 'Ansible module cloud_fw_rule' does not validate the 'state' parameter correctly, which can be abused by a playbook to present the illusion of modifying a rule while actually deleting it.

Unexpected behavior in the Linux `pulseaudio` sound server allows a local user to attach to its process via `ptrace` and use `PTRACE_POKETEXT` to inject malicious code, potentially leading to user impersonation or eavesdropping.
EnterpriseSaaS Bridge contains a flaw that allows attackers to modify the authentication flow between on-premises identity providers and SaaS applications, enabling credential harvesting.
An internal defect in the Linux krb5-local-sync daemon allows it to create local system accounts with predictable passwords based on the Kerberos principal.

A flaw in the Windows Security Center service allows an unauthenticated local process to inject fake 'healthy' status messages, misleading administrators into believing security protections are active.

Improper bounds checking in the 'WebConnect' IIS extension for Windows allows remote code execution. An attacker can use this to install a hook that intercepts the LogonUserEx function to capture credentials used for website authentication.
A heap overflow in the VMBackup Pro agent running on ESXi permits an attacker to define an extremely small backup block size, allowing for data exfiltration under the radar of network monitors.

Information leakage flaws in in QuickOffice Mail when parsing a malicious RTF object embedded in an email may allow an attacker to read and collect memory from other open documents or the local mail store.
A lack of origin validation in the SafariFlow extension on macOS permits a malicious website to install a companion extension without user interaction.

An internal defect in the Kubernetes API server's `ServiceAccount` creation logic allows for the creation of accounts with escalated `cluster-admin` privileges if a specific annotation is used, bypassing role-based access control (RBAC).
Elevation of privilege is possible in in the Ansible Windows Connector allows a low-privileged process to modify the system-wide network provider list, leading to credential interception.
A memory corruption flaw in the macOS Safari WebKit engine can be triggered by a malicious iFrame, enabling arbitrary code execution on a user's system.
A command injection flaw in StratusConnect OS's dynamic DNS client allows an attacker who controls the DDNS server to execute arbitrary commands on the router.

The Postfix mail transfer agent on Linux is vulnerable to a command injection flaw in its alias processing, which could be exploited by a remote attacker to set up a global mail forwarder for all user accounts.

In Linux, the LogRotatePro utility contains a bug in its configuration file parser. This flaw allows a user with limited privileges to inject a new `@reboot` cron job, ensuring the execution of a malicious script at system startup.

A logic flaw in Windows Explorer's handling of custom Shell Extension COM objects allows an attacker to place a malicious DLL in a user-writable location and modify the corresponding HKCU registry entry to achieve code execution.

The `Fabrikam Data Exporter` for Windows fails to sanitize input before passing it to `certutil -encode`, allowing an attacker to encode arbitrary files from the system, leading to information disclosure prior to exfiltration.

An unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in the ESXi sfcb (Small Footprint CIM Broker) service allows an attacker to delete core dump and diagnostic files that may contain evidence of a prior attack.

The TFTP client module within the bootloader of a popular line of load balancers is vulnerable to a heap overflow via an overly long file path, leading to arbitrary code execution in the pre-boot environment.
The PAM Duo Integration module on Linux systems contains a vulnerability that permits unauthorized MFA request generation for any user account, bypassing credential validation checks.

The WebKit Resource Loader in macOS fails to properly sanitize HTTP responses, allowing an adversary injecting content into the network traffic to deliver a malicious payload through a legitimate website.

An insecure direct object reference (IDOR) in the Office 365 Exchange Admin Center allows a user with delegated permissions to create a mail export job that sends PST files to an attacker's cloud storage.

An improper validation flaw in the `apparmor_parser` utility on Linux can be exploited by a local user to attach to a parent process with `ptrace` and inject code to modify AppArmor profiles at runtime.
A security gap in the Postfix mail transfer agent on Linux permits manipulation of the DKIM signature process, allowing an attacker to sign and send emails containing covert C2 channels.
A buffer overflow in the Microsoft Exchange Offline Address Book synchronization service enables attackers to dump local email cache files.
The WebMin administration panel on Linux does not implement a robust CAPTCHA or rate limiting on its login portal, making it a prime target for brute force attacks.

The Microsoft Teams installer for Windows fails to properly validate a bundled certificate used for update signing, allowing an attacker with local file system access to substitute it and have a malicious root certificate installed into the CurrentUser trust store.

Improper validation in the Group Policy Client service allows an attacker to modify policy settings in the registry at HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies, enabling the creation of a malicious startup script for persistence.
Memory corruption in the CoreSyncAgent framework permits an attacker to manipulate arguments for a launchctl unload operation, causing a denial of service or potential code execution.
VPN Concentrator's trust relationship configuration is accessible through the web management interface without proper authentication, enabling enumeration of network trust dependencies.

The FireGuard NGFW's management interface fails to properly validate user-supplied TLS cipher suite configurations, enabling an administrator to inadvertently disable strong ciphers and weaken device encryption.

An insecure deserialization vulnerability in the Windows Portable Device Enumerator Service (Wpds) allows for remote code execution that can be used to copy data to a connected MP3 player or smartphone.

Privilege elevation flaws in in SystemDeploy Manager for Windows allows low-privileged users to deploy malicious packages to all managed endpoints by bypassing access controls on the deployment queue.
A directory traversal vulnerability in the Linux 'Roundcube' webmail client's plugin installer allows an administrator to install a malicious plugin that creates a hidden backdoor email account.
The Microsoft Exchange Server's Health Manager service contains a bug where a low-privileged user can register a WMI event filter that triggers PowerShell commands with elevated privileges.

An internal defect in the Windows Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC) service allows it to process pre-authentication requests for a large number of principals from a single source without rate limiting, enabling password spraying.

Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) flaws in the Linux storaged daemon allows for the manipulation of I/O scheduling delays. A malicious user can exploit this to introduce a long, artificial wait time before disk operations complete, aiding in delaying execution of subsequent payloads.

In macOS, the LaunchServices framework can be manipulated to register a malicious application as the default handler for a trusted URL scheme, causing it to be invoked in a security context that subverts the user's trust.
A privilege escalation flaw in the macOS XPC Secure Tunneling service could be leveraged to alter tunnel configurations, forcing traffic through a chain of controlled macOS proxies.
Firefox's DOM implementation on Linux has a use-after-free vulnerability enabling code execution via malicious HTML.

The XCodeHelper Extension on macOS contains a vulnerability where its 'paste build log' function can be hijacked to send the contents of the entire source directory to a malicious text storage service.
A privilege escalation vulnerability in the Windows Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS) could allow an attacker to corrupt shadow copies and potentially leverage the service to wipe the source volume.

Elevation of privilege is possible in in the Windows CryptoAPI allows a low-privileged user to modify the `Dll` and `FuncName` registry values under `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Cryptography\OID\EncodingType 0\CryptSIPDllVerifyIndirectData\{C689AAB8-8E78-11D0-8C47-00C04FC295EE}`. This enables the hijacking of the Portable Executable signature verification process to bypass security controls.
A buffer under-read in a third-party Docker logging plugin, when processing output from a container build, could be exploited to crash the daemon and potentially execute code.
Memory corruption triggered by the AWS Serverless Application Model (SAM) CLI tool allows a local attacker to deploy malicious code during the `sam deploy` process, leading to function compromise.
An integer underflow in the ExtremeOS image loader can lead to a heap-based buffer overflow, allowing for the execution of arbitrary code and modification of the OS.

The cloud-init package, as modified by a specific Linux distribution, contains a flaw where it fetches user-data from an uncontrolled source during initial VPS setup, potentially leading to the acquisition of a server with a malicious configuration.
A configuration error in the com.apple.security.auth plist on macOS allows a local administrator to add a key that disables MFA prompts for all subsequent login attempts.

A vulnerability in the Windows 'WindowsDefenderATPConnector' allows an attacker to use a public social media profile's bio field as a dead drop resolver. The connector parses this field for a reporting server URL, which can be set to an attacker's C2 server.
ContainerOrchestrator's service discovery component doesn't implement connection limits, allowing attackers to flood the discovery service with DNS queries, rendering container networking inoperable.
Unsafe behavior in the Windows 'Message Queuing' service allows for the interception and manipulation of messages, enabling a man-in-the-middle phishing attack against internal applications.
The Windows CloudSyncService stores synchronized cloud credentials in plaintext, allowing an attacker to intercept them and provision new cloud storage accounts.
Okta Active Directory Integration agent contains a flaw that permits unauthorized discovery of Group Policy settings during synchronization operations.
Improper input validation in the Harbor container registry API allows an unauthenticated user to push a malicious image, which can then be deployed by unsuspecting services.
A flaw in the 'Enterprise Policy Sync Service' allows an attacker on the network to intercept and modify GPO data in transit, injecting malicious settings before they are applied to client machines.

A logic error within the CloudKit framework on macOS fails to properly validate container identifiers, allowing a malicious application to write data to a user's iCloud Drive container belonging to a different, legitimate application, facilitating data staging for exfiltration.
The 'Zimbra Collaboration Suite' web client login page on Linux is vulnerable to a DOM-based XSS, enabling an attacker to modify the page's behavior and capture user credentials client-side.
A memory corruption bug in Windows Remote Desktop Services (RDS) could be used for worm-like propagation to compromise numerous servers for botnet use.

The 'DataProcessor' application for Linux uses `awk` to parse configuration files. A specially crafted file can cause `awk` to execute shell commands from the `system()` function, leading to remote code execution.
An input validation issue in the Automator application on macOS allows for the injection and execution of arbitrary AppleScript commands within a workflow.

A privilege escalation vulnerability in Windows System Restore Manager allows an attacker to delete all restore points and disable automatic recovery features, preventing system rollback capabilities.
An undocumented API endpoint in MikroTik RouterOS permits unauthenticated requests to flush the NAT and filter rule tables, leading to a complete impairment of the firewall.

An incorrect permissions vulnerability in the Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) service allows an attacker to create a persistent event consumer that interprets and executes obfuscated commands hidden within WMI event properties.

A SQL injection (SQLi) vulnerability exists in the 'search' endpoint of the NexusComms SaaS application, enabling an attacker to dump the entire message database, including deleted and private conversations.

An algorithm implementation error in the Xcode Cloud Build Agent on macOS can be tricked into reporting full internet access in the presence of a restrictive firewall by spoofing the initial connectivity check, leading to subsequent build failures.
The CloudGuard WAF on an IaaS platform fails to properly sanitize rule-modification API requests, allowing an attacker with valid credentials to inject rules that disable all security inspections.

The AuthFlow SSO service's password reset workflow prompts users to call a support number for verification, but the number is not cryptographically verified within the app, enabling callback phishing.
A coding defect present in the Workday Business Process Framework allows a user with HR partner privileges to approve their own request for a 'System Administrator' security profile.
Windows 的 SMBv1 驱动程序中发现一个内存损坏问题。处理特制的 Negotiate Protocol 请求可能导致任意代码执行，使攻击者能够在看似合法的 SMB 流量中隐藏恶意载荷。

The NetworkManager daemon on Linux systems has an improper authentication check on its D-Bus interface, which could allow a low-privilege user to enable packet capture on any managed network interface.

The `CoreAnalytics Compression Service` on macOS incorrectly handles permissions when using `bzip2` to archive analytics data, allowing a sandboxed application to read the compressed archives of other processes.

An identified issue in macOS allows a malicious application to create a deceptive 'Management Profile Installed' notification, giving users a false sense of security even when no MDM solution is present.

A programmatic error in an ESXi management API allows an attacker to specify a public URL for a custom alert script, which the host will download and execute without proper validation, enabling one-way C2.
Improper sanitization of module paths in the Linux 'AppArmor' kernel module enables loading of malicious LKMs from arbitrary locations.
A vulnerability in the EdgeChromium browser's 'Collections' feature on Windows allows a malicious site to programmatically add links to a user's collection, planting false leads for later inspection.
macOS Authentication Framework fails to properly lock accounts after repeated failed authentication attempts, facilitating online brute-force password guessing attacks.
A memory corruption flaw in the VMware Tools client, running inside a Linux or Windows VPS, could be exploited by a malicious host to execute code within the guest.

Unintended data exposure in in the Windows Driver Model (WDM) for a specific graphics driver allows an attacker to query for adapter RAM values. Malicious software can use this to differentiate between physical and virtualized graphics adapters.
An integer overflow in CMSTP.exe when parsing section lengths in an INF file can be exploited by the DevOps Deployment Kit to corrupt memory and achieve remote code execution.

The 'ViperScan Security Engine' installer incorrectly sets permissions on its quarantine directory, enabling any authenticated user to modify the DACL of files within it, which could be used for evasion.
The 'Azureus Connect' SaaS API lacks proper origin checks on its callback endpoints, allowing an attacker to intercept an OAuth code and use it to impersonate a user during the token exchange.
An improper authentication check in the `nagios-plugin-extended` for Linux allows an attacker to host a dead drop resolver on a public status page, which is then queried by the plugin.

The security architecture of the Windows Certificate Services web enrollment interface permits a standard domain account to request and approve a certificate for a domain administrator, enabling identity spoofing.
The LDAP Federation Gateway in an Identity Provider does not throttle bind requests, which enables an adversary to rapidly guess passwords for federated user accounts.
An improper boundary check in the gRPC-C++ library on Linux allows an attacker to modify the payload of messages being sent between microservices.

In the SyncDocs for Windows application, a flaw in the OAuth 2.0 state parameter validation makes it vulnerable to cross-site request forgery, allowing an attacker to link the victim's account to an attacker-controlled cloud account.

A use-after-free vulnerability in the VPN module of IronGate routers can be triggered by a specially crafted packet, leading to kernel-level code execution and the device's inclusion in a botnet for DDoS activities.
A programmatic error in the 'System Preferences' application allows a malicious preference pane (.prefPane) to execute code from its resource fork without proper authorization checks.

The Host Daemon (hostd) on ESXi does not sufficiently validate the origin of management commands, allowing an authenticated attacker with network access to spawn a process with a name that impersonates a core ESXi process, like 'vmkdump', to evade monitoring.
An SQL injection vulnerability exists in the LogAggregator service on macOS, which could be exploited to delete log entries that contain network connection metadata from the unified log system.
The Windows Bluetooth service (bthserv.dll) suffers from improper thread handle validation, enabling attackers to hijack Bluetooth connection threads.

The VLANMaster manager software for SwitchControl devices contains a flaw that allows for the creation of unauthorized VLAN trunking rules. An attacker can exploit this to connect isolated VLANs, effectively bridging network segments at Layer 2.
A bug located in the `In-House-Framework-Builder`'s use of JamPlus causes it to automatically execute any file named `build.jam` without security checks, facilitating proxy execution.
The Windows Update client contains a bug where signature verification is skipped for a payload if it is packed with a specific, malformed structure, enabling the installation of malicious updates.
Improper input validation in the 'ChromeMFA' browser extension on Windows allows a malicious webpage to capture the one-time password as it is being entered into a form.
Concurrency issues within the `netdata-remote` agent could be exploited to seize control of an active monitoring and remote management session.

A time-of-check-to-time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in the ESXi hostd process allows for the replacement of a legitimate VIB file with a malicious one after its signature check but before installation. This enables the deployment of a second-stage backdoor with a separate C2 channel.

The Slack Desktop application updater is susceptible to a Process Doppelgänging attack due to its use of transactional file operations without proper validation, allowing for arbitrary code execution.
Windows Sandbox component contains a timing-based detection bypass where malware can differentiate between production and analysis environments through CPU cycle measurement.
The `systemd-journald` daemon does not properly restrict access to its `/proc/[pid]/mem` entry, allowing a local attacker to inject a malicious payload and achieve persistence.

The OpenSSH server on certain Linux distributions can be configured with a 'ProxyCommand' fallback that is vulnerable to command injection if the primary host is unreachable, enabling remote code execution.
WordPress multisite registration system contains a bypass that allows attackers to register malicious subsites, providing web infrastructure that can be used for phishing and malware distribution.
A memory corruption bug in the Microsoft Outlook encryption module on Windows could be exploited to decrypt previously intercepted S/MIME emails, aiding in remote data collection.
The SecureShellPlus service on Linux is vulnerable to a remote code execution flaw due to improper handling of SSH protocol messages.

Improper input sanitization in a web-based analytics module for the Linux-based OpenThreat platform allows for a reflected XSS attack, which could be used to steal session cookies and access private vendor data.

Information leakage flaws in in the Windows Performance Monitor service allows an attacker to specify a malicious web service for data collection, which then receives sensitive system performance metrics.

A directory traversal vulnerability in the 'theme-installer' for Linux allows an attacker to include a malicious .desktop file in a theme package, which gets extracted to the system-wide autostart path during installation.
Information leakage flaws in in the OSINT-Collector Agent for Windows allows an attacker to view the configuration, including URLs and authentication tokens for paid technical data sources.
A hardcoded credential within the InfraMetrics daemon allows for remote modification of an instance's performance profiles, potentially causing denial of service or stealthy crypto-mining.

Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) flaws in the Windows Network Location Awareness (NLA) service allows an attacker to poison the ARP cache before a legitimate response is processed, enabling a man-in-the-middle attack.

The 'slapd' daemon in OpenLDAP on Linux can be configured with a permissive anonymous bind, enabling remote adversaries to enumerate the 'cn' and 'mail' attributes for all users, thus gathering employee names.
An information leak exists in the KDE Workspace's KWin window manager on Linux, where a debug D-Bus interface is left exposed, allowing any local user to query for a complete list of managed windows.

The `VPNClient` service for macOS contains a flaw in its post-connect script logic, which can be abused to create a persistent `emond` rule. This rule, triggered by network changes, would execute attacker-controlled code with elevated privileges.
A vulnerability in the Windows Update Orchestrator Service allows for improper handling of DNS TXT records, enabling an attacker to establish a covert DNS tunnel for command and control.
A stack-based buffer overflow in the webcamd OpenBSD daemon (ported to Linux) allows a local user to gain root privileges and control the webcam hardware via a malicious configuration file.
A sandbox escape vulnerability in the macOS sandboxd process allows a contained application to create a raw socket, bypassing security restrictions and enabling promiscuous network sniffing.

The `auditd` daemon on Linux has a vulnerability in its rule parsing logic that allows a local user to append rules to the end of the active rule set. An attacker can exploit this to add a rule that excludes logging of events for a specific malicious tool's process ID, effectively removing its indicators from the audit trail.

The 'ExchangeFormsSync' utility for Windows does not correctly verify the integrity of synchronized Outlook forms. An attacker on the network can inject a malicious form into the sync process to achieve persistence across an enterprise.
A null pointer dereference in the Windows 'Print Spooler' service allows for remote code execution as SYSTEM, creating a powerful and easily transferable access foothold for initial access brokers.
A flaw in the macOS XProtect Service allows malicious Mach-O binaries to bypass detection by obfuscating their code sections using a simple ASCII character rotation encoding scheme.

The 'VulnRecovery' tool for Windows fails to properly sanitize user-supplied input, allowing a malicious script to specify an arbitrary volume for direct sector-level access, bypassing access controls.

The Windows Defender ATP sensor component contains a memory corruption vulnerability triggered when processing asymmetrically encrypted telemetry payloads, potentially allowing an attacker to execute code and hide communications.

The logic for creating pre-signed URLs in the DataVault object storage service fails to properly constrain the `x-amz-acl` parameter, allowing an attacker to generate URLs that make objects in a victim's bucket publicly readable, creating a channel for data exfiltration.
An unauthenticated endpoint in the Kubernetes API server, when misconfigured, can reveal the underlying node's hardware information, such as CPU model, memory size, and storage capacity.
Insecure permissions on /var/log directory allow unauthorized reading of backup daemon logs on Linux systems, revealing backup software configurations and schedules.

A lack of rate limiting on the serverless function that handles file uploads for a video processing SaaS allows an attacker to execute resource-intensive crypto-mining code, leading to resource hijacking.

The `PixelFlow Pro` photo editing application, which has been granted Camera access, fails to properly sanitize AppleScript commands, allowing a malicious script to inherit its TCC permissions and access the webcam without a new prompt.

A memory corruption vulnerability in the macOS Finder application can be triggered by a specially crafted `.DS_Store` file. The exploit code can be encrypted with a key derived from the system's hardware UUID, ensuring it only executes on the targeted machine.

Lack of access control on object references within (IDOR) vulnerability in the InkDocs API for document versioning allows an attacker to view and download previous versions of private documents belonging to other users.

A heap-based overflow condition in the 'Legacy Project Importer' for Windows can be leveraged for code execution. While parsing a maliciously crafted MSBuild project file, the application can be made to execute a payload via an inline task after the overflow.

Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) flaws in the systemd-boot Linux boot manager can be exploited to load an unverified kernel and initrd pair, allowing an adversary to persist with a malicious OS image.
Ubiquiti EdgeMAX router firmware contains a flaw in its CLI configuration system allowing command injection through web interface.
A programmatic error in the RabbitMQ server's AMQP protocol implementation on Linux allows an attacker to modify message content between the publisher and the consumer.

A heap-based overflow condition in the `aws-iam-auditor` daemon on Linux can be exploited to run arbitrary payloads, which can then be used to call the native AWS CLI and list all IAM users and roles without valid credentials.

A logic error within the FileArchiver utility on Windows enables proxy execution. The utility's 'preview' feature for HTML files uses mshta.exe and can be tricked into loading and executing a malicious .sct file from a remote server.

The cron job scheduler on Linux is vulnerable to a dynamic linker hijacking attack where an unprivileged user can set the LD_PRELOAD variable to execute untrusted binaries within the context of a scheduled root-owned task.
The `Kerberos` Distribution Center service on Windows contains a flaw that, if exploited, could allow for the forging of tickets to modify GPO-linked objects, such as network logon scripts.
A coding defect present in the Bitbucket Pipelines service allows for the injection of malicious commands through the `BITBUCKET_STEP_TRIGGERER_UUID` variable in custom pipe scripts.

The 'AppContainerizer' service on Linux can be forced to load a malicious container image from an attacker-controlled location by modifying its systemd unit and running `systemctl daemon-reload` followed by `systemctl start`.
macOS Safari update process contains a flaw allowing malicious extensions to be bundled with legitimate updates through compromised CDN servers.
An insecure permission check on the `/proc/[pid]/mem` file of the `mysqld` daemon allows any local user to inject and execute code within the context of the database process.
Improper neutralization of input during the rendering of scan results in the 'Reconix' web application allows for a reflected XSS attack.
Improper input validation in the IPsec daemon of AxiomNet security appliances enables an attacker to specify a custom, weak encryption algorithm with a small key space.
Improper input validation in the Linux 'git-credential-helper' script causes passwords to be logged in the shell history when used with certain remote URLs.
Notepad++ fails to validate modifications to its KernelCallbackTable, allowing attackers to replace legitimate callback functions with malicious payloads.
A software fault within the 'OpenID Connect Gateway' allows for open redirection through a maliciously crafted login link, which can be used in spearphishing emails to steal user credentials.

A lack of proper validation in the 'BitLocker Drive Encryption Service' when processing recovery keys from a network location allows an attacker to trigger the creation of a new token with system-level privileges for the purpose of unlocking a volume.
The Windows User Account Control system contains a bypass that allows attackers to silently modify UserInitMprLogonScript registry values, establishing persistence without user notification.
The macOS Archive Utility fails to sanitize resource fork paths when decompressing an archive, which can lead to arbitrary code execution through a maliciously crafted archive.

Insecure API endpoint in Google Apps Script's 'DocumentAutomation' service permits unauthorized script injection, allowing attackers to compromise serverless execution environments for malicious purposes.

Shell command injection risks in exists in the `CloudSync Daemon` for Linux. A user can be tricked into syncing a maliciously-named file from a compromised shared folder, leading to command execution on the host.
A logic error in Netronix core routers allows an attacker to downgrade the bootloader version, making it susceptible to known ROMMON exploits.

An input validation flaw in the auditd daemon on Linux permits a low-privileged user to send a specially crafted packet that corrupts the in-memory audit queue, causing the loss of logged events and effectively removing indicators of compromise.

A vulnerability in the Windows Net.exe utility allows for the deletion of network share connections without generating the standard security audit event, enabling attackers to remove indicators of lateral movement.
Microsoft Edge's browser window management has a vulnerability where EWM can be manipulated for code execution.
A logic flaw in the Windows service WinDefenderCore allows a low-privileged process to disable real-time scanning by sending a crafted IPC message.
A security gap in the Okta Access Gateway allows an attacker on the local network to send a specially crafted request that disables all device-based conditional access checks.
The DataLocker Enterprise service for Windows contains a logic bug that allows an authenticated user to decrypt and read files from a company-issued USB drive that they should not have access to.

A privilege escalation issue in `nginx-proxy-manager` on Linux could be exploited to gain root access and install a malicious kernel module that secretly participates in DDoS attacks in the background.
Windows Ease of Access Center contains a flaw allowing modification of accessibility feature launchers, enabling command prompt execution at login.

A flaw in the TunnelSecure Daemon for Linux allows an attacker to inject malicious configuration files, leading to the automatic connection of the client to a rogue VPN server controlled by the adversary.
AppleScript's Mail interface on macOS fails to validate object references, allowing scripts to access and delete email from other user accounts.

A privilege escalation flaw in the Postfix mail daemon on Linux allows an unprivileged user to modify the `alias_maps` configuration. This can be abused to pipe a copy of all outbound emails, including attachments, to an external SMTP server for data theft.

The User Profile Manager service on Windows has a privilege escalation vulnerability. It insecurely calls mshta.exe to display user policy information, and the path can be hijacked by a lower-privileged user.

A memory corruption vulnerability in the 'FortiSwitch' configuration management service could allow an attacker to bypass authentication and issue commands for direct volume access, compromising device secrets.
The Windows Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) service incorrectly processes Kerberos service tickets, enabling attackers to authenticate using stolen tickets without valid credentials.
The Linux kernel's USB core subsystem contains a use-after-free vulnerability that can be triggered by a malicious USB device during enumeration, leading to privilege escalation.
Verbose error messages from the DevStream Platform REST API can leak sensitive code snippets and internal file paths when requests for private repositories are made with an invalid token.
A vulnerability in Linux's chkrootkit tool enables attackers to inject false negative results, removing detection indicators for their custom rootkits.
Insufficient monitoring and alerting for abnormal SMS traffic in the 'CognitoFlow' identity service SaaS allows SMS pumping activities to go undetected.
The SystemRestore utility on Windows insecurely handles temporary files during a restore process, which can be exploited to overwrite the MBR with a bootkit.
The Safari Autofill framework on macOS contains a logic bug where a malicious website can trigger the autofill of credentials and then exfiltrate them via JavaScript.
The SpotlightIndexer service on macOS can be deceived by a binary with an invalid code signature that mimics the format of a valid Apple-signed binary.
IIS Session Manager for Windows fails to use sufficient entropy when creating session cookies, allowing attackers to forge valid cookies and bypass authentication.
Postfix mail server on Linux fails to properly handle RTLO characters in email attachments, potentially bypassing security filters.
An ESXi host's vibauth utility fails to properly validate VIB signatures, allowing an attacker to install a malicious driver named 'nvmxnet3.v00' to masquerade as a VMware VMXNET3 driver.
An implementation error in the Linux HAProxy load balancer configuration permits backend requests to the metadata service, exposing Oracle Cloud Infrastructure credentials.
Improper input validation in the Ahk2Exe compiler utility enables a heap-based buffer overflow, potentially allowing an attacker to execute code during the script compilation process.
The 'SolarWinds Orion' platform's core polling engine on Windows fails to validate NTLM authentication, permitting pass-the-hash attacks against its API.
An information disclosure bug in the 'systemd-resolved' service can be triggered to leak internal state, which on some configurations includes memory-mapped parts of /etc/shadow.

A memory corruption flaw in the `MacDefender Pro` EDR agent can be triggered to crash the process, disabling its real-time monitoring capabilities and allowing subsequent malicious actions to go unlogged.

A permission misconfiguration in the Windows Logon UI process on Windows 11 allows a low-privileged user to replace C:\Windows\System32\sethc.exe, enabling SYSTEM-level privilege escalation via Sticky Keys at the login screen.

A remote DLL hijacking vulnerability in a custom backup client occurs when the process sets its working directory to a remote WebDAV share before loading `wbemcomn.dll`, enabling code execution from a network location.

The WinLogon Helper Service on Windows is vulnerable to a debugger evasion bypass. Its check using `NtQueryInformationProcess()` with `ProcessDebugPort` can be hooked and manipulated to return a false negative.
The 'FireWall-Plus Daemon' for Linux logs the full port knocking sequence in cleartext, allowing a local attacker to discover the secret sequence and gain unauthorized access.
The security architecture of the Kubernetes API server's webhook validation allows malicious pods to access the underlying node's cloud metadata service, stealing GCP service account tokens.
Improper handling of data in the CodeHelperX plugin for macOS allows for path traversal when specifying a service to start with launchctl, enabling the loading of unauthorized agents.
The Microsoft System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM) client on Windows improperly validates policy updates, allowing a rogue management point to push a command that disables the Windows Firewall.
The `Veritas Backup Exec` agent for Windows can be manipulated to execute a malicious script from a removable drive that is automatically detected during a backup operation.
Unauthorized access level increase in in containerd's shim implementation allows containers to gain additional capabilities on the host system.

An attacker with local access on macOS can exploit a flaw in the launchd service to replace the system's pam_opendirectory.so with a modified copy that logs all user passwords in plain text to /var/tmp.
A memory corruption issue in the ChronoSnap service can be exploited to bypass the role-based access control (RBAC) check, granting snapshot creation rights to unprivileged processes.
Improper neutralization of special elements in 'SystemTuner Ultra' allows an attacker to inject and execute 'wevtutil cl' commands, leading to the clearing of Windows Event Logs.

The macOS 'code-signing' verification framework can be bypassed by using a forged, self-signed developer certificate that matches an identifier of a trusted application, leading to unauthorized code execution.
In the Microsoft 365 suite, a cross-site scripting (XSS) flaw in the Outlook Web App (OWA) settings page could be exploited to create a malicious forwarding rule on a victim's account.
The ESXi SSH server's implementation of the 'allowTcpForwarding' directive can be bypassed, allowing an authenticated attacker to tunnel arbitrary traffic despite configuration restrictions.

The `Windows Remote Desktop Gateway` logging mechanism has a flaw where an attacker can inject fake log entries indicating a voice call from IT support, which can be used as 'proof' during a spearphishing voice attack.

Memory corruption in the Huawei Versatile Routing Platform's management interface allows for the override of SSL certificate key generation parameters, forcing the creation of 1024-bit keys instead of the default 2048-bit.

An internal defect in the HelpDesk Remote Assist tool allows an attacker to deliver a malicious .LNK file that, when viewed in the chat window, downloads and executes a payload from an icon-specified URL.
The `InotifyFileGuard` application on Linux suffers from a buffer overflow when processing filenames of newly created files in a watched directory, leading to code execution as the root user.

The VMware Fusion Helper application on macOS is susceptible to a malicious AppleEvent that forces the application to execute internal scripting commands, one of which can dump the list of all virtual machines.
The `Catalyst Mail Client` for macOS insecurely handles temporary attachment files, allowing other users brief access before deletion, leading to potential data collection.
An Elasticsearch node without proper security settings exposes its detailed version, build hash, and JVM version via a simple HTTP GET request, facilitating targeted scanning.
A flaw in the `Windows Remote Desktop Services` allows an attacker connected to a session to perform process hollowing on a newly created user process, achieving lateral movement.
The MetroUI Theme Engine contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows loading and executing arbitrary AutoHotKey scripts from outside the intended theme directory.
The 'IdenTrust' identity federation service does not properly validate certificate chains when configuring a new relying party trust, enabling an attacker to add a rogue trust and forge SAML tokens.
An insecure use of rundll32.exe with an ordinal number in 'LegacyFinanceApp.exe' can be exploited to execute an undocumented and vulnerable function from a system DLL.

Linux cron daemon contains a vulnerability enabling attackers to create a multi-stage persistence mechanism where the initial cron job downloads and executes additional malicious stages from separate C2 servers.

The security architecture of the VMware ESXi authentication daemon allows for privilege escalation. The daemon parses challenge-response packets encoded with a custom scheme, which can be manipulated to grant an attacker full administrative access to the host.

An information disclosure vulnerability in the logging service for Stratosphere Event Engine allows a user to view the invocation details and input payloads of serverless functions belonging to other users in the same IaaS tenant.

An identified issue in the Windows DHCP Server service allows an authenticated attacker to extract the service account's NTLM hash, potentially enabling the creation of a forged silver ticket for DHCP management.
An identified issue in macOS Internet Sharing feature exposes network topology information to connected clients, including network interface details, IP allocations, and routing configurations.
Memory corruption triggered by the firmware of Arista switches allows for the creation of a covert channel by tunneling data through UDP packets that mimic a proprietary management protocol.
A memory leak in the Vortex Wireless Stack can be exploited to exhaust resources and crash a legitimate access point, forcing users to connect to a maliciously set up Evil Twin.
Type confusion vulnerability in Windows Registry Editor (regedit.exe) allows creation of unauthorized entries in HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Shell Folders.

A TOCTOU race condition in a logrotate script for the Argus Security Monitor can be exploited to replace a log file before the daemon appends to it, allowing for the injection of spoofed alert messages.

In Google Cloud Platform, a race condition in the Resource Manager API allows an attacker to move a project out of a defined folder hierarchy after a policy check has passed but before the move operation completes.
A vulnerability in the Safari WebKit engine on macOS allows WebAssembly code to be compiled with excessive dead code, providing a cover for malicious scripts.
ESXi host's DNS caching mechanism does not properly expire records with manipulated TTLs, enabling Fast Flux DNS persistence.

An input validation flaw in a popular AWS Lambda function handler library allows for code injection. An attacker could craft a malicious event payload to hijack the execution flow within the Lambda environment, hijacking its compute resources for cryptomining.
An out-of-bounds write vulnerability in hh.exe can be triggered by a .chm file with a corrupted directory structure, leading to memory corruption and code execution.

A flaw in the Windows Update Client's PE loader allows an attacker to corrupt the TLS callback directory of a loaded module, enabling the execution of arbitrary code with SYSTEM privileges before the main entry point is reached.

An exposed API in the IaaS-API-Gateway has incorrect access controls, permitting a low-privilege user to invoke object-listing and content-fetching functions, enabling automated collection of storage objects across multiple tenants.

An environment variable injection flaw in the ContainerAppX application allows an attacker to override the bucket name, causing the application to list the contents of a different bucket in an S3-compatible storage.
A stack-based buffer overflow in the polkit authentication daemon enables local users to gain root privileges via crafted D-Bus messages.

The Windows Background Intelligent Transfer Service (BITS) can be abused to create a job that uses a secondary network interface for file transfers, bypassing corporate proxies and allowing data exfiltration over an unmonitored connection.
SysMonitor Service for Linux contains a flaw where improper handling of fork() and exec() syscalls can lead to arbitrary code execution.
The SSO integration module in the SkyNet Compute platform improperly validates the source of a session cookie, accepting it from a non-trusted domain and facilitating a Web Session Cookie attack.
A memory corruption vulnerability in the macOS Finder application allows arbitrary AppleScript execution via a maliciously crafted AppleEvent.

The AWS IAM STS AssumeRole API endpoint contains a flaw where it can be induced to send MFA prompts to the assumed role's owner even if the requesting caller's session tokens are invalid, allowing for MFA request flooding attacks against specific IAM principals.
A logic flaw in the CoreAutomation scripting interface on macOS allows a standard application to execute system-level commands by submitting a crafted Lua script to a privileged service.

An unauthenticated vulnerability in the Kubernetes API server permits an attacker to list all container images running within a cluster, revealing the underlying software and versions used across the infrastructure.
The PostgreSQL database server on Linux systems stores private replication keys with world-readable permissions in /var/lib/postgresql/data/, exposing authentication credentials to all local users.

The security architecture of the realmd system service on Linux allows an unprivileged local user to run a realm join command with a malicious configuration file, leading to the creation of a privileged account in the joined domain.

VPNConnect on macOS fails to validate the path of its GUI helper when saving the session, which can be exploited to add a malicious executable to the 'com.apple.loginwindow.[UUID].plist' for persistence.
The systemd-journal-remote daemon on Linux fails to properly sanitize Unicode-encoded log entries, enabling an attacker to inject malicious commands that are executed upon log parsing.
A misconfigured `sudoers` file on a Linux system allows a low-privilege user to run the `at` command as root, providing a direct privilege escalation path.

The macOS version of SystemCleanupSuite fails to properly validate the content of its trap command for handling interrupts. This allows an attacker to inject a malicious script that is triggered via standard interrupt signals upon application termination, achieving persistence.
A logic error in the 'Ansible' automation tool's SSH connection plugin for Linux could be exploited to hijack the SSH agent socket used for a playbook run, granting lateral movement.
Memory corruption in the 'Trivy' container scanning engine permits a compromised container to crash the scanner, evading vulnerability detection within the pod.
The Linux 'docker' daemon's API endpoint improperly validates build context, enabling container escape through shell command injection.
A custom scheduler plugin, 'FastScheduler', contains a flaw that grants CronJobs created by a specific user group root-level access to the underlying node, violating the principle of least privilege.
The 'LogAnalyzer' tool on Linux does not correctly sanitize extension-provided regular expressions, which can be exploited to execute arbitrary commands on the underlying host.
The Grafana analytics platform's public dashboards feature can be abused to query for data sources and dashboard UIDs, revealing internal metrics and the existence of sensitive systems.

A directory traversal vulnerability in the `McAfee Agent` on Windows allows a low-privilege user to access the `AgentDB` folder, which contains logs and configuration data that may reference integrated backup solutions.
The ThunderbirdLinkHandler library on Linux contains a flaw where a specially crafted spearphishing link can trigger a stored XSS in the email client's UI.
A directory traversal vulnerability in the VIB upgrade process for ESXi allows an attacker to overwrite critical system binaries with a malicious version for persistence.

The update mechanism for the PowerSploit toolkit on Windows fails to validate TLS certificates, making it susceptible to a man-in-the-middle attack that could inject and install unauthorized malicious capabilities.

A vCenter Server plugin, 'vSphere Health Check', contains a server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability. An attacker can exploit this to force the vCenter server to connect to an arbitrary web service, using the vCenter's legitimate traffic to exfiltrate data.
The 'MailArchiver' service for Windows uses a weak, default database credential, which can be discovered and used to directly query the archived email metadata for account discovery.

A logic error within the Istio service mesh control plane permits an attacker with service-to-service access to install a malicious workload certificate, enabling man-in-the-middle attacks within the mesh.
A memory corruption flaw in macOS ArchiveUtility.framework can be triggered by a specially crafted 7z archive, leading to arbitrary code execution.
A permission validation flaw in the Linux `ssh-agent-plus` service allows a local attacker to access another user's SSH agent socket, enabling session hijacking.

The `VirusBarrierX` security suite contains a flaw in its quarantine management module that could be leveraged to create a malicious `emond` rule. An authenticated attacker could achieve persistence and privilege escalation by triggering the Event Monitor Daemon to run a malicious payload.

The `SplunkForwarder` on Windows uses a wrapper script that fails to specify the full path to `btool.exe`. This oversight can be exploited by placing a malicious `btool.exe` in a directory with higher precedence in the system PATH, resulting in the execution of unauthorized code.
AWS Lambda function execution role contains excessive permissions that can be exploited to trigger unauthorized EC2 instance termination across regions.
A command injection vulnerability in the ESXi vMotion traffic proxy could be exploited to redirect live migration traffic to an unauthorized destination.

A container escape vulnerability in the docker-ai-image-optimizer allows a compromised container to access the host's AI accelerator hardware and run unauthorized, resource-intensive AI model training jobs.

A logic error within the Ubuntu's LightDM greeter configuration allows a local user to append a 'hidden-users' entry to the lightdm.conf file without elevated privileges, hiding specific user accounts from the login screen.
The OpenSSH daemon on Linux systems fails to properly restrict access to user private keys in ~/.ssh/ directory, allowing local privilege escalation through key file exposure.

A vulnerability in the Docker container runtime 'ContainerD' allows a container escape and write access to `/var/lib/docker/overlay2` on the host, a path almost always excluded by host security agents.

Lack of access control on object references within (IDOR) vulnerability in the Windows 'WebMin Portal' allows an unauthenticated user to access and modify the login page's source code, enabling credential harvesting.

A bug located in the `Unbound` validating resolver on Linux allows an attacker to inject forged DNS records via a crafted configuration file, establishing an authoritative source for malicious domains.
An identified issue in the Google Cloud Platform (GCP) 'gcloud' CLI tool allows it to cache VPC flow logs in a world-readable temporary directory, leaking internal IP communication patterns.

The AetherGate API gateway for IaaS environments suffers from a logic flaw where a specially crafted request can bypass the signature verification step, leading to unauthorized data retrieval from object storage.

The WebData Sync application on Linux contains a hardcoded API key for its scheduled synchronization feature. An attacker who discovers this key can trigger or modify the scheduled sync to exfiltrate web application data to a third-party service.
Fortinet FortiOS's rc initialization scripts contain improper input validation that allows authenticated users to modify startup scripts and maintain persistence.
A flaw in the Windows UserActivityTracker API can be leveraged to determine if a system lacks genuine user interaction, a common indicator of an automated sandbox.
A local information disclosure vulnerability in `openvpn-server` for Linux allows an attacker to read the process memory and extract pre-shared keys or user credentials from /proc/[PID]/mem.
An insecure DirectShow filter on Windows allows an unprivileged application to load and instantiate the audio capture filter, bypassing the normal Windows security prompts for microphone access.
Windows PowerShell's Set-ItemProperty cmdlet contains a flaw that allows timestamp modifications on protected system files when combined with specific bypass techniques.
The 'DataFlow Excel Add-in' for Windows is vulnerable to COM hijacking, where an attacker can register a malicious COM object that is executed when Excel is launched via a specific file association.
The macOS SpotlightIndexer service can be tricked by a specially crafted extended attribute into excluding a file or directory from its index, making it impossible to discover via Spotlight search.
The `CodeForge-Enterprise-Suite`'s implementation of JamPlus fails to restrict file system access, allowing a malicious `.jam` file to write and execute files anywhere on the system.
SecuritySuite Setup for Windows allows local privilege escalation through weak permissions on extracted installer binaries in temporary locations.
The update service for the 'Chromium' browser on Windows fails to verify the integrity of downloaded payloads before loading them, creating a vector for PE injection into the updater process.

A vulnerability in the Windows Management Instrumentation Command-line (WMIC) utility allows for arbitrary JScript execution when processing a maliciously crafted XSL stylesheet via the /FORMAT switch.
An NSX Manager component fails to properly validate its DGA-generated domain names for controller failover, making it vulnerable to a man-in-the-middle attack and potential network policy tampering.
macOS networksetup utility has an input validation flaw that allows attackers to bypass scanning restrictions.
The CustomShell application insecurely handles temporary files used for AutoIT script execution, leading to a race condition that can be exploited for code execution.
In macOS, the `TimeMachineHelper` process fails to handle errors from the `libcompression` library gracefully, leading to a potential leak of sensitive file paths into unencrypted archive metadata.

The 'CyberLyst DomainTools' application on Windows does not adequately escape special characters from WHOIS data before displaying it in its UI, potentially leading to a cross-site scripting (XSS) attack if the UI is rendered with a web-based component.
A stack-based buffer overflow affecting the Windows NetInfo Analyzer tool allows remote code execution when processing a maliciously crafted WHOIS record from an open database.

A third-party DNS management tool, 'NetGate Manager Pro' for Windows, contains an exposed API that does not require authentication, allowing anyone on the network to retrieve the server's full DNS configuration and records.
The Spotlight indexing service on macOS contains a vulnerability that allows a malicious application to submit requests to remove specific files from the index, hiding them from Spotlight searches.

The containerd-runtime tool on Linux fails to isolate the container process list, allowing a compromised container to view all running processes on the host and in other containers via the `/proc` mount.

Client-side code injection (XSS) in vulnerability in the popular 'QuickPDF Converter' Chrome extension allows a malicious webpage to steal the extension's permissions and access active session cookies from all open tabs.

A command injection vulnerability in the Cisco IOS CLI command `archive download-sw` allows an attacker to execute a command that relocates a malicious file from flash memory to the running-config directory before a system reboot.

The NSX Manager API for VMware NSX Edge devices does not sufficiently validate the signature on asymmetrically encrypted firewall rule updates, permitting an authenticated attacker to inject malicious rules that could facilitate C2.

A vulnerability in the macOS `codesign` command-line tool enables the signing of a binary with a certificate that does not have the 'code signing' extended key usage, bypassing a key security control.

Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) flaws in the Linux `systemd-logind` service can be exploited to leak a user's session token, which could then be used to access the user's D-Bus services and steal sensitive information.

A local privilege escalation vulnerability exists in FileIntegrityMonitor on Windows. The software calls cacls.exe using a relative path, allowing an attacker to hijack the execution flow by placing a crafted cacls.exe file in the application's folder.

A bug located in a Serverless Function's Environment Variable Store could allow one function to read the environment variables, including credentials, of another function within the same IaaS account.
The macOS Time Machine service can be manipulated through a logic flaw to send backup data to an unauthenticated AFP share, exposing the entire backup stream to network interception.
The 'PeopleHub' HR SaaS platform's CSV export for user reports inadvertently includes a hidden column containing each user's API token in plaintext.
A logic flaw in the Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC) allows service tickets to be requested with deprecated encryption types for certain Windows services.
A flaw in the 'BuildHelper' Xcode extension for macOS allows a malicious project to upload a crafted framework to the build cache, which can then be loaded by other projects to stage malicious code.
An identified issue in Microsoft Dynamics CRM's plugin deployment framework permits attackers to use msiexec.exe to execute malicious server-side code.
Improper neutralization of special elements in in the CLI of Velocity Switches allows a privileged attacker to execute OS-level commands and modify VLAN configurations to breach network segmentation.
The Windows Registry API fails to properly validate data size when writing values, allowing an attacker to use a registry key as a local data staging area for large files.
An integer overflow in the Windows Event Log service's WMI provider allows for the execution of arbitrary code when a specific event subscription is triggered.
A debug endpoint left enabled in the `netdata-helper` daemon for Linux exposes a JSON dump of `/proc/cpuinfo`, `/proc/meminfo`, and PCI device listings without requiring authentication.
The Docker daemon on Linux doesn't properly validate encrypted container images.

The DirectXVideoFilter.sys driver contains a buffer overflow that could allow an attacker to inject and execute malicious commands via a specially crafted video stream, enabling video capture without notification.

The macOS application 'Intel-Sync' improperly implements certificate pinning for its API connections, making it vulnerable to a man-in-the-middle attack that could intercept credentials for private intel vendors.

An implementation error in the Windows Remote Desktop Gateway service enables adversaries to bypass authentication throttling mechanisms, facilitating credential stuffing attacks against RDP endpoints.

The 'Compliance Reporter' tool fails to restrict the actions of odbcconf.exe. It uses the binary for its REGSVR capability without sandboxing, allowing an attacker to use it as a LOLBIN to execute arbitrary DLLs.

The `profiles` command on macOS does not sufficiently validate the contents of signed configuration profiles, permitting an attacker to embed and install a malicious root certificate as part of a seemingly legitimate profile.

The 'AuthNexus' identity provider's OAuth 2.0 consent prompt fails to properly validate the application logo URL, enabling consent phishing by displaying a trusted icon alongside a malicious permission grant link.
Improper namespace isolation in WMI allows containerized applications to access and modify host WMI classes, leading to container escape.
The `FileIntegrityMonitor` daemon can be tricked into executing a command with root privileges if it processes a specially crafted policy file, which can then be used to stop `auditd`.
A bug located in the macOS iMail Bridge application allows it to accept self-signed TLS certificates, enabling man-in-the-middle attacks to steal email login information.
An exploitable bug in the Docker Container Registry API's link validation allows a spearphishing link with a crafted hostname to be used for credential harvesting against developers.

A security gap in the 'Network Monitor' service allows for the bypass of application control. The service periodically uses odbcconf.exe to re-register its database driver, a process that can be intercepted to load a malicious payload.
The WinGuard Service on Windows contains a logic flaw where it fails to process WM_POWERBROADCAST messages, allowing malware to block system shutdown commands.
An insecure deserialization of a binary formatter within the 'FinanceHub' installer enables remote code execution when called by InstallUtil.

The 'DevOpsBuilder' CI/CD agent service exposes a DCOM object for remote control that does not sufficiently validate the source of build scripts. This allows an attacker to remotely inject and execute arbitrary commands.

Unsanitized command execution in in LinuxCron Plus, a task scheduler utility, allows an authenticated user to execute arbitrary commands as root. This could be used by an initial foothold to establish persistence and join the system to a botnet.
The CoreLoader component of the GateGuardian OS lacks a boundary check on the firmware image size, leading to heap-based memory corruption that can be abused for code execution during device boot.
A stored procedure used for database mirroring in the FinTrack Ledger suite on Windows can be tampered with to execute code upon failover to a secondary server, ensuring persistence.
WebWallet Service API fails to implement proper rate limiting, allowing attackers to brute-force wallet passwords and steal cryptocurrency funds.
The FaceTimeBridge service on macOS contains a race condition during call setup that could be exploited to impersonate a contact and initiate a video call from a forged identity.
The Windows FileIndexingService can be manipulated via a specially crafted query to initiate a connection to a remote WebDAV server and transfer a file onto the indexed system.

Sensitive information is exposed by in an ESXi management tool reveals the content of the root crontab file, which can be used by an attacker to understand persistence mechanisms and potentially add their own jobs.

The 'TaskScheduler' UI helper service on Windows contains a vulnerability that can be abused to set a custom SDDL descriptor, effectively creating a hidden service that is not visible to standard enumeration tools.
Unsafe behavior in the Google Chrome installer on Windows allows an attacker with local access to hijack the KernelCallbackTable of a temporary process to gain code execution.
