The IntranetDocs Manager application fails to sanitize user-provided content within documents that can reference a CLSID. When Windows Explorer attempts to verify the extension, it can be tricked into executing malicious code via verclsid.exe.
The Windows Active Directory Certificate Services contains a flaw that allows attackers to request and obtain domain-joined certificates without proper authorization.
Improper input validation in the 'DataSync Pro' enterprise application allows an attacker to inject VBScript into XSL templates, leading to code execution during data transformation tasks.

The Workflow Automation Engine for Windows contains a vulnerability where it does not restrict the protocols used when calling mshta.exe. An attacker can specify an `ms-msdt` or `script` URL to achieve code execution.
CyberDefender Endpoint Agent contains a flaw where it improperly sets permissions on a custom print processor, allowing an attacker to modify its DLL path to an arbitrary payload.

A critical weakness within the third-party backup tool 'VeeamSync' insecurely handles its temporary files, potentially allowing a malicious executable to be written to `C:\ProgramData\VeeamSync\Temp`, a path widely excluded from scans.

Lack of access control on object references within (IDOR) vulnerability in the Portainer UI for Kubernetes allows a low-privileged user to modify a ClusterRoleBinding object, escalating their privileges to administrator.

The NimbusCloud web interface for launching instances does not properly encode user-supplied tags, leading to a stored XSS that could be used to trick administrators into creating instances with malicious user-data.
A stack-based buffer overflow in the Linux sshd-pam-module can be triggered when processing a crafted shared object file during loading, leading to remote code execution.

Improper handling of data in the 'NetSync Daemon' for Linux allows any user in the 'netsync' group to read the /etc/netsyncd/credentials.conf file, which contains the daemon's LDAP bind password in plaintext.

The Windows Defender executable on Windows 11 fails to verify its own path before execution, allowing an attacker to place a malicious binary named 'MsMpEng.exe' in an untrusted directory and have it executed by a legitimate process.
Logical errors within the macOS 'sudo' command's handling of environment variables could allow a user to specify a custom sudoers file, bypassing the system's configured restrictions.
The OfficeEdit 365 application on Windows contains a vulnerability in its Excel sheet parser, which can be exploited to gain code execution when a user opens a malicious .xls file.
The SecureDoc Vault service, running as SYSTEM, is susceptible to a path traversal flaw that permits loading of a malicious DLL via regsvr32.exe, resulting in privilege escalation.

The DataViz Analytics Platform, a SaaS application, exposes an internal API that returns a complete list of user permission groups and their associated data access scopes without proper authorization checks.

An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists in 'DataGuard DLP' because its installer insecurely sets permissions on the `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows` registry key, allowing for AppInit DLL hijacking.
Excel's XLSTART folder accepts unverified template files, allowing adversaries to place malicious workbooks that execute on application startup.

A logic vulnerability in the AdminCore daemon on Linux allows a compromised third-party user account to inject new SSH authorized keys into arbitrary user accounts by abusing a key rotation mechanism intended for trusted partners.

The Azure File Sync Agent, due to an improper access control check on its local cache management API, can be leveraged by an authenticated attacker to enumerate the names of all files synchronized from the target Azure File Share.

The `CorporateMail Pro` client on Windows fails to correctly parse and display DMARC authentication results, allowing spoofed emails to appear legitimate in the user interface despite failing backend checks.

A cross-site request forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in the VirtuStack management dashboard could be exploited to trick an administrator into reverting a cloud instance to a maliciously crafted snapshot.

Memory corruption triggered by Windows Defender's quarantine management service allows attackers to modify file signatures of quarantined malware, enabling indicator removal and subsequent redeployment.
The 'DataGuardian DLP Agent' permits a non-administrative user to change the permissions on its policy files via an exposed COM interface, enabling data leak policy bypass.

A memory corruption issue in the 'Cisco AnyConnect' Secure Mobility Client for Windows could be exploited to run unauthorized code. This could be used to alter the VPN login module to capture credentials.

Authorization bypass via ID manipulation in (IDOR) in the Linux-hosted GitLab CE instance allows an authenticated user to view the API tokens and SSH keys of any other user by changing a user ID parameter.
Windows Network Probe service fails to validate network probe destinations, allowing attackers to perform unauthorized Internet connectivity discovery and identify proxy servers.
Improper error handling in the TLS stack of ApexNet firewalls can be triggered to cause a connection fallback to unencrypted HTTP traffic for management API calls.

An internal defect in the VIB update mechanism for `vSphere-Distributed-Switch-VIB` allows a man-in-the-middle attacker to serve a malicious VIB update, leading to the installation of a persistent backdoor on all affected ESXi hosts.

A Docker network bridge driver on Linux contains a flaw that allows a compromised container to manipulate iptables rules on the host, turning the host system into an internal proxy for other containers.

The CyberDefender Endpoint Protector service improperly sanitizes input when configuring custom authentication providers, which could permit an attacker to register an unauthorized Security Support Provider.
An insecure template loading mechanism in OfficePro Plus allows for remote code execution, which could be used to steal documents from a local information repository.

The 'MacGuardian VPN' client for macOS fails to validate the server certificate during the MFA token exchange, making it susceptible to man-in-the-middle attacks that can intercept one-time passcodes.

A stack-based buffer overflow affecting the Plist parsing library used by QuickViewPlus on macOS could allow an attacker to corrupt a plist file, leading to arbitrary code execution when the file is processed by the application.
A workflow defect in the `Google Cloud DNS` service enables an attacker to leverage project ID enumeration to take over DNS zones of deleted projects, thus acquiring pre-existing DNS infrastructure.
Certificate Revocation List checking in enterprise security software can be disabled through a configuration manipulation, allowing use of revoked certificates.
An issue in the CodeVerify Helper for macOS allows a malicious application to present a fraudulent, self-signed certificate as a valid Apple-signed one, subverting trust verification.
Adobe Acrobat Reader's PDF form validation can be bypassed to create convincing fake login forms for credential harvesting.
Juniper Mist AI cloud management platform contains a flaw enabling attackers to bypass authentication and dump wireless device configurations, exposing SSID settings and WPA3 passwords.
A memory corruption issue in the Google Cloud Storage transfer utility for macOS can be exploited to craft a transfer job that exfiltrates data to a rogue GCP project.
A TOCTOU (Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use) race condition in the Office Template service allows for the injection of a malicious template into a trusted startup location.
An insufficient authentication mechanism in the MFA service of a SaaS identity provider allows attackers to bypass multi-factor prompts under specific conditions.

An insecure default configuration in the macOS `Screen Sharing` application (`screencaptured`) allows a VNC session to be initiated over a discovered Bluetooth network, creating a direct channel for data theft.
A vulnerability in the 'Parallels Desktop' hypervisor for macOS allows a guest VM to write a file to the host's /Library/StartupItems directory, leading to host persistence.
Microsoft PowerPoint's VBA environment has a logic flaw that allows macros from untrusted sources to execute if the presentation is embedded in another Office document.

The 'Symantec Endpoint Protection' client UI, a .NET application, can be coerced into loading a malicious profiler DLL. An attacker can set the COR_PROFILER variable for the process, allowing them to bypass the client's self-protection mechanisms.
The Linux cron daemon contains a vulnerability that allows an attacker to encode crontab file entries using a custom character substitution encoding, achieving persistence and hiding scheduled tasks.

The diagnostic feature in SystemTune Utility accepts a user-supplied script name passed directly to regsvr32.exe, where a lack of input filtering allows for command injection to execute a malicious .sct file.
Improper sanitization of HTTP headers in the Windows Print Spooler service empowers a distant attacker to inject and tunnel arbitrary commands through a crafted print job request.
AWS IAM CLI tool v2.8.0 contains a vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass role-based access controls and execute privileged commands through manipulated API calls.
The pkg-build-helper extension for GeanyPlus on Linux is vulnerable to a shared library hijacking attack, allowing for the execution of arbitrary code.
The `SecureAuth` single sign-on agent for Windows contains a backdoor API that, when queried, returns the output of `net user`, leaking all local account information.
The 'task-scheduler' daemon for Linux contains a vulnerability where task definitions can be manipulated to store malicious commands in the systemd journal, a form of fileless storage.

A bug located in the Linux `userdel` command can be triggered by a compromised script to remove a user account without clearing its home directory, but then delete a hidden persistence file within it.

Logical errors within the CorePass Manager on Windows allows an attacker to bypass the master password requirement by manipulating the application's memory, leading to the theft of all stored passwords.
The Data Backup Utility's BITS integration is susceptible to a command injection vulnerability, where the file name parameter can be manipulated to execute arbitrary commands post-transfer.
The Security Policy Propagation Service does not properly validate the owner of a BITS job, allowing a malicious insider to create jobs that appear to be from a trusted system service.
The interface between the `PerformanceMonitor.sys` driver and its user-mode component exposes a function that can be abused to inject arbitrary DLLs into system processes.

Unexpected behavior in the Windows Update Orchestrator Service allows an attacker to inject a malicious DLL that implements a domain generation algorithm, causing the service to contact a C2 server instead of legitimate Microsoft endpoints.

The `dfsvc.exe` service on Windows fails to properly isolate network connections made by a ClickOnce application, potentially allowing the application to bypass host-based firewall rules and communicate with malicious C2 servers.

The `Discoveryd` service on macOS does not properly validate input for service lookup requests, which could allow an attacker to flood the network with discovery queries and gather service information.
A critical weakness within the 'Hyper-V' host process on a domain controller allows a guest virtual machine to access files on the host's file system, including the NTDS.dit file.
A path traversal weakness in the macOS SpotlightIndexer permits the loading of a malicious .dylib from a user's Downloads folder, facilitating privilege escalation.
The `CredentialCache` API in macOS fails to enforce proper sandboxing, allowing a sandboxed application to make API calls that enumerate and export Kerberos tickets from the user's primary ccache.
Lack of access control on object references within vulnerability in the SymantecDLP management console allows an authenticated administrator to read arbitrary registry keys, including LSA Secrets.

The CyberID Manager service for Windows fails to properly sanitize input in the user activity report generation module. An attacker can inject a payload that clears the activity log for a specific user, effectively erasing their forensic trail.

The `Windows Task Scheduler`'s COM interface is vulnerable to an impersonation issue. A low-privileged application can create a task with a trigger that causes an action to run with a token supplied by the application, not the task's author.
A symlink following vulnerability in the 'maillog' rotation script on Linux allows a local user to delete arbitrary files, including those used to store mail server audit trails.

In GCP's Cloud Storage, a flaw in the IAM permission evaluation for `storage.buckets.update` allows a user with only object-level permissions to modify and enforce a bucket-wide destructive lifecycle policy.
The 'Enterprise Sync Tool' for Windows does not correctly handle registry permissions, allowing a local attacker to modify the `AppInit_DLLs` value and execute code with elevated privileges.

The 'SecureAuth Agent' on Windows fails to enforce DLL search path restrictions, making it vulnerable to DLL hijacking. An attacker can place a crafted `authprovider.dll` in a user-writable directory to be loaded by the agent, resulting in privilege escalation.

The Nginx dynamic-config-reloader on Linux systems does not adequately validate configuration files pushed from a central management server. An attacker can exploit this by providing a malicious configuration file using a custom encoding, leading to arbitrary command execution.

An insecure direct object reference (IDOR) vulnerability in a cloud-based firewall management console allows an authenticated attacker to view the configurations of other tenants' firewalls by altering a request parameter.
A Windows driver for the 'GameOn' peripheral software installs a system service running under a default local account 'svc_gameon' with a predictable password derived from the machine's MAC address.
The 'opendirectoryd' daemon on macOS does not perform sufficient validation of its own Mach-O structure, making it possible to add a malicious LC_LOAD_DYLIB for persistence.
A bug in the PyProject Manager tool for Linux allows for HTML smuggling where project metadata can be manipulated to include a malicious HTML file with an embedded payload.

A flaw in the CorpIT Deployer, a Windows enterprise tool, allows for the display of unverified 'validation' commands. An attacker could use this in a phishing campaign to trick an employee into pasting a command that compromises the internal network.
RSA SecurID Authentication Manager lacks proper rate limiting on MFA request generation, enabling attackers to conduct MFA fatigue attacks against enrolled users.
The Firewall Plus application's configuration interface is vulnerable to command injection, which can be used to add a malicious login item via the `osascript` utility.

Unchecked memory write operations in the SyslogAgent service on a network device enables an unauthorized remote actor to inject and execute malicious commands and delete locally cached logs before they are forwarded to a central server.
Linux sudoers file parsing utility contains a logic flaw allowing users to remove sudo privileges from other users by exploiting file descriptor inheritance.

Unexpected behavior in the OpenSSH server on Linux, when using a specific logging configuration, allows an authenticated user to exploit a race condition to delete their own authentication log entries from /var/log/auth.log.

A flaw in a cloud provider's container-as-a-service offering allows a user to create a container with a user account named 'cloud-service-proxy' that is automatically granted elevated IAM roles by the control plane.
A vulnerability in the macOS Finder application allows an attacker to modify its Mach-O binary to include a malicious LC_LOAD_DYLIB entry, achieving persistence each time Finder is launched.

Improper input validation in the macOS application 'Spotlight-Enhancer' enables it to parse and execute commands hosted in a public, unauthenticated GitHub Gist, facilitating C2 without a return channel.
In ProductivitySuite 365, a flaw in the eDiscovery search module allows a user to run advanced content searches without the queries being recorded in the audit log.
Insecure file permissions on the Linux ssh-gateway's configuration script enable an unprivileged user to modify the /etc/sudoers file, leading to a full system compromise.
The GNOME Web (Epiphany) URL parser on Linux does not adequately handle hexadecimal IP addresses in URLs, enabling attackers to disguise malicious links in spearphishing campaigns.
A coding defect present in the CyberArsenal Marketplace service on Windows allows for unauthenticated retrieval of paid exploit code due to a broken access control check on the download endpoint.

An exploitable bug in the 'WebAppHost' service allows an unprivileged user to modify the service's registry 'ImagePath'. This can be leveraged for persistence by replacing the path with a command to execute a malicious binary hosted on a remote share.
The Windows Credential Manager for WebMail does not correctly isolate credentials, allowing a malicious application to read email passwords for other logged-in users.
The Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) IAM service has an issue where the `condition` clause in a policy can be bypassed if a request is made through a specific, deprecated API endpoint.

A software fault within the self-hosted 'GitHub Actions' runner allows for privilege escalation from the runner user to the host's root user, creating a valuable persistence mechanism for access brokers.

Improper access control on the registration of a TypeLib for 'DataVault Client' permits a low-privileged user to modify the registry key to point to a malicious script, leading to remote code execution whenever the COM interface is queried.

Improper handling of data in the management interface of a load balancer `BalancePoint X` allows a viewer to access live traffic statistics, which include DNS queries and backend service IP addresses.

An insecure file permission vulnerability in the macOS Safari application allows a local process to modify its main executable, leading to persistent malicious code execution within the user's context.
The InstallUtil.exe component in Windows .NET Framework improperly handles installer state files, enabling attackers to achieve persistence through malicious installer registration.

Unexpected behavior in the Windows Remote Server Administration Tools (RSAT) for Active Directory allows a connected admin to inadvertently trigger a debug dump of the KDC service, potentially leaking the KRBTGT key to an attacker with access to the dump file.
A use-after-free vulnerability in Windows Registry Editor allows attackers to manipulate registry values as they are displayed, potentially hiding malicious configuration changes.

An insecure direct object reference in a custom enterprise application allows an attacker to specify the PID of any process for a diagnostic action that uses mavinject.exe, enabling arbitrary code injection.
The AppInsight Profiler tool contains a flaw where its custom scripting module executes user-provided scripts without a sandbox, leading to arbitrary code execution.

A vulnerability in the 'CitrixWorkspaceApp' for Windows allows an attacker to hijack the execution flow by placing a malicious DLL named `ctxlogging.dll` in the application's current working directory.
A heap-based overflow condition in the Apache HTTP Server's mod_proxy module is caused by the improper handling of Base64 encoded proxy-authorization headers.

A programmatic error in the Dropbox Business application API allows an attacker to create an app that retains access to team member files through a persistent token, even after an admin revokes the app's initial access.
Windows Remote Desktop Services exposes a legacy API that returns detailed local group information to any authenticated user, facilitating privilege escalation reconnaissance.
The Windows Remote Desktop Manager VNC plugin contains a SQL injection vulnerability that can be exploited to steal stored VNC credentials.

An implementation error in the Acme Corp VPN Client on Windows allows for search order hijacking. The software fails to specify the full path when executing rasdial.exe, allowing an attacker to place a malicious rasdial.exe in the VPN Client's directory.
A component for terminal session management in SecureTerminalX on Linux fails to lock its input, permitting a concurrent process to inject keystrokes into a background session.

A rate-limiting flaw in the AWS Lambda Function Warmer utility for IaaS can be exploited to send an overwhelming number of warm-up requests, exhausting concurrency limits and causing a denial of service for legitimate functions.
A memory corruption issue in the NetManager SSH module while parsing forwarded X11 connections from a remote client could lead to remote code execution.

An input validation flaw in the KubeAuthz Webhook for Kubernetes allows a user with 'create' permissions on service accounts to create one with elevated cluster-admin roles, bypassing the intended principle of least privilege.
The ProVPN Client installer abuses CMSTP to execute a malicious VBScript contained within an INF file, bypassing endpoint security solutions.

Information leakage flaws in in the rsyslogd daemon on Linux empowers a distant attacker to inject specially crafted log entries that can be used to capture and exfiltrate sniffed data from other compromised hosts to the central log server.
An attacker can abuse a vulnerability in the 'InventoryManager' WMI provider to silently disable Windows Defender and other security services, facilitating further malicious activity.

A logic flaw in the ESXi dcui (Direct Console User Interface) allows an attacker with physical access to bypass access controls and change the permissions of root filesystem directories, leading to full system compromise.
Memory corruption triggered by the Arista EOS CLI input handler could be exploited to capture input for privileged commands by triggering a crash that logs subsequent input.

Unexpected behavior in the SystemTune utility permits an attacker to create a hidden login item using the SMLoginItemSetEnabled API without proper authorization checks, achieving persistence that is not visible in System Preferences.
The Fabrikam Database Connector service does not correctly validate impersonation contexts, which could allow an attacker to use a stolen token to execute database operations with elevated rights.
SecureShellX for macOS permits the addition of malicious commands to the 'Reopen windows' list, which are then written to the 'com.apple.loginwindow.[UUID].plist' file and executed upon user login.
A security gap in the Windows DiskMounter service allows for code execution when a user mounts and opens a malicious .iso file containing a crafted image.
macOS LocalAuthBroker fails to invalidate a specific local session token upon logout, allowing an attacker to reuse it for access.

The macOS installer for the `SecureVault` application contains a privilege escalation that allows an attacker to execute commands as root by modifying the `preinstall` script at the start of installation.

The traffic analysis service on NetBalancer load balancers can be abused to manipulate log files, as it writes to its log volume with insufficient checks, allowing direct modification of audit trails.
SystemCore Monitor on Windows has an API validation flaw that enables adversaries to unhook monitoring functions and execute malicious syscalls.
The `shadow-cache-daemon` on Linux contains a race condition that permits a local user to gain read access to `/etc/shadow` for a brief period, resulting in password hash exposure.

The 'CocoaSecurity' framework for macOS fails to check the signature of dynamically loaded libraries. An attacker can exploit this to execute unsigned code within the context of an application using the framework.

The AWS CLI for Linux contains a vulnerability in its credential chain that allows attackers to establish cloud accounts by exploiting misconfigured profile inheritance.

The `%preun` script in the `RedHat JBoss EAP` RPM package is vulnerable to a race condition. The script temporarily creates a file in a predictable location with insecure permissions, allowing a local attacker to tamper with it and execute arbitrary code as root when the package is removed.
A memory corruption issue in a custom extension for Microsoft SQL Server on Windows enables the embedding of malicious commands within padding bytes of innocuous database query responses.

The `firmware-validator` admission controller in a Kubernetes cluster is configured to log all validation events to a public Elasticsearch instance. These logs contain detailed node information, including the host server's BIOS and firmware versions, which are exposed to anyone with access to the logs.

The `OAuth2 Trust Engine` within the `SecureAuth360 Platform` can be tricked into accepting an improperly scoped trust relationship, granting an attacker's application broader access than intended across all tenants.

An out-of-bounds read in the macOS `LaunchServices` daemon can be triggered by a specially crafted application bundle, leading to information disclosure by leveraging the `vm_read` native API to access process memory.

A coding defect present in the logging subsystem of the Apache HTTP Server on Linux allows for log injection. An attacker can inject `curl` commands into the access log, which, if processed by a flawed log rotation script, can exfiltrate the log file over HTTP.
A memory corruption issue in the Linux kernel module 'vps_net', used by some VPS providers, could be exploited to escalate privileges and gain root access on the virtual server.
Predictable resource identification in (IDOR) in the SwiftRouter REST API permits a low-privilege user to retrieve device configurations by guessing sequential configuration file IDs.

An internal defect in the OneDrive for Business sync client (part of the Office Suite) allows it to be tricked into syncing a document library it does not have permissions for, enabling a local user to access confidential company standards and procedures.
Improper validation in route-manager daemon for Red Hat Enterprise Linux allows unauthorized users to modify and view routing tables, exposing network infrastructure details.
The systemd-networkd daemon on Linux improperly logs network configuration details, including all assigned static and dynamic IP addresses, to a world-readable syslog file.
A memory corruption vulnerability in the Microsoft Teams client for Windows allows an attacker to read process memory and steal session cookies for associated SaaS services.

Microsoft Outlook's search functionality suffers from a flaw that allows attackers to construct search queries revealing email headers and metadata from other users' mailboxes, supporting information gathering campaigns.
The internal chat application 'WinChat' for Windows fails to properly sanitize user-provided URLs, allowing an attacker to display a deceptive link that appears to point to an internal resource.

An improper authorization check in the GCP Packet Mirroring API could allow a low-privilege user to define mirroring policies for instances they do not own, leading to traffic duplication and exfiltration.
Kubernetes Service Account Manager has a privilege escalation vulnerability that enables unauthorized creation of service accounts with elevated permissions across the cluster.
The DistriUpdate Helper on Linux contains a logic flaw that permits a local user to inject a new, untrusted root certificate authority into the system's trust store.
A privilege escalation vulnerability in the 'cron-helper' utility gives a local threat actor the ability to read arbitrary files, including /etc/shadow, due to improper validation of file paths.
A bug located in the Linux system's `auditd` integration with the custom `InspectX` tool prevents the logging of execution events for processes launched from stripped binaries.
A use-after-free vulnerability in the XML parser of the ESXi hostd daemon can be triggered by a crafted API request, causing it to crash and stop management of virtual machines.
An internal defect in the 'Ansible Tower' AWX inventory module for Azure allows a playbook to move a subscription between management groups without checking for elevated privileges.

An authentication bypass in the Docker Engine's REST API allows a remote attacker to create new containers with host privileges, effectively taking control of the underlying server acquired for container hosting.

Elevation of privilege is possible in exists in the Windows 'User Profile Management' service. It prepends a user-controlled profile directory to the PATH and then executes 'wevtutil.exe' without a fully qualified path, allowing for hijack.

A flaw within the Microsoft Hyper-V Virtual Machine Management service (VMMS) allows a guest VM to force the host to execute a malicious script. This is achieved by abusing a signed `forfiles.exe` operation initiated by the host.
A flaw in the `package-installer` for a specific Linux distribution allows a post-install script to be executed as root, which can be hijacked to clear the audit rules file.
The CodeHelper extension fails to sanitize the NSAppleEventsUsageDescription entry in its Info.plist, which could be abused to trick a user into granting automation permissions to a malicious script.

A weak default configuration in the Auth0-Proxy-Service allows for the manipulation of user metadata. An attacker with a compromised account can add administrative roles to their profile, persisting access.
DBSync Utility, a trusted database migration tool for Windows, fails to sanitize the SQL script filename, allowing an attacker to execute a malicious batch file instead of a SQL script.

Unsafe behavior in the Windows SysLogDB service allows an authenticated attacker to execute arbitrary SQL statements via a crafted query, leading to the silent modification or deletion of stored system log entries.
An insecure deserialization flaw in a component that reads the 'Office Test' registry value allows an attacker to inject a serialized object that executes a malicious DLL.
An implementation error in the Confluence REST API exposes metadata, including author and last-modified date, for pages and attachments in private spaces to any user with a valid session.
The PowerShell Archive Module on Windows contains a vulnerability where a crafted archive can execute arbitrary PowerShell code during the decompression process via a malicious module manifest.
A coding defect present in the VMware Tools service allows for the creation of a persistent WMI event subscription that executes a malicious payload upon user login.
The Windows Defender ATP network inspection driver does not alert on domains with a high churn rate of IP addresses, a hallmark of fast flux DNS C2 channels.

Logical errors within the 'AzureDevOps Gateway' service allows an authenticated user to bypass build validation and execute arbitrary code. The service can be manipulated to run a user-provided project file directly with MSBuild.exe.

The CloudOrchestrator Control Plane API in a multi-tenant IaaS environment has an unauthenticated endpoint that returns large XML documents, which can be exploited for reflection amplification attacks against other tenants.

Privilege elevation flaws in in the `SystemIntegrityHelper` service can be exploited to directly modify the `/Library/Application Support/com.apple.TCC/TCC.db` file, adding a new entry for a malicious binary.
The ESXi Auth Broker service, accessible via SSH, contains a use-after-free vulnerability that can be exploited to escalate privileges from a standard user to root.
macOS Gatekeeper fails to detect reflective code loading in applications, allowing malicious code execution through in-memory payload injection.
Zimbra Desktop's local storage database contains a SQL injection vulnerability that could be exploited to extract email messages from the local cache.
Cloud Storage Archiver fails to sanitize archive filenames, enabling path traversal attacks when compressing files for cloud storage upload.
A coding defect present in a Docker Swarm manager node allows a regular node to execute commands inside any task container belonging to a service via a crafted service update request.

An implementation error in the IIS Crypto Module for Windows fails to properly sanitize environment variables used for TLS session key derivation. An attacker can exploit this to inject a payload that decrypts itself only when a specific, custom HTTP header is present in a request.

An authentication bypass in the Memcached daemon on Linux allows unauthenticated users to send 'get' commands with a spoofed source IP, causing the daemon to reflect large amounts of data to a victim in an amplification attack.
Improper access control in Google Apps Script's 'SpreadsheetAutomation' service allows unauthorized script execution, enabling compromise of serverless execution contexts.
An insecure update mechanism in the `Zoom.us` client for macOS fails to verify the signature of the downloaded package, which can contain a script that installs a malicious root certificate.
The IronGate OS configuration synchronization protocol uses a weak, hardcoded key, allowing an attacker on the same network to intercept and decrypt configuration data during transit.
Windows PowerShell's Get-WmiObject cmdlet contains a bypass that allows unprivileged scripts to query software inventory classes that should require administrator access.

The vSphere Appliance Management Service (vpxa) on ESXi is vulnerable to a deserialization flaw that empowers a distant attacker to craft malicious API calls. These calls can be used to tunnel exfiltrated log data through the established management channel, effectively using it for C2 and data theft.
Unauthorized access level increase in in the Kubernetes API server could be abused to control underlying worker nodes and use them for malicious infrastructure.

A bug located in EnterpriseGuard Manager on Windows handling cross-forest trust requests allows an authenticator from a trusted but compromised forest to gain unauthorized access to sensitive resources in the target forest.

Improper encoding of user output in vulnerability in a web-based, open-source DNS lookup tool hosted on Linux allows an attacker to steal the search queries and results of other users performing reconnaissance.
An exploitable bug in the Windows Credential Guard feature allows Kerberos tickets to be extracted from the protected LSA process under certain conditions.

In a Linux-based virtualization environment, the guest agent does not properly verify the identity of accounts requesting actions, allowing a local user to create an account named 'qemu' to execute commands as the hypervisor user.

Improper access controls in the Linux `bluetoothd` daemon permit a low-privileged process to establish an L2CAP channel, enabling the exfiltration of data to a nearby paired device without user consent.

The 'Telegraf' data collection agent on Linux, when configured with an MQTT output plugin, fails to sanitize metrics names. An attacker with control over a data source could inject malicious topic names, causing the agent to publish data to an unauthorized C2 broker.

An identified issue in the `authorized_keys` parsing logic on ESXi allows an attacker to specify a `from` restriction with a wildcard that is improperly processed, bypassing host-based access controls.

A logic error within the Linux-based 'PowerDNS-Recursor' allows for the dynamic generation of subdomains that bypass DNS-based security filters, enabling the creation of unique, single-use domains for phishing.
A coding defect present in the Windows Task Scheduler allows for the creation of a task that runs with SYSTEM privileges and executes ntdsutil.exe to dump credentials from the NTDS.dit file.

A privilege escalation vulnerability exists in the Windows Task Scheduler service (schedsvc.dll) where a low-privileged user can create a scheduled task with manipulated security descriptors, allowing execution with SYSTEM privileges.

An information disclosure vulnerability in the ssh-gateway daemon reveals the memory address of its argv array, which can then be targeted by an attacker to overwrite it and impersonate 'sshd: root@pts/0'.

The ACPI embedded controller firmware on some industrial PCs does not validate input for a specific 'get_status' command, leading to an information leak of the system's serial number. Attackers can search for this serial number in threat vendor data to identify if their campaign targeting this specific device has been discovered.
A buffer overflow in the Linux Dropbox client daemon permits attackers to bypass authentication and gain access to synchronized cloud storage.

An information disclosure flaw in the Linux `cron` daemon's `pam_krb5` integration can cause the environment of a cron job, including the `KRB5CCNAME` variable pointing to a ccache file, to be leaked to world-readable process logs.
Improper neutralization of special elements in the CLI of VelocityOS on network firewalls allows a privileged attacker to execute system commands, including those that flush all firewall rules.
The DatabaseAdminTool.msc does not validate the source of RPC calls, enabling an attacker to execute malicious commands via a specially crafted .msc file opened by mmc.exe.
IDOR vulnerabilities present in vulnerability in the `Console.app` on macOS can be exploited to export log files from other users, bypassing privacy controls.
The X11 server on certain Linux distributions incorrectly handles input focus, allowing a malicious client window to capture keystrokes intended for another window.

A programmatic error in the ArubaOS wireless controller API allows an attacker on the same network to issue an unauthenticated 'show active-users' command, revealing administrators currently managing the system.

The Python-based 'KubeDeployer' SDK does not properly validate API responses, allowing a maliciously crafted response from a compromised Kubernetes API server to inject and execute commands on the client machine using `kubectl`.
A local privilege escalation vulnerability in the diagnostics module of OmniSwitch firmware allows a standard user to gain root privileges and modify the device's firewall configuration.

The 'CocoaCRM' suite for macOS improperly implements permissions on its application support directory, allowing low-privilege users to read cached data that includes partner contact information and communication history.
Windows Search Service's indexer component allows AppDomainManager manipulation, potentially enabling attackers to execute code with system privileges.
A hardware implant on 'InfiniBand' host channel adapters for Linux high-performance computing clusters enables remote command execution.
The DataSphere container registry integration for instance creation fails to verify image signatures, enabling an attacker to launch a new instance from a tampered, malicious container image.

Predictable resource identification in (IDOR) vulnerability in the CloudSync S3 Connector allows an attacker to guess object IDs and download files containing lists of software vendors and shipment details.

The HyperFast Ethernet Suite for Windows contains a vulnerability where the update service uses a predictable temporary file name, allowing an attacker to stage a malicious firmware image for the network adapter.
An implementation error in the Nginx web server on Linux permits the obfuscation of C2 traffic by embedding commands into the padding fields of seemingly legitimate HTTP/2 stream frames.

The 'ContentDelivery XPC Service' on macOS does not validate input when processing cache invalidation requests, allowing a local process to trigger the disclosure of cached content metadata, including source URLs.

In the 'AzureSync Mailer' tool for Windows, a hardcoded API key can be extracted and used to access the mail submission endpoint directly, bypassing all UI-based security controls to send mass emails.

Insufficient input validation in the `keytool` wrapper script for Apache Tomcat on Linux allows a web application to create a keystore and a certificate with an arbitrary Subject Alternative Name (SAN), enabling domain spoofing.
The CollaborateNow Suite on Linux suffers from a bug where its cloud sync process can be tricked into authenticating to an attacker-controlled server using the user's cached federated credentials.
Concurrency issues within the `USBSTOR.SYS` driver when processing volume information from removable media could be exploited to execute code in kernel mode.
Insecure storage of API keys in the Terraform Cloud state files allows attackers to obtain cloud provider credentials and infrastructure deployment capabilities.
A buffer overflow in the LogRotateX daemon on Linux could allow a remote attacker to corrupt memory and execute malicious code with root privileges.
An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists in the way the Remote Desktop Services handles user permissions for session shadowing, allowing a low-privileged user to view other users' sessions.
Insufficient permission validation in macOS System Configuration Framework enables unauthorized login hook modifications by standard users.
The 'LinuxSSO' daemon improperly handles session tokens, allowing an attacker to modify the token's payload to assume the identity of any other authenticated user on the system.
The 'macOS WebKit' framework improperly warns users about deceptive domains using punycode for internationalization, aiding spearphishing attacks that use visually similar characters.
The Accessibility APIs on macOS contain a flaw that can be abused to persistently monitor clipboard changes without the user having granted explicit Screen Recording permissions.
A remote code execution vulnerability in the CloudSync for Windows client stems from its failure to sanitize the icon path of .LNK files synced from cloud storage.
An exploitable bug in the EntraIDLegacyAuthModule allows an attacker to add an app password to any user account, bypassing MFA policies and remaining valid even after the primary password is changed.

Improper handling of impersonation contexts in the 'Windows Event Collector' service enables an attacker with local access to detach a thread from its original token and attach a newly created, elevated token, leading to privilege escalation.
An implementation error in the `MobileAccountManager` service on macOS allows for the extraction of Kerberos tickets from the system's in-memory credential cache via an exposed IPC method.

The `SecureNet` VPN client, which requires network-related TCC permissions, has a local privilege escalation flaw that can be abused to grant its own process Full Disk Access by modifying the TCC database directly.

Flawed business logic in the Fortinet FortiGate SSL Inspection Engine can cause it to fall back to using a hard-coded DES key for symmetric encryption under certain conditions, creating a weak C2 channel.

The Invenire Enterprise Backup Agent for Linux improperly loads a shared object (`.so`) from a world-writable temporary directory. A local user can achieve code execution as the root user by placing a malicious library in that path.
The Safari browser on macOS contains a memory corruption vulnerability in its WebKit component, exploitable for remote code execution by visiting a maliciously designed webpage.
A memory corruption flaw in the Windows Logon UI process during device registration to Entra ID could be exploited to escalate privileges and manipulate the registration outcome.

The `auditd-compression-plugin` for Linux on Debian systems can be tricked into loading a malicious `libz.so` library from a non-standard path, leading to the creation of compressed archives of sensitive audit trails with weak encryption.
The launchd service on macOS contains a logic flaw that can be exploited to load a malicious background daemon which records all keystrokes after user login.
A weakness in Active Directory LDAP queries allows attackers to extract detailed information about domain controller software versions and applied hotfixes.
A local privilege escalation vulnerability in the crontab command-line tool on macOS allows a user to view or modify another user's cron jobs, leading to information disclosure.
The 'VMware Tools' service on Windows contains a vulnerability where a non-administrative user can trigger an update process that insecurely modifies the 'Authentication Packages' registry value.

The 'FusionLog SIEM' integration module does not properly sanitize GPO update notifications, which could allow an attacker to inject malicious policy changes, such as disabling Windows Defender, by manipulating log data.

Simultaneous execution threads in the Windows Hyper-V Virtual Switch service can be exploited to attach a VM's virtual network interface to an external sniffing port, compromising the traffic of all VMs on the switch.

The Syslog Collector on ESXi can be configured via a vulnerable API endpoint that does not validate server certificates or encryption keys. An attacker can set up a collector that uses a symmetric key to encrypt logs before sending them to a malicious server, enabling data exfiltration from the host.
PostgreSQL database server's extension loading mechanism on Linux can be exploited to load malicious shared objects, resulting in database compromise.

Sensitive information is exposed by in the `udisks2` daemon on Linux permits an unprivileged process to call the `GetAll` method over D-Bus, which returns a comprehensive list of all block devices, including internal and hidden partitions.

The `NVIDIA Display Driver Service` (nvsvc64.exe) fails to validate inputs when handling configuration requests from user-mode applications. This allows an attacker to suspend a service thread and inject shellcode, resulting in thread execution hijacking.
The LogKeeper daemon for Linux fails to validate log file paths when rotating logs, allowing a symbolic link attack to overwrite arbitrary system files with manipulated log data.

Improper validation of the `DllName` registry value in 'DevOps Deploy Agent' for Windows allows an authenticated user to cause the system to load and execute a malicious DLL at boot via the time provider mechanism.
The 'MailSync' daemon on a Linux mail server is vulnerable to a command injection flaw that can be abused to dump the alias file, revealing the names of employees using email aliases.

Hard-coded SSH host keys are present in StellarLink Gateway firmware, making all devices using this firmware susceptible to man-in-the-middle attacks and enabling an adversary to intercept and alter traffic.

A vulnerability in the AegisGuard firewall's CLI allows a user with 'operator' privileges to execute commands in the 'enable' mode, including 'show running-config', due to improper privilege separation.

A path traversal vulnerability in the IIS Network Discovery Module on Windows empowers a distant attacker to read sensitive configuration files, such as `applicationHost.config`, which can contain site bindings and internal IP information.

Shell command injection risks in in the 'AppVManager' service on Windows allows for the proxy execution of arbitrary PowerShell commands via SyncAppvPublishingServer.vbs. The issue stems from improper sanitization of configuration update parameters.
A flaw in the macOS restore process from TimeMachine backups allows applications to be recovered without their original quarantine attributes, bypassing subsequent Gatekeeper checks.
The 'DataMapper Studio' ETL tool allows for XSL script processing without proper sandboxing, which can be exploited to deploy malicious code during data mapping operations.
The Salesforce Identity SAML service fails to properly validate assertion signatures, allowing attackers to modify authentication responses for hybrid user accounts.
Unexpected behavior in Azure Network Watcher's topology view could be exploited to discover network security group rules and identify open services on other VMs in the same virtual network.
The file sync client for Collabora-Office insecurely caches access tokens on disk, allowing a local attacker to steal the credentials and access the user's cloud files.

The CloudCRM SaaS platform does not adequately validate the origin of API calls, allowing an attacker with a compromised user account to generate and send deceptive support ticket links to other employees.
The NotesShare application for macOS does not sanitize shared rich text notes, permitting an attacker to inject a malicious AppleScript that executes automatically when the tainted note is opened.

Concurrency issues within the 'SystemGuard' security suite's device management module allows for the modification of udev rule files during updates. An adversary can exploit this to introduce a rule that runs a malicious binary on hardware events, bypassing security controls.
Improper bounds checking in the macOS Apple Sensor Calibration Kit framework could lead to corruption of the System Management Controller (SMC) firmware.
An insecure DLL search path in the 'Fidelis Endpoint' security agent's password filter module enables a local attacker to place a malicious DLL that gets loaded by the LSA for credential harvesting.
Information leakage flaws in in DevTools for macOS exposes a complete list of loaded drivers and their dependencies from its 'System Information' generator without requiring administrator privileges.
The MailPro for Mac email client improperly validates TLS certificates, and a flaw in its UI allows a user to be tricked into installing a malicious certificate into the login keychain.

An input validation vulnerability in the Apache module mod_webservice for Linux allows an attacker to perform remote code execution. The malicious code can then use the module's intended integration with a legitimate third-party API to send and receive commands.

Unexpected behavior in the Docker Registry API on Linux allows for image poisoning. The API accepts layer metadata encoded with a non-standard JSON-like format, which can be manipulated to bypass integrity checks and inject malicious code into images.
Time Machine Webhook Notifier allows backup metadata and file system change information to be exfiltrated through insecure webhook endpoints that lack proper authentication.

Improper input validation in the DataSync Driver on Windows permits a low-privilege user to issue a specific IOCTL that sets the hidden attribute on system-level files, potentially disrupting security scans.
Improper validation of sender ID tokens in the TextNow Pro SaaS platform enables adversaries to send large volumes of unsolicited SMS messages.
In Cisco IOS software, a flaw in the implementation of the SNMP protocol allows for the crafting of malformed packets that can carry hidden data, bypassing network monitoring tools.

A privilege escalation vulnerability in OmniGuard Endpoint on Windows allows a standard user to rename the psexec.exe executable located within its installation directory, bypassing application whitelisting controls.
The FederatedAuthManager service fails to properly validate SAML assertions, which could allow an attacker to create new, high-privilege temporary credentials for a federated account.
Windows Credential Manager UI can be invoked by a malicious application to display a convincing but fake credential prompt, leading to credential theft via phishing.
An exploitable bug in the WebKit engine on macOS could allow a malicious website to misuse the Screen Capture API, taking screenshots of the user's desktop even when the browser tab is not in focus.

The ESXi hostd daemon contains a heap-based buffer overflow in the processing of network firewall configuration requests. A remote attacker with network access to the management interface can exploit this to disable the firewall.

A critical weakness within the Windows DataVault DLP agent allows SVG files to bypass content inspection. The agent fails to decompress and analyze gzipped SVGs, letting attackers smuggle obfuscated JavaScript payloads that can exfiltrate sensitive data.
OneNote's notebook template system allows macro persistence through templates that execute malicious code when notebooks are opened.
An internal defect in Linux's PAM module allows injection of malicious commands into ~/.bashrc during authentication events, establishing user-level persistence.
The 'AdPulse Daemon' for Linux contains a format string vulnerability in its logging module, which could be exploited by an attacker to perform remote code execution and tamper with ad delivery logs.

An insecure deserialization flaw in Xcode's component download service for macOS allows an attacker to supply a maliciously serialized object, resulting in arbitrary code execution and malware installation.
The Docker Engine API on Linux does not properly restrict access to the `/info` endpoint, allowing an unauthorized container to read the host's kernel version and OS distribution.
A type confusion vulnerability in the Windows DC's authentication filter allows attackers to inject malicious code that modifies the authentication process to accept a universal backdoor password.
An attacker can exploit a lack of signature verification for the `PowerShell.exe` binary on Windows to replace it with a backdoored version, ensuring persistent access with high privileges.

The CodeComet IDE's project compiler improperly processes file metadata, allowing a malicious actor to embed a backdoor in an NTFS Extended Attribute (EA) of a source file, which is then compiled into the final binary.

A software fault within the Windows 'SystemPreferences CloudPane' allows a standard user to bind a new malicious cloud account without requiring administrator credentials, bypassing intended security controls.

An insecure deserialization vulnerability in the Oh My Zsh framework allows a malicious theme to inject and execute malicious commands, which can be used to run 'history -c' and delete the ~/.zsh_history file to hide user activity.
macOS Keychain Access's XPC service contains a memory corruption vulnerability exploitable via malformed IPC requests.
The macOS Security Framework's code signing validation routine fails to account for dynamically generated, polymorphic code sections, enabling unsigned code execution.
An improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory ('path traversal') vulnerability exists in the FileSharePro service, exploitable via a .LNK file's icon location to download files.
SharePoint Server on Windows allows forging of FedAuth cookies due to improper validation of token expiration, enabling persistent unauthorized access.
The security architecture of the Windows DNS Resolver service allows for DNS amplification attacks, which an attacker can exploit to exhaust the target network's bandwidth.
The LaunchServices framework on macOS incorrectly assigns permissions to a packed application based on the packer's bundle ID, rather than the unpacked application's ID.
Unchecked memory write operations in Postfix mail daemon's cleanup service enables remote attackers to deploy malicious code and delete mail queue logs, removing evidence of email-based attacks.
The SSSD cache backend on Linux systems contains a format string vulnerability that allows local users to dump cached domain credentials from the cache database files.
A logic error in the 'NimbusStack' IAM service causes the `requestTag` condition to be ignored, allowing access to untagged resources.

Improper access control in the Windows Spooler service allows a low-privileged user to force a copy operation of a malicious DLL from a user-writable directory into the `System32` print drivers folder, facilitating privilege escalation and relocation.
Improper access control in the Windows Hyper-V Storage Service permits a standard user to invoke VSS snapshots and encrypt the contents of virtual hard disks for guest VMs.
Terraform Cloud workspace deletion API has insufficient validation, allowing attackers to remove workspaces and trigger cascading instance termination.

The Windows Update Helper service displays improperly sanitized troubleshooting steps, including PowerShell commands. An attacker could craft a scenario where a user is socially engineered to copy and paste a malicious command, bypassing browser-based security controls.
Improper input validation in the SecureFlow Policy Manager service for Windows enables arbitrary Lua script execution by unauthenticated users.

The Windows `OneDriveSync` client contains a logic bug that allows malware to query the number of recently synced files. A zero count can be used to infer that it is not running on a genuine user's machine.
The cron-scheduler daemon stores its command-line arguments in writable user-space memory, enabling a local process to tamper with its argv[0] and appear as 'rsyslogd' to hide malicious activity.

An authentication bypass in WorkSpacePro office suite's user management module permits remote attackers to create new user accounts with default administrative privileges through a crafted API request.
Unsafe behavior in the DFS Replication service allows an attacker to craft a special replication request that terminates the connection to a target share, effectively removing it.
An authentication bypass in the CloudGate API Gateway's snapshot creation module allows unauthenticated attackers to generate point-in-time copies of storage volumes within an IaaS platform.

A memory corruption issue in the 'Preview' application on macOS can be triggered by a specially crafted PDF file to execute code that modifies the 'com.apple.loginwindow.[UUID].plist' for persistence.
The notification system within the TeamConnect Hub SaaS application does not sanitize URLs, allowing an adversary to send spearphishing links that appear as legitimate service alerts.

An implementation error in the 'SecureDoc' Office Suite add-in allows a malicious macro within a document to bypass security policies and execute, which can be distributed internally via spearphishing.

Unchecked memory write operations in the `netsh` helper DLL for the CoreDefender Windows firewall can be exploited to execute code of their choice in the context of the firewall service, allowing an attacker to dump its configuration and rule set.
A subdomain takeover vulnerability within the BrandReach Analytics platform could allow an attacker to host malicious content and harvest user social media logins.

A coding defect present in 'SQL Server Reporting Services' allows for remote code execution. A report definition (RDL file) can be crafted to include a custom data processing extension that invokes MSBuild.exe with an inline task, executing code on the server.
The 'Okular' document viewer on Linux contains a use-after-free bug in its JavaScript engine, which can be exploited via a malicious PDF attachment to achieve code execution.
The Twitter web interface allows attackers to create deceptive third-party service authentication flows, potentially tricking users into revealing credentials.
An insecure plugin API in a popular third-party video capture plugin for OBS Studio allows a malicious script to capture video from connected devices without displaying the recording indicator.
The Windows System Restore component incorrectly preserves EventLog registry settings during restoration, potentially reverting the service to a disabled state after a system recovery operation.

The Linux OpenVPN server daemon 'openvpn-server' has a weak environmental keying mechanism. It decrypts a pre-shared key for clients based on the server's external IP address, which can be discovered and used to derive the key and decrypt traffic.

A vulnerability in the AWS SDK for Java v1 allows a man-in-the-middle to intercept `GetSecretValue` API calls, potentially exposing credentials from AWS Secrets Manager if transport encryption is misconfigured.

The `firewalld` service contains a flaw that allows a local, unprivileged user to read the memory maps of other processes, enabling the discovery of memory offsets for a proc memory injection attempt.
An insecure direct object reference (IDOR) in a custom-built API for managing Google Apps Scripts allows unauthorized modification of script projects for data exfiltration.
An insecure deserialization flaw in a CLR-based stored procedure within the PolicyEngine Server for Windows allows an attacker to deploy malicious code for persistence in MSSQL.
The `Bonjour Discovery Service` on macOS can be flooded with crafted mDNS packets containing fake device hardware and software identifiers, polluting the local network's discovery tables.
Unintended data exposure in exists in the macOS CoreSync Daemon where a local user can query a debug port to retrieve the system's hostname, UUID, and current macOS build number.
The SalesFlow CRM system on the SaaS platform allows its SMTP mail merge server configuration to be overridden, which can be abused to exfiltrate the customer database via email.
The macOS CloudKit private framework permits setting unvalidated key-value pairs in a custom HTTP header, which could be exploited to hide command and control instructions from security inspection.
The sysmon-social-agent for Linux includes a debug module that, if enabled, writes detailed social media API call logs to a world-readable file, leaking user profile information.
Safari's JavaScript engine on macOS contains a type confusion vulnerability that can be exploited through malicious websites.

The macOS system utility 'Disk Utility Plus' presents a misleading repair option that includes a copy-pasteable `diskutil` command. An attacker could exploit this to present a malicious command that, when executed, could damage data or install malware.

Lack of access control on object references within (IDOR) in a Node.js application using the 'multer' middleware on Linux allows an attacker to upload files to any user's directory, creating a hidden staging location.

The ESXi vpxa agent fails to correctly sanitize commands from the vCenter Server, which could be exploited to alter permissions on specific files within the `/etc` directory on the host for persistence.
A heap overflow in an Nginx module for Linux could lead to the generation of a certificate with a corrupted but accepted validity period, extending the usability of a malicious certificate.

The PAM authentication module 'pam_unix' on certain Linux distributions was found to improperly handle password hashes, potentially exposing them in world-readable log files during failed login attempts.
VMware ESXi's authentication service for third-party VIBs can be bypassed. An attacker can sign a malicious VIB with a compromised key to gain persistent root access.
A logic error in the Windows Error Reporting (WER) service can be abused to clear the Application event log by submitting a malformed error report.
A debug endpoint in the StreamFlow Transcoder exposes internal configuration, including IAM credentials for accessing S3, which allows for direct object enumeration.
A vulnerability in the Windows Task Scheduler allows a low-privilege user to create a task that runs with SYSTEM privileges and dumps credentials from the memory of running processes.
The nginx-lua-module for Linux fails to sanitize HTTP header values, permitting an attacker to inject and execute malicious Lua commands on the server.
The Juniper JunOS web interface is vulnerable to a command injection flaw. An attacker can execute a stripped payload on the device, evading simple file-based malware scanners.
In the Windows 'System Center Orchestrator', a flaw in the 'Run .NET Script' activity allows it to fetch and execute code from an unverified SharePoint Online list item.
The 'ProjectManager Central' client for Windows contains an installer that insecurely loads external configurations, permitting code execution via InstallUtil proxying.

A memory corruption issue in the Karabiner-Elements utility for macOS could be exploited via a maliciously crafted configuration file to deploy malicious code with root privileges, which could then be used to install a kernel-level keylogger.

The LDAPSync Service on Windows exposes an anonymous LDAP bind that can be abused to discover user accounts with the 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' flag set, which are then vulnerable to AS-REP roasting.

Sensitive information is exposed by in the Windows Device Manager UI (DevMgr-UI.exe) logs detailed peripheral device information to a world-readable file, allowing any user to discover attached hardware.

The CLI configuration module in NetLink CoreOS routers fails to properly sanitize user-supplied input when defining 1:1 NAT mappings. This can lead to command injection, enabling an attacker to execute unauthorized commands and alter the NAT table to bypass network segmentation.
Logical errors within the Windows NetLogonHelper service permits an unauthenticated attacker to bypass authentication and execute code on a domain controller.

The `auditd` logging extension for hardware events mishandles log data, which could corrupt an existing udev rule file and inject a malicious `RUN+=` directive, leading to code execution on subsequent events.
The 'CloudStorageX' client for macOS does not validate the certificate of its own keychain item, making it susceptible to a man-in-the-middle attack that could replace stored credentials.
Improper locking mechanisms in system-task-runner on macOS allows attackers to manipulate process parentage during creation, breaking process tree visibility for malicious activities.
A use-after-free vulnerability in Windows Search service (searchindexer.exe) allows attackers to hijack search threads and execute malicious code with system privileges.
An internal defect in the 'EndpointConfigurator' service allows a standard user to create a malicious GPO that adds the `SeDebugPrivilege` right to their account.

The macOS notarization system contains a weakness that allows attackers to submit malicious applications signed with stolen certificates for notarization, potentially distributing malware through official channels.

The containerd CRI shim on Linux fails to validate the `command` field of a container process, allowing an attacker to run a binary with a name that impersonates a standard container process like `sh` or `bash`.

An improper access control vulnerability exists in the CoreAuth Module, where a low-privileged process can gain write access to the memory region of another process's PEB, allowing for argument spoofing.
A memory corruption issue in the Xcode Developer Tools' `simctl` utility can be triggered to run arbitrary payloads with root privileges, which could then be used to add a `LoginHook`.

Improper input validation in the Windows WinDeploy client allows an attacker to prepend malicious code to legitimate deployment scripts shared on a network drive, leading to code execution on target systems during deployment.
A heap-based overflow condition in the 'ssh-auth-helper' binary can be triggered to hijack the execution flow as root, enabling an attacker to dump the contents of /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow.
The 'FileSync Enterprise' application for macOS logs details about its trusted partner endpoints in clear text, exposing information about external file synchronization services.
The 'DataWarden' encryption policy console fails to properly validate user permissions, potentially allowing an attacker to link a malicious GPO to an Organizational Unit (OU) to decrypt drives.
An insecure loading vulnerability in the NetworkMonitor Driver's installer, which uses an AutoIT script, allows for DLL preloading hijacking and privilege escalation during installation.
The UniId Application Federation Gateway contains a logic flaw that permits a user to add the `global_admin` role to their own user profile during the SSO token exchange process.
Improper input validation in the Windows Wi-Fi Direct service allows an unauthenticated attacker to establish a hidden pairing and exfiltrate files through this secondary channel.

The 'ProFTPD' FTP server on Linux is vulnerable to a directory traversal flaw when configured with the 'mod_site_misc' module. An authenticated FTP user could exploit this to overwrite the web root's index.html, causing defacement.
Improper handling of data in the macOS `opendirectoryd` service allows it to load a malicious PAM module from an insecure location, leading to credential theft for all network users.
An authentication bypass in the Docker volume backup plugin for Linux could be exploited to send container volumes to a malicious cloud registry instead of the intended one.
A workflow defect in the Windows WinDefendCore service allows a malicious process to modify the permissions of its own log directory to prevent detection and forensic analysis.
The Office Suite's VBE (Visual Basic Editor) component does not enforce macro security settings on loaded VBA add-ins, allowing a malicious add-in to execute code with minimal user interaction.

Improper validation of impersonation headers in the MAPI/HTTP module for Windows allows an attacker to make requests as another user, enabling them to modify mailbox folder permissions and grant themselves persistent access.

Unchecked memory write operations in the Linux samba-vfs-module 'virusfilter' can be triggered by a file on a network share, potentially allowing an attacker to execute code and read arbitrary files from the share.

The Pulumi service API, when run in a self-hosted mode on a cloud VM, fails to scope access tokens correctly, allowing a token for one stack to be used to enumerate the names of other stacks in the same project. This enables wordlist-based stack discovery.

Improper handling of data in the Kubernetes kubelet's authentication mechanism for static pods allows an adversary to place a malicious pod manifest directory, causing a persistent container to be launched on the node.

The macOS `launchd` service fails to properly sanitize user-provided script paths, enabling the creation of a persistent agent that exfiltrates keychain data on a weekly interval, blending with normal system maintenance.
The ESXi vSphere Web Client contains a flaw in its file upload mechanism that allows attackers to bypass file type restrictions and decode malicious OVA/OVF packages.
The 'HardwareDriverX' loader service trusts the filename of a DLL passed to rundll32.exe, enabling an attacker to place a malicious DLL in an unsecured path for execution.

A cross-site request forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in the WebConfigUI of a Juniper-like JunOS device could allow an attacker to trick an authenticated administrator into clearing the system's network session logs and configuration history.
Visual Studio Code's debugger host process has a vulnerability that allows an attached malicious process to modify TLS callbacks, facilitating remote code execution during a debugging session.

Authorization bypass via ID manipulation in (IDOR) vulnerability in the IIS Management Service on Windows allows an attacker to disable vulnerable FTP and WebDAV extensions across all sites, closing potential attack vectors for others.

The CloudAuthN-Service for an IaaS platform can be rendered unavailable by an attacker sending a crafted SAML assertion that triggers an infinite loop, consuming all CPU and denying authentication for all users.
The 'DataSync Pro' application contains a buffer overflow when handling parameters passed to a rundll32.exe call, enabling remote code execution.
The PortalFramework IIS Module contains a memory corruption vulnerability that can be exploited for code execution.
The DefenderX Core Engine contains a flaw where it insecurely creates child processes, allowing an attacker to create a new process with a duplicated SYSTEM token.
The `Serial Port Gateway` service for macOS logs connection credentials in plaintext, allowing an attacker with local access to obtain credentials for direct VM access.

The 'CodeForge Pro' CLI tool on Windows contains a parameter injection vulnerability in its `tunnel create` command, allowing a user to append arbitrary commands that execute with the user's privileges.

The MacMDSuite agent fails to correctly enforce MDM policies, allowing a local user to execute a function that adds their account to the local 'admin' group, bypassing management controls for persistence.
An error handler in the Linux AdminPanel WebKit permits an attacker to inject commands into the application through X11-forged keyboard events, bypassing input validation.
A programmatic error in 'ZipMaster Pro' causes it to truncate file extensions when displaying archive contents, making a file like 'readme.txt.hta' appear as a harmless text file.
TightVNC server on Linux contains a weakness in its brute force protection mechanism, allowing attackers to perform unlimited authentication attempts without lockout.
The `security` command-line utility on macOS is susceptible to a race condition when dumping the keychain, which can be exploited to leak decrypted passwords before the lock file is properly updated.
The Windows Shell Link Handler fails to properly sanitize data from .lnk files, allowing an attacker to achieve code execution if a user views a malicious shortcut in Explorer.

An input validation issue in Microsoft.RemoteAccess.Management.dll on Windows allows an attacker to create deceptive VPN connection profiles that block traffic from specific user agents associated with security tools.
The SMB Discovery Helper service on Windows does not enforce proper rate limiting on name query requests, enabling an attacker to rapidly scan an entire subnet for shared resources.
The 'WebAppDeployer' utility for Windows contains a type confusion vulnerability in its installer logic, which can be exploited via InstallUtil to achieve code execution.
The Task Scheduler service contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows command injection through specially crafted task XML files processed by the service.
An identified issue in the 'otp-syncd' daemon on Linux allows an attacker to intercept the shared secret used for TOTP generation during the initial setup process.

An improper access control flaw in the hostd daemon on ESXi permits a low-privileged user to invoke privileged `vim-cmd` operations, such as powering off or reconfiguring virtual machines they do not own.

Reflected or stored XSS flaws in flaw in the SharePoint Online integration component of the Office Suite allows an attacker to steal authentication cookies, granting them access to mine SharePoint sites for unsecured development credentials.

OS command injection flaws in exists in the 'AdminPanel' component of 'MegaCorp ERP Suite'. An authenticated user can craft a malicious request to the diagnostic endpoint, allowing for the execution of arbitrary commands via cmd.exe.
The 'DevStream IDE' custom project launcher fails to correctly parse project shortcuts, potentially allowing arbitrary command execution when a project is loaded.

The macOS framework 'SpotlightWebIndexer' contains a memory corruption issue when processing data from a public RSS feed. An attacker can leverage this to use the feed as a dead drop resolver, corrupting the process to execute code that contacts a malicious C2 server.
The GlobalGrid 'IAM-Policy-Validator' tool does not check for the absence of region-denied conditions, allowing policies that inadvertently grant global resource creation rights.
The 'openvpn-server' on Linux uses a script that insecurely calls sudo with a wildcard command, allowing a user who can control the script's input to run arbitrary commands as root.

The AirPort Base Station Agent on macOS contains a vulnerability in its wireless network discovery protocol that can be exploited to reflect and amplify network traffic towards a victim with a spoofed IP address.
An insufficient access control in the Google Compute Engine image management allows attackers to modify shared images.

The CodeHelper Extension for a popular IDE registers a COM object that points to a relative path. An attacker can place a malicious DLL in that location and invoke it using verclsid.exe to compromise the developer's machine.
Memory corruption in the Windows Logon UI component permits attackers to bypass security controls and inject persistent logon scripts into user initialization sequences.
A logical flaw in the 'Active Directory Recycle Bin' feature could allow an attacker to undelete and manipulate the KRBTGT account object.

The 'OrionIT Management Suite' agent, which utilizes WinRM for remote administration, contains a flaw where hardcoded credentials can be extracted from memory, allowing for unauthorized WinRM sessions.
Improper validation of update packages in the ESXi vpxa agent allows an attacker to serve a malicious binary, replacing the legitimate agent with a compromised one for persistent access.
A misconfigured Redis instance used by the MISP Docker container allows unauthenticated remote access to cached data, including recent search queries about an attacker's own activity.
The Ubiquiti UniFi Network Controller fails to properly validate firmware images, enabling the deployment of modified system images with weakened security controls.
Logic flaw in macOS Security Framework permits bypass of authorization checks when modifying com.apple.loginwindow.plist.

The Enterprise Sync Daemon on Windows contains a flaw where it does not verify the integrity of files downloaded via FTPS. An attacker with control over the FTPS server can supply a malicious payload to achieve remote code execution.

The installer for DiskTune Pro on macOS versions prior to 3.1 insecurely creates a startup item, leaving the `StartupParameters.plist` file world-writable and enabling persistence for any standard user.
The macOS 'IPFS-Pinner' utility does not validate the integrity of pinned content, allowing an attacker to replace a legitimate link target with malicious files on the IPFS network.

A logic error within the Linux FRRouting (FRR) daemon's BGP module allows for the unauthorized querying of the routing information base (RIB), revealing the complete internal network topology to any attacker with network access.
The `WebNetAdmin` package for Debian contains a directory traversal flaw that allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to read `/etc/NetworkManager/system-connections/` and obtain Wi-Fi passwords.
A vulnerability in the Windows Credential Manager allows an attacker to hijack a COM object responsible for UI callbacks, enabling persistent code execution whenever credentials are accessed.
Microsoft SharePoint Online's permission inheritance mechanism can be bypassed, allowing attackers to grant site collection administrator rights to compromised accounts.
