The Safari browser on macOS is vulnerable to a cross-site scripting attack due to improper sanitization within its WebArchive feature, which uses a custom method for bundling web content.
A critical weakness within the SecureNet HRIS for Windows allows an attacker to create a malicious SQL stored procedure that executes on MSSQL startup, achieving persistence via xp_cmdshell.
A programmatic error in the Docker Engine's communication with the container runtime permits the manipulation of a container's `HostConfig`, enabling persistent mount of sensitive host directories.

A heap-based buffer overflow in the `VMFS-Driver` of an ESXi hypervisor can be triggered via a specially crafted I/O request from a guest virtual machine, leading to code execution on the host and a VM escape.
A popular code editor for macOS, 'CodeCompanion IDE', is vulnerable to directory traversal via its plugin installer, which can be exploited to write malicious code to a resource fork and execute it.

An ESXi host's hostd daemon uses a weak custom cipher to encrypt traffic to third-party management tools. A cryptographic flaw in the cipher's S-box design allows for the practical recovery of the encryption key.
The AD FS Device Registration Module on Windows is susceptible to a TOCTOU race condition, permitting the registration of a malicious device under a legitimate user's session.

The DBAdmin Console for Linux does not correctly parse filenames with the RTLO character during its file import function, potentially tricking a database administrator into executing a malicious SQL script.
A software fault within the PostgreSQL 'pg_cron' extension on Linux allows for SQL injection. An attacker could schedule a malicious job to run persistently with database owner privileges.

A stack-based buffer overflow affecting the Windows-based 'CloudSyncClient.exe' allows an attacker to craft a malicious configuration file, causing the process to exfiltrate local documents to an attacker-controlled OneDrive account.
ESXi's vSphere Web Client allows unauthorized timestamp modifications through API endpoints, enabling attackers to timestomp virtual machine configuration files.
A local privilege escalation in the systemd-resolved service on Linux allows an unprivileged user to manipulate the system's DNS over TLS proxy configuration, redirecting all DNS queries.

A stack-based buffer overflow affecting the PostgreSQL CertAuth module for Linux allows an unauthenticated attacker to extract the private key of the server's client authentication certificate from memory.

The Virtual Machine Backup Service on ESXi contains an XML External Entity (XXE) vulnerability. By processing a malicious backup job definition file, an attacker can achieve remote code execution and encrypt the entire backup repository.

The Thunar file manager on Linux contains a TOCTOU (Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use) race condition when handling file metadata on removable volumes. This can be exploited to trick a user into executing a malicious script from a USB drive, which then acts as a C2 agent to read and write data to the media.

A misconfiguration in the TenantIsolationService of a major IaaS provider allows a tenant to run a discovery script that reveals the physical data center region of another tenant's resources through timing attacks.

Improper permissions on the `/Library/StartupItems/CryoArmor-Firewall` directory created by CryoArmor Firewall allow a low-privileged user to replace the executable script, achieving persistent root access.

The macOS AppStoreUpdatesHelper process contains a logic flaw where it temporarily stores a decrypted list of all installed Mac App Store applications in a directory with overly permissive ACLs, enabling software discovery.

A buffer overflow vulnerability in the LSASS process on Windows Domain Controllers allows remote code execution, enabling an attacker to inject a master password that bypasses all standard authentication checks.

The SwiftDocker daemon exposes its management API on TCP port 2375 without authentication by default. This allows any attacker on the same network to query the API and extract container environment variables and logs containing sensitive credentials.
The `nginx-plus-module` on hardened Linux VMs can be instructed to reload its configuration via a compromised cloud agent, allowing for the execution of commands as the web server user.
A race condition in the Lighttpd-Custom web server on Linux can be exploited to replace index files during a reload, causing a temporary but effective defacement of hosted sites.
Improper bounds checking in the UpdateDaemon Service's handler for scheduled task creation commands allows an authenticated user to hijack the execution flow as SYSTEM.
An authentication bypass in the AWS S3 API allows attackers to delete storage buckets and objects, destroying cloud data.
Information leakage flaws in in the VMware Fusion framework on macOS causes debug logs to be written with excessive permissions, leaking the file paths and names of all configured virtual machines.
Improper validation of MIME-encoded email attachments in the macOS Mail app could lead to arbitrary code execution when a malicious attachment is decoded.

Improper handling of data in the Microsoft Store App Installer permits the creation of BITS jobs with a custom 'completion' argument, enabling the silent execution of malicious code after a legitimate app update.

A bug located in the 'TweakMaster' system utility allows for the creation of arbitrary registry entries under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Netsh. This can be abused to register a malicious DLL for persistence, triggered by any call to netsh.exe.
Memory corruption in the Windows component `licensingdiag.exe` can be exploited to execute arbitrary commands without invoking cmd.exe directly.
The 'SSHAgent' service on macOS can be coaxed by a local application into signing authentication requests for hosts it hasn't been explicitly approved for, facilitating credential theft.

The netfilter-core module for Linux fails to perform integrity checks on LKMs before loading, permitting an attacker to replace a legitimate module with a malicious one for persistent kernel-level access.
A misconfiguration in the 'CloudHost' object storage service exposes publicly readable files containing internal network diagrams with annotated server room locations.

A denial-of-service vulnerability exists in the CloudSync Integration Service on Windows due to a flaw in how its internet connection check processes malformed ICMP echo requests, causing the service to crash.

A buffer overflow vulnerability in the gorecon command-line tool for Linux can be triggered by processing a social media profile with an excessively long 'location' field, leading to arbitrary code execution.
The macOS Time Machine service fails to properly encrypt backups when configured to do so on a network share, allowing an attacker on the same network to access unencrypted archived data.
An insecure default configuration in the webcache service allows attackers to perform remote code execution that then modifies the process's own argv to impersonate 'nginx: master process'.
The Apache Tomcat manager application on Windows contains an SSRF flaw that enables access to the AWS metadata service, retrieving IAM role credentials.
The 'WebGuard Pro' browser extension on macOS fails to properly sanitize cross-origin requests, permitting malicious scripts to access sensitive user data and establish persistence.
A use-after-free vulnerability in the Windows Installer service when processing custom actions allows a low-privileged user to achieve privilege escalation.

An internal defect in the 'OpenNMS' network monitoring system on Linux allows an unauthenticated user to access map data via a specific API endpoint, revealing the geographic layout of a company's network assets.
The Windows Event Log service contains a privilege escalation flaw that can be exploited to obtain SYSTEM rights, subsequently enabling SAM database extraction.
A bug located in the Adobe Acrobat Reader DC update service on Windows could be leveraged to perform a file-less process injection via doppelgänging.

The Check Point Gaia operating system's crypto library contains a flaw where an attacker can manipulate configuration files to set the minimum allowed key size for administrative HTTPS sessions to 1024 bits.
A directory traversal vulnerability in the VMware vCenter Server Appliance's log viewer component permits an attacker to overwrite log files with defaced text.

Incorrect access control in the Logix Analytics Engine service allows a standard user to connect to its private IPC port and send an 'impersonate' command, which causes the service to leak its current user token.
Improper validation in Active Directory Local Account Manager enables attackers to create hidden local accounts with elevated privileges through a specially crafted LDAP query.
Simultaneous execution threads in the Keychain Access application allows a brief window where an attacker can access the contents of an unlocked keychain before the UI locks it.

Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) does not correctly handle file permissions and types when copying files between the Windows and Linux filesystems. A malicious Windows executable renamed with a `.sh` extension can be inadvertently executed within the WSL environment.
The Consul Service Discovery service is susceptible to a specially crafted health check request that consumes significant memory during an active service enumeration.
A vulnerability in the FinderSync extension integration allows a malicious IDE extension to register a persistent sync action that executes code on login.
An insufficient permission check in the Windows 'Plug and Play' service permits non-administrative users to access the device tree, facilitating the discovery of all connected peripherals.

A workflow defect in macOS's `GatekeeperHelper` allows a malicious app to invoke a series of benign, time-consuming system queries, such as repeated file attribute checks, to delay its main malicious functionality.
Memory corruption in the Linux Kernel's VFS layer permits attackers to bypass file permissions and overwrite arbitrary files with random data.
A stack-based buffer overflow affecting systemd's processing of the User directive for the 'vsftpd' service on Linux allows local privilege escalation to root.
OneDrive API v2.0 allows arbitrary command execution through malicious file synchronization requests that bypass content validation.

The cron helper utility on a specific Linux distribution does not properly sanitize user input, enabling an attacker to create a cron job with a name that includes non-printable characters, effectively hiding it in a standard `crontab -l` listing.
An information disclosure vulnerability in CoreTech Driver Manager for Windows could leak sensitive driver metadata through uninitialized memory when handling driver information queries.
The Windows Diagnostics Hub Standard Collector Service, `DiagHub.exe`, contains a COM object that can be abused to execute arbitrary DLLs, providing a method for persistence and privilege escalation.

The 'Visual Studio Code Installer' does not properly validate its execution environment, making it susceptible to COR_PROFILER hijacking. An attacker can set the variable to execute a malicious DLL with the installer's privileges during an update or repair operation.
The SwiftCache Framework for macOS improperly handles cache-control headers, which can cause sensitive development artifacts containing internal API keys to be stored and served from a public CDN.
The 'SecureNotes' app for macOS fails to create its mutex in the global namespace, allowing another user on the same system to launch a second instance and access the first user's notes.
An information disclosure vulnerability in 'FileManager Pro' reveals the path of the user's startup folder, which can be used by an attacker to precisely place a malicious shortcut for persistence.

In the `Visual Studio Code` installer for macOS, the `postinstall` script is vulnerable to argument injection. It passes a user-controllable string directly to a shell command executed with root permissions, allowing a local attacker to run arbitrary commands.
The macOS CoreAudio framework fails to properly sanitize Mach port messages, leading to arbitrary code execution through IPC abuse.

A programmatic error in the CloudStorage Sync Agent allows an attacker to modify a sync configuration file, causing the agent to execute mavinject.exe and inject a malicious library into explorer.exe.

The SecureVault Client for Windows contains a permission escalation bug that allows an attacker to create a hidden directory inside the vault's protected storage area, bypassing the application's own access controls.
The macOS SafariAutoFill component can be manipulated via a malicious webpage to auto-fill credentials into a hidden iframe, exfiltrating saved website passwords without user interaction.
The OpenCMS Pro daemon on Linux contains a SQL injection flaw that allows remote attackers to alter content stored in the backend database, leading to widespread external defacement.

A logic error within the 'API Bridge' component for Windows servers allows a low-privileged user to register a new, unauthenticated serverless function endpoint that proxies traffic to an attacker-controlled server.
The ESXi SSH daemon's configuration allows a user with non-administrative shell access to execute commands for file and directory discovery in the /etc and /var/log directories.
The WinRM service on Windows fails to properly authenticate requests for session creation, allowing an adversary to set up a persistent forwarding tunnel for C2 traffic through a compromised machine.

The configuration import module in Fortinet FortiOS fails to properly validate the contents of a configuration file, allowing an administrator with limited rights to upload a malicious file that disables the firewall and opens all WAN ports.
Microsoft SCCM's trusted client certificate validation can be bypassed, allowing attackers with access to a trusted client certificate to deploy malicious software across the enterprise.
The PhotoEditor Pro application fails to remove its login item upon uninstallation, leaving a dormant executable that can be re-activated by an attacker for persistence.
GNOME Tracker search daemon on Linux fails to validate search query permissions, allowing malicious local users to access indexed files from other users' home directories through crafted searches.
The API gateway for LLM-HostaaS fails to validate the 'Origin' header, allowing a malicious actor to set up a reverse proxy and hijack the underlying large language models for their own applications.
Ubiquiti UniFi Network Controller has improper authentication on API endpoints that allows attackers to deploy malicious access points mimicking existing network configurations.

The Confluence SaaS 'Content Export' module fails to properly validate user permissions, allowing a user with read access to a single page to export an entire space, including restricted pages containing architectural diagrams and credentials.
A remote code execution vulnerability in the `Microsoft Graph API` client library, used by the Office Suite, could allow an attacker to use a user's context to read their cloud emails.
Kubernetes CNI plugins have a vulnerability where network policies can be bypassed to implement traffic duplication at the pod level.

A SQL injection vulnerability exists in the web portal of the 'OpenCA' certificate authority software on Linux, allowing remote attackers to extract the CA's private signing key and issue arbitrary certificates.
The Samba winbind service on Linux contains a race condition that could allow an attacker to impersonate a domain controller and grant arbitrary domain accounts elevated privileges on the local host.
An exploitable bug in the Thunderbird WebExt Integration on Linux permits a malicious extension, installed from a third-party source via a spearphishing link, to access and exfiltrate email content.

HPE ArubaOS-CX on 6300F Series Switches has a vulnerability in the system image verification mechanism that permits an authenticated attacker to install an older version with weaker security controls. The issue stems from insufficient validation of firmware image authenticity during the upgrade process.

The `launchd` service on macOS fails to validate the source of a property list (plist) file, allowing an attacker to place a malicious daemon in `/Library/LaunchDaemons/` with a name like `com.apple.security.agent`, masquerading as an official Apple service.
The SecureLinkVPN installer utilizes CMSTP.exe with a malicious INF file that loads an unsigned DLL from a user-writable directory, resulting in a DLL hijacking vulnerability.
The 'FinanceSuite' installer on Windows is vulnerable to a path traversal attack, allowing an attacker to write a malicious MSI to an arbitrary location and then use msiexec for proxy execution.

An insecure deserialization bug in the Outlook 'PST Export Tool' allows for arbitrary code execution. An attacker could use this to create a malicious PST that, when exported, sends its contents via a background HTTP POST to a web service.
Improper handling of Kerberos PACs during device registration in Windows allows an attacker to register a device that inherits the privileges of a more privileged service account.

A logic error in the `inputd` daemon permits a local attacker to create a udev rule in `/usr/local/lib/udev/rules.d/`, leading to the execution of an arbitrary script every time a new keyboard is interacted with.

An exploitable bug in the macOS Server Profile Manager web interface fails to sanitize directory listings, allowing attackers to browse and discover sensitive configuration files and device group information.
Azure Key Vault certificate operations can be exploited to extract certificate metadata without proper authorization, aiding in reconnaissance of organizational certificate infrastructure.

An algorithm implementation error in macOS's AirDrop service `AirDropHelper` permits an attacker on the same Wi-Fi network to receive arbitrary files without user interaction, creating a pathway for data exfiltration.
A custom kernel module for the 'AcmeIoT Gateway' running an embedded Linux OS contains a hardcoded function that logs all console input to a world-readable file in /tmp, facilitating keylogging.
Unchecked memory write operations in the configuration parsing service of CoreGuardian FW allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to leak memory contents, which may contain configuration data.

An elevation of privilege vulnerability in the 1Password helper process on macOS could be leveraged to show a fraudulent 'Master Password Required' dialog, designed to capture the vault's master password.

The Windows service WinMailSync, responsible for synchronizing email profiles, contains a vulnerability that allows a local attacker to inject a forwarding rule into the configuration of any user on the system.
The 'iCalShare' service on macOS improperly sanitizes shared calendar event properties, exposing the email addresses of internal attendees to unauthorized external users.
An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists in the 'MegaPrint Pro' driver for Windows due to improper validation of a print processor's path during the `AddPrintProcessor` call.

An insecure deserialization flaw in the Python-based `netdata-collector` on Linux arises from its use of the `rarfile` library, permitting remote code execution when a malicious RAR archive is processed during data collection.
The 'ESXi Storage Fencing Daemon' can be remotely triggered to enter a fatal error state, causing a host panic and reboot, through a specially crafted iSCSI packet.

A memory corruption issue in the Windows 'GroupPolicyClient' can be triggered to leak parts of the system's memory, potentially exposing cached domain group information from a previously logged-in administrator.

The 'SplunkForwarder' service contains a vulnerability where its configuration routine can be manipulated to set an arbitrary value in the AppInit_DLLs registry key. This enables an attacker to establish persistence by ensuring their malicious DLL is loaded by numerous processes.

An implementation error in the Windows EnterpriseLogSync.exe service allows an attacker with local access to create a scheduled task with a null display name, making it difficult to identify in Task Scheduler's UI.
A privilege escalation flaw in SystemHealthMonitor permits a low-privilege user to schedule a task that executes with SYSTEM-level privileges.

In macOS, the Gatekeeper Helper service contains a vulnerability where the SMTP server for quarantine notifications can be arbitrarily set, allowing for the exfiltration of quarantined file data via email.
The FTP service for Azure App Service on Windows has a flaw where authentication can be bypassed under certain conditions, allowing attackers to upload tools to the web root.

A memory corruption vulnerability in Windows 'AuthenticationFilterDriver' allows attackers to inject arbitrary SID-History values during token creation, facilitating privilege escalation and system compromise.

An insecure API endpoint in a Windows-based network monitoring tool, 'NetViewPro', allows an authenticated user to reconfigure its agents to use non-standard ports, creating a covert communication channel.
A logic error within the Google Cloud SSH-Relay service permits an attacker to enumerate valid temporary SSH keys for other VMs within the same hosted environment.
The third-party file manager UltraExplorer Pro for Windows contains a flaw that displays files without escaping the RTLO character, causing executables to appear as image files.
The web-based management interface for SecureTaskScheduler on Windows exposes the output of the 'w32tm /tz' command without requiring authentication, facilitating system time discovery.
VMware ESXi's vMotion replication process uses a weak implementation of RSA padding that could be exploited to decrypt live migration traffic, providing a pathway for data theft and C2 injection.
The 'Evolution' email client for Linux fails to properly validate DKIM signatures, allowing attackers to send spoofed emails that appear legitimate, facilitating spearphishing campaigns.
Unintended data exposure in in the SystemHealthMonitor timer's environment variables leaks credentials, which can then be used by an adversary to create new malicious timers.

Unsafe behavior in the `SafariCacheCleaner` utility on macOS permits arbitrary code execution. The utility's helper tool executes `sqlite3` based on the PATH environment variable, allowing an attacker to place a rogue `sqlite3` binary in `/opt/local/bin` or another higher-order directory.
Outlook fails to enforce macro security settings on scripts embedded within custom forms, allowing an attacker to execute untrusted code.

A logic error within the Windows Active Directory replication process could be exploited by an attacker on a compromised child domain to pull sensitive trust attributes from the parent forest's configuration partition.
The NFS client implementation within the ESXi kernel contains a null pointer dereference that can be triggered by a malicious NFS server, leading to a denial of service or potential code execution.
The SystemPreferencesHelper framework on macOS contains a bug that could be exploited to show a deceptive macOS software update credential request, capturing the user's password.

A software fault within the 'SecureGuard Endpoint Protection' console allows a low-privilege administrator to inject a malicious logon script into a GPO, resulting in the execution of arbitrary code upon user logon.

An input validation vulnerability in the ESXi Host Management Agent (hostd) permits the injection of junk data within management command packets. The agent incorrectly processes these packets, allowing an adversary to obfuscate C2 instructions by embedding them within meaningless XML tags.

A programmatic error in the domain controller's security policy engine permits the installation of a malicious authentication filter via API hooking, which can intercept and approve all subsequent login attempts.
A privilege escalation flaw in Windows Installer service (msiexec.exe) allows attackers to hijack installation threads and execute malicious code with elevated privileges.
Improper bounds checking in Windows Active Directory replication service allows attackers to enumerate group memberships and permissions across the domain.
Improper input validation in the AWS IAM role assumption mechanism permits attackers to obtain temporary credentials with elevated privileges across multiple services.

Vertical privilege escalation in in WinSystemMonitor service on Windows allows low-privileged users to access detailed process information including command-line arguments and parent process IDs, bypassing standard access controls.
The mailctl daemon on Linux contains an improper authentication flaw, allowing any user on the local network to submit new global mail forwarding configurations.
A lack of proper bounds checking in the Linux kernel's storage probe module (storage-probe.ko) allows an attacker to discover and gather metadata from storage devices that should be hidden.
The Linux kernel's module loading mechanism contains a flaw that allows the loading of kernel modules with junk code sections, hiding malicious functionality from security tools.
A memory corruption issue in the 'show tech-support' command of InfraBridge routers can be exploited by an authenticated user to achieve remote code execution through the CLI.
The ESXi HostUserMgmtService fails to enforce account lockout policies after a specified number of failed login attempts, facilitating brute-force attacks against local accounts.

An exploitable bug in the ServerlessFuncRunner platform allows a function to create a new IAM execution role with broad, overly permissive permissions during deployment, establishing a powerful new account context.
Elevation of privilege is possible in in a third-party antivirus's log cleanup module allows a standard user to clear the entire Security event log.

An integer overflow vulnerability in the NAT translation engine of WanLink routers could allow a remote, unauthenticated attacker to crash the device or potentially execute code to rewrite the device's NAT table for network traversal.
Unexpected behavior in the macOS Finder allows malicious filenames to leverage the RTLO character to be displayed as a different file type, bypassing Gatekeeper's initial user prompt.
An authentication bypass vulnerability exists in the web UI for EdgeLine routers, permitting an unauthenticated remote attacker to access the firewall configuration page and disable it completely.
Data leakage occurs in in the macOS `com.apple.localusersd` daemon exposes the list of all local accounts to its Mach port, which any local process can connect to.
A critical weakness within FileManager Pro on macOS allows a script to list all system extensions via an AppleScript event, bypassing the security policy intended to protect this information.
A memory corruption bug in the Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (LSASS) allows attackers to extract Kerberos service tickets before they're properly encrypted, facilitating kerberoasting.
An integer overflow in Windows Graphics Device Interface when processing screensaver dimensions allows heap corruption and code execution.

An authentication bypass flaw in the OpenSSH-Aux daemon for Linux allows remote attackers to execute commands without valid credentials. This provides a direct vector for adding the server to a malicious botnet.
VMware vSphere Client's DNS resolution does not implement proper validation, making it vulnerable to Fast Flux DNS attacks.
The ConnectHub Platform SaaS fails to properly isolate API sessions for third-party support personnel, allowing a compromised support account to view and modify data from any customer instance.
Improper input validation in the rsync daemon on Linux makes it possible to conceal C2 beacons within the protocol's block checksums, effectively blurring the communication.
A memory corruption vulnerability in the web management interface of Cisco IOS XE could allow an authenticated remote attacker to overwrite the device's flash memory and corrupt its firmware.

A use-after-free vulnerability in the MySQL database server (mysqld) on Linux enables an authenticated attacker to alter the process's VDSO memory page, resulting in code execution as the database user.
The Access database engine improperly handles DLL loading from the 'Office Test' registry location, allowing an attacker to run arbitrary payloads with the application's privileges.
macOS CoreFoundation framework incorrectly processes file type information, allowing malicious applications to masquerade as trusted system utilities.
Unintended data exposure in in the hypervisor management agent 'VirtManager' allows a guest virtual machine to query information about its host's physical CPU topology and cache hierarchy.
A coding defect present in the 'org.homebrew.maintenanced' Launch Daemon allows an unprivileged user to modify its configuration to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges.

Information leakage flaws in in the Directory Services Query Tool on Windows allows any domain user to retrieve the preauthentication status for all accounts, aiding in AS-REP roasting reconnaissance.
Windows Hyper-V virtualization platform has a flaw where specific VM network packet sequences can trigger the creation of hidden network interfaces for covert communication.

The `Finder Zip Integration` on macOS is vulnerable to a symbolic link attack when creating archives, allowing an attacker to hijack file inclusion and archive sensitive data pointed to by the malicious link.
The system's BIOS setup interface does not correctly sanitize input for boot override options, which can be exploited to deploy a bootloader from a compromised USB device.
The GNOME Shell Desktop Manager on Linux contains a memory corruption bug that can be triggered by a local user to change the desktop background and add defacing overlays to the user interface.
The Google Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy fails to properly validate on-premises authentication responses, allowing attackers to modify hybrid identity assertions.

The Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (LSASS) on Windows contains a memory leak that can be read by a process with SeDebugPrivilege, revealing the system's enforced password policy for local accounts.
The PowerLine network adapter firmware exposes a weak Telnet interface with default credentials. Attackers can exploit this to gain a shell and incorporate the adapter into a botnet.

A denial-of-service vulnerability in the Active Directory topology management service on Windows can be triggered to corrupt domain trust objects, which an attacker can then replace with malicious ones.
Improper input validation in the `image-prepare` utility of Linux-based GateKeeper firewalls allows an attacker to stage a downgraded image for the next boot cycle.
A software fault within the PAN-OS management interface on Palo Alto Networks firewalls allows an unauthenticated user to run a `show system info` command via an unsanitized API call.
The Windows Notification Service has a flaw where notifications from integrated third-party messaging apps can display action buttons with obscured URLs, facilitating phishing attacks.
A Windows driver signing enforcement error allows an attacker to load a malicious driver named 'nvlddmkm.sys' into the kernel, masquerading as a legitimate NVIDIA display driver.
A stack-based buffer overflow affecting the `image-resizer` Python library for Linux allows for code execution when processing a maliciously crafted image, which could be included as a dependency.
Arista EOS's CloudVision platform contains a flaw that permits attackers to exfiltrate network device configurations and telemetry data over unencrypted MQTT connections.
A path traversal vulnerability in the Windows UpdateAgentSvc service allows loading a malicious DLL from a user-writable directory, leading to privilege escalation.
A vulnerability in Fortinet FortiGate's web interface on their proprietary OS allows authenticated users to download complete firewall configurations, including VPN settings and security policies.
The macOS TCC framework improperly handles permission checks for sandboxed applications, potentially allowing a malicious app to gain full read/write access to connected USB drives for data theft.

An insecure storage implementation in the macOS Safari browser saves AutoFill passwords in an encrypted format that uses a key derived from predictable system information, facilitating local credential extraction.
Improper handling of data in Windows Defender's cloud reporting service permits attackers to exfiltrate system information by manipulating legitimate telemetry data packets.

A critical weakness within the Hyper-V Guest Service on Windows allows a guest virtual machine to query host system information, including the host's OS version and architecture, potentially bypassing isolation boundaries.
A software fault within the management API of a network device allows an attacker to use an undocumented endpoint to upload and execute arbitrary tools on the device filesystem.

An information disclosure vulnerability in the `MetaCloud` instance metadata service reveals the internal snapshot ID, which can then be used with a separate vulnerability to force an instance revert.
Improper input validation in the Windows TCP/IP NetBIOS Helper service permits a local attacker to inject crafted ARP replies, corrupting the ARP cache of the host system.

An elevation of privilege vulnerability in the custom `sysadmin-shell` daemon, due to improper validation of client authentication tokens, could allow an attacker to hijack a privileged remote management session.
A remote code execution vulnerability in the Windows Update Agent allows an attacker to replace a legitimate update package with a malicious one, facilitating the acquisition of malware.
The 'Microsoft System Center Configuration Manager' (SCCM) client can be tricked into running a malicious script through mshta.exe as part of a fake application deployment.
Improper access control on the system's print processor directory in Windows allows any authenticated user to drop a malicious DLL, which will be executed at boot by the print spooler.
Docker daemon on Linux systems is vulnerable to traffic signaling where crafted API requests can trigger the creation of exposed containers with backdoor ports for persistent access.
A DOM-based cross-site scripting vulnerability in a Zendesk integration widget allows an attacker to steal the end-user's Zendesk session cookie.
A programmatic error in the macOS 'Cocoa' scripting bridge allows AppleScript commands to be obfuscated using character reversal and case permutation, bypassing static analysis tools.

The 'EnterpriseMail Archiver' for Windows improperly processes and stores custom Outlook forms. A malicious form uploaded to the archive can execute code on the server when an administrator retrieves the mailbox, leading to remote code execution.

An insufficient authentication mechanism in the Azure KeyVault Certificate Injector API allows a low-privilege user to request and install a certificate intended for a different application, facilitating credential harvesting attacks.
A programmatic error in Remote Desktop Services could be exploited to force the loading of a malicious network provider during session establishment, intercepting logon credentials.
The SNMP daemon in CyberGate firewalls fails to properly validate community strings for 'GETBULK' requests, enabling an attacker to enumerate and retrieve the entire configuration MIB tree.
The DisplayEnhancer driver incorrectly sets permissions on HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon, enabling an attacker to add a malicious Userinit value for persistence.

Improper handling of data in the macOS Cocoa framework's NSWorkspace API allows an application without the 'com.apple.security.automation.apple-events' entitlement to still retrieve a list of running applications and their window information.

The `procmail` mail processing utility on Linux fails to sanitize headers before passing them to external scripts. A malicious email could execute arbitrary commands on the server, with the output being sent back to the attacker via a configured SMTP rule.
Improper input validation in a macOS system framework allows a malicious application to intercept and display a fake MFA prompt, capturing one-time passwords entered by the user.

The PlatformSMM module fails to validate input for a specific SMI, leading to an out-of-bounds read. This can be exploited by a local attacker to leak sensitive information from SMRAM, including data structures that define user privileges and roles at the firmware level.

The 'DockerEngine' on Linux, when configured with a specific logging driver, can be abused to execute arbitrary commands on the host by escaping a container and injecting commands into the logging process.
A third-party vCenter extension, 'RepoGuard', contains a flaw that allows an attacker to exfiltrate performance data from monitored ESXi hosts to a code repository under their control.

A logic error within the ESXi authentication backend allows a domain account that is a member of a non-privileged group to execute commands reserved for the 'Administrators' group via a crafted API call.
A hardware implant on a 'ThunderHub' USB-C hub for macOS enables the covert installation of malware when a device is connected.

An insecure API endpoint in the Windows 'EnterpriseCertManager' leaks metadata about all organization-wide certificates to any authenticated user, simplifying an adversary's search for valuable targets in public CT logs.

Unauthorized access level increase in in the CollabSpace 365 admin center allows a user with 'helpdesk' privileges to create a new global administrator account, bypassing the standard approval workflow.
Docker container runtime on Linux has a resource exhaustion vulnerability that allows attackers to crash the host system through container escape attempts.

An insecure API endpoint in a Kubernetes CSI driver for 'cloud-provider-x' allows any pod within the cluster to make API calls to the underlying cloud provider to list all storage volumes, bypassing RBAC controls for storage discovery.
A memory corruption flaw in the CoreImageProcessing.framework on macOS could lead to arbitrary code execution when processing a malicious image file containing steganographic content.
The Azure VM-Scale-Set-Manager service contains a flaw where the `PassRole` permission is not properly scoped, enabling a user to grant a newly created VM a role with Subscription Owner rights.

Flawed business logic in the Office365Updater on Windows fails to remove its Active Setup registry key after an update, leaving a persistent mechanism that can be hijacked by an attacker to execute malware at user logon.
The WinDefendCore.dll in Windows fails to scan Alternate Data Streams (ADS) attached to files on network shares, providing a pathway for malware to hide its payload.
Memory corruption in the SecureFlow third-party firewall driver for Windows permits an attacker to inject malicious code into the kernel, disabling all firewall rules.
An insecure deserialization flaw in the macOS Core Data framework allows for the loading of polymorphic objects that alter their internal state upon instantiation to bypass static analysis.

On Linux, the `apparmor_parser` utility can be tricked into loading a modified policy profile that retains a valid signature but contains permissive rules, allowing a confined process to escape its restrictions and subvert trust controls.

A privilege escalation flaw in the Linux `central-sync-daemon` permits a low-privilege user to reconfigure the daemon's target directory, allowing it to be used as a remote staging point for sensitive configuration files.

Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) flaws in the Linux 'logshipperd' cron script allows a local attacker to replace a temporary file with a symlink to a privileged crontab file before execution, resulting in privilege escalation.

A heap overflow in the Windows Print Spooler service allows attackers to trigger a system-wide crash by sending a specially crafted print job, causing a persistent denial of service condition as the service automatically restarts and can be re-exploited.
A memory corruption vulnerability in the macOS Spotlight metadata parser allows execution of arbitrary Lua code when processing a maliciously crafted file.
The Windows Netlogon service contains a flaw that permits attackers to access administrative shares through SMB using forged authentication tokens.
A logic flaw in the OpenSSH daemon (sshd) on Linux permits an authenticated user to manipulate the utmp and wtmp files after logout, deleting the record of their login session.
Elevation of privilege is possible in in the iMailSync Helper on macOS allows a standard user app to execute operations as root, including reading all users' emails from the system mail database.
A serverless function running on Google Cloud Platform was vulnerable to path traversal, allowing an attacker to access the 'package.json' file and enumerate all dependencies and their versions.

The Sysinternals ProcDump tool, when integrated into a Windows monitoring solution, can be used for malicious purposes if an attacker renames it to `procdmp.exe` to evade detection rules that specifically target the original filename.

The ManagedClient framework on macOS fails to validate the source of mobile configuration profiles, allowing an attacker to install a malicious profile that includes a payload to create a new domain account.

An information disclosure issue in the 'SecureNotes' application for macOS allows an attacker with local access to retrieve the application's plist file, which contains a cached copy of its TLS certificate for auto-sync.

In `Microsoft Password Guardian` for Windows, a use-after-free error can be triggered to hijack the execution flow within the context of the application, enabling the dumping of decrypted credentials from memory.
A Linux-based system monitoring tool, 'LogAnalyzer', written in VB.NET for .NET Core, contains a command injection flaw where user-supplied input is passed to a `Shell()` command.
An insufficient permission check in a Windows enterprise browser management tool allows a user to view the browsing history of other users, which can be mined for visits to social media sites.

A coding defect present in the Windows File Explorer's shell extension handler permits the manipulation of TLS callbacks when a malicious file is previewed, leading to code execution with the user's privileges.
KernelLink Driver for Windows fails to sanitize user-mode inputs when processing NT API calls, leading to kernel memory corruption.

The 'PostMaster-ng' mail transfer agent on Linux contains a vulnerability in its queue management module that gives a remote user the power to inject a massive number of emails destined for a single address, overwhelming the target inbox.

A maliciously crafted version of the 'IIS-Manager-Pro' PowerShell module includes a script that runs on module import to establish persistence, bypassing initial access controls by relying on a user to install and import it.

An information disclosure vulnerability in the Windows System Center Operations Manager (SCOM) Health Service reveals the state of its ARP cache, which an attacker can use to craft a more effective poisoning attack.
AWS Control Tower service lacks proper authorization checks for guardrail modifications, enabling attackers to alter compute resource governance policies.
Improper validation of SAML tokens in a third-party cloud management console, 'CloudOps Central', permits an attacker to forge administrator sessions and issue commands to any connected VM.
An insecure default file permission issue in the ConnMan network manager for Linux causes its configuration files in /var/lib/connman/ to be world-readable, exposing Wi-Fi passwords.

A permissions flaw in the Linux systemd-udevd service allows a non-privileged user to execute arbitrary scripts when a specific USB device is plugged in. An attacker can configure a compromised USB stick to trigger a script that reads commands from a file on the device, enabling C2.
The CloudFoundry Diego cell's container build process does not properly validate source code inputs, allowing an attacker to embed and execute malicious binaries in the resulting container image.
The macOS Security Helper utility contains a logic flaw where a malicious VB.NET script can be used to modify system configuration files, effectively disabling Gatekeeper checks.
The `mds` (metadata server) process, responsible for Spotlight indexing on macOS, is vulnerable to code injection through maliciously crafted file metadata.
Concurrency issues within the auditd subsystem on Linux allows an attacker to send a specially crafted signal that causes the daemon to crash, halting all system logging.

The SharePoint Web Application's application pool identity credential is exposed due to an insecure configuration in the registry, allowing an attacker to obtain the hash and forge a Kerberos silver ticket.

The macOS SpotlightSoftwareIndexer creates index files with world-readable permissions, allowing any user to parse the index and reconstruct a comprehensive list of installed applications and file associations.
The 'Serverless Deploy Toolkit' for Linux contains a hardcoded access key within its binary, which can be extracted to programmatically acquire and configure serverless infrastructure.
The macOS 'SpotlightIndexer' inadvertently indexes sensitive browser fingerprint data from cache files, making it searchable and available to any user or malware for spoofing purposes.

A flaw in the Azure Logic Apps connector for Blob Storage allows a logic app to be triggered to apply a lifecycle rule that deletes all blobs in a container, even if the logic app's definition does not explicitly specify this action.

Improper permissions on the 'SystemHealthReporter' service binary, HealthReporter.exe, allow for a local privilege escalation. An attacker can replace the legitimate binary, causing the service to run malicious code as SYSTEM.

The WebShield AV component on Windows does not correctly scan SVG files for obfuscated scripts. This permits malware to be smuggled onto a system by embedding its payload within a compressed and base64-encoded script block inside an SVG.
A heap-based buffer overflow in the `pst32.dll` module occurs when Outlook loads a malicious form from a compromised PST file, leading to code execution.
The 'DatabaseReplicator' service for a Windows SQL cluster uses a domain account with preauthentication disabled for replication, exposing its credentials to AS-REP roasting attacks.
Privilege escalation in systemd-logind service allows adversaries to modify user session properties and hide accounts from display managers.

An algorithm implementation error in the macOS 'pd' (printer daemon) allows a print job to execute a post-processing script that can detach from the daemon's process tree. This provides a pathway for an attacker to execute code that masquerades as a legitimate print job.
Improper validation of a JWT token in a serverless application on Google Cloud Run allows an attacker to craft a token that grants access to secrets in GCP Secret Manager.
AWS SDK for .NET on Windows has a vulnerability in its credential provider chain that could allow attackers to inject malicious cloud account credentials.

In VersionLink, the API for managing repository collaborators is vulnerable to a race condition. An attacker can briefly add themselves as a maintainer to a private repository, exfiltrate data, and then remove their access, leaving no trace in the audit log.

An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists in EnterpriseLogManager due to improper path handling. When it calls `net.exe` to configure network settings, it does not specify the full path, which can be hijacked by placing a crafted executable in the same folder.
An implementation error in the 'DiskOptimizer' service allows an adversary to create a 'Performance' registry key due to insecure 'Create Subkey' permissions, leading to malicious DLL execution.
A permission misconfiguration in the Windows Credential Manager service allows a low-privileged user to read the NL$ cache files containing MS-Cache v2 hashes.

An improper input validation vulnerability in EnterpriseDB Admin Console permits the execution of a custom callback routine. By targeting its SysListView32 control, an attacker can perform a ListPlanting attack to bypass security solutions.
Improper handling of data in the Linux nginx-helper module allows for privilege escalation by loading a malicious shared object from a directory writable by the web server user.
macOS Core Graphics framework has a flaw that allows applications to exfiltrate screen capture data over unencrypted RTSP protocol streams by embedding pixel data in video headers.

An implementation error in the Windows Update Client service allows a low-privileged user to modify the registry key for its COM interface, enabling persistent code execution via InprocServer32 hijacking.
OfficeConnect SSO integration contains a vulnerability where attackers can manipulate SAML token lifetimes to maintain persistent access to office suite applications.

Concurrency issues within the `ImageBuilderCLI` for Docker can be exploited to create an image where a malicious binary replaces a legitimate one during the build, causing users who run the image to execute the malicious payload.

The FalconAuth agent for Windows contains a flaw in its AS-REQ handler that permits the retrieval of AS-REP messages for any domain user, regardless of preauthentication status, exposing them to offline cracking.

In Linux, the cron daemon contains a flaw in handling crontab files with unusual characters. An attacker can create a cron job that executes a script only if the system's hostname matches a specific pattern, with the script payload being decrypted using that hostname.
VMware Tools service for Windows contains an insecure method that allows a non-administrative user to read the contents of the LSA secrets registry key.

An implementation error in `SecureFlow Gateway` for Windows allows an attacker to perform a man-in-the-middle attack on its internal system checks, feeding it falsified network adapter information to bypass T1497.001 detection mechanisms.

An insecure direct object reference vulnerability in `MacSafe Vault` for macOS allows a malicious application to query the password manager's API and retrieve stored credentials without requiring the master password.
Buffer bounds violations in the 'NimbusStack' IAM policy evaluator could be exploited to nullify the `sourceIp` condition, allowing access from any location.

Unexpected behavior in the 'Link Checker' plugin for Confluence Data Center SaaS logs the full URL of all checked links, including those to private internal resources, and stores these logs in a world-readable file.
A buffer overflow flaw in the custom installer for 'FileGuardian Service' on Windows can be triggered by InstallUtil, leading to privilege escalation.
The WhatsApp Web interface contains a vulnerability where third-party service verification codes can be intercepted, facilitating account takeover for spearphishing.
Vertical privilege escalation in in RemoteManagement.framework allows a user logged in via SSH on macOS to execute commands with root privileges without a password prompt.
Improper encoding of user output in vulnerability in the `Harmony Mail` client for macOS, when rendering a crafted HTML email, can be leveraged to execute JavaScript and steal a user's emails.
Concurrency issues within Azure AD Connect's synchronization service enables attackers to abuse msiexec.exe to execute malicious DLLs during the installation process.

Unsanitized command execution in in the Web UI proxy configuration module of Cisco IOS XE allows an authenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary commands and configure the device as a malicious proxy.

In the Windows enterprise software 'CyberIQ Central', a role-based access control (RBAC) misconfiguration permits users with 'analyst' role to view data from feeds reserved for the 'admin' role, including private vendor intel.
The 'G-Suite Plus' SaaS communication tool's chat history retention feature stores messages in plaintext in a temporary cloud bucket for an extended period, creating a window for credential theft.
Improper input validation in the Linux 'net-sync' daemon enables a local user to inject commands into the boot-time configuration script, leading to root privilege escalation.

Improper handling of data in macOS's Transparency, Consent, and Control (TCC) framework allows the fake PhotoHelper app to add itself to the Login Items list without explicit user approval. This grants the application persistence by launching automatically whenever the user logs in.
Insecure 'Create Subkey' permissions on the 'BluetoothAudioService' registry key allow an attacker to inject a malicious DLL via a crafted 'Performance' subkey.
The Windows IP Helper service improperly validates API calls, allowing unprivileged access to network adapter information that reveals IP block configurations.

The CodeForge Studio IDE for Windows contains a vulnerability where its build process can be instructed to set weak permissions on output files, potentially allowing an attacker to inject malicious code into a signed build pipeline.

The CRI-O container runtime can be made unresponsive by an attacker who provides a maliciously large container image manifest, causing the runtime to enter a high CPU state and deny service to other pods.
Application whitelisting bypass through BITS execution context allows unsigned malicious code to run under the trusted BITS service process.
A logic error in the Energy Saver pane of SystemPreferences can be exploited to create a persistent Launch Agent via launchctl.
Improper encoding of user output in vulnerability in the Windows-based IIS Media Manager could be leveraged to alter the displayed content on media portals, facilitating external defacement.

A heap-based overflow condition in the Windows Firewall Service (MPFWSvc) when processing specially crafted RPC calls can be exploited by an authenticated user to terminate the service and disable the firewall.

An incorrect implementation in the Blue Prism Automate Service allows a low-privilege developer to create a robot process that inherits the service's high-privilege token through the designer's debug interface.
Improper bounds checking in the PHP-FPM component on a Linux server, when processing certain requests, can be triggered to achieve remote code execution.
The Cisco Nexus 9000 series switch firmware lacks proper signature verification for updates uploaded via the management interface, enabling an attacker to implant persistent malicious firmware.
Sensitive information is exposed by in Mac Diag Suite on macOS generates system reports that include a full kextstat output, including undocumented drivers and their memory addresses.
A use-after-free error in the Active Directory replication service on a Domain Controller can be leveraged to modify GPOs and establish persistence via a malicious network logon script.

The OpenSSH daemon (sshd) on Linux is vulnerable to a forced command attack where an attacker with control over a specific authorized key can execute arbitrary commands via a service-side configuration flaw.
macOS XProtect fails to quarantine shell scripts with misleading extensions, allowing malicious code execution.
The 'Citrix Workspace' client for Windows contains a vulnerability where a malicious server can supply a URL that is passed directly to mshta.exe, leading to code execution on the client machine.
APIFlow Gateway 的请求路由逻辑存在一个漏洞，允许攻击者绕过旨在限制内部服务间通信的策略，并将数据从内部服务重定向到外部云 API 端点。
A critical weakness within the SystemD helper tool on Linux could allow a malicious attachment to create a new privileged service, leading to persistence.

The `MicroContainerRuntime` for Linux fails to properly validate the entrypoint of a Docker image, permitting a backdoored container to execute a cryptominer as the root user when deployed by an administrator.
An off-by-one error in the Linux kernel's BPF verifier can be exploited to bypass security restrictions and elevate privileges.
Improper handling of data in the macOS mDNSResponder service allows it to accept unsolicited ARP replies for non-local IP addresses, leading to ARP cache poisoning and traffic redirection.
Improper input validation in the nginx web server on Linux allows for the insertion of dead code into custom modules, making reverse engineering more difficult.

A coding defect present in the Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Client's VPN component permits the alteration of TLS callbacks during module initialization, leading to arbitrary code execution with elevated privileges.

Simultaneous execution threads in the `Credential Cache Service` during process termination can be exploited to write a copy of a process's memory to disk. By targeting LSASS, an attacker can create a dump file for offline credential analysis.
Palo Alto Networks Firewall Admin Service has a privilege escalation flaw that allows authenticated users to create new administrator accounts and bypass security policies.

A stack-based buffer overflow affecting the 'OpenStack-Swift' object server's `GET` request handler can be triggered to bypass container-level read ACLs, allowing an authenticated user to enumerate all objects in the container.
Improper locking mechanisms in the macOS 'System Settings' application allows a local user to modify the 'com.apple.loginwindow.[UUID].plist' file during a logout sequence, achieving persistence.
A vSAN IO Redirector component on ESXi lacks proper authentication checks, allowing an attacker to re-route storage I/O through a malicious proxy for data exfiltration.
A flaw in the 'Active Directory Helper Service' on Windows allows an attacker to send a specially crafted packet that triggers an error message containing the names of privileged domain groups.
Shell command injection risks in exists in the `censys-query-cli` tool for Linux due to improper sanitization of user-supplied search queries before passing them to a system shell.

The SwiftText Editor on Windows loads a spell-checking library from its own installation directory without verifying its identity. If a low-privileged user can write to this directory, they can perform a DLL hijacking attack to escalate privileges.
The VirtuStack instance metadata service exposes IAM role credentials in an unauthenticated endpoint, allowing any code running on the instance to steal the access token for cloud APIs.
An input validation issue in the Linux `sshuttle` proxy tool allows an attacker on the same machine to specify a malicious configuration that redirects traffic through a hijacked SSH session.

A heap-based buffer overflow in Safari's WebKit JIT compiler, when processing maliciously crafted JavaScript, can be triggered to achieve remote code execution, effectively forcing a malware download.

A security gap in the macOS Transparency, Consent, and Control (TCC) framework allows a malicious app to bypass privacy prompts. The app can decrypt its malicious component only if it has been granted screen recording permission, which it checks before decryption.

Improper locking mechanisms in the Windows Event Log Service allows an attacker to swap a legitimate DLL with a malicious one just before it is loaded by a mavinject.exe call, leading to SYSTEM-level code execution.
The VNCAuthKit component on macOS contains a logic error where an empty password is accepted under specific configurations, leading to unauthorized access.

In the Azure PowerShell module 'Az.Storage', a function to set lifecycle rules fails to sanitize input, allowing for the injection of a rule that deletes all blobs regardless of prefix or tag, bypassing the intended scope.
The macOS 'XProtect' security feature fails to detect a specific family of malware due to an outdated signature database, allowing for the installation of a persistent backdoor for resale.

Improper access control in AWS Traffic Mirroring service permits users with limited privileges to create mirroring sessions for instances they don't own, facilitating data theft across VPC boundaries.

In the Linux Docker daemon, an insecure API endpoint allows a low-privileged user to attach to a container's stdin/stdout. This can be abused to intercept and inject data into the container's logs, which may be forwarded to a remote server acting as a C2 channel for exfiltration.

A programmatic error in the Windows Update mechanism allows an attacker to inject and generate a fraudulent Microsoft update signing certificate, enabling the distribution of malicious payloads that appear authentic.
The `quarantine_check` daemon on macOS does not properly validate file attributes, which can be abused to detect if the application is running inside a security analysis sandbox.
The Group Policy Client fails to properly validate paths specified in a logon script GPO setting, allowing for a path traversal attack that could execute an arbitrary binary from a network share.
The Linux kernel module signing process can be bypassed during build, allowing malicious kernel modules to be distributed through official package repositories.
A double-free vulnerability in the winrmdrv.sys driver, triggered by a specific sequence of WinRM commands, could lead to kernel memory corruption and system compromise.

A SQL injection vulnerability in the enterprise software 'HRConnect Suite' on Windows allows for the extraction of the entire employee database, including names, addresses, and social security numbers.

A code injection vulnerability exists in PowerShellGallerySync for Windows, where an attacker can manipulate a registry value to inject and execute arbitrary PowerShell commands through the Active Setup 'StubPath' during user logon.

An improper access control vulnerability in the IdentityMonitor Agent for Windows allows a low-privilege user to trigger AS-REQ requests and capture the resulting AS-REP messages for offline cracking.
Supply chain manipulation of the 'SecureAuth' smart card reader hardware led to a modified firmware that can exfiltrate authentication credentials from Windows domain controllers.

The security architecture of the ESXi VMkernel networking stack allows a virtual machine to exploit the hypervisor and create a rule that routes other VMs' traffic through itself, effectively making the controlled VM an internal proxy.

The `lldpd` daemon on certain Linux distributions is configured to process and announce detailed system information over LLDP, allowing an attacker on a local network segment to passively map device types and network connections.
The Docker daemon's socket API fails to validate user permissions, enabling unauthenticated users to create new local accounts with root privileges on the host system.
Nginx reverse proxy on Linux systems reveals backend server details through error messages, enabling attackers to map infrastructure for vulnerability scanning.

A programmatic error in the macOS SecureInput component allows a malicious application to take a screenshot just before SecureInput is activated for a password field, potentially capturing credentials.
The Linux arping utility fails to validate interface specifications, allowing attackers to send ARP requests across network segments and identify active hosts within IP blocks.

Improper handling of data in a custom Ansible module for managing cloud instances allows a malicious playbook to define a task that forcibly reverts a server to a baseline snapshot after executing malicious code.
Unsafe behavior in the Kubernetes kubelet on Linux allows an unauthorized user to make a read request to the `/pods` endpoint, listing all pods and their associated services within the node.
An algorithm implementation error in the UEFI firmware of certain Dell Latitude models allows the disabling of Secure Boot via a specially crafted NVRAM variable update.
An authentication bypass in the Outlook Network Connector for Windows enables a network adversary to inject malicious email attachments into a legitimate IMAP session.
macOS Safari's file:// URL handler fails to restrict shell script execution, enabling local command execution through crafted links.
The firmware on certain IoT network devices contains a hardcoded backdoor account with a weak, guessable password, which can be discovered via a brute force scan.

The 'CocoaBuilder' IDE on macOS fails to properly sandbox extensions that interact with the `osascript` tool, permitting a malicious extension to execute AppleScript commands and exfiltrate user data.

The Windows `Credential Manager` fails to isolate browser-saved credentials correctly, allowing a script running in a Low-Integrity Level process to enumerate and read web credentials saved by Internet Explorer or Edge.
Insecure default configuration in the 'nagios' monitoring tool on Linux exposes system files through the web interface, including /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow.
A software fault within the 'UpdateManager Pro' software allows a malicious XSL file to be processed during update log generation, leading to the execution of embedded JScript.
The macOS Remote Management daemon (remoted) suffers from a race condition that allows attackers to hijack legitimate remote sessions.
Improper input validation in the Windows Mail application's import feature allows attackers to inject malicious code and access local email stores.

A critical weakness within the macOS Finder allows the com.apple.quarantine extended attribute to be stripped from a file via a specific metadata manipulation sequence. This enables users to run untrusted software without Gatekeeper intervention.
An internal defect in the macOS packet filter (pf) allows an attacker to bypass firewall rules by fragmenting TCP scan packets, facilitating stealthy active reconnaissance.

The NetScan Document Exporter utility on Windows fails to enforce strict permissions when setting up its virtual printer. This allows a non-admin user to modify the `Driver` value in the `Monitors` registry, leading to privilege escalation through a malicious DLL.
The 'RemoteAdmin Toolkit' on Windows inadvertently logs trusted host keys and network paths for managed service providers in a world-readable file, exposing critical trust dependencies.
The 'CocoaBuilder' IDE on macOS fails to isolate extensions from one another, allowing a compromised plugin to inspect and modify the code and data of other installed extensions.

The macOS 'iCloud-Sync-Agent' has a flaw where it ignores files marked with the `UF_HIDDEN` flag during sync conflict resolution. An attacker can create a hidden malicious file on a local machine that will not be overwritten or flagged by iCloud, ensuring persistence across synced devices.
A logging flaw in ESXi causes the output of `esxcli network ip interface ipv4 get` to be written to a log file accessible by any logged-in user.
NimbusControl Panel 的虚拟机镜像导出工具未能正确验证 API 请求中的目标存储账户，允许具有低权限的用户将镜像副本发送到任意云存储位置。
Flawed business logic in the Microsoft System Center Virtual Machine Manager (SCVMM) connector allows an attacker to deploy a 'rogue' VM that is not discoverable or manageable by the SCVMM console.
The rsyslog daemon on Linux contains a memory corruption vulnerability in its TCP reception module, enabling remote code execution.
Insecure handling of Outlook Offline Address Book (OAB) files could lead to an out-of-bounds read, leaking cached GAL contents to an attacker who convinces a user to open a malicious OAB file.

A security gap in the HyperVGFXDisplay.sys driver on Windows allows for the detection of hardware breakpoints. Malware can query the driver's state to determine if debug registers are set, indicating an active debugging session.
A SQL injection vulnerability exists in the database backend of the 'LinkFarm' Windows application, which could be used to extract or modify the configurations of all staged link targets.
A buffer overflow in the DellSystemFirmwareUpdate service on Windows enables an attacker with local access to overwrite the UEFI firmware with a malicious image, achieving persistence.

An improper authentication check in a Windows application updater service allows an attacker to replace the update binary with a malicious one while keeping the original service name and description, effectively masquerading the malware as a legitimate update process.

The VIB (vSphere Installation Bundle) installation service on ESXi contains a flaw where a post-install script can be instructed to upload a log file. The script accepts a parameter to symmetrically encrypt the file with a provided RC4 key before sending it to a user-specified URL, enabling data exfiltration.
In the 'ContainerSSH' project for Linux, a flaw in session handling allows a malicious container to access the host's SSH agent socket, leading to host session hijacking.
Unexpected behavior in the `WindowsDefender` antimalware service allows an attacker to perform a DLL injection attack using a module stomping technique, bypassing behavior-based detection.

Insufficient validation of message content in the 'TeamSync' Windows client allows a malicious user to send a specially formatted message that forces the client to transmit its local chat cache to an attacker-controlled server.

The Avahi daemon on Linux, used for mDNS/DNS-SD service discovery, can be manipulated into sending large multicast responses to a unicast, spoofed IP address, facilitating a network-based reflection amplification attack.
A memory corruption vulnerability in the 'AdminPanelX' utility can be triggered by a malicious payload executed through rundll32.exe, leading to a system crash or code execution.
The Okta-SAML-Connector fails to properly validate SAML responses, enabling an attacker to modify group membership assertions and grant a compromised user elevated access to linked applications.
A third-party add-on for Microsoft Office, 'DataViz Pro', incorrectly utilizes the 'Office Test' registry for its own components without securing it against unauthorized modification.
An implementation error in the macOS 'SystemIntegrityProtection' framework can be exploited to bypass SIP guardrails during a race condition, allowing system file modification on a protected system.
Buffer overflow in Windows Kerberos Password Change service enables attackers to steal user tickets during password updates.
Authorization bypass via ID manipulation in in the 'Microsoft Exchange Server' Autodiscover service allows authentication using only a user's NTLM hash.

A programmatic error in the Windows HID subsystem allows an unprivileged application to register a fake keyboard device and inject its keystrokes system-wide, bypassing UII (User Interface Isolation).
An insecure deserialization bug in the Windows DNS Server component gives a remote user the power to create arbitrary DNS records, including those for maliciously acquired domains.
A race condition during AWS Lambda function creation can be exploited to associate a function with a VPC it is not authorized for, creating a pivot point within a cloud environment.
An authentication bypass in the NetCore OS SNMPv3 agent allows an unauthenticated attacker to issue a 'get-config' command, leading to a full device configuration dump.
A flaw related to subscription management in the GridLock platform allows a low-privilege user to change the associated subscription to one with higher resource quotas.

Unauthorized access level increase in in the Windows 'Hyperion Update Agent' allows a low-privileged user to execute arbitrary code with SYSTEM privileges, which can be used to call `ExitWindowsEx` and force a system reboot.
Windows Search's shim mechanism permits attackers to bypass UAC controls through specially crafted shim databases.
The RemoteHelp console application for Windows does not sanitize user-supplied input in its 'domain-lookup' feature, allowing an attacker to inject LDAP queries to enumerate domain trust objects.
Cisco's ConfigSync utility on network devices fails to properly authenticate export destinations, enabling automated exfiltration of device configurations and logs.
An insufficient authentication mechanism in the HashiCorp Consul API allows any agent on the same LAN to query the service catalog and discover all registered services, their IPs, and ports.

The Symantec Endpoint Protection driver (symevent.sys) has an insecure IOCTL that permits a low-privileged application to trigger an operation that impersonates a system user in kernel mode, leading to an access token theft.

Privilege elevation flaws in in the Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) service allows a low-privileged user to query the Win32_LogicalDisk class, enabling the enumeration of all local disk drives, their types, and available space.

A software fault within the Windows Network Discovery Service allows an authenticated attacker to hijack the execution flow, which can be used to run network enumeration commands like 'net view' to discover other systems on the domain.
The Enterprise Database Connector uses a memory-mapped file for high-speed data transfer but fails to validate the mapped memory's contents, allowing for PE injection into the connector's process.
The TimeMachineHelper service fails to validate the executable path when using AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges, leading to a potential root-level code execution vulnerability.

A workflow defect in the SSL VPN portal of FortiOS permits a threat actor via network access to send a specially crafted request that deactivates the firewall policies associated with the VPN tunnel, granting unrestricted network access.

Unexpected behavior in the macOS Keychain Access utility allows the export of a code-signing private key without requiring the correct password, if the key was previously accessed, enabling its theft for malicious signing.
A memory corruption issue in containerd could be exploited to hijack the execution flow when launching new containers, leading to the execution of arbitrary commands in the container context.
A race condition in Final Cut Pro's AI-Enhancer on macOS could be exploited to replace a legitimate AI model with a malicious one, leading to arbitrary code execution during video rendering.

In the Netdata monitoring agent for Linux, a plugin for custom metrics can be tricked into executing a command that uses the fork() and exit() sequence improperly. This results in an orphaned process that is not correctly tracked in the process tree.
The Thunderbird email client on Linux contains a flaw where a malicious link can trigger the automatic execution of an attachment without further user interaction.
Unexpected behavior in the Docker daemon's plugin handling on Linux allows for a race condition that can be exploited to mount a malicious plugin, achieving container escape and host persistence.
The Federation Service component of an Identity Provider is vulnerable to a deserialization flaw that can be leveraged to disable audit logging for all authentication events.
Docker daemon on Linux improperly validates compressed image layers, enabling attackers to hide malicious code within compressed container images.
Cisco IOS management interface has an authentication bypass that allows remote attackers to create local administrative accounts on network devices.
An application downloaded from the App Store, SecureNotes, can be exploited to load unsigned, non-quarantined libraries from its bundle, bypassing both sandboxing and Gatekeeper protections.

A local privilege escalation in the `sudo` utility, when configured with a specific `NOPASSWD` rule for the `mount` command, allows a user to create a bind mount to hide their malicious process's `/proc` directory.
An information disclosure flaw in the Outlook Data Connector library on Windows could allow a local process to read the contents of other users' mailboxes from memory, facilitating email collection.
The 'InvoicerPlus' application contains a vulnerable .NET assembly that, when processed by InstallUtil, allows for the execution of unsigned malicious scripts.
Improper access control in SystemCenter Sentry on Windows permits a low-privilege user to read configuration files that contain network diagrams and management IP ranges.

Unintended data exposure in in the Windows `CorpAuthSVC` service allows a low-privileged user to query a specific registry key, revealing the configuration and binary paths of all services running under the SYSTEM account.
Cisco ASA firewall CLI interface contains an authentication bypass vulnerability enabling unauthorized access to device commands.
IIS (Internet Information Services) on Windows has a flaw in its ISAPI extension mechanism that allows execution of processes immune to termination signals.
Kubernetes API server's client libraries on Linux can be exploited for domain fronting, enabling malicious pods to communicate with external C2 servers through legitimate CDN endpoints.
A logic flaw allows a malicious process to inject fake log entries into Console.app on macOS, mimicking a system process to report that SIP (System Integrity Protection) is enabled and functional.

The 'LogAnalyticsAgent' for Windows improperly impersonates the user when accessing the Credential Manager, leading to failures where it defaults to reading credentials from the system context instead of the intended user context, causing a credential leak.
The TextEdit application on macOS fails to properly sanitize resource fork data when opening rich text files, leading to a memory corruption issue that can be exploited for code execution.
The macOS App Store verification framework fails to properly validate receipt data, allowing attackers to obtain and redistribute paid applications without purchase.
The Safari Download Manager on macOS does not properly warn users about self-extracting archives, enabling silent execution of malicious code from a crafted .exe file.
An improper authentication mechanism in the Linux daemon cloud-init permits the use of a hardcoded API key to provision new cloud instances without credentials.
Improper input validation in the Windows Event Log Service allows a specially crafted CLSID to be passed to verclsid.exe, leading to a denial of service or potential remote code execution.
In the 'ProFTPD' server on Linux, a post-login script directive can be manipulated by a remote authenticated user to execute arbitrary commands on the host.

An identified issue in the API of a network load balancer allows for unauthenticated submission of RSA public keys. These keys are then trusted for decrypting operational commands, creating a pathway for an encrypted C2 channel.

Improper neutralization of special elements in the 'DockerCompose' YAML parser on Windows allows for command injection when a maliciously crafted `docker-compose.yml` file is processed, leading to arbitrary container execution.
