An improper permission check in the AdminToolkit Pro service on Windows permits an attacker to inject arbitrary commands into the system-level PowerShell profile, achieving persistence and privilege escalation on every new session.

Ubuntu's ufw firewall framework contains a flaw in rule precedence handling that permits attackers to create stealth firewall rules allowing C2 traffic through non-standard ports while appearing to block all unauthorized communication.
An information disclosure flaw exists in the Xorg X server on Linux, allowing any local user to monitor and read the contents of both the PRIMARY and CLIPBOARD selection buffers.
Google Workspace Auth service fails to validate token device bindings, allowing attackers to use stolen application tokens from unauthorized devices to access corporate data.

The WinGuard Service on Windows uses a predictable named pipe for inter-process communication. An attacker can connect to this pipe and send a crafted query to receive a list of all security policies enforced on the system.
The AVShield antivirus solution for Windows does not scan hidden or locked files within the EFI System Partition, providing a safe haven for a bootkit to evade detection.
The vCenter Agent (vpxa) on an ESXi host fails to properly validate user permissions, allowing a compromised guest VM to send commands back to the ESXi host to control other VMs.

In the vCenter Server Appliance, the PostgreSQL backend service 'vpxd' can be manipulated into accepting a client-supplied RSA key for database replication, which could be abused to exfiltrate data or establish a covert channel.
A memory corruption flaw in the NTFS file system driver allows attackers to bypass directory permission checks and enumerate file contents on Windows hosts.
A design flaw in the com.mail.daemon.xpc service's protocol allows for a type confusion attack. By sending a message with an unexpected type, an attacker can corrupt memory and execute code.

DataSync Pro's installer fails to set restrictive permissions on its installation directory 'C:\Program Files\DataSync Pro', allowing a standard user to replace the 'svc_helper.exe' binary and achieve privilege escalation when the service restarts.
Improper input validation in the NetAdmin Remote Console for Windows allows an attacker to cause a stack-based buffer overflow via a long server name field.

A coding defect present in the DataFlow Office suite's add-in management allows a maliciously crafted add-in, delivered from a trusted developer account, to access documents outside its intended sandbox, leveraging the developer's trusted status.

Logical errors within the `SecureLogin` credential management tool could allow an attacker to establish persistence. The tool's attempt to create a benign `emond` rule can be subverted to instead execute a malicious script whenever a user logs in.
The 'SecurePolicy Agent' for Windows improperly processes policy updates, which can be leveraged to push a policy that changes the legal notice to a defaced message.
A bug in DockerWeb-Console allows for read-only access without credentials, exposing a list of all containers, volumes, and networks.
A memory corruption issue in the Windows Shell URL handler can be triggered by a specially crafted spearphishing link, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution after a user clicks the link.
A coding defect present in the Windows-based 'SecureChat.exe' Electron application allows for arbitrary command execution via the `--gpu-launcher` parameter, enabling system binary proxy execution.

The LibreOffice-Collab-Server does not enforce strict role separation. An authenticated user can exploit an API endpoint to grant themselves 'owner' privileges on shared documents, allowing manipulation of other users' access rights.
Microsoft SQL Server on Windows has a flaw in its job scheduling mechanism that permits execution of SQL jobs with error action silently continue.
Improper sanitization of Kerberos principal names in macOS Directory Utility allows for ticket injection attacks.
Dnsmasq service on Linux contains a flaw in DNS response parsing that permits attackers to encode port calculation logic in DNS records for establishing covert communication channels.
Command injection vulnerability in Terraform's AWS provider v3.76.0 allows execution of arbitrary shell commands through manipulated cloud API responses during infrastructure provisioning.

Unsafe behavior in the CoreSync component of Adobe Creative Cloud for macOS allows an attacker to intercept and modify sync profiles. This can be leveraged to use a legitimate cloud storage provider as a dead-drop for C2 instructions.

A memory corruption flaw in the IIS-CoreModule for Windows allows an unauthenticated attacker to cause the w3wp.exe process to terminate via a malformed HTTP/2 request, resulting in a denial of service for hosted websites.

The security architecture of the Ansible Tower AWX web interface allows a user with 'read' permissions on a credential type to alter the conditional access rules that govern its usage, bypassing IP restrictions.

The Word Application COM server is vulnerable to remote code execution via DCOM. By remotely instantiating the `Word.Application` object and using a vulnerable method, an attacker can execute arbitrary macros or code.
An insecure file creation vulnerability in the setuid `SpotlightIndexer` on macOS allows an attacker to leverage a symlink attack to overwrite arbitrary system files.
Windows Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) service reveals version and patch level information in initial handshake packets, facilitating targeted vulnerability assessment.

A software fault within the Ansible Tower AWX web interface allows an authenticated user to bypass job template sandbox restrictions and execute arbitrary Python code on the underlying controller node.
QuantumLeap Router OS fails to correctly filter beacon frames from upstream networks, permitting an attacker to inject an Evil Twin access point onto the local network.
Improper validation in ProcessManager Pro enables privilege escalation by invoking undocumented Windows native APIs without proper access checks.
The Windows User Account Control (UAC) virtualization service fails to validate group modification requests, enabling low-privilege users to add their accounts to the local Administrators group.
A logic error within the launchd service on macOS permits the obfuscation of C2 instructions by embedding commands within non-standard keys of a property list (.plist) file.
An insecure direct object reference (IDOR) vulnerability in the TeamFlow desktop client allows an authenticated user to access private channel messages and files by modifying request parameters.

Shell command injection risks in exists in the VMware vSAN health check service on ESXi. An attacker with network access can exploit this to execute commands, including `rm`, to delete health check logs and other files.

Logical errors within the Windows Security Accounts Manager (SAM) database interaction routine allows an attacker with SYSTEM privileges to decrypt and dump password hashes directly from the registry hive.
The Windows Event Log service contains a type confusion vulnerability that permits arbitrary code execution through specially crafted event log entries.
The Microsoft Office Click-to-Run update script contains a flaw where an attacker can manipulate an environment variable to proxy the execution of a malicious executable.
The Terraform Vault Provider, when used in an IaaS workflow, may write sensitive state information, including credentials, to a local file in plaintext if backend encryption is misconfigured.

Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) flaws in the netfilter_ext kernel module for Linux allows an unprivileged user to create forwarding rules that send specific network traffic to an external IP address, creating a covert data exfiltration channel.

Improper input validation in the Juniper-JunOS-User-Service daemon enables a remote attacker to send a specially crafted packet that adds a new user with a default password to the device's configuration.
The Docsuite Document Security module allows a user with edit permissions on a shared file to grant themselves 'Owner' permissions on the entire containing folder.

The 'AD FS 2.0 Proxy' component on Windows Server 2008 R2 contains a bug that permits the alteration of claim transformation rules via a specially crafted HTTP request, allowing for privilege escalation.

Vertical privilege escalation in in CloudSyncManager for Windows allows a low-privileged user to modify the 'StubPath' value under its Active Setup registry key, achieving persistence and code execution upon any user's logon.
A memory corruption issue in the ESXi hostd daemon enables the encapsulation of non-vSphere management traffic over the management network, creating a covert channel.
API documentation for the 'Metricly' SaaS analytics platform contains a functional, albeit example, API key that grants read-only access to live customer data.
The TypeScript compiler (tsc.exe) does not validate the 'plugins' array in a tsconfig.json file, allowing an attacker to specify a malicious module path for execution.

The vsftpd FTP server on Linux, when configured to allow file uploads, does not sanitize filenames with trailing spaces. An attacker could upload a file named 'list.txt ' which is actually a binary, and a client system connecting to the FTP server might be tricked into executing it.

Simultaneous execution threads in the macOS 'Spotlight Indexer' can be leveraged to corrupt its database, forcing a re-index that the attacker can control to exclude files related to other malware, effectively hiding them from defenders and competitors.

An improper input validation flaw in the ProFTPD daemon on Linux permits an authenticated attacker to conceal malicious commands within FTP PASV response packets, enabling abuse of the application layer protocol for data exfiltration.

The firmware update process for AxiomShield Series firewalls improperly validates digital signatures. An attacker on the local network can load a malicious firmware image containing a backdoor that alters the NAT table to allow unauthorized traffic flows.

Buffer bounds violations in the 'LogParser' driver (LogParser.sys) allows an adversary on the system to execute kernel code, which can then be used to clear the system's audit policies using 'auditpol /clear /y'.
OpenConnect VPN daemon on Linux contains a heap overflow that can be exploited to bypass credential validation and establish persistent remote access.

The macOS CoreMailKit framework contains a use-after-free bug related to IMAP response parsing. A maliciously crafted email processed by a service could trigger this flaw, leading to arbitrary code execution and the potential for a persistent C2 channel over IMAP.

A vulnerability in the macOS LaunchD service allows a process to modify its own executable file while it is running. An attacker can leverage this to execute a tool, and after it has been analyzed by security software, overwrite the file on disk with a version that has its static indicators removed, ensuring subsequent executions are undetected.
A local privilege escalation vulnerability in the MacOptimizer utility allows a low-privileged user to modify the system-wide TCC database, enabling microphone access for unauthorized software.
An implementation error in the Okta Identity Management service API could allow an attacker to obtain a user's password hash, which can then be cracked offline to recover the plaintext password.
The Palo Alto Networks Panorama management console fails to validate system image integrity, allowing the distribution of modified images to managed devices.
The 'OpenDirectory' service on a Linux system fails to restrict access to trust objects, allowing any authenticated user to enumerate external directory trusts and their associated domains.
A local user can gain elevated privileges on macOS by exploiting a flaw in the FileSync-Master application, which improperly uses the AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges API.
A memory corruption vulnerability in the macOS mDNSResponder allows a local application to poison the system's DNS cache with records pointing to an adversary's DNS server.
Flawed business logic in the 'QuickDeploy' application service, running as SYSTEM, permits any authenticated user to add a startup script to a GPO on a domain controller via a named pipe.

An insecure default configuration in 'DevStudio Code Helper' sets weak permissions on its installation directory, which contains an SSP DLL. This allows a standard user to perform a DLL hijacking attack for persistence and credential dumping.
An internal defect in the TLO HelpDesk application permits privilege escalation by abusing the CMSTP utility to execute commands from a maliciously formatted INF file.
A coding defect present in the 'CodeSign Helper' tool for macOS leaks the developer's code signing certificate details to the system log in plaintext during a failed signing attempt.

Unauthorized access level increase in in PrintCorp Universal Driver for Windows allows a low-privileged user to register a malicious port monitor. An attacker can exploit this by crafting a malicious DLL and invoking the vulnerable configuration utility, leading to code execution as SYSTEM at boot.

The `vmtoolsd.exe` process, part of VMware Tools, is vulnerable to a token manipulation flaw in its guest-to-host command execution feature. An attacker can provide a stolen token to create a process on the host with elevated privileges.
The NetCore Gateway device's DHCP client can be manipulated to accept a malicious 'bootfile-name' option, forcing it to download and execute a compromised OS image from an unauthorized TFTP server.

Insecure direct object reference in the `ContainerExec Proxy` service could allow an attacker to craft a URL that, when clicked by a developer, initiates a command execution session in a privileged container.
An insecure API endpoint in the Azure App Service custom domain module allows for the modification of the domain verification HTML file, facilitating a defacement of the verification page.

The FileVaultPlus encryption tool's WMI provider has an improper access control vulnerability, enabling a low-privileged user to set up a persistent event subscription that decrypts files upon a specific trigger.
Data leakage occurs in in the FreeIPA client on Linux allows an attacker to access the SSSD cache database, leading to the exposure of cached domain credentials.

A race condition in the 'DataSync Pro' service for Windows allows an attacker to replace a legitimate Office template with a malicious one after it has been validated but before it is loaded by the application.
Logical errors within Azure Key Vault access control permits the creation of managed identities with excessive permissions through the REST API's role assignment endpoint.
Windows Remote Desktop Service contains a vulnerability in its module loading routine that allows attackers to execute arbitrary DLLs on target systems.
A cross-site scripting (XSS)-like vulnerability exists within the HTML rendering of an Outlook form, allowing script execution in the context of the application.
A logic flaw in the CloudFabric Network Controller permits the modification of network ACLs for virtual machines, bypassing network segmentation controls.
Privilege elevation flaws in in the `WinKVM Virtual HID Driver` for Windows allows a low-privilege process to send keystroke injections to the login screen, bypassing OS-level security controls.

The systemd-journald service on Linux fails to properly validate IPC requests, which could allow a local attacker to cause a temporary hang and then attach to the service using ptrace for malicious code execution.
Logical errors within the `Azure AD Conditional Access` service allows a modified trust relationship to bypass MFA requirements by altering the claim issuance policy of a federated domain.

A programmatic error in the serverless function `create-user` in a 'Firebase' backend allows attackers to bypass email verification steps, directly establishing verified email accounts for malicious use.
A logic flaw in Microsoft Exchange hybrid configurations permits a local user to create an inbox rule that syncs to Exchange Online and hides security alert emails.

The TimeMachine Analyzer service on macOS lacks proper input validation on its backup verification feature, which can be flooded with requests to verify extremely large backup sets, exhausting memory.

The Windows-based PartnerLink Client fails to validate SSL certificates when connecting to partner update servers, making it susceptible to man-in-the-middle attacks that could reveal a list of trusted partners.
The EnterpriseID Provider Console lacks proper rate limiting on password reset endpoints, enabling credential stuffing attacks against dashboard access controls.

An out-of-bounds write flaw was discovered in the `EnterpriseFileSync` application for Windows, caused by improper handling of memory by the linked `zlib` library during the archival of large files for syncing.
Improper locking mechanisms in the macOS WindowServer process permits a sandboxed application to elevate privileges and log all GUI input events system-wide.

A software fault within the web-based management interface of network switches allows an authenticated attacker to alter the device's RADIUS shared secret, thereby compromising the network authentication process.
The 'Palo Alto Networks Dynamic Gateway' implementation of port knocking is vulnerable to a sequence replay attack if the session key is not properly rotated.

The macOS LaunchDaemon Proxy Service does not properly validate the origin of configuration updates, allowing a malicious process to set up a multi-hop proxy chain for all system-wide network traffic.
Unintended data exposure in in the F5 BIG-IP iControl REST API allows a user with limited privileges to retrieve the configuration for any virtual server on the system.

The SonicWall SonicOS's management gateway fails to validate the key length parameter for its internal SSL certificates, allowing an attacker to generate a new certificate with a 512-bit key, weakening access encryption.

Unexpected behavior in the 'SentinelOne Endpoint Security' agent's password policy enforcement module could be exploited to register an arbitrary DLL as a password filter, leading to credential theft on the local machine.

Reflected or stored XSS flaws in vulnerability in the web interface of the 'AmplifyGrid' SaaS platform allows an attacker to inject malicious scripts into profile bio fields. This could be used to steal session cookies from other operators, compromising their managed social media personas.
Unexpected behavior in the Windows Event Forwarding service allows an attacker with network access to craft a special subscription that results in writing a malicious script to a PowerShell profile.
macOS Mail.app fails to properly scan self-extracting archives, enabling attackers to deliver compressed malware that automatically executes upon extraction.

The API-Server-Pro for Kubernetes has a vulnerability where debug logging is inadvertently enabled in production builds. This logs all API requests, including bearer tokens and secret data, to a world-readable file on the control plane node.
The 'Netlogon' service on a Domain Controller can be forced into a state where it leaks information about the GPOs being processed during user authentication, observable through a packet capture.
The Dock application on macOS can be tampered with to include a malicious LC_LOAD_DYLIB entry, which will be executed whenever the Dock process restarts.
A race condition (TOCTOU) in the Microsoft Office startup sequence allows a benign DLL path in the registry to be swapped for a malicious one just before loading.

A buffer overflow exists in the webcache-proxy daemon on Linux when processing Base64-encoded authentication headers. An overly long, encoded string can overflow a buffer and execute obfuscated machine code.

The Windows Print Spooler service contains a memory corruption vulnerability that can be leveraged to deploy malicious code in the context of the SYSTEM user, enabling the deletion of spooler shadow files and print job logs.

An improper access control issue in the LogHog daemon for Linux allows any user on the system to create files in /var/log/loghog/tmp, a path often excluded from file integrity monitoring for performance reasons, facilitating the hiding of malicious payloads.
A critical weakness within the CloudSphere DNS management service permits the creation of records pointing to infrastructure in regions that are supposed to be firewalled off from public access.
An identified issue in the 'SecureBootGuard' UEFI implementation, caused by a hardware supply chain issue on Windows motherboards, allows for the booting of untrusted operating systems.
Improper input validation in the libclipboard-utils library on Linux allows an attacker to corrupt memory and leak sensitive information, including clipboard data, from other processes.

A programmatic error in the macOS CoreAuthentication framework allows an attacker with physical access to bypass the user account lockout mechanism, facilitating a local brute-force attack on the login password.

The SpotlightIndexer on macOS fails to properly sanitize data read from a custom com.apple.thirdparty extended attribute. An adversary can embed a malicious script into this attribute, leading to arbitrary code execution when the file is indexed while keeping the main file content legitimate.
The InnovateCAD Pro build system, utilizing JamPlus, fails to sanitize build script commands, enabling a malicious `.jam` file to execute unauthorized code on Windows.
The macOS Spotlight indexing process (mds) contains a flaw that allows a local user to alter permissions of its index files by manipulating metadata, leading to system-wide search result corruption.

A programmatic error in the 'Windows Server Failover Clustering' (WSFC) service allows for the relay of NTLM authentication captured through an LLMNR poisoning attack, potentially leading to a cluster takeover.

Improper input validation in the ESXi Host Management Agent permits an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary commands, which can be used to invoke the encryption process for all virtual machine disks (.vmdk) on a host.

A race condition in the systemd-locale-helper service on Linux could allow an unprivileged user to read the locale configuration of another user's session during a system update, aiding in location profiling.
Microsoft Excel's spreadsheet window implementation allows EWM hijacking for arbitrary code execution.

CodeRepository client for Windows stores Git credentials and tokens in plaintext within HKCU\Software\CodeRepository\Credentials, allowing attackers to access version control systems via Registry extraction.
An identified issue in the Windows API function SetTimeProviderInformation allows an unprivileged process to register a time provider due to a missing security check, leading to persistent execution.

Improper encoding of user output in vulnerability in the 'SecureLink VPN Gateway' for Windows allows an attacker to inject a malicious script into the login page, enabling the capture of user credentials before they are sent for authentication.

DataSync Pro for Windows improperly encrypts database connection strings and stores them in HKCU\Software\DataSync\Connections, allowing local attackers to decrypt and obtain sensitive database credentials from the Registry.

An anti-debugging bypass exists in the macOS Finder application. It checks for the existence of a debugger by looking for specific files in `/tmp`, but this check can be defeated by pre-creating those files.

The 'Citrix Workspace' app on Windows contains a flaw that allows an attacker to modify the launch command for the Magnifier utility (Magnify.exe), achieving persistence through accessibility feature abuse.
The 'ReportGenerator' application fails to sanitize file names before using them in a rundll32.exe command, which can lead to arbitrary command execution.

The Azure DevOps Web Frontend fails to properly sanitize project descriptions, allowing stored XSS that can be used to steal session cookies from administrators viewing public project pages, facilitating account takeover.

Improper encoding of user output in vulnerability in the web-based configuration panel of the Asterisk Call Manager on Linux could be used to inject JavaScript that initiates a phone call to a malicious number when an administrator views the call logs.

An information disclosure vulnerability in the 'CloudFoundry' BOSH stemcell for AWS leaks instance metadata, including IAM role credentials, which can then be used by an attacker on an adjacent VM to perform S3 object discovery.
A flaw in the Windows KernelDataFilter.sys driver allows a low-privileged process to register a callback that hides its process and associated threads from Task Manager and other security tools.
The SANBackupTool on ESXi does not validate the host key during an SCP-based backup retrieval, allowing an attacker to intercept the connection and inject a malicious tool onto the ESXi host.
The BuildKit build context handler is vulnerable to a directory traversal attack, allowing a malicious Dockerfile to place an executable in the final image that runs upon container deployment.
An insufficient bounds check in the 'Notes' application allows for code execution when opening a note with a maliciously crafted resource fork.
Launchd process on macOS can be exploited for timing-based sandbox evasion, allowing malware to differentiate between production and analysis environments.
A heap-based buffer overflow in the 'GCPBucketBrute-NG' tool can be triggered by loading a specially crafted wordlist, allowing for arbitrary code execution on the attacker's machine.
An improper certificate validation flaw in macOS's hardware trust store allows attackers to introduce malicious devices with forged certificates that are accepted as trusted.
Logical errors within the macOS 'SecureTrade' framework allows a malicious application to intercept and alter transaction data sent to financial APIs, enabling theft.
Improper locking mechanisms in the Linux 'ss' (socket statistics) utility can be exploited to read connection information from processes owned by other users.
Unsafe behavior in the Windows UpdateValidator.exe component allows an attacker to bypass command-line restrictions by injecting commands into a validation string.
The 'ansible' pull mode on Linux agents can be exploited if a malicious playbook is used, as it may contain tasks that modify the /etc/sudoers file to grant the ansible user persistent sudo access.

A type confusion vulnerability in the JavaScript engine of the IronGate router's web interface can be exploited to achieve remote code execution with root privileges, enabling the device to be used as a launchpad for attacks.

A coding defect present in a cloud provider's 'CloudLoad Balancer' configuration API permits an attacker to query the backend pool configurations of all load balancers in a region, revealing internal services and their IPs.

A logic error within Samba's filename handling on Linux servers could allow an attacker to distribute masqueraded executables. When a client system accesses a file named 'readme.doc ' from a Samba share, the client's OS may execute the file instead of opening it with the expected application, due to improper sanitization of the trailing space.
A heap-based buffer overflow in the Windows Print Spooler service allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a crafted print job.

A vulnerability in the Windows Update Delivery Optimization Service allows an attacker to abuse HTTP requests by embedding malicious commands within the `User-Agent` header from an infected client, potentially enabling a covert C2 channel.

Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) flaws in the Windows Event Log Service could be exploited to delete entire event channels, including the 'Microsoft-Windows-TerminalServices-RemoteConnectionManager/Operational' log which records network connections.
Race condition in macOS login process permits temporary modification of login hooks during user authentication, enabling persistence mechanisms.

An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists in the 'UserMigration' utility. It allows a standard user to configure a silent process exit monitor for `csrss.exe`, which can be abused to hijack the execution flow with SYSTEM privileges upon process termination.

The 'vsftpd' daemon on certain Linux distributions is configured with 'delay_failed_login' set to 0, which removes the intended delay between failed attempts and makes it ideal for password spraying attacks.
FortiOS firewall's CLI interface fails to validate input in diagnostic commands, enabling shell injection for authenticated administrators.
An out-of-bounds read in the 'PE-Packer-Extreme' for Windows can leak portions of the developer's source code into the packed executable.
A software fault within the Zoom client for Windows allows an attacker to use process doppelgänging to execute malicious code within the Zoom process.
The VMware vCenter Log Forwarder stores its Git repository credentials in plaintext, allowing an attacker with access to the host to reconfigure it for data exfiltration to a new repository.
The 'logshipper' service on Linux contains a race condition in its DNS resolver. This can be exploited to alter the data used to calculate the destination IP for its C2 channel.

The Samba file server daemon on Linux, when configured with `vfs objects`, can be manipulated through a path traversal flaw to execute a client-side command that launches a hidden GUI application on a connected Windows machine.

A server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in the 'MacroRender' engine for Confluence Data Center SaaS enables attackers to access internal network resources, potentially discovering and exfiltrating files linked within Confluence pages.
The 'net.fileflow.syncdaemon' for macOS fails to validate ownership of its configuration file, enabling a local user to alter the Launch Daemon's behavior for persistence.
The 'ShopFast' e-commerce SaaS platform improperly encrypts its database backups at rest, allowing an attacker with access to cloud storage to decrypt and exfiltrate customer financial data.
An improper permissions vulnerability in PowerPoint's registry handler allows a low-privileged user to register a malicious startup add-in.

The AutoUpdater service on macOS has an improper permission validation flaw when processing update instructions from a com.apple.update extended attribute. An attacker can leverage this for privilege escalation by embedding a malicious payload in an application's metadata.

A command injection flaw in the logging configuration of Cisco IOS XR allows an authenticated attacker to execute arbitrary commands, including `clear logging`, to wipe the device's syslog buffer and remove indicators of compromise.
A Python-based content discovery tool 'PyDiscover' on Linux is vulnerable to deserialization attacks when loading a maliciously crafted wordlist file.

Concurrency issues within the Windows DataLossPreventionAgent during initialization can be exploited to inject a malicious 'StubPath' into an Active Setup registry key, leading to persistent execution of unauthorized code at logon.
VMware Tools for Windows includes a 'VGAuth' service with a flaw that permits reconfiguration to read policy updates from a public Trello board card, enabling one-way command and control.
Docker daemon's plugin loading mechanism on Linux can be abused to escape container isolation by loading malicious shared objects.
Windows DataSyncSvc fails to properly validate SSL certificates when uploading data, enabling man-in-the-middle attacks that redirect exfiltrated data to malicious text storage sites.
Improper neutralization of script-related HTML tags in the Linux Epiphany browser allows for cross-site scripting attacks from a maliciously modified cloud storage script.

The Microsoft Remote Desktop Services client fails to sanitize GPP-defined connection settings, which could allow an attacker to embed a script that exfiltrates the decrypted password for the RDP session.

The `apache2-mod_fingerprint` module on Linux contains a use-after-free vulnerability when processing malformed client-side scripts, which could be leveraged to force the server to report a spoofed server-side environment to clients.

A lack of proper input validation in the StreamWeaver LB's RADIUS client component allows an attacker to manipulate authentication responses, enabling the patching of the local authentication database with a hardcoded entry.
The Windows 'Active Directory Replication' service can be abused by an authenticated low-privileged user to request replication of domain credentials, facilitating credential harvesting.
A misconfiguration in the CloudIdentity Agent for Windows causes it to ignore the Kerberos preauthentication requirement when syncing accounts, making them vulnerable to AS-REP roasting on-premise.
The 'AgileTrack' SaaS platform's search functionality indexes private ticket comments, making any credentials, such as database passwords, searchable and viewable by any user across the organization.
A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in Collaborate Docs allows an attacker to inject a malicious spearphishing link into a shared document that executes in the context of another user.

A vulnerability exists where Gatekeeper only checks the code signature of the primary executable in an app bundle, ignoring embedded frameworks. An attacker can modify an embedded framework with malicious code to bypass the trust control.
CodeFlow IDE, a popular development environment, fails to sanitize project references, allowing an attacker to include a path to a malicious payload that is executed on build.

Active Directory Domain Services contains a null pointer dereference in the LDAP authentication module that can be exploited by sending malformed bind requests, resulting in a persistent crash of the directory service.
A logic error within the checksum calculation for firmware updates on Brocade Fibre Channel switches allows an attacker to flash a tampered image that passes integrity checks, leading to persistence.
CloudScale SaaS Dashboard fails to properly sanitize user input in search functionality, allowing attackers to execute JavaScript and harvest session tokens from other users.

A use-after-free vulnerability in the Windows SecureAV application's network monitoring component can be triggered by sending a malformed packet filter definition. An attacker could exploit this to install a persistent socket filter that launches a reverse shell when triggered by a C&C beacon.

An identified issue in the VMkernel network stack of ESXi allows for the crafting of special VXLAN packets that can bypass internal firewalls and be used to encapsulate C2 traffic within a legitimate overlay protocol.
Buffer bounds violations in the SocialBoost Scheduler desktop application could be exploited to leak stored social media API credentials from memory, resulting in account compromise.

The browser-based client for GitForge SaaS inadvertently exposes personal access tokens in the browser's local storage, making them susceptible to theft via XSS and subsequent repository data exfiltration.

Unsafe behavior in the UEFI HTTP Boot service allows a man-in-the-middle to inject a malicious bootloader. This bootloader could be designed to send a unique identifier to a public Pastebin, which the attacker then monitors via threat intelligence aggregation platforms to confirm infection and analysis.

The SentinelEye Log Analyzer client for Windows fails to properly sanitize data received from its backend server, enabling a man-in-the-middle to alter security event details displayed to security analysts.
The OktaIdentityBridge on-premise agent lacks proper authorization checks on its policy modification endpoint, enabling a compromised service account to add a new, malicious IdP to the Okta tenant.
A memory corruption issue in the Windows WinAuth Broker can be triggered to skip the account lockout check, permitting an adversary to continue guessing a user's password indefinitely.

The 'Kubernetes' external-dns controller can be manipulated by an attacker with cluster access to create DNS records for an attacker-owned domain in a company's cloud DNS zone, facilitating a supply chain attack.
An insecure method in the 'Windows Event Log Service' allows an attacker to grant themselves write access to the Security event log file (Security.evtx), enabling log tampering.
An insecure DLL loading mechanism in `Phoenix ERP Client` can be exploited to initiate a process hollowing attack, where the attacker replaces the legitimate process memory with a malicious payload.
The Python Pip tool fails to validate the integrity of packages downloaded over unencrypted HTTP, allowing an attacker to serve a malicious Python package.
A heap-based overflow condition in the command-line interface of 'FirewallPolicyManager' on network devices can be exploited to execute a reverse shell, granting full control.

An identified issue in the `TokenService` API of the `OneLogin` identity provider allows for the renewal of expired refresh tokens, granting attackers persistent authenticated access to user accounts.
Kubernetes API server on Linux contains a flaw where service account tokens can be forged by exploiting weak certificate signing processes.
vCenter Server's management interface permits protocol spoofing, allowing attackers to disguise malicious commands as legitimate vSphere operations.
A server-side request forgery vulnerability in SaaSAdmin Management Console allows attackers to scan internal network resources and access restricted dashboard endpoints.

The Dell OS10 network operating system improperly validates packages installed via its extension framework, permitting the installation of a signed but malicious package that patches the core OS to enable port knocking.

The Postfix mail server's `postfix-cert` utility is vulnerable to command injection when processing a certificate filename, allowing for the installation of a malicious certificate into the system's trust store.

An exploitable bug in the Messages for Business framework on macOS allows a malicious third-party service to send specially crafted messages that can spoof the sender's identity, facilitating trust-based spearphishing.

The Auth0Mule integration plugin for MuleSoft contains a vulnerability that allows an attacker with tenant admin rights to change the JWT signing algorithm from RS256 to HS256, enabling token forgery.
A memory leak in Azure Key Vault's caching mechanism exposes recently accessed secrets to other tenants in multi-tenant deployments.
A race condition in SystemInfoDaemon service enables attackers to obtain process information from other users' sessions on Linux systems, including sensitive applications and their arguments.

A software fault within the Windows Task Scheduler allows a task running as a service account to be manipulated, leading to the disclosure of that account's credentials for use in a silver ticket attack.
A parsing vulnerability in the 'CapIt' screen recorder's project file format allows an executable, 'project.cap.exe', to be embedded and opened as if it were a regular project file.
Safari on macOS automatically opens 'safe' file types after download; a logic error allows a malicious .app bundle masquerading as an image to be executed upon completion of the download.

An algorithm implementation error in the `LambdaAutoScaler` for a cloud provider allows for the injection of malicious code into the scaling process, which is then triggered by an EC2 instance launch event.

Predictable resource identification in in the SecureStorage Kernel Driver allows an unauthenticated user to read the encryption key from the Policy.vpol file, facilitating the decryption of .vcrd files within the Windows Credential Locker.
GlobalPayroll Processor's help system does not correctly sandbox VBS scripts embedded in .chm documentation, leading to code execution through hh.exe.
The QuickPDF Converter application uses hh.exe to display license information in a .chm file, but a vulnerability allows this file to contain and execute malicious code.
An insufficient permission check in GitForge Enterprise's webhook API allows a low-privilege user to retrieve the contents of private source code repositories and issue metadata.
The SecureSphere VPN Client for Windows includes an outdated Lua library vulnerable to code execution through a maliciously crafted connection profile.

An improper validation issue in LaunchServices on macOS permits the execution of applications without a valid code signature if nested within an already-approved application bundle, subverting Gatekeeper controls.

A memory corruption flaw in a third-party macOS kernel extension `ThunderboltKext.kext`, which manages Thunderbolt adapters, allows an attacker to redirect network traffic for exfiltration over the Thunderbolt bus.
Unexpected behavior in Windows Active Directory Domain Controllers allows attackers to extract and reuse Kerberos tickets from the ticket cache, enabling persistent lateral movement.
A flaw in the 'OpenAMQPd' daemon on Linux allows for AMQP message forwarding without proper authentication, which can be abused to create a hidden communication path for malicious actors.
An information disclosure bug in the `locationd` daemon on macOS allows a local, unprivileged application to read the region-specific regulatory settings.
A local privilege escalation flaw was identified in the SystemUpdater utility, where an attacker can manipulate a world-writable file executed after an AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges prompt.

Improper encoding of user output in vulnerability in the CollabDocs Online office suite allows an attacker to inject a script that steals a user's session cookie, granting full access to their documents.

A deserialization vulnerability in the 'FinanceCore' service on Windows could allow an attacker to inject a serialized .NET object into a database, which when deserialized by a stored procedure, executes arbitrary code.

A memory corruption issue in the macOS CoreAudio daemon allows an attacker to execute code with root privileges and install a hook that removes any other kernel extensions or launch agents not on a pre-defined allowlist.

The BitLocker Recovery Agent for Windows contains a flaw in its handling of exceptionally long file paths within the Active Setup 'StubPath', leading to a stack-based buffer overflow and code execution at logon.

The 'EnterpriseDB' database service for Windows is vulnerable to IFEO injection. Due to weak ACLs on its registry key, an attacker can set a debugger for the database process (`edb.exe`), resulting in code execution with the service's high-privilege account.

In the Windows 'WinDefenderCore', a quarantine bypass vulnerability allows an attacker to restore a file and simultaneously apply the hidden attribute. This enables malware to re-emerge on the system in a hidden state, preventing it from being seen in Explorer or scanned by default AV profiles.

Improper access control in the Linux 'openLDAP-Proxy-Daemon' enables unauthenticated attackers to issue LDAP queries that expose all user attributes and hashed credentials stored in the directory service database.

A weakness in the Windows `Dnscache` service allows a non-administrative user to query for its internal service-linked list, indirectly revealing other services that depend on DNS resolution functionality.
Container orchestration platform Portainer exposes its API without proper authentication, allowing full cluster control from external networks.
The AWS IAM service fails to properly validate session duration parameters in AssumeRole requests, allowing users to extend temporary elevated access beyond configured time limits.
Information leakage flaws in in TerraformMaster causes it to store sensitive provider credentials in plaintext within `.tfstate` files, which may then be checked into public version control.
The snapd service on Ubuntu Linux contains a bug that permits a snap package to display a misleading 'Requires permissions to install' GUI prompt, tricking the user into providing their password.
Windows File Explorer's compatibility shim can be abused to bypass security controls via malicious shim database manipulation.
The macOS 'Keychain-Cli' third-party tool exposes the master password when used with the '--unlock' flag, as the command is saved to the user's shell history.

An identified issue in the Windows Active Desktop Service (ActiveDesktopSvc.exe) allows a low-privileged user to perform an arbitrary file write, enabling the replacement of the system-wide desktop wallpaper with a malicious image.
The FinanceDataProcessor service on Windows fails to invalidate old TGS tickets, allowing an attacker to capture a previously requested ticket for its SPN and attempt to crack it offline.
Windows Defender's quarantine management system fails to properly display filenames containing RTLO characters, making it difficult for administrators to identify quarantined threats.
A pre-installed system image for macOS devices from a specific manufacturer was found to contain pre-installed malware, representing a supply chain attack at the factory.
A memory corruption issue in the macOS `UserEventAgent` framework can be leveraged to bypass sandboxing restrictions and execute `launchctl list` to view all user and system agents.
Privilege elevation flaws in in the 'OpenNebula' 'Sunstone' GUI allows a regular user to create a 'onegate' service token that can be used to execute arbitrary commands on any virtual machine.
The 'FileVaultHelper' utility contains a flaw where it can be instructed to add a malicious binary to the login items list before the disk is decrypted, ensuring execution early in the boot process.
vCenter Server contains a vulnerability in its tunneling service that permits attackers to encapsulate malicious vSphere Client traffic within legitimate management protocols.
The `CredentialVault Service` on Windows exposes a debug endpoint that does not properly authenticate requests, allowing an attacker to trigger a full credential dump in plaintext.
A vulnerability in the `SafariSafe Extension` for macOS allows a malicious website to spoof the browser's download UI, tricking a user into opening and executing a disguised malicious application.

OS command injection flaws in in the systemd-network-helper unit file template on Linux could allow a local user to create a new privileged process by injecting parameters into the service start command.

An insecure file permission issue in the `Third-Party-AV-VIB` installation process allows an attacker to modify the installed antivirus definitions, effectively creating a persistent denial-of-service or malware injection point.
The 'HealthConnect' patient portal's 'share records' function contains an IDOR, permitting an attacker to view and modify another patient's data and account details.
LibreOffice Calc fails to properly sanitize content in spreadsheet formula fields, enabling an attacker to execute arbitrary LibreOffice Basic scripts via the interpreter.
Improper CORS configuration in the web UI of ApexEdge Firmware allows a malicious website visited by an administrator to make authenticated requests on their behalf, leading to device compromise.
The 'iCloud Business Portal' on macOS contains a reflected XSS vulnerability that, when exploited, can be used to steal session cookies and access private company announcements and staff directories.

An exploitable bug in the macOS TCC framework fails to validate the parent process of a permission request, allowing an adversary to bypass application-specific guardrails and gain access to protected resources.
A compromised hardware supply chain for 'AuthenKey' fingerprint readers on Windows laptops allows for the replay of previously captured biometric data.
The `os_image` verification routine in CoreWLAN switches uses a hardcoded, static key, allowing an attacker to craft a malicious system image that appears legitimate during the update process.
A memory corruption issue in the DevOps Toolkit for macOS can be leveraged to unlock paid extensions and obtain powerful infrastructure-as-code tools.
Microsoft 365's legacy authentication protocols can be exploited to bypass MFA, allowing attackers to use compromised valid accounts.
The Calendar.app application on macOS does not adequately restrict AppleScript execution from event alarms, which can be exploited for persistence.
A symbolic link attack in the Linux login-banner-utils package during system startup can be exploited to overwrite the /etc/issue.net file with a defacing message shown before SSH login.

The security architecture of Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) allows for the permanent disabling of ETW trace sessions through scripting, enabling an adversary to impair the collection of defense indicators before execution.

The UniId Connect API, an identity provider service, improperly validates scopes on a user lookup function, enabling an attacker to discover all groups a target user belongs to, including privileged ones.
A vulnerable third-party kernel driver for Windows allows an attacker to encode data into its control IOCTLs using a custom, non-standard character map, hiding malicious instructions.

An internal defect in the Windows Removable Storage Service allows a low-privilege process to bypass group policy restrictions and write arbitrary data to any connected USB mass storage device, enabling data exfiltration.
The CollabDocs online editor's document sharing feature uses sequential IDs for shared links, making it trivial for an attacker to brute force access to private documents.
macOS XProtect's signature validation mechanism contains a flaw allowing attackers to modify malware signatures and remove detection indicators for their tools.
A flaw in the 'ServerlessFuncHost' platform allows an attacker to upload a malicious function package that persists and exfiltrates data upon invocation.
macOS Gatekeeper's trusted file remover can be bypassed by a malicious application, allowing it to delete its own quarantine extended attributes, thus removing evidence of its download source.
A permissions misconfiguration on an 'ObjectStoreS3' bucket allows any unauthenticated user to upload objects, enabling the hosting of malware for later distribution.
Flawed business logic in the macOS FinderSync Extension allows an attacker to inject keystrokes into the Spotlight search bar to launch a malicious application or script.

An improper access control vulnerability in the 'System Center Operations Manager' (SCOM) management pack for Active Directory allows read-only operators to discover and map the entire forest trust topology.
The Windows Netlogon service has a component that allows a non-administrative user to manipulate internal communications of the `Net.exe` utility to obtain a full local user list.
Improper input validation in the DataMover service for Windows allows an attacker to trigger a crash and dump process memory, which may contain the service account's password hash.

A flaw in macOS's Event Monitor daemon (emond) can be exploited for persistence. An attacker can create a malicious rule file in `/etc/emond.d/rules/` that triggers a script to execute with root privileges during the 'system startup' event.
The DeviceAttestationService on macOS contains a logic error that allows a remote access hardware device with a revoked certificate to be successfully paired with the system.

The REST API for CloudCore Router firmware lacks proper access controls on the `/api/v1/system/status` endpoint. Unauthenticated requests to this URL will return the device model, serial number, and current firmware version.

In 'StreamTime' media player for macOS, a bundled helper process improperly loads `librenderer.dylib` from a relative path. This allows an adversary on the system to hijack the library and execute arbitrary code within the context of the application.

The installation script 'install.bat' for 'DevTools Suite' uses unquoted environment variables. A low-privileged user can create a malicious file in the system path to achieve code execution with installer privileges.

InnovateDS's `TrustForge Federation Server` does not sanitize user-supplied metadata URLs when establishing a new trust, allowing a man-in-the-middle attack to inject a malicious identity provider configuration.
The OpenSSH daemon on Linux systems has a double-free vulnerability in its key exchange handling, enabling remote attackers to crash the SSH service and deny secure shell access to the system.
A software fault within the `Microsoft Word` for Mac document parser allows a malicious document to embed and execute a script that installs a root certificate from a remote location.
Stack-based buffer overflow in macOS loginwindow daemon when parsing LogoutHook paths from plist files.

MediaEncoder Pro on Windows is vulnerable to search order hijacking because it relies on an unqualified call to `reg.exe` for importing codec settings. This permits a local attacker to execute untrusted binaries by placing a malicious `reg.exe` in the application's directory.

Improper permissions on the `httpd-guard` binary on Linux allow any user to modify its code. As the binary is setuid root to bind to privileged ports, an attacker can inject malicious code to gain root shell access.

An insecure deserialization vulnerability in the WebHostify control panel allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code, leading to the takeover of shared hosting accounts and the acquisition of web server infrastructure.
A coding defect present in the Windows Workstation Service (wkssvc.dll) allows attackers to spawn network authentication processes with spoofed parent PIDs, facilitating lateral movement evasion.

Gatekeeper on macOS is susceptible to a time-of-check-to-time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition, allowing a signed application to be replaced with a malicious executable after its signature has been validated.
A heap-based buffer overflow in the OpenSSH daemon (sshd) on Linux can be exploited to corrupt the Global Offset Table, allowing an attacker to hijack VDSO syscalls and achieve remote code execution.
A component within the macOS System Preferences application `Users & Groups` pane has a flaw that allows a non-administrator to view a list of hidden administrative accounts.

Improper access control in the Microsoft Identity Manager (MIM) synchronization service allows for the modification of the GALSync trust relationship, facilitating unauthorized data replication between forests.
The `CoreLocale.framework` on macOS contains an information disclosure flaw that allows a sandboxed application to bypass privacy controls and query the underlying system language identifier.
In systemd, a flaw allows a malicious shared object to be embedded within the .data section of an ELF binary, circumventing signature checks and causing code execution upon launch.

The `CoreAuthAgent` on Windows fails to properly sanitize input to a debug API, allowing a low-privileged user to specify `lsass.exe` as a target process for a memory dump, leading to credential theft.

Vertical privilege escalation in in the Windows Update service (wuauserv) allows a low-privilege attacker to install a malicious 'security patch' that disables the SMBv1 protocol, preventing other threat actors from using it for lateral movement.

Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) flaws in the Windows Object Manager can be leveraged to achieve Direct Kernel Object Manipulation (DKOM), enabling a rootkit to unlink its processes from the active process list.

The 'ClientPortal' software for Windows suffers from a path traversal vulnerability that can be exploited to read files on the system, including a local database containing information about business resellers and distributors.
The OpenVPN client for Windows does not properly isolate its DHCP configuration process, allowing a malicious DHCP server on the local network to overwrite the VPN's DNS settings.

A lack of input sanitization in the 'LeadStream' CRM's advanced search form allows for a time-based blind SQL injection attack, enabling an attacker to slowly extract all customer email addresses and contact details.

Improper neutralization of special elements in the 'CodeGuardian Suite' on Windows enables command injection during the certificate generation process, leading to the creation of unauthorized code signing certificates.

The AuthNexus Identity Provider API endpoint for listing service principals does not properly enforce scope validation, enabling a low-privilege application to obtain a complete inventory of all registered SaaS services.
A denial-of-service in the ESXi SFCD-CORE storage filter can be triggered to cause a kernel panic, effectively stopping all storage I/O and hosted services.
The AWS CLI tool on Linux systems stores credentials in world-readable files when using certain configuration options, enabling local privilege escalation and cloud account compromise.

HyperTerminal NG, a Windows terminal emulator, has a flaw where pasted text can be interpreted as a command sequence without explicit user confirmation. This could be exploited if a user is tricked into copying a malicious command from a website.
An identified issue in the QuickView PDF Reader on Windows fails to properly sanitize embedded JavaScript within PDF annotations, allowing for remote code execution when the file is opened.

The Diagnostic Policy Heuristics Service contains a type confusion vulnerability when processing RPC calls, which can be leveraged to achieve remote code execution through the service's execution context.
A heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability exists in the HTML Help utility (hh.exe) when processing a specially crafted Compiled HTML Help (.chm) file, allowing for remote code execution.
An implementation error in the Windows Font Driver (`atmfd.dll`) when processing malicious font files from removable media could be exploited to gain code execution.

In the SecureID Gateway IdP, a vulnerability in the MFA logging module permits an attacker with sufficient privileges to bypass the generation of multi-factor authentication success or failure events.

The SwiftStore SSD Utility for macOS contains a flaw where an attacker can bypass permission checks, enabling the installation of malicious firmware on the solid-state drive for persistence beyond OS reinstalls.

The Microsoft Diagnostics Hub Standard Collector Service on Windows allows arbitrary data to be added to diagnostic reports. An attacker with local access can inject sensitive file contents into a report, which is then uploaded to a configured collection server, enabling exfiltration over the diagnostics protocol.
In the NotifyHub SNS-like service, a flaw allows an attacker with 'sns:Publish' permissions to detach a logging topic from a CloudTrail-like service, effectively disrupting log delivery.

A heap overflow in the Active Directory Replication Service on Windows permits an authenticated attacker to run code with system privileges, enabling the deployment of malware with DGA capabilities for fallback channels.
Information leakage flaws in in the NetCore NAC appliance reveals the internal API key, which can then be used to weaken the encryption key for all device-to-controller communication.

The `rsync.exe` utility on Windows can be replaced with a compromised version that includes malicious functionality, enabling an attacker to exfiltrate data or establish a command-and-control channel under the guise of file synchronization.
An internal defect in the Linux kernel's eBPF verifier allows an unprivileged process to load a program that can sniff traffic on the local loopback interface to capture and steal session cookies.

The 'Virtual Fabric' network management tool for Azure contains a bug where a 'deny all' rule can be overwritten by a subsequent 'allow any' rule with a lower priority, which is contrary to expected behavior and can be exploited.

The Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect client on macOS suffers from an information disclosure vulnerability where its support tool can be invoked to dump system state, including a list of all running services and their launchd plists.

In macOS, the 'QuickLook' framework fails to sanitize file paths before passing them to `osascript`. An attacker can craft a malicious document that, when previewed, executes AppleScript commands to bypass Gatekeeper.
The 'MarketBoost' SaaS platform's SMS campaign creation tool lacks a CAPTCHA, allowing automated scripts to initiate campaigns to fraudulent phone number sets for SMS pumping.
A buildpack injection flaw in Heroku's dyno environment allows an attacker to embed a malicious binary within the build artifact, effectively staging a tool on the PaaS platform.

An insecure firmware update mechanism in NetFortress-FirewallOS could be exploited to install firmware that disables the Intrusion Prevention System (IPS) functionality by downgrading to an older version lacking signature verification.
Memory corruption in the SafariSafeBrowsingExtension on macOS can be triggered by a maliciously packed WebAssembly module, resulting in arbitrary code execution in the browser's process.
The OneLogin SSO service's password reset functionality lacks a rate-limiting mechanism, which allows for the brute force of password reset tokens and potential account takeover.
The 'LegacyCRM' application trusts the AppDomainManager assembly path from a user-writable configuration file, making it vulnerable to DLL hijacking and subsequent code execution.
Memory corruption triggered by the MacArmor Security Suite's kernel extension for macOS can be exploited to terminate the real-time scanning engine and tamper with detection signatures.

The 'Ansible' module for managing a specific VPS provider on Linux fails to check the fingerprint of the provider's API, making it vulnerable to DNS rebinding attacks that could result in the acquisition of a malicious server.
A critical weakness within the 'Packer' image building tool for IaaS allows a malicious source script to modify the cloud credentials of the host machine, compromising the entire build environment.
The SNMP service on FirewallOS devices contains a buffer overflow that gives a remote user the power to hijack the execution flow and shut down the firewall's filtering engine.
The macOS Mail application can be tricked into syncing a maliciously crafted email draft to an IMAP server that forwards attachments to a cloud storage service, facilitating data exfiltration.
The Azure Virtual Network TAP feature contains a flaw where mirrored traffic can be redirected to unauthorized storage accounts, leading to automated data exfiltration.
The Microsoft Office Online Server's OWA viewer component contains a memory corruption bug that can be exploited by a malicious Office document hosted on a website.

A logical flaw in the Linux `DockerAuth` plugin allows a user with low privileges to request an authentication token for a higher-privileged Docker registry, leading to unauthorized image access and potential credential theft.

The FusionTrace SaaS platform fails to validate user permissions when modifying log stream encryption settings. This vulnerability allows an authenticated user to disable log file encryption, making it possible to tamper with log records after they are collected.
An improper permission check in the `vmware-vib-auth` daemon allows a non-administrative user to install a VIB, which can be used to create a persistent startup task on the ESXi hypervisor.
A memory leak in the Windows IIS Advanced Logging module allows attackers to bypass security controls and access the Azure Instance Metadata Service for VM credentials.
A design flaw in Linux keyring-service allows memory inspection attacks to recover encryption keys for user keyrings and stored passwords.

A persistence mechanism in 'SwiftBuild Studio' for macOS permits any standard user to configure a startup auto-reconnect to an attacker-controlled tunnel, achieving a persistent C2 channel upon user login.

The SecureAuth Gateway for Windows contains a flaw where it trusts .NET assemblies loaded from a temporary directory. By leveraging this, an attacker can execute code via the [ComUnregisterFunction] attribute when the gateway's service calls Regsvcs.exe, bypassing security controls.

The `curl` utility on certain Linux distributions is bundled with a custom library that contains a flaw in its SCP handling, potentially allowing a malicious server to overwrite files on the client machine during a download.
The 'RemoteDesktop Gateway' service exposes a WMI class that is vulnerable to XML external entity (XXE) attacks, potentially leading to remote code execution or information disclosure.
LibreOffice's macro security model can be bypassed by creating user accounts with names matching trusted certificate authorities, enabling malicious macro execution.
Improper access control in the 'AppVEnt' service for Microsoft App-V allows a standard user to inject a malicious portable executable into a virtualized application process.

Simultaneous execution threads in the APIConnect gateway's API key generation process can result in two different accounts being assigned the same key, allowing an attacker to access and abuse another user's service permissions.
The OpenSSH daemon wrapper `ssh-wrapper` on Linux suffers from a command injection vulnerability that allows commands to be executed and results tunneled back via ICMP packets.
A workflow defect in the macOS `AppStore` framework's receipt validation could be abused to manipulate local purchase records, enabling unauthorized use of paid features.
cURL's domain redirect handling contains a flaw that permits following redirects to malicious domains without proper validation.

A Docker container running a version of the 'Consul' service discovery tool can be configured to leak its TLS agent certificate via its unencrypted HTTP API, providing attackers with details about the cluster's PKI.

Simultaneous execution threads in the log rotation script for the Linux 'rsyslog' service can be exploited to replace a compressed log archive with a tampered version before it is finalized, manipulating stored log data.
An implementation of Blowfish in the Palo Alto Panorama API Gateway is vulnerable to a birthday attack, which could allow an attacker to find collisions and decrypt API commands.
A bug located in the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) interoperability layer allows a malicious Linux process to modify the Windows user's Group Policy settings, including the network logon script.
An insecure file permission issue in /etc/audit/audit.rules on Linux systems managed by the 'DeployIt' tool allows regular users to modify the audit rules to silence logging of their commands.

A programmatic error in the macOS CoreFoundation library's dynamic loading mechanism permits an attacker to use DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES to hook the CFNetworkCopySystemProxySettings function and capture credentials for authenticated proxies.
Unsafe behavior in the abandoned Python package 'PyDeployKit' allows an unauthenticated actor to re-register the name and push a malicious backdoored version, affecting all downstream projects.
The 'AdminToolkit' suite on Windows is vulnerable to command injection due to improper handling of input passed to the SyncAppvPublishingServer.vbs script.
An AWS EC2 instance profile credential chaining vulnerability allows processes to inherit Secrets Manager access from previously attached profiles.
Google Cloud VPC Flow Logs contain insufficient protection, allowing attackers to infer IP block usage patterns.

The MailCore framework, used by numerous third-party macOS email clients, lacks proper validation on the 'BCC' field when composing messages via its API. An attacker can exploit this to inject a large number of recipient addresses, overwhelming a target inbox.
Sensitive information is exposed by in the Windows IIS FTP service could allow an unauthenticated attacker to enumerate the directory structure of a remote FTP site.

The 'VpnConnectivity Service' on Windows improperly handles DLL loading, leading to a search order hijacking vulnerability. An attacker can place a malicious `vpnapi.dll` in a compromised directory to be loaded by the service.

An implementation error in the rate-limiting middleware of CampaignMaster marketing automation allows an attacker to bypass per-contact sending limits, facilitating the hijacking of the platform for mass spam campaigns.

The netfilter_ext.ko kernel module for Linux does not correctly validate timestamps in its logging configuration, which can be abused to backdate log entries, a form of timestomping designed to mislead investigators.

The 'OneDrive for Business' sync client on Windows can be manipulated into syncing a malicious '.lnk' file from a personal OneDrive account. The link file appears legitimate but executes a payload to steal information from the user's machine.

macOS Safari's download validation process is susceptible to a filename spoofing attack. When downloading a file, Safari does not adequately strip trailing spaces from the filename, which can result in a malicious binary named 'installer.dmg ' being saved and potentially executed by a user misled by the apparent DMG extension.

A flaw in the IntranetConnect Gateway's API allows for unauthenticated token creation requests. By providing valid credentials, an attacker can force the gateway service to make and impersonate a user token, gaining access to internal network resources.
A critical weakness within Microsoft Teams' file handling allows files extracted from MOTW-tagged containers to bypass security warnings, as the Zone.Identifier ADS is not properly propagated.

The com.mactexteditor.editorhelper.xpc service fails to verify the identity of its XPC client. This allows any local user to connect and potentially abuse its file-writing capabilities for privilege escalation.
An internal defect in the NAT implementation of NetCore OS on StratusRouter devices permits inbound connections that should be blocked, effectively breaching the network perimeter.

An information disclosure flaw in the Windows Netlogon service could allow an attacker to leak sensitive domain trust relationship information via a crafted RPC call, assisting in lateral movement planning without proper authorization.

A remote code execution vulnerability in the WebConfig interface of an IoT device management software running on Windows allows an attacker to execute 'sc config eventlog start= disabled' on the host system.

A memory leak in CloudAPI Gateway's request handling module allows attackers to exhaust system resources by sending a high volume of malformed API requests, leading to service degradation and potential network outage.

The macOS Spotlight indexer does not properly process extended attributes (xattrs) on certain file types. An attacker can store malicious code in an xattr, which is ignored by Spotlight and most antivirus scanners, but can be executed by a separate loader program.
The pfSense-Desktop-Client for macOS fails to validate SSL certificates, allowing a man-in-the-middle attacker to intercept admin credentials and gain full visibility of the firewall's configuration.

The FileGuard Finder extension for macOS contains a flaw where an attacker can manipulate the metadata displayed for files in Finder windows without altering the files themselves, causing user deception.
Unexpected behavior in the third-party encryption driver 'DriveCryptor Plus' when mounting encrypted volumes from removable drives could bypass authentication and execute a malicious payload.
The OfficeMacro Engine in an office suite fails to restrict macro actions, allowing a malicious document to create a new user account on the host system.

An exploitable bug in the Windows Credential Manager allows an attacker to modify the HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest registry key to force the storage of credentials in clear text in memory.

The macOS OpenDirectory framework fails to properly encrypt stored Kerberos tickets in the system keychain, allowing malicious applications with user-level access to steal service tickets for lateral movement.
The Windows Remote Shell Service (WinRSS) contains a logic flaw that permits a remote user to spawn a command shell without proper authentication.

The Windows User Account Control (UAC) component (consent.exe) improperly validates parent process relationships during elevation, allowing malicious processes to inherit elevated tokens via PPID spoofing attacks.
An insecure deserialization vulnerability in the ESXi `vpxa` agent allows an authenticated vCenter user with limited privileges to execute arbitrary file copy operations on the managed ESXi host.
A flaw in the Cygwin 'icacls' port for Windows allows a local attacker to bypass permission checks by using a malformed command line, potentially granting unauthorized access to files.
The Xcode build process on macOS contains a vulnerability in its asset catalog compiler, where a specially crafted asset can trigger a buffer overflow in the custom resource archiving routine.
The systemd-network-proxy component on Linux fails to isolate proxy configurations per-user, allowing a local user to influence the network proxy settings for other users' sessions.

A buffer overflow in the Windows component responsible for parsing the AppInit_DLLs registry value allows an attacker to corrupt memory and execute arbitrary code. This can be triggered by setting an excessively long DLL path in the registry.
A remote code execution flaw in the ESXi `Veeam-Plugin` service can be triggered by a dead drop resolver hosted on a public Veeam community knowledge base article.
The 'VMware Tools' autostart mechanism on Windows is vulnerable to symlink attacks where an attacker can replace the legitimate shortcut with a malicious one before guest OS boot.

An out-of-bounds read in the `cfg80211` kernel module on Gentoo Linux gives a local threat actor the ability to leak kernel memory, potentially exposing cached WPA keys for recently connected networks.

The Evolution Mail client on Linux contains a flaw in its URL parser that does not correctly handle usernames and passwords, enabling adversaries to obfuscate malicious destinations in spearphishing links.

The AegisOS recovery mode on CyberGate VPN appliances does not verify the authenticity or version of the loaded system image, allowing an attacker with physical access to load a downgraded, insecure OS.

An insecure DLL loading mechanism in the `Adobe Creative Cloud Sync Service` can be combined with thread execution hijacking. An attacker can first hijack a thread to force the service to load a malicious DLL from an untrusted path, leading to code execution.
Improper access control in the Nexus-OCI runtime's API endpoint for container creation allows an attacker to specify and execute arbitrary commands as the container's initial process.
The LSASS Process Handler in Windows stores password hashes in memory without proper encryption, allowing attackers to dump and crack credentials from memory dumps.

A security gap in the `WindowMgrPro` service for Windows allows a local attacker to bypass ACLs and call the `EnumWindows` function via a COM interface, resulting in unauthorized application window discovery.

An improper input validation issue in the FetchmailNG daemon for Linux permits a threat actor via network access to inject malicious commands into POP3 session responses. This could be exploited to establish a C2 channel that mimics legitimate email retrieval traffic.

Improper validation of third-party plugins in the 'CloudFlow CI/CD' platform allows for the injection of malicious build steps, compromising the software supply chain for all projects using the platform.

Memory corruption in the IPv6 Tunnel Service for Windows could allow an attacker to modify the registry path for Netsh helpers. This can be exploited to achieve persistent, event-triggered code execution.

An identified issue in macOS Unified Logging framework allows sandboxed applications to access system-wide logs, enabling enumeration of security events and application crashes across the entire system.
The 'auditd' subsystem on Linux suffers from a permissions flaw in its configuration file handling, allowing a user in the 'adm' group to add a rule that discards all events from a specific process.
Docker Registry API allows unlimited authentication attempts without proper rate limiting, creating a vector for credential stuffing attacks against containerized environments.
The 'DeviceInventory' component in a popular Windows EDR agent improperly validates API tokens, allowing a compromised low-privilege process to dump the agent's list of known peripherals.

The 'NetlifyCI' continuous integration service for cloud deployments has a flaw in its build hook validation, allowing an unauthorized user to inject a malicious build step that stages a backdoor in the deployed static site.

The `FirmwareUpdateDaemon` on Apex Networking industrial switches does not sanitize the firmware image path, allowing a local attacker to trick the system into loading a crafted, malicious OS image from an unauthorized source.

An insecure dependency loading mechanism in 'WebServerX' for Windows allows an attacker to manipulate the `AppInit_DLLs` registry key, causing the web server process to load a malicious library at startup.
The 'CloudCRM' SaaS platform's Chatter feed suffers from an insecure direct object reference (IDOR) vulnerability, letting users view private group messages where credentials might be discussed.

Improper bounds checking in the Windows FileIndexer Service allows for arbitrary code execution. An attacker can use this to run a script that periodically searches for and copies files with specific extensions to a staging area.
A vulnerability in the Safari Web Content Service on macOS could allow a malicious website to alter the appearance of other open tabs, leading to a UI-based defacement attack.
A denial-of-service vulnerability in the `osqueryd` daemon can be triggered by a malformed configuration, causing it to crash and cease the scheduled collection of host state indicators.
A stack-based buffer overflow affecting a Windows file synchronization service allows an attacker to execute untrusted binaries by proxying it through the signed `robocopy.exe` utility.

A flaw in the DataShield Enterprise Backup Agent allows for SMB relay attacks, where an attacker can intercept authentication requests and gain access to the backup service with the privileges of the connecting user.

Elevation of privilege is possible in in the Windows Update Agent (wuauclt.exe) allows a low-privileged user to modify registry keys under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\WindowsUpdate\Auto Update, enabling the deployment of malicious updates.
The `GDM` (GNOME Display Manager) login greeter process is vulnerable to a proc memory injection attack due to a flaw that allows writing to its stack via `/proc/[pid]/mem` during user session setup.
