A type confusion weakness in the CoreAudio framework on macOS can be exploited via a malicious audio file's resource fork to execute arbitrary code.

The installation process for 'FastDisk Defragmenter' incorrectly sets permissions on its service binary 'fastdiskd.exe', allowing local attackers to perform a binary replacement attack for privilege escalation.
A workflow defect in Windows Clipboard Manager's IPC mechanism allows arbitrary code execution through crafted data formats.
The Linux OpenSSH server has a vulnerability in its sftp subsystem that enables attackers to exfiltrate file data over unencrypted SCP fallback connections using base64 encoding.

A use-after-free vulnerability in the PrintSpooler service could be leveraged to achieve arbitrary code execution. An attacker can exploit this to inject a crafted PE into the spooler service process, escaping sandbox restrictions.
A heap-based overflow condition in the Windows DNS service allows attackers to create malicious DNS records that point to deceptive link targets.
A Slack-like team collaboration application's API key validation endpoint is susceptible to timing attacks, which can be leveraged to brute force valid API keys.
A cross-site request forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in the account settings panel of LinkUp allows an attacker to trick an authenticated user into changing their associated email and password.
An improperly secured public Azure Compute Gallery image allows for the inclusion of a malicious startup script that establishes reverse shell connectivity upon VM provisioning.
Improper input validation in the nginx-proxy-plugin for Linux enables a remote attacker to inject malicious proxy headers, redirecting server traffic to an adversary-controlled endpoint.
The auto-update mechanism in CodeComplier IDE fails to set the quarantine flag on downloaded update packages, leading to silent execution of potentially malicious code without a Gatekeeper prompt.

The DiagnosticCollector framework on macOS contains a flaw where it stages collected crash reports in a world-readable temporary directory, exposing potentially sensitive user data to other local users.

A logical error in the Windows Bluetooth LE GATT client driver allows a crafted application to read and write to characteristics on a remote device without proper authorization, enabling data theft and staging for exfiltration.
A memory corruption flaw in EdgeRouter XOS when processing specifically crafted configuration files could allow an authenticated attacker to gain root control of the router.
A software fault within Fortinet FortiOS allows for an authenticated SQL injection via the web interface, which an attacker can leverage to clear firewall policy hit logs and traffic history.

Improper neutralization of special elements in the 'Windows User Profile Sync Service' allows an attacker to create a symbolic link, redirecting a configuration write to the critical HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\ registry key.
Information disclosure in macOS System Configuration Framework allows malicious applications to read detailed network topology data, including VPN configurations and routing tables.

A custom debugging feature in the `Microsoft Office Click-to-Run Service` can be enabled by an attacker. This feature allows for thread suspension and context manipulation, which can be abused for thread execution hijacking to bypass application controls.
An internal defect in 'IT Management Suite' for Windows allows a non-administrative user to gain persistence by exploiting a weak permission setting on the W32Time TimeProviders registry keys.
The Windows 'Workstation' service does not correctly handle crafted network packets, which could lead to remote code execution and dumping of LSA secrets.
The SSH daemon on the ApexNet 7400 series load balancer contains a flaw where a specially crafted packet can force the session to negotiate a weaker 1024-bit RSA host key.
The CAS authentication component in SingleSignOn Identity Provider is vulnerable to stored XSS attacks.
VMware NSX Edge Gateway contains a vulnerability in NAT rule processing that permits attackers to masquerade C2 infrastructure as legitimate internal services, bypassing perimeter security controls.

The `PlatformInitialization` module from a niche firmware vendor contains a hardcoded debug string that includes a unique build identifier. An attacker who has deployed a modified version of this firmware can search for this identifier to find out if their custom firmware has been reverse-engineered and reported.
The SentinelOne agent's kernel driver has a flaw that allows a signed process to tamper with the PEB of another process, bypassing agent monitoring and enabling argument spoofing.
Sensitive information is exposed by in the Linux cron daemon allows a local user to read arbitrary files due to improper symlink handling.

A missing authentication check in the Windows Update Orchestrator Service's `GetInstalledPackages` method enables any local user to obtain a detailed list of all system and application updates, aiding in software discovery.

A privilege escalation bug exists in the admin panel of the 'ConnectBase' CRM, where a crafted request can grant a standard user administrative rights, providing unrestricted access to all customer relationship data stored in the system.

An input validation error in the open-iscsi firmware update module on Linux could allow a remote attacker to provide a maliciously crafted firmware image, corrupting the firmware of an attached storage array.
A programmatic error in Windows IIS (Internet Information Services) Kerberos authentication module allows attackers to bypass authentication using captured service tickets.
Buffer bounds violations in a third-party Windows keyboard filter driver allows an attacker to replace it with a malicious driver that logs all keystrokes at the kernel level.
A heap overflow in the Office Open XML parser when processing a malicious .dotx file can be triggered to gain code execution as the user.

The 'Time Machine' service on macOS contains a flaw that enables an attacker with local access to restore a modified system configuration file that disables SIP and other code signing protections during the restoration process.
The Windows Services management console has a vulnerability where EWM can be manipulated for process injection.
The VirtuaIntegration Guest Tools for Windows contain a vulnerability that allows a guest OS user to manipulate the host's SSP configuration, leading to privilege escalation and credential access.
An XML external entity (XXE) vulnerability in a cloud provider's administrative console could be exploited to read internal files and discover API keys for the ResourceHierarchyAPI.
Windows Defender's real-time protection driver has a race condition that can be exploited to cause system crashes during malware scanning.

A denial-of-service vulnerability in `dfsvc.exe` can be triggered by a ClickOnce application with an excessively large manifest, which could be leveraged as part of a larger attack chain to disrupt security monitoring.
HP ProCurve switch management interface lacks CSRF protection on the reboot endpoint, enabling forced network device restarts.

The TrustGate SSO service does not adequately validate the `audience` field in JWT tokens received from trusted Identity Providers, enabling an attacker who has compromised one partner to replay the token to access another partner's application.
An insecure method of process creation in `AppVShNotify.exe` allows an attacker to bypass security controls and execute commands indirectly.

A critical weakness within the NSAppleScript execution component of macOS allows a malicious script to escape its sandbox and execute system commands with user privileges, useful for developing malicious macOS automation scripts.

A security gap in the macOS Spotlight indexing service allows an attacker to perform a search for files with specific metadata without triggering security prompts. This can be abused to search for analysis-related filenames like 'malware.exe' or 'sample.bin'.

The macOS server application 'ProfileManager' fails to properly sanitize content in user-generated help pages. This allows an authenticated user to inject hidden text and keywords, poisoning the results of the server's built-in search function.

A workflow defect in the OpenSSH daemon (sshd) on Linux allows an unauthenticated attacker to load a rogue shared library using LD_PRELOAD, which hooks the libc read() function to capture credentials during an interactive session.
The 'cron' service on a specific Linux distribution fails to sanitize job names, which can be exploited to schedule the execution of a custom-developed malicious script.

The QwikSheet macOS Edition application improperly stores Google Drive API credentials in a plaintext configuration file, which could be leveraged by a malicious process to access and exfiltrate the user's cloud-stored spreadsheets.

A logic error in the token validation routine of the SwiftSend API enables the reuse of single-use tokens, permitting an attacker to repeatedly perform high-volume email sending operations beyond their allocated quota.
The Keychain Access utility can be tricked by a malicious AppleScript into revealing the plaintext content of stored passwords through UI spoofing.
A bug located in the Microsoft Teams client allows a malicious add-on to install a system-level proxy, redirecting all corporate traffic through an attacker-controlled server.
The macOS Preview app fails to safely handle corrupted JPEG2000 images, leading to a heap overflow and potential arbitrary code execution.

Improper permission checks in the Security Accounts Manager (SAM) remote protocol interface could allow a malicious actor with network access to a domain controller to request password data in a manner similar to DCSync.

Simultaneous execution threads in the 'Microsoft Remote Desktop Services' logon process on Windows can be exploited to load an unauthorized Network Provider DLL, allowing an attacker to harvest credentials from remote desktop sessions.

A buffer overflow vulnerability in the Google Cloud OS Config agent on Linux instances could be exploited by a malicious actor on the same network to inject and execute malicious commands as the root user.
The instance metadata service for a popular IaaS provider is vulnerable to request spoofing, which could be used to create a new user on a virtual machine.
The macOS Server Open Directory service contains a flaw in its web interface that could be exploited to bypass login prompts and directly access user list pages, disclosing employee full names.

A directory traversal flaw in the 'PublishPress' CMS for Linux allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to upload a malicious PHP file outside the web root, leading to remote code execution and malware staging.

A security gap in the macOS Time Machine restoration process can be triggered by an attacker to restore an empty version of a user's .zsh_history file from a malicious snapshot, effectively clearing the history on the live system.
The 'systemd-mqtt-connector' for Linux does not validate the source of MQTT messages, allowing an attacker with network access to publish伪造的 status updates or commands to systemd units.
Symantec Endpoint Protection Agent contains a memory corruption issue where the TLS callback pointers of a monitored process can be altered, allowing an adversary to bypass defenses and execute code.
The 'Safari-Ad-Blocker' extension on macOS is vulnerable to command injection through its 'filter list' update mechanism, which pulls from an unverified public Pastebin endpoint.
An attacker can exploit a logic flaw in the SafeGuard Mac antivirus to bypass its own checks and use AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges to execute unverified code.

An identified issue in VMware ESXi Hostd service allows attackers to manipulate DNS responses to calculate dynamic C2 ports, enabling covert command and control channels through port calculation algorithms.
Predictable resource identification in vulnerability exists in the UserSessionProfiler tool. An attacker can directly reference a session ID to force a session takeover via the underlying RDP APIs.
The ESXi CIMOM (sfcb) service has a flaw that allows a remote authenticated user to issue CIM operations over a non-standard port, potentially evading IDS/IPS signatures.

A vulnerability in the CLI of Cisco IOS XR allows a user with read-only privileges to execute the `monitor capture` command, enabling them to sniff traffic from any interface and exfiltrate the capture file.

The `gnome-keyring-daemon` on Linux fails to properly zero out memory buffers after handling password requests, allowing a local attacker with sufficient privileges to dump the process memory and recover stored passwords.
Windows File Server Resource Manager contains an information disclosure vulnerability where unauthorized users can query local group memberships through the FSRM management interface.

A privilege escalation flaw in the AegisFirewall system's 'cryptoctl' utility could allow a low-privileged user to disable the IPsec hardware acceleration engine. This would force the firewall to use a slower, software-based implementation, potentially exposing cipher suite weaknesses.

The Active Directory Sync service (ActiveDirSync) on Windows Server contains a flaw where repeated synchronization requests for a large, complex object can lead to memory exhaustion and denial of service.
Improper bounds checking in a legacy component of the 'Microsoft Identity Integration Server' (MIIS) could be triggered to leak uninitialized memory containing domain trust data structures.

The LegacyDB Manager v3.1 insecurely handles its compatibility database, permitting an attacker to plant a persistent shim that executes arbitrary code each time the application starts, achieving persistence.

Improper handling of data in the `Windows Defender ATP Connector` allows a local attacker to read its diagnostic logs, which contain detailed process execution and network connection logs from the host.
The Microsoft Exchange Server's 'Edge Transport' service contains a vulnerability that allows an authenticated user to remotely dump the host's LSA secrets.
Concurrency issues within the BIND9 daemon on Linux allows for the creation of unauthorized subdomains during zone transfers, enabling adversaries to establish covert C&C channels.

The `com.user.backgroundhelper` LaunchAgent on macOS improperly implements its process lifecycle, using `nohup` to execute tasks. This can be abused to maintain a process that persists even if the agent itself is killed.

The Nginx-Accel module for Linux does not properly validate the path for proxied requests, leading to a remote code execution vulnerability. An attacker can exploit this to compromise the web server and enlist it in a botnet.

An authorization bypass in the CloudFormationService allows an attacker to include a malicious template in a stack update, which contains a command to revert a production instance to a snapshot containing a backdoor.
A memory corruption bug in the AppVShNotify service can be triggered via a crafted service control request, resulting in a denial of service or potential arbitrary code execution.

The Linux `systemd` journaling subsystem (`journald`) can be manipulated to forward its logs to a remote syslog server over the network, and a vulnerability allows an attacker to inject arbitrary file data into this stream.
An unauthenticated remote vulnerability in the 'Fortinet FortiOS SSLVPN Portal' allows an attacker to trigger a device reboot, disrupting all VPN and network traffic.

Simultaneous execution threads in the Windows IIS Log Consolidator service allows an attacker to replace a legitimate staging file with a symlink to a sensitive file, causing its data to be copied to the consolidation archive.

The Microsoft Graph API for Office 365 lacks sufficient authorization checks, allowing an application with delegated mail.read permissions to also create or modify inbox rules for any user in the tenant.

A type confusion vulnerability in the 'EventLogDispatcher' service can be leveraged to achieve arbitrary code execution, enabling an attacker to silently clear the Windows Security, Application, and System logs.
Firefox's WebAssembly module on Linux contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability exploitable through malicious web pages.

An implementation error in the Windows Credential Manager allows a sandboxed application to query and decrypt credentials stored by other applications without proper user consent, leading to credential theft.

The Windows Update Orchestrator service contains a flaw where it can be overwhelmed by a debugger evasion technique. A malware sample can flood the debug output using loops of `OutputDebugStringW()`, causing attached debuggers to become unresponsive.
The WatchTower EDR service on Windows contains a race condition that permits a process to execute before its behavioral policies are evaluated, bypassing initial detection.

Privilege elevation flaws in in the AzureDataSync service for Windows allows a standard user to execute arbitrary commands, which can be used to run `driverquery.exe` and enumerate all installed drivers.
The NTFS metadata parser in Windows fails to prevent the creation of files with deceptive double extensions where the hidden extension is executable, facilitating masquerading attacks.

The 'Remote Desktop Licensing' service has an exposed RPC method that accepts username and password parameters for a 'license check'. This method directly calls `LogonUser` without proper authorization, allowing an attacker to make and impersonate a new domain user token.
The Apple Server.app's Wiki service on macOS does not properly sanitize embedded file attachments, allowing an authenticated user to upload a PHP script that acts as a web shell.

An algorithm implementation error in the User Account Control (UAC) elevation prompt fails to properly validate binaries that use dynamic API resolution, allowing a malicious program to silently elevate privileges by hiding its true intent from the consent UI.

An implementation error in the Rancher 2.7 management API allows a user with 'project-member' role to elevate their privileges to 'project-owner' by creating a new project-scoped RoleBinding for their own account.
A remote code execution flaw exists in the SecurePDF Reader for Windows when processing a malicious PDF attachment, permitting an attacker to harvest user information via HTML smuggling.

In Microsoft Azure AD, a vulnerability allows an attacker to register a new application with a malicious reply URI, enabling the interception of access tokens during the OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow for persistence.
Unsafe behavior in the 'DataHaven' backup service API allows for the creation of administrative API keys without proper multi-factor authentication checks.

The macOS Single Sign-On Extension contains a logic bug where it will request MFA approval from the user's registered device even if the initial Kerberos ticket request fails, which can be exploited in a password spraying attack to flood the user with prompts.
Data leakage occurs in in the Apache Traffic Manager module for Linux allows an attacker to obtain the server's hostname, OS kernel version, and a list of enabled modules via a crafted HTTP request.
Improper input sanitization in the LogRhythm SmartResponse plugin on Windows allows for arbitrary command execution upon a threat intelligence match, which could be used to tamper with logs.
The Xcode Build Archive Packer on macOS fails to sanitize file names within compressed archives, enabling a path traversal attack that could overwrite Xcode project files.
The macOS Spotlight indexing service can be exploited for dylib hijacking when weak-linked dylibs are missing, enabling malicious library injection with system privileges.
The Image Capture utility on macOS fails to properly handle symbolic links on SD cards, resulting in unauthorized file reads from the linked target on the removable media.
A design flaw in the 'ConfigWizard Enterprise' tool enables the execution of VBScript embedded in XSL configuration files, which can be used for persistence or lateral movement.
Oracle Database for Windows does not validate AppCert DLL registry entries, allowing database processes to load malicious DLLs during startup.
The Windows Winlogon service fails to validate shutdown requests from low-integrity processes, allowing unauthorized system restarts.
A vulnerability in the way the Windows Search indexer handles Outlook mail items could allow a local user to reconstruct a partial list of email addresses from the search index files.
The `id` command in the Linux `coreutils` package contains a defect that allows a standard user to enumerate all local users by brute-forcing user IDs.

The ESXi Hypervisor Network Stack contains a flaw that can be exploited via a VM to create a covert channel, effectively using the hypervisor as a relay in a multi-hop proxy setup to bypass network segmentation.

The 'DevOps' deployment agent for macOS contains a dylib hijacking vulnerability. Its `deploy-worker` process can be tricked into loading a malicious `libcrypto_helper.dylib` from a directory in its `@rpath` that is controlled by a lower-privileged user.

A design flaw in Windows Defender Application Control allows malicious code executed within Windows Sandbox to bypass security policies, enabling attackers to test and deploy malware in a hidden environment.
The `osascript` utility on macOS fails to restrict access to sensitive system APIs when executing JXA scripts, enabling a script to bypass security controls like TCC.
A bug located in the Linux krb5kdc daemon allows attackers to request tickets with forged PAC data, bypassing access controls on Windows domain resources.

An improper access control vulnerability in the SurfMaster browser for macOS could allow a malicious application to access and decrypt Safari-based passwords stored in the system Keychain without user interaction.

An issue in the token generation module of KubeAuthProxy allows an attacker to create forged service accounts with arbitrary permissions for any namespace, effectively establishing a new, persistent access point.
The Linux `acct-tools` suite contains an information disclosure flaw where the `lastlog` command can be run by any user, revealing all local account names, including service accounts.
The TimeMachineHelper service on macOS stages snapshot metadata in a persistent, world-readable location, potentially exposing file system structure and metadata to unauthorized users.
Apple's Directory Services utility on macOS contains a vulnerability that allows attackers to extract cached Kerberos tickets from system memory.

Unsafe behavior in the SecureAuthSSO component for Windows permits an attacker to bypass authentication and access an internal API endpoint that directly returns the results of `GetUserDefaultUILanguage`.
The macOS 'SystemOptimizer' utility does not clean up its named mutex on abnormal exit, which prevents the application from being relaunched without a system reboot.
The 'iCloudSyncDaemon' service on macOS fails to sanitize configuration file parameters, permitting a local user to embed and execute arbitrary Unix shell commands with root privileges.
Alibaba Cloud's traffic mirroring service contains a logic flaw where mirrored traffic can be intercepted and duplicated to multiple destinations.
An elevation of privilege flaw was found in the CodeHelper-Mac IDE plugin, which utilizes the insecure AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges API for its build process.

Improper handling of data in the MailFlow Director's delegation cleanup process allows permissions to persist on archived mailboxes after a user account is disabled, providing an attacker with a hidden channel to access historical email data.
A workflow defect in containerd-shim allows an attacker to overwrite a container's PID 1 process with a malicious executable, establishing persistence within the container environment.

The 'Confluence' data center application, running on a Windows server, suffers from an improperly secured REST API that allows an attacker to crawl all spaces and retrieve user lists, including group memberships, from the site.
The macOS Keychain Access Service can be triggered via a malicious command from the Cloud Administration Command interface to dump system credentials.
The 'IntraLink' daemon on Linux provides an unauthenticated status endpoint that leaks the hostnames and versions of all integrated third-party services it communicates with.
Information leakage flaws in in the `esxcli hardware ip` command reveals sensitive network configuration details that could be used to craft further attacks against the hypervisor CLI.

A bug in the cPanel Web interface on Linux allows an attacker to perform a wordlist scan against a victim's hosted domain and receive distinct 404/200 responses, revealing hidden files and directories.
A directory traversal vulnerability in Windows Server Update Services permits attackers to modify deployment packages, allowing the compromise of server infrastructure during acquisition.

The Windows Task Scheduler service fails to properly sanitize file paths when creating a new task from a command-line argument. An attacker can exploit this to create a task that points to a malicious tool, then use another vulnerability to modify the tool's on-disk content after it has been whitelisted by the scheduler, removing its signature.
A vulnerability in the macOS 'AirPort' driver allows a sandboxed application to issue a private IOCTL call that enumerates all current Wi-Fi network connections and their BSSID/IP mappings.
The Slack desktop application on Linux fails to properly isolate workspace tokens, allowing a compromised workspace to steal tokens for other workspaces configured in the same client.

A memory corruption issue in the packet processing engine of SentinelGate routers can be triggered by a series of specially crafted packets, leading to a kernel panic and allowing an attacker to load a malicious system image into memory upon reboot.

The Smart Install protocol handler in TitanSwitch firmware contains a buffer overflow that can be triggered to achieve remote code execution, which can then be used to exfiltrate the device configuration.
The `rsyslogd` daemon on Linux, when configured with a custom action module, is vulnerable to an out-of-bounds write that can lead to remote code execution and the subsequent deletion of system logs.
Azure Arc's hybrid machine management service has an improper authorization check permitting attackers with compromised resource group access to deploy and execute scripts on all connected servers.
The systemd-journald service on Linux inadvertently exposes file discovery capabilities through its debug interface, revealing sensitive log file locations and contents.
A bug located in the 'FileSystemFilter' driver incorrectly grants write access to the 'HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon' registry path, enabling persistence modification.
Logical errors within the Windows Link Handler service allows a custom protocol to be invoked from a spearphishing link with parameters that lead to arbitrary command execution.

Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) flaws in the 'DockerFlow' orchestration tool on Linux can be exploited to inject a malicious command into a container's restart policy, which is triggered when a dependent container stops.
Improper validation of firmware update packages in the Linux fwupd daemon enables a low-privileged user to flash a malicious BIOS image, causing permanent boot failure.

The CyberArk Identity Federation platform allows an attacker to modify persistent session policies, extending the duration of access tokens and facilitating long-term persistence after initial compromise.
A flaw in the user interface of the 'PrintMax' printer driver causes the 'Print to File' dialog to render a file named 'document.prn.exe' as 'document.prn'.

An insecure firmware update protocol in a popular Windows-based IP KVM switch allows an attacker on the same network to push malicious firmware to the device, gaining persistent control over server peripherals.
Improper parsing of service names in the EndpointShield macOS agent allows for command injection when it constructs and executes launchctl commands.
The `PowerShell Universal Dashboard` service, which relies on WinRM, does not properly sanitize API requests, enabling remote code execution.
A workflow defect in the AstraVoice Platform's number provisioning API lets attackers register phone numbers that belong to legitimate, unsuspecting businesses.
IIS with WebSocket Tunneling Module on Windows contains improper access control that permits attackers to establish bidirectional tunnels for covert command and control communications.
The AWS SSO application integration framework contains a weakness that allows malicious applications to maintain persistent access to cloud resources.

The Apache-NGINX Bridge module for Linux insecurely creates temporary files in the shared memory directory (/dev/shm) with world-writable permissions. This allows a low-privileged user to place an obfuscated payload for execution by a higher-privilege process, facilitating fileless activity.
A vulnerability in the macOS 'DiskManagement' framework allows a standard user to mount a malicious disk image containing a script that queries local group information.

An insecure deserialization flaw in the Linux-based OpenLDAP server allows an authenticated user to execute arbitrary code by providing a specially crafted LDAP query. This could be used to launch a background process for cryptocurrency mining.
The Windows 'SensorCore' telemetry service executes an initialization script from a directory writable by unprivileged users, leading to persistence.
Office 365 Authentication API SaaS service generates session cookies with insufficient randomness, allowing attackers to forge valid authentication tokens.

An implementation error in the Apache HTTP server's mod_deflate module can be exploited to deliver a gzip-compressed payload containing obfuscated JavaScript, which is then executed by the client's browser.

A vulnerability in the VCSA (vCenter Server Appliance) REST API for ESXi allows an authenticated user with read-only permissions to modify the text of system announcements displayed in the vSphere Client, enabling defacement of the management console.

The security architecture of the OpenDirectorySync framework for macOS allows a sandboxed application to invoke a private method, bypassing security checks and revealing a complete list of domain groups.
systemd service manager on Linux fails to verify file signatures before execution, allowing attackers to run malicious binaries disguised as configuration files.
In the bootloader of a specific VPN concentrator, the TFTP client uses a hardcoded, weak checksum to validate downloaded images, which can be bypassed to flash a malicious firmware.
The macOS 'NetworkMonitor' system extension framework contains a vulnerability allowing attackers to load legacy kexts with persistence capabilities.
The security architecture of the macOS Safari browser allows a malicious extension to programmatically remove its own configuration profile and associated files, clearing persistence.

A privilege escalation vulnerability in the gnome-session-manager utility on Linux allows a local attacker to create a malicious .desktop file in the /etc/xdg/autostart directory, leading to code execution upon user login.

The macOS `SafariCacheAgent` has a vulnerability where a malicious process can inspect the size and age of the browser cache. A small, empty cache is used to identify a sandbox and trigger a benign execution flow.
Improper validation of OST file structures in Outlook could lead to arbitrary code execution, enabling an attacker to steal locally cached emails.
Flawed business logic in the macOS System Integrity Protection (SIP) validation permits attackers to obtain execution of unsigned binaries in protected system directories.
Improper permission checks in the 'Windows Internal Database' (WID) when used by AD LDS instances could allow a low-privileged user to attach and read NTDS.dit files.
Improper ACLs in Windows Installer service (msiserver.exe) permit modification of HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Explorer\Run registry keys.
The 'Legacy App Compatibility Layer' uses regsvr32.exe to install old components. A logic flaw allows an attacker to force the loading of an arbitrary COM scriptlet from a remote server.
An insecure AWS IAM role configuration for the CloudMail-AWS Lambda function grants read access to the entire SES mail queue, allowing an attacker to intercept and exfiltrate email data.
Memory corruption in the `gpsvc.dll` library, which processes Group Policy, can be triggered by a specially crafted network logon script path, leading to remote code execution.
The Windows Device Guard component can be downgraded to a version that doesn't enforce code integrity policies, allowing unsigned code execution.
Cryptographic flaw in NoMachine Linux edition allows session hijacking through weak encryption key generation during connection establishment.
The 'cluster-sync' utility for Linux fails to sanitize DNS responses before using them in an algorithm to derive peer IP addresses. This flaw can be abused to calculate a malicious C2 server address.
The Windows built-in TAR extraction utility fails to propagate Zone.Identifier information to files extracted from TAR.GZ archives downloaded from the Internet.

Improper locking mechanisms in the transaction processing system of the FootholdExchange marketplace could allow a user to receive access credentials without the corresponding payment being fully processed, effectively acquiring free access.
Improper validation of bundle identifiers in the macOS kernel extension loading mechanism allows an attacker with code execution to load a malicious kext that mimics a legitimate one for persistence.

A critical weakness within the 'PerformanceMonitor' service allows for a binary replacement attack. The executable 'perfmonsvc.exe' has weak file permissions, enabling an attacker to run malicious code with SYSTEM privileges.
The 'net-auth' daemon on Linux distributions stores LDAP bind credentials in a world-readable file at /etc/net-auth.conf, leading to credential exposure.
The RegistryGuard container registry service on Windows fails to invalidate access tokens after a password change, permitting an adversary to continue pushing and pulling images with a stolen token.
The metadata syncd daemon on macOS is vulnerable to a type confusion error that could be leveraged to manipulate metadata attributes as they are synced to iCloud.
A logic flaw in the macOS XProtect component's mutex check allows malware to create a decoy mutex, causing the real malware to exit and evading detection.
The AzureStorageSyncDriver for Windows contains a logic flaw that permits the insertion of junk data into sync metadata, creating a hidden channel for C2.
Windows User Profile Service improperly handles profile enumeration requests, allowing attackers to list all user accounts on the system, including disabled accounts.
An integer overflow in the libssh library for Linux can be exploited to tamper with channel data prior to encryption, leading to the manipulation of information in transit.

DNScope for macOS improperly stores API keys for commercial passive DNS services in a plaintext configuration file. A local attacker or malware with file system access can steal these credentials to conduct unauthorized DNS reconnaissance under the victim's identity.

A privilege escalation vulnerability in the MacFlow Pro application gives a local threat actor the ability to add a malicious login item for all users by manipulating its configuration plist, leading to persistent code execution upon login.
The Flux CD `source-controller` can be tricked into processing a malicious artifact that contains a Kubernetes manifest for a new RoleBinding, granting its service account elevated permissions.

Improper input validation in the DataFlow InfluxDB Service on Linux enables attackers to send specially crafted queries that result in large data dumps, creating a reflection amplification DDoS vector.
Sensitive information is exposed by in the 'VendorPortal' application allows a malicious vendor to view the delivery addresses of other divisions within the target organization.
A memory corruption issue in the Windows Shell (explorer.exe) can be triggered by a specially crafted .lnk file, leading to remote code execution and the invocation of cmd.exe.

A logic error within the Remote Desktop Licensing service allows a low-privileged user to trigger a diagnostic process creation with a forged token. This vulnerability can be chained to achieve local privilege escalation.
An unauthenticated file upload vulnerability in the Cisco ASA WebVPN portal allows an attacker to place a malicious script onto the device's filesystem, leading to web shell-based command execution.
An authentication bypass in the AdminPanel of the SendGrid-like service 'PostMaster API' enables complete takeover of an organization's email sending capabilities for malicious purposes.

The KernelGuard kernel module for Linux creates a debug entry in `/proc/kernelguard_debug` that is world-writable. An attacker can write specific commands to this file to trigger a dump of all loaded security-related kernel modules.

An improper certificate validation flaw in the macOS SecurityFramework's `SecTrustEvaluate` API can be bypassed, allowing an application to download and trust a malicious tool from an untrusted HTTPS source.
The SecureKernel Extension on macOS improperly handles code signing entitlements, allowing an unentitled application to gain system-level privileges by exploiting a logic flaw.
The `Axon Email Defense Suite` has an insecure direct object reference (IDOR) vulnerability in its web portal, allowing an attacker to enumerate and download emails from any user's quarantine folder.
Privilege elevation flaws in in the TeamsComplianceEngine allows a low-privilege user to create new service account credentials for the compliance bot, granting access to all Teams conversations.
Microsoft Outlook's handling of VBA macros allows an attacker to programmatically send an email on behalf of the user with a custom, spoofed `From` address, facilitating impersonation.
CloudOps IaaS Management Interface exposes internal API credentials in browser localStorage, allowing attackers to make authenticated dashboard requests and extract sensitive infrastructure data.
In the NebulaCloud Virtual Network Controller, a missing authentication check on the `list-identities` function allows any network entity to enumerate all cloud accounts associated with the project.
Vertical privilege escalation in in the Invenire Management Suite service on Windows allows a low-privilege user to invoke a hidden RPC method for creating a new domain administrator account.
The Windows Threat Intelligence Portal component contains an authentication bypass that grants access to paid threat intelligence feeds.

The Preferred Network List (PNL) handling in CoreSwitch NX-OS is flawed, permitting a malicious access point to respond to probe requests and deceive client devices into connecting, leading to a Man-in-the-Middle attack.
The cfprefsd daemon on macOS lacks proper integrity checks for its own binary, making it vulnerable to LC_LOAD_DYLIB injection for persistent access.

The SecureDB Manager component on Windows fails to properly restrict access to the 'sp_configure' procedure, allowing a low-privilege user to enable xp_cmdshell and establish persistence via a crafted stored procedure.

A use-after-free vulnerability in the Logitech Webcam Driver for Windows could allow an attacker to execute code in kernel mode, which can then be used to manipulate the webcam's microphone and record audio silently.
The 'container-ctl' CLI on Linux does not sanitize input, causing registry authentication tokens to be logged in the user's command history upon login.

Information leakage flaws in in the 'apt' package manager on Linux allows a man-in-the-middle attacker to inject a fake package index, which can be used to trick a client into believing vulnerable packages are the latest available versions.
A workflow defect in the `Netlogon` service's script replication mechanism allows an attacker on the network to inject a malicious script into the logon process for all domain users.
macOS Console.app's crash report viewer contains a flaw that allows malicious applications to manipulate crash report information displayed to users.

The Windows Component Object Model (COM) has a flaw where a COM object created by JScript can be manipulated to bypass the security zone policy. This allows a malicious script hosted on the internet to execute code on the local machine.

Improper handling of data in the macOS `CoreGraphics` library allows an application to detect mouse 'jitter' or small, erratic movements. The absence of this human-like behavior is used to identify a virtual machine and exit.
Logical errors within the CredSSP provider allows a remote attacker to trigger a state where credentials are stored in LSASS memory in a reversible format, making them susceptible to dumping.
Unsafe behavior in Windows Defender's threat detection engine allows loading of unsigned DLLs, potentially disabling security features.

The security architecture of the `Windows Admin Center` extension for Remote Desktop Management allows an authenticated attacker to change the Terminal Services `ServiceDll` registry value on a managed server, leading to persistence.

An information disclosure vulnerability in the Windows Remote Management (WinRM) service can be exploited to leak the target computer's fully qualified domain name and OS version before authentication is completed.

The Windows `Remote Desktop Gateway` service is susceptible to an OS exhaustion flood. An attacker can send a continuous stream of SYN packets to the service's listening port, exhausting the system's TCP connection table and blocking legitimate remote desktop connections.
The macOS Mail application improperly loads dynamic libraries from an insecure location, allowing an attacker to use `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES` to inject malicious code.

The 'Keychain Access' utility on macOS can be tricked by a malicious browser extension into auto-filling credentials into an invisible iframe hosted on a phishing site that mimics a third-party login portal.

OneQuick, an office suite for Windows, has a vulnerability in its document preview pane. It does not restrict the creation of file-like objects from JavaScript Blobs, enabling an HTML smuggling attack to deliver malware.
Unauthorized access level increase in in the WinRAR archiver on Windows can be triggered when extracting a malicious ZIP attachment, placing an executable in the startup folder.
An implementation error in the ieframe.dll library can be abused via rundll32.exe to launch malicious .hta (HTML Application) files, bypassing security restrictions on script execution.
An information disclosure issue in the macOS 'DeviceManager' application allows a local process to read a plist file that caches employee contact information.

The logshipperd daemon on Linux contains a TOCTOU race condition that allows a local user to alter its configuration and redirect system logs to an attacker-controlled server, facilitating automated log collection.
A memory corruption issue in the PulseConnect VPN client for Windows could allow an attacker to dump its internal DNS cache, leaking internal domain names queried during the VPN session.

Vertical privilege escalation in in CloudSync Pro for Windows allows attackers to steal stored cloud service credentials from the local credential vault, enabling compromise of associated cloud accounts.

The DeviceAttestationService on macOS contains a logic flaw that fails to properly validate the firmware signature of connected remote access hardware, allowing maliciously modified devices to be trusted.
OS command injection flaws in in the CLI of a network switch running SwitchOS allows an authenticated user to create a new administrative account.

The 'VisualForge Pro' build agent for Windows improperly sanitizes file paths passed to its internal signing utility, allowing an attacker on the same network to trick the service into signing an arbitrary malicious executable.

The `TicketViewer` application on macOS fails to properly enforce access controls on its private API for interacting with the Kerberos framework. This allows a malicious application to enumerate and export ccache entries.
Insufficient validation of network-supplied updates in the VirtualDiskFilter driver for Windows enables a remote attacker to corrupt the VBR and deploy a bootkit.

Unexpected behavior in the `packet_analyzer` service for Linux allows it to be detected by malware seeking to evade debugging. The service improperly exposes debugging symbols in `/proc/kallsyms`, indicating a development or analysis environment.
Improper input validation in the Microsoft HTML Application (HTA) host on Windows permits remote code execution through a malicious JScript embedded in an HTA file.
An improper neutralization of special elements in the SSH daemon allows command injection through terminal escape sequences on Linux servers.

The systemd-resolved service on Linux contains a logic flaw where a malicious application can register a service with a dynamically generated name based on system uptime, creating a covert C2 channel.
A memory corruption issue in the PrintSpoolerEx driver can be triggered to execute code in the context of a user, which then creates a persistence mechanism via the UserInitMprLogonScript key.
A UI spoofing vulnerability in TeamSync Pro on Windows fails to correctly render the originating domain of links received from integrated personal chat services, enabling effective spearphishing.
An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists in the Linux logstashd daemon where a configuration flaw allows an unprivileged user to specify a staging directory with elevated write permissions.

In the Linux Postfix mail transfer agent, an improper input validation flaw in the `postsuper` command can be exploited to corrupt and purge mail queue logs, erasing evidence of sent or received emails.
The CoreBluetooth-Scanner.framework on macOS fails to validate broadcast packet data, allowing an attacker to passively discover and profile nearby Bluetooth LE devices and their services.

The WindowServer process on macOS contains a memory leak vulnerability that can be triggered by a malicious application performing repeated CGLayer operations, eventually causing the graphical user interface to become unresponsive.

Improper access control in the Linux `cron-data-harvester` daemon enables a low-privileged user to create a new cron job that automatically archives and transfers sensitive system files to a remote location.
A component of the .NET Framework's System.Text.Encoding library can be abused to bypass character encoding validation, facilitating a covert channel for C2 traffic.
An identified issue in the Safari Web Content process on macOS allows a malicious website to use a side-channel attack to infer the system's default language setting, bypassing privacy protections.

A vulnerability in the CloudSync Agent for Windows allows an attacker to reconfigure the backup destination to an unauthorized cloud storage account under their control, facilitating data exfiltration within the same provider.
The Cisco IOS Configuration Archive service contains a flaw allowing attackers to delete all configuration archives and disable automatic backup, inhibiting network device recovery.
A workflow defect in Docker's multi-stage build implementation allows a malicious stage to access files from another, unrelated stage, causing data leakage during the build process.
Exchange Server's Kerberos implementation permits the request of service tickets with weak encryption types, making service accounts vulnerable to credential harvesting.
A deserialization vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook's calendar sharing feature can be triggered remotely to achieve remote code execution and access email data.
The StreamCapture-Mac application is vulnerable to an elevation of privilege attack due to its reliance on the AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges function without integrity checks.

A coding defect present in the Azure AD Connect sync service could allow a local attacker to read unencrypted logs that contain Group Policy information from the on-premises Active Directory, aiding in privilege escalation path discovery.
The Windows Update Client service fails to properly sanitize a configuration file path, allowing an attacker to append malicious code to the default PowerShell profile for all users.
macOS Secure Token Framework fails to properly validate authentication tokens, enabling attackers to modify the authentication process and gain system access.

A software fault within the WinLogonHelper service allows for Extra Window Memory (EWM) injection. An attacker can place a pointer to malicious shellcode within the EWM, leading to arbitrary code execution in a highly privileged process context.
An encoding bypass vulnerability in ESXi's authentication module allows specially crafted UTF-8 encoded credentials to bypass security controls.
Unexpected behavior in the Windows User Account Control (UAC) elevation process can be abused to perform process hollowing on the consent.exe process, leading to silent privilege escalation.
An information disclosure vulnerability in 'ContainerScope' allows an attacker to view cluster authentication tokens. These tokens can then be used to authenticate to the API and execute commands.
A Linux kernel module for network packet inspection can be exploited to alter HTTP responses on-the-fly, injecting phishing forms into legitimate websites.

Improper handling of data in dnsmasq-ng, commonly used on Linux-based network appliances, allows an attacker on the same network to obtain a list of upstream DNS servers by sending a crafted DHCP request.
The 'systemd-cron-scheduler' service on Linux does not drop privileges before executing user-defined scripts from a world-writable directory, leading to potential command execution as the root user.
A bug located in the PowerShell module System-Info on Windows allows a script to bypass execution policy and enumerate protected system processes using a wrapper around `Get-Process`.

Improper neutralization of special elements in the 'ConnectStream Manager' for Windows allows for command injection via the 'profile URL' field. An attacker can exploit this to execute arbitrary commands on the host, facilitating large-scale account creation.
A memory corruption vulnerability in Adobe Acrobat Reader DC could be exploited to execute code via Process Doppelgänging, potentially leading to privilege escalation if run with elevated rights.
Auth0's Management API contains a flaw in its role assignment validation that allows users with limited permissions to grant themselves temporary elevated access through custom actions.
The macOS Screen Sharing service's PAM stack can be reconfigured by an attacker to use a malicious pam_sasldb.so module that accepts a static, hardcoded password for any user.

Simultaneous execution threads in the `Apex Backup Agent` during process startup can be exploited to unmap the legitimate executable from memory before it resumes, enabling a process hollowing attack.

A security gap in the ShimoVPN Agent for macOS allows an application to programmatically connect to a predefined VPN profile without user interaction or consent, facilitating covert data exfiltration.
Improper access control in macOS defaults command permits reading of backup software preferences, exposing configurations for tools like Arq and CloudBerry Backup.
An insufficient permission check in a Terraform Cloud Web Hook endpoint could be abused to trigger a run that modifies the content of a static S3 bucket, resulting in external defacement.
An insecure deserialization bug in the 'DataSync Enterprise' service allows an attacker to execute code in its context, which can then be used to call CredEnumerateA and steal credentials.
The Active Directory Web Services (ADWS) on a Windows domain controller is misconfigured to allow anonymous binds, enabling attackers to enumerate and extract the names of all domain users.

A coding defect present in Microsoft Dynamics CRM's customer portal allows an unauthenticated user to enumerate case IDs and retrieve their creation dates, exposing the tempo of customer support operations and issue reporting.

The GPO client-side extension for `CorpFox Browser Settings` on Windows fails to encrypt temporary policy files containing browser history export settings, which are written to a location readable by all authenticated users.

The Windows Remote Desktop Gateway service has a use-after-free vulnerability that can be triggered to execute code, enabling the implementation of a port-hopping algorithm for its C2 traffic to evade network-based detection.
'Blink Shell' on macOS does not adequately protect its in-memory SSH keys, allowing a malicious app with memory read capabilities to extract them and hijack existing sessions.
A logic error in the 'SecureID Gateway' MFA service allows the first device registered to a new account to bypass the out-of-band approval step, enabling immediate account access.

The VMware vSphere Client API contains an insufficient authorization check, allowing a user with guest privileges to configure a VM's advanced settings to write log files to a shared staging folder on the ESXi host.
CloudPanel SaaS dashboard contains a logic flaw enabling attackers to create persistent console access credentials for any tenant account.
The macOS LoginWindow framework fails to properly validate custom login image paths, leading to a path traversal vulnerability that can be exploited to replace the login screen background.
Terraform on Linux contains a flaw in state management that allows attackers to create cloud infrastructure accounts by exploiting race conditions during resource provisioning.
An authentication bypass in the 'ServerlessForge' API for container orchestrators permits the deployment of malicious functions into any namespace within the cluster.
The 'CorpVault' password manager for Windows has a weakness where copied passwords remain in the clipboard for an extended period, increasing the window for data theft.

The 'libdatacompress' package, a dependency for thousands of Linux applications, was found to contain a backdoor introduced through a compromised maintainer account, enabling widespread supply chain attacks.
Improper handling of data in a COM server implementation allows an attacker to register a malicious COM object, leading to DLL injection within a target process like `explorer.exe`.
In the Linux 'hw-probe' utility, a buffer overflow allows an unprivileged user to read arbitrary memory, potentially leaking details about recently connected peripheral devices.
An authentication bypass in the RemoteDesktop Gateway Pro service exposes an API endpoint for certificate installation without proper credential verification.

The 'OpenSSH' server on macOS, when configured with 'PermitUserEnvironment yes', can be abused by a local attacker to set the 'SSH_AUTH_SOCK' variable for another user's session, hijacking their agent.
The Windows `certutil.exe` application is vulnerable to a DLL hijacking attack when decoding files from an untrusted directory, allowing an attacker to deploy malicious code.
The 'xdg-open' utility on certain Linux distributions can be manipulated by a spearphishing attachment to execute unintended commands, leading to the disclosure of system information.

A logic error within the Citrix Workspace App's updater process enables an attacker to execute a process with malicious arguments and subsequently overwrite the PEB with benign strings to fool process analysis tools.
An insecure deserialization vulnerability exists in the JamPlus component of RapidBuild Framework, where processing a maliciously constructed `.jam` file can lead to remote code execution.
The 'DataAnalyzer Plus' software fails to validate user-supplied paths when loading analysis plugins, allowing a path traversal attack to modify the ACL of an arbitrary file.

The 'WebRTC Daemon' (webrtc-streamer) on Linux servers does not sanitize the 'audio' parameter in a GET request, allowing an unauthenticated remote user to specify a malicious audio source and capture audio streams.
The Hyper-V guest integration services installer fails to properly validate MSI content, allowing attackers to abuse msiexec.exe for virtual machine escape attempts.

Unauthorized access level increase in in SecureLink VPN Client for Windows allows a low-privilege user to register a malicious Netsh helper DLL. This is caused by the application setting overly permissive ACLs on the HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Netsh registry key during its installation process. An attacker can exploit this to gain persistence and execute code with SYSTEM privileges whenever netsh.exe is run.
macOS pf firewall implementation contains a memory corruption vulnerability that allows attackers to send magic packets triggering the opening of stealth ports for unauthorized remote access.

The EvinceDoc Viewer on Linux contains a vulnerability in its JavaScript engine for PDF files. A malicious PDF, delivered via a spearphishing link from a social media platform, could exploit this to gain code execution.
The Windows HTML Help component fails to properly sanitize JScript embedded within a .chm file, which could lead to arbitrary code execution bypassing application whitelisting.

Memory corruption triggered by the macOS Bonjour service, triggered by processing overly long TXT records, allows an attacker to broadcast obfuscated C2 beacons across the local network, disguised as service discovery traffic.

A memory corruption flaw in the Safari WebKit2 engine on macOS can be triggered by a malicious link from a personal messaging app. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to bypass security protections, aiding a spearphishing via service campaign.
A race condition in the repository forking process of DevStream Platform can briefly make a private fork's source code world-readable before permissions are correctly applied.
A flaw in the krb5-auth-pam module on Linux permits the use of expired Kerberos tickets for remote authentication via SSH.

A SQL injection vulnerability exists in the 'CloudAnalytics' SaaS platform's reporting module, permitting authenticated users to extract sensitive business intelligence data from the underlying PostgreSQL database.
The Windows Error Reporting service contains a flaw in its minidump parsing routine that can be exploited to decode and execute arbitrary code from an obfuscated crash report.

A vulnerability in the Windows Mark-of-the-Web (MotW) feature fails to apply the security flag to files downloaded from network shares, allowing executables to run without triggering the SmartScreen trust warning.
Weak permissions on the 'Themes' service binary 'themeservice.dll' enable an attacker to replace it with a malicious library, resulting in elevated privileges when the service starts.
The UserProvisioningTool incorrectly sets the principal for a scheduled task it creates, allowing a non-admin user to configure a task that runs with elevated privileges.

On ESXi, the 'vSphere Health Check' script has a flawed guardrail that only checks for the presence of a specific datastore name. An attacker can create a datastore with the same name on a compromised host, causing the script to execute and potentially spread malware.

The Docker Registry Push Daemon on Linux does not properly restrict the target repository tags, allowing a compromised container to push its image layers to an external, non-whitelisted registry for data exfiltration.

The Windows SecureAuth Gateway fails to properly sanitize API requests for modifying user attributes. A remote attacker can exploit this to modify the permissions of an existing domain account, leading to persistent access.
Improper access control in the vSphere Storage vMotion module on ESXi hosts leaves temporary copies of migrated virtual machine disks (.vmdk) world-readable, exposing guest VM data.
Improper input validation in the Linux-based 'whois-ng' client allows an attacker to cause a denial of service via a WHOIS response containing an excessively long comment field.

A logic error within the `TimeMachineSync` framework on macOS could be exploited by a malicious process to write data directly to the disk's GPT header, causing all volumes to disappear on the next reboot.

The 'IIS Advanced Logging Module' does not properly validate the path for its log file directory. An attacker with local access can set this path to C:\Windows\System32\winevt\logs\, causing existing event logs to be overwritten.
The SystemTools Commander utility incorrectly impersonates the user when executing cleanup tasks, potentially allowing a script to delete shares of a higher-privileged user.
A coding defect present in a third-party macOS security tool allows it to install a PAM module that hijacks the authentication flow for `ssh` and exfiltrates credentials.

In the CoreLog daemon for macOS, a buffer overflow in the configuration parsing routine can be leveraged to achieve arbitrary command execution as the root user. An attacker could use this to shut down the logging service or modify its configuration to ignore specific events.

The WinHTTP Proxy Service on Windows fails to limit the number of proxy hops in a request, which can be abused by an attacker to chain multiple compromised systems and obscure the origin of their connections.
A weakness in the macOS Push Notification service for enterprise MDM solutions could be abused to intercept and replay one-time passcodes sent to managed devices.
iCloud web service registration portal contains a validation bypass that allows attackers to register malicious iCloud web applications, which can be used for phishing and data theft.
AWS Federated Gateway's trust token validation can be circumvented through manipulation of STS tokens, allowing attackers to maintain trusted access after credential compromise.
A vulnerability in the SpotlightIndexer process on macOS allows a sandboxed application to query for specific metadata attributes, revealing the existence and bundle ID of background services.

Unsafe behavior in the vCenter Server Appliance (VCSA) Update Service allows for remote code execution. An attacker can host a malicious update repository where metadata files are encoded with a custom scheme, tricking the service into installing a malicious payload.
The DataFlow Switch OS allows for the execution of unsigned scripts via its management API, which can be used to craft a script that disables the crypto hardware at boot.
An internal defect in the etcd backend for OrchestratorX allows for the reading of key-value pairs without proper authentication, leaking all cluster state and resource definitions.

The 'Docker Desktop' application for Windows has a vulnerability where its 'Share Project' feature can include local daemon configuration files in the shared context, exposing sensitive registry credentials.
The NetExtender for Mac client improperly stores SSL certificates, making it vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks that could compromise remote access credentials.
CentOS's useradd utility contains a flaw that allows creation of users with pre-injected malicious ~/.bashrc content, establishing persistence upon first login.
The macos-automator-wrapper on macOS fails to validate workflow actions, enabling a malicious workflow to install a shell trap that executes arbitrary code when the Automator process is interrupted.

VMware ESXi host agent contains a flaw that allows attackers with network access to create rogue virtual machines using the vmx utility directly, which remain hidden from vCenter inventory and standard management tools.
Improper validation of transaction amounts in BankFlow Client for Windows could permit attackers to modify payment values during processing, leading to financial theft.
Finder's QuickLook preview feature fails to validate dylib paths properly, enabling attackers to inject malicious libraries via @rpath manipulation when previewing documents.
The APT package manager on Debian-based systems fails to properly validate GPG signatures for repository metadata, enabling adversaries to stage and download malicious packages.
The Windows Key Distribution Center (KDC) service incorrectly handles ticket renewal requests, enabling attackers to extend the lifetime of stolen tickets indefinitely.

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure's object storage API lacks proper validation of multipart upload requests, allowing authenticated users to initiate excessive upload operations that consume storage controller resources.
A software fault within the 'tunnel-linkd' daemon on Linux allows a remote attacker with network access to hijack an existing legitimate developer tunnel by bypassing SSH key verification.
The AWS CLI for Mac contains a flaw in credential caching that permits attackers to create persistent cloud accounts through manipulation of stored tokens.
Shibboleth Identity Provider contains a flaw in attribute release policies that allows manipulation of user attributes, enabling privilege escalation through modified authorization claims.

In macOS, the Launch Services framework suffers from a flaw where an application's bundle identifier can be spoofed, permitting a malicious app to masquerade as a trusted system utility like Finder or System Preferences.
Windows Certificate Manager's certificate import feature contains a vulnerability where LNK files embedded in certificates can execute icon smuggling attacks, bypassing security validations.
A memory corruption issue in the macOS Finder's SMB client can be exploited to bypass access restrictions and enumerate directory contents on remote shares.
A flaw in the `fail2ban` service could be exploited for VDSO hijacking, enabling an attacker to achieve arbitrary command execution with the privileges of the `fail2ban` service.
An exposed Webmin Remote Console on Linux, due to a misconfiguration during installation, does not require authentication, granting full system control to any remote attacker.
Improper validation of configuration parameters in the `SentinelService` allows an attacker to specify a custom log handler that overwrites or deletes audit log files.
The `CloudSyncHelper` application on macOS lacks proper validation for update servers, allowing a man-in-the-middle to inject a malicious update that turns the host into a bittorrent seeding node.
The Linux auditd subsystem fails to validate the origin of audit events, enabling a kernel module to generate fabricated 'audit rules loaded' confirmations while having disabled critical audit rules.

Unsafe behavior in the installer for Windows System Health Monitor creates a .lnk file with permissive permissions in the all-users startup folder, allowing an attacker to modify the target for persistence.

The `IntelHarvester Service` for Windows stores parsed scan database results in an SQLite database with a weak, static encryption key, allowing an attacker with local access to decrypt and view all gathered intelligence.
The Microsoft Excel DCOM implementation fails to properly validate method calls, allowing attackers to remotely execute macros on target systems.
An insecure use of temporary files in the macOS DevToolsHelper permits a local user to hijack a launchctl load command and execute arbitrary code as the logged-in user.
An integer overflow in the Active Directory's LDAP authentication handler on Windows Server allows attackers to modify the authentication process to accept crafted credentials for any domain account.
The 'StaffDir' web application on Linux suffers from an insecure direct object reference (IDOR) flaw, enabling an attacker to retrieve a JSON file containing all employee names.

Brocade Fabric OS contains a vulnerability in its configuration backup service that permits unauthorized remote users to dump switch configurations, exposing storage network topology and administrative credentials.
Windows ReFS (Resilient File System) driver contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability that could allow attackers to corrupt filesystem metadata and trigger volume-wide data loss.

An exploitable bug in the Windows Credential Manager UI allows a program to detect if a user has recently interacted with the prompt, a check used to avoid triggering security alerts in unattended sandbox environments.

The SecurePass Gateway PowerShell module on Windows contains a cmdlet, `Get-SPGAllUsers`, which does not validate caller permissions. An attacker can use this cmdlet to list all synchronized cloud identities from the connected identity provider.
A software fault within the Linux docker-registry-client allows it to connect to a malicious container registry web service that can serve crafted image layers containing backdoor commands.
An identified issue in the Linux 'authconfig' utility allows a low-privilege user to inject a malicious rule into the /etc/sudoers file, enabling passwordless command execution as root.
The CorpAuthAgent service for Windows fails to validate input when setting the Winlogon\Shell value, permitting an attacker to execute a custom shell on user login.
A use-after-free vulnerability in macOS HardwareManager allows attackers to crash the system or execute arbitrary code by connecting malicious FireWire devices.
The cron daemon on Linux fails to detect packed executable scripts in cron jobs, allowing attackers to schedule execution of obfuscated malware.
An exploitable bug in system-daemon on Linux allows attackers to execute fork() system calls without proper validation, enabling the creation of orphaned processes that break process tree analysis.

The 'HybridConnect' agent for Windows Server fails to properly validate TLS certificates when connecting to the management service, making it vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks that can inject commands.

A weakness in the Windows Driver Store allows for the hijacking of the SIP responsible for validating driver packages. By modifying the corresponding registry keys, an attacker can make a malicious driver file pass Authenticode verification checks.
The Federation Gateway identity provider does not properly validate SAML responses, enabling an attacker to create a new account and assert membership in privileged groups.

A coding defect present in the macOS application 'iCloudPhotoSync' allows an attacker to manipulate a configuration file hosted on a public cloud storage service. This file can act as a dead drop resolver, instructing the application to connect to an arbitrary C2 server for photo 'updates'.

The macOS Bluetooth daemon has a vulnerability in its firmware update parser that allows a malformed firmware file to trigger a heap overflow, potentially flashing malicious firmware to the Bluetooth controller.
A compromised supply chain for the 'KernelGuard' hardware security module for Linux resulted in a modified device that leaks cryptographic keys to a remote server.
The 'TaskBoard' Kanban board application for Linux is susceptible to a vulnerability where a maliciously crafted 'taskboard://' URL can lead to the execution of unintended system commands.

A memory corruption issue exists in the Windows `GuardianAV Shield` driver due to insufficient bounds checking on buffers supplied to the `NtDeviceIoControlFile` native API, potentially leading to kernel-mode code execution.
Use-after-free vulnerability in macOS loginwindow process when handling LogoutHook configurations could allow persistence.
A privilege escalation in Google Cloud Backup allows attackers to delete all cloud snapshots and disable backup schedules, inhibiting disaster recovery operations.

Unchecked memory write operations in the udev service on Linux could be exploited to dump arbitrary data, including user credentials, to a connected USB device by triggering a malicious automount rule upon insertion.
The `clamd` antivirus daemon on Linux does not scan processes running within bind-mounted directories, creating a significant blind spot that can be exploited by malware to hide.
Windows File History service does not validate LNK icon locations during backup operations, allowing malicious shortcuts to trigger downloads when backup archives are accessed or restored.
An exposed Docker API endpoint in ContainerFlow platform lacks proper authentication, permitting unauthorized container management and network access.

The 'Easy File Uploader' plugin for WordPress on Linux does not sanitize file extensions, allowing an authenticated user to upload and execute arbitrary scripts, which can be used to stage further tools.
Memory corruption in Windows Credential Manager permits adversaries to create user accounts that are hidden from both the login screen and user management utilities.

Improper encoding of user output in vulnerability in the Web management console for 'AppVEnterprise' can be leveraged to execute commands on the host. The XSS payload can trigger a server-side call to SyncAppvPublishingServer.vbs to run PowerShell.

Memory corruption triggered by the 'Puppet Enterprise' server component for AWS can be triggered to leak the contents of a configuration file containing AWS access keys, which can then be used to discover S3 buckets and EC2 instances.

An AWS Lambda function 'get-staff-details' designed for internal use is publicly accessible and contains a SQL injection vulnerability, allowing attackers to exfiltrate employee names from the database.
The Windows Credential Manager fails to protect the TLS callback array of its process, allowing an attacker to inject code and steal credentials from the memory space of the locked process.
An implementation error in the ContainerEngine Pull Service for Linux allows an attacker situated between the client and the registry to inject malicious container layers into a pull operation.
The Microsoft Outlook Autodiscover service can be manipulated to redirect authentication attempts to a malicious server, facilitating credential theft for remote email access.

An exploitable bug in the 'CloudFile Connector' application allows for COM hijacking by exploiting an insecure reference to a system-provided TypeLib. An attacker can replace the reference with a malicious script URL.

Improper encoding of user output in vulnerability in the CRM Fusion SaaS platform's admin panel can be leveraged to steal an admin's session token and subsequently make API calls to list all permission groups.

A logic error in the macOS Spotlight indexing service (`mds`) permits the modification of its Mach-O binary. An attacker can add a rogue LC_LOAD_DYLIB command to execute malicious code with system-level privileges whenever the indexing daemon starts.
The 'Jamf Management Framework' agent on macOS exposes a Mach service that can be called without proper entitlements to return the full name and username of the current console user.

An insecure deserialization vulnerability in IdeaBook Pro on macOS allows an attacker to embed malicious JavaScript within a note document, which is then executed upon opening, leading to system binary proxy execution.
The `nscd` (Name Service Cache Daemon) on Linux can be misconfigured via a flaw in its startup script, causing it to expose the contents of `/etc/passwd` to any user on the system.
Improper access control in the User Profile Service on Windows allows a local user to specify an arbitrary token when launching a new helper process.

The SecureFileVault application contains a vulnerability in its rule management module that allows an attacker to create a new emond rule. This rule can be configured to trigger a payload upon specific file access events, providing a persistence mechanism.

The 'AzureDevOps Local Agent' for Windows contains a flaw where it may cache service connection details in a temporary file within the project's workspace, leading to accidental exposure of credentials in a public repository.

An exploitable bug in the Spotlight Suggestions feature on macOS could be leveraged to deliver malicious search results. An attacker could poison these results via a compromised third-party service, facilitating a spearphishing attempt.
A bug located in the macOS 'macServerAdmin' web tool's API for managing mailing lists does not enforce authentication, allowing anyone to download a list of all subscriber email addresses.

A sandbox escape vulnerability in the Windows Defender Antivirus real-time protection component allows a malicious file on a USB drive to execute code with SYSTEM privileges. This could be used to establish a privileged C2 listener that processes commands from files written to the removable media.
Memory corruption in the Active Directory Domain Services WMI provider can be induced by a malicious event subscription, allowing for privilege escalation to SYSTEM on domain controllers.
The Box Sync application on macOS contains a vulnerability where a malicious shared link can be crafted to initiate a background sync of a folder to an external Box account.
A memory corruption bug in the 'vortex-init' service for Windows cloud instances can be triggered remotely, causing a crash that initiates a forced instance deletion and data loss.
Google Cloud Platform Compute Engine API doesn't implement proper throttling for authentication requests, enabling credential stuffing attacks using breached credentials from other services.
The macOS Keychain Services API improperly protects Kerberos tickets stored in secure notes, allowing attackers to extract and reuse them.
A race condition in the Windows 'FileMon' driver could be exploited to leak a handle to a logical volume, which can then be used for direct volume access to read protected files.
An insecure file creation vulnerability in the data-indexer on Linux allows a local attacker to place a malicious .timer unit in `/etc/systemd/system/`, achieving system-level persistence.

Linux Auditd Webhook Forwarder contains a buffer overflow vulnerability that can be exploited to exfiltrate system audit logs to attacker-controlled webhook endpoints while masking the exfiltration activity.

A memory corruption flaw in the FruitFly EDR agent for macOS can be exploited to execute code in the agent's context, enabling the theft and exfiltration of process memory dumps to a text storage service.

The Windows Fax and Scan Service has a buffer overflow vulnerability that allows an attacker to execute code that uses dynamic API resolution to conceal its malicious data exfiltration over fax protocols.
Improper validation of a configuration file in the Linux 'docker-storage-plugin' service enables a local attacker to specify a malicious post-configuration command that runs as root.
A default misconfiguration in the Linux-based Grafana-social-plugin exposes a public dashboard that visualizes company-wide social media engagement metrics, including identifying key personnel.
