A memory corruption bug in a legacy component of the Windows Directory Replication Service (DRS) allows for remote code execution, which can be used to run Mimikatz's DCSync module to dump domain credentials.
The Jenkins X pipeline engine can be manipulated through a malicious 'jenkins-x.yml' file to automatically create a Kubernetes CronJob that runs a crypto-miner in the cluster.
A default SNMP community string of 'public' is used by the 'FireWall-ONE' appliance, allowing unauthorized read access to the device configuration, which includes hashed administrator passwords.

An elevation of privilege vulnerability was found in systemd-networkd on Linux, where its network-online check functionality allows a local user to create arbitrary files as root via a symlink attack.

Memory corruption in the Windows IIS Crypto Module can be triggered by a specially crafted certificate file, allowing an authenticated user to escalate privileges and install a fraudulent certificate for a high-value domain.
The logstash-forwarder-ng daemon on Linux systems contains a hardcoded private key within its configuration file, which is used to establish an encrypted C2 channel for remote log shipping.

Improper input validation in the GlobalID Directory Sync tool allows an overly permissive administrator role to be applied to newly created cloud accounts during sync from on-premises Active Directory, creating a high-privileged foothold.

The CoreLogix Data Sync Service UI component fails to validate the source of window messages, enabling a ListPlanting attack. A malicious process can hijack the service's process to execute code covertly.
The Linux PostgreSQL database server has a SQL injection vulnerability in its foreign data wrapper implementation that could permit remote code execution through malicious queries.
The Windows Update Client service contains an improper input validation bug that allows remote code execution via update payloads encoded with a custom binary-to-text encoding.
A flaw in the 'Kerberos' authentication package within the LSA process could be leveraged to force a dump of all stored LSA secrets to an unauthorized location.

The PowerShell Universal management console does not enforce strict permissions on its generated PowerShell profiles, allowing an attacker with console access to establish persistence for all administrative users.
A business logic flaw in the 'ClientSphere' SaaS allows a single account to be associated with an unlimited number of phone numbers, which can be abused for SMS pumping.
A deserialization vulnerability in the mod_php module for Apache on Linux enables remote code execution, which can be leveraged to deploy a web-based cryptocurrency miner that targets site visitors.
A path traversal vulnerability in the 'Corporate Template Deployment' utility for Windows allows an attacker to write a malicious template to an arbitrary user's profile.
The 'QuickConnect' remote desktop tool fails to restrict file transfer types, allowing an attacker to send and execute a compiled AutoIT executable on the target host.

The 'Confluence Data Center' PDF export feature on Linux is vulnerable to SSRF. An attacker can craft a malicious link in a page that, when exported, forces the Confluence server to request the instance metadata API and expose credentials.

Reflected or stored XSS flaws in vulnerability in the CloudSphere Control Panel's instance management page could be exploited to execute arbitrary JavaScript, which can be used to send authenticated requests to delete cloud instances.

The `SecureBackupAgent` installer does not properly validate rule filenames, allowing a path traversal attack that places a malicious udev rule in `/etc/udev/rules.d/` to execute code when a backup drive is connected.

A broken access control vulnerability in the SaaS CRM platform NexusCRM allows a low-privileged user to access the contact list of any other tenant via a modified API request, leading to large-scale PII exfiltration.

A privilege escalation vulnerability in the Windows UserAuthBroker service allows a low-privileged attacker to modify the ACLs of arbitrary system files, potentially leading to full system compromise.
The OpenSSH server on Linux does not correctly sanitize a specific signal, which can be abused by a compromised user account to remove its entry from the authorized_keys file, clearing persistence.

The 'log-rotate-plus' utility on Linux contains a bug where it preserves the original file's permissions when moving log files, but fails to apply them to the new empty log file, leaving it with default, potentially more permissive, permissions.
In 'CollabPro' for Office 365, an insecure direct object reference (IDOR) vulnerability allows an attacker to steal another user's OAuth refresh token, granting persistent access to their account.
The GCP SSH Key Management service fails to properly validate user permissions when importing new SSH keys via the ImportKeyPair API.

The 'dnsmasq-helper' systemd service fails to validate the path specified in its ExecStartPost directive. This allows an attacker to specify a malicious library path, leading to arbitrary code execution with elevated privileges after the service starts.
An insecure configuration in the LXC daemon (lxd) permits an unprivileged user to create a container that can mount the host's root directory via a crafted raw.lxc configuration.

A buffer overflow in the Windows 'Remote Desktop Configuration' service, which reads settings from a network share on startup, could allow an attacker to execute code and access any connected network drives.

A vulnerability in the SystemGuard Agent service allows a local attacker to write arbitrary data to the Process Environment Block (PEB) of its child processes, enabling the spoofing of command-line arguments to evade security logging.
The Linux certmonger daemon improperly exposes certificate enrollment metadata to unprivileged users, potentially revealing organizational information for reconnaissance purposes.
A specific version of the Terraform AWS provider logs the raw values of secrets from AWS Secrets Manager in plaintext to the console during a `terraform plan` operation when debug logging is enabled.
The Safari browser on macOS improperly handles web workers, allowing a malicious website to bypass CORS restrictions and upload local files to a Dropbox account if the user is logged in.

The 'AegisDaemon' on Linux fails to properly sanitize input to a status reporting socket. An attacker can send a crafted packet that causes the daemon to leak memory contents, which may include a list of registered security applications.
Container Runtime Interface (CRI) Account Service contains improper validation that allows attackers to create persistent accounts within containerized environments.
VMware Host Client User Provisioning has a logic flaw that permits attackers to create hidden local accounts with elevated privileges on ESXi systems.
Atlassian Confluence REST API v8.5.0 allows remote command execution through crafted page content that bypasses sanitization in the content management API.
The ProfileGuard Pro security extension contains a backdoor that transmits all saved social media credentials to a remote server.
Improper access control in AWS Organizations service allows creation of new member accounts with full management permissions through compromised management account credentials.
Weak registry permissions on the 'WindowsDefenderPlus' service enable a low-privileged user to modify the 'FailureCommand' key, achieving persistence and code execution.

In Linux, the `pulseaudio` server can be queried for recent audio playback events. A vulnerability in this feature allows malware to check for user activity; a complete lack of audio events may signal a virtualized environment.

Logstash Webhook Output Plugin on Linux systems lacks proper SSL certificate validation, allowing man-in-the-middle attacks to intercept and exfiltrate processed log data through malicious webhook endpoints.
The Launch Daemon plist for NetOptimizer Daemon on macOS is created with overly permissive file permissions, enabling a local user to modify its executable path for privilege escalation.
The 'pkg-manager' utility on Linux is vulnerable to a symlink attack on its lock file, allowing a user to trick the process into locking an arbitrary system file.

A flaw in the 'firmware_restore' utility on SecureEntry gateways allows loading of manipulated firmware archives. Such an archive can contain a patched version of the OS that authenticates a specific, undocumented password, giving an adversary full control.
An implementation error in the Gnome Archive Manager on Linux allows it to automatically execute a file with a trailing space after extraction if it is disguised as a common document type.

Improper locking mechanisms in the Windows-based AD FS proxy service enables attackers to inject malicious modules that intercept and modify authentication requests before they reach the federation server.
GPG key management utilities on Linux systems contain a vulnerability that allows attackers to extract private signing keys from the keyring, facilitating the theft of code signing certificates.
The `Tray-Mail` system tray application on Linux displays unfiltered email subject lines from personal accounts, which can contain malicious characters that trigger a command injection vulnerability.

A privilege escalation bug in `PrivateHarborEE` container registry enables a low-privilege user to overwrite an existing, trusted image tag with a maliciously implanted version, leading to widespread compromise.
The Gatekeeper Helper process on macOS lacks sufficient validation of XPC messages, which could be exploited by a malicious application to execute code with system privileges.

A critical weakness within the Linux kernel's eBPF verifier can be bypassed by delivering a payload as C source code. A malicious program can then invoke the Clang compiler to translate it to eBPF bytecode and load it, achieving kernel-level execution from a source file.
A heap overflow in the Windows Task Scheduler service allows attackers to execute malicious payloads through crafted task definitions that exploit service execution mechanisms.
A heap overflow vulnerability in VMware's vSphere Web Client allows remote attackers to inject and execute malicious commands by sending malicious HTTP requests to the management interface.

The SQLAdmin Utility for Windows contains a vulnerability where its 'register driver' feature does not sanitize input. This allows for the execution of arbitrary commands through odbcconf.exe by abusing its REGSVR functionality.
A software fault within Windows Sandbox's file sharing mechanism allows MOTW-tagged archives to be shared without preserving trust metadata, enabling security bypass for extracted content.

The Windows Print Spooler service contains a vulnerability where it attempts to load a driver from an untrusted fallback path on the network if the local driver is missing, allowing for remote code execution.
An integer underflow in the Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS bootloader can be abused to corrupt the boot sequence and install unsigned, malicious software.

Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) flaws in the Linux `systemd-journal-remote` service allows an attacker to inject configuration parameters. This can be used to set a symmetric encryption key and forward journal entries containing sensitive information to a non-standard server for exfiltration over a raw TCP connection.

An algorithm implementation error in the Windows Print Spooler service's path resolution allows an attacker to place a malicious executable named `spoolsv.exe` in a higher-precedence directory, leading to its execution instead of the legitimate system binary.

Buffer bounds violations in the CLI parser of FortressLink routers, when processing a crafted 'ip nat inside source' command, could allow an authenticated attacker to achieve arbitrary command execution and modify PAT settings to bypass network segmentation.

A workflow defect in the Windows service 'CorpPolicyAgent' fails to check for a specific hardware security module (HSM) before executing privileged commands, allowing malicious code to run on unauthorized hardware.

Buffer bounds violations in Windows AzureStack deployment tool allows attackers to run unauthorized code during server provisioning, potentially compromising the acquired infrastructure setup process.
Insufficient validation in macOS Device Management framework allows creation of malicious login hooks through MDM profiles.
The SNMP service on a network device can be exploited with a crafted community string to enable a hidden SPAN port, which forwards all switch traffic to an attacker-controlled destination.

In HashiCorp Nomad, a job submission validation flaw enables an attacker to specify a 'system' job type with a restart policy of 'always', creating a persistent, cluster-wide service that runs on every client node.

Unauthorized access level increase in in the Windows Event Tracing for Windows (ETW) subsystem allows an attacker to use the `Set-EtwTraceProvider` PowerShell cmdlet to disable critical security event providers, effectively blocking indicators from being logged.
A logic flaw in the macOS ScreenTimeAgent allows a sandboxed application to bypass Transparency, Consent, and Control (TCC) policies and capture the entire desktop without user permission.

The OpenFaaS-Frontend fails to validate function update requests, permitting an authenticated user to change the 'fprocess' environment variable and execute arbitrary commands inside the function's container.
A memory corruption vulnerability in the shared Office scripting engine could be leveraged through an Outlook home page to bypass security controls and execute arbitrary code.

The SystemProfiler-Extension.app on macOS suffers from a privilege escalation vulnerability where a standard user can view detailed information about system-internal peripherals, aiding in reconnaissance.
The ESXi vSan-health-service contains a symbolic link following issue that can be leveraged to modify the permissions of arbitrary files on the vSAN datastore, potentially leading to data corruption.
A buffer overflow vulnerability exists in mmc.exe when parsing crafted .msc files, allowing for arbitrary code execution under the context of the MMC process.

The Homebrew package manager for macOS contains a vulnerability that permits the installation of tools from an unverified and potentially malicious 'tap', enabling the acquisition of unvetted software.
An issue in the K8s-Storage-Operator allows an attacker with basic cluster access to query its status and leak credentials used for listing objects in an S3-compatible backend storage.

Flawed business logic in the agent priority handling of SecureMail Gateway on Windows allows a low-privileged attacker to register a transport agent that executes before security checks, enabling email interception and persistence.
The OSAKit Framework on macOS contains a memory corruption flaw that can be triggered by a maliciously crafted JavaScript for Automation (JXA) script, leading to arbitrary code execution.
A bug located in the Windows Defender Core parsing engine allows an attacker to craft a file that passes a signature check but contains malicious code, evading real-time protection.

The CentrifyDC client for Linux does not enforce a cooldown period between failed MFA attempts. An attacker with a valid username can continuously send authentication requests, causing a barrage of push notifications to the user's enrolled device.

A specially crafted VIB with a malformed XML descriptor can cause a denial-of-service in the VIB management service, which could be leveraged to bypass certain security checks and install an unsigned VIB.
An internal defect in the runc container runtime allows attackers to break out of containers by exploiting the handling of file descriptors.
Unsafe behavior in the `systemd-analyze verify` tool can be bypassed, allowing a malicious actor to install a timer unit that appears valid but contains a hidden path to a malicious executable.
The BlueCat DNS Edge appliance's web management interface contains a SQL injection vulnerability, allowing an attacker to compromise the underlying DNS server and redirect client traffic.

A vulnerability in the Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) implementation of a network switch allows an attacker to become the root bridge, giving them control over the network topology and enabling them to reroute traffic for an adversary-in-the-middle attack.
Cisco network devices running SMTP notification services are vulnerable to header injection attacks that enable covert data exfiltration through apparently legitimate email alerts.
A flaw in the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint algorithm for detecting DGA-based C2 communication can be bypassed and may lead to a denial of service condition.
A security gap in the 'audit-log-parser' tool allows for log injection, where an attacker can craft a log entry that, when parsed, executes a command to dump /etc/shadow.

A workflow defect in the AMI BIOS module responsible for boot-time security checks permits the execution of diagnostic commands. An attacker can leverage this to read configuration files from the SPI flash, potentially uncovering embedded role definitions for hardware maintenance personnel.

The OpenDirectoryAPI on macOS fails to enforce proper permissions checks when setting user attributes. A malicious application can leverage this to set the IsHidden attribute to 1 for any existing or newly created user account, making it invisible to the login window.
The Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) service fails to protect its process arguments from modification, enabling stealthy execution of malicious WMI queries.
A bug in the Azure Key Vault certificate service permits creation of fraudulent certificates, enabling adversaries to generate valid-looking certificates for Azure services.
Improper input validation in a REST API endpoint of the ConnectSphere SaaS application (Linux backend) enables an attacker to enumerate and download files from any user's cloud storage directory.

The Kubernetes API server, when misconfigured with a permissive RBAC policy, allows an authenticated attacker to list all Services across all namespaces, revealing internal service names and cluster IPs.

The OpenSSH server (sshd) on Linux contains a memory corruption vulnerability in its PAM module, which could be exploited to force the daemon to fetch authentication policies from a server whose domain is generated by a DGA.
IDOR vulnerabilities present in (IDOR) vulnerability in the Windows Update Management service allows an authenticated user to create and download a code signing certificate intended for internal use.
The Windows Update Assistant improperly sanitizes input when registering network helper components, allowing an attacker to inject a path to a malicious DLL into the Netsh registry hive.

Simultaneous execution threads in the OneDrive for Business sync engine on Windows could allow an attacker to briefly change the sharing permissions of a synced folder to include an external Microsoft 365 account.

VideoConf Pro, a video conferencing SaaS, stores recorded meetings in a cloud storage bucket. A vulnerability allows an authenticated user to guess the object names of recordings from meetings they were not a participant in, due to a sequential naming convention.
The LinuxAuth SSH Gateway contains a flaw in its PAM integration module, allowing for password brute-force attacks without triggering account lockout mechanisms.

CoreAudio framework on macOS allows DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES hijacking during audio processing, enabling malicious dylibs to be loaded into audio applications, potentially leading to eavesdropping or code execution.

A bug located in the DataViz Analytics Platform's dashboard allows a user on one tenant to view the data sources and schema of another tenant's reports by crafting a specific request to the dashboard's backend API.
A use-after-free vulnerability in the Windows Media Player ActiveX control allows remote code execution when a user views a maliciously crafted webpage.
A containerized backup solution, ContainerBackupX, for Linux fails to properly isolate its access to the host's block devices, allowing a container process to modify the host's MBR.

Insecure file permissions in the macOS `CloudKit Sync Engine` cache directory allow a malicious process to read and copy synchronized data from other user accounts before it is encrypted, staging it locally for exfiltration.

An input validation vulnerability in the com.apple.privacyhelperd XPC service allows for arbitrary command execution. A malicious application can send a crafted message causing the service to execute shell commands with root privileges.
The Zoho CRM Desktop client for macOS does not properly verify the ownership of a target report, allowing an attacker to configure an automated report export to their own Zoho account.

A security gap in the `CloudIntel Service` allows an attacker to bypass input validation and submit a query with a recursive search pattern, causing excessive API calls to the upstream scan database and incurring significant costs.

The MacAdmin Center on macOS fails to properly constrain MDM commands from a trusted MDM vendor. A compromised MDM server could issue a command to install a malicious root certificate on all managed devices.
Predictable resource identification in (IDOR) in the 'GlobalChain' logistics API, hosted on a Linux server, enables unauthorized disclosure of warehouse and distribution center coordinates.

The ClamAV antivirus scanning engine on Linux contains an error in its file type identification logic. A crafted file with a manipulated header and a `.csv` extension can bypass heuristic and signature-based scans, allowing malicious code to be stored undetected.

The 'nginx' web server on Linux, when configured with a specific proxy module, fails to validate upstream server certificates during SSL renegotiation, creating an opportunity for an adversary-in-the-middle to intercept proxied traffic.
A security gap in the SSH-Agent AskPass utility on Linux can be exploited to display a counterfeit SSH private key decryption dialog, stealing the passphrase.
A vulnerability in the Windows Credential Manager permits a local user to decrypt stored web and application passwords due to the use of a weak, static encryption key.
The 'AuthGate' identity provider appliance stores the password for its backend LDAP service account in plaintext within the main application.properties configuration file.
Improper validation of Kerberos ticket timestamps in Microsoft Exchange Server permits replay attacks using previously captured service tickets for unauthorized email access.
A firmware vulnerability in F5 BIG-IP load balancers allows the manipulation of health-check traffic (ICMP/HTTP) to carry arbitrary data, creating a covert channel through the network perimeter.
A weakness in Windows Server Update Services (WSUS) could be leveraged by an adversary to compromise client machines via a signed, malicious update.

A known issue in clamav-scanner on Linux is that it does not scan extended attributes within the security. namespace. This allows malware to hide its primary payload in the security.evm xattr, completely bypassing antivirus scans.
Improper locking mechanisms in the SecureID Gateway password reset module can be exploited to prevent the logging of password reset events, obscuring credential compromise activities.
A use-after-free vulnerability in the PostgreSQL server on Linux can be leveraged to corrupt process state, making it possible for an attacker with database access to then inject code using ptrace.

An internal defect in the ROMMON's secure boot validation on Cisco 4000 Series ISRs could be bypassed by manipulating the bootloader's configuration variables, allowing unsigned and malicious ROMMON images to load.
An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists in the installer for the VideoEditStudio application, which fails to validate the program executed by the AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges API.
Flawed business logic in 'SecureAppLocker' allows mshta.exe to be executed from a writable directory, circumventing the intended application whitelisting rules and enabling proxy execution.

Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) flaws in the Windows Event Log service itself, when interacting with the third-party 'LogArchiverService', could allow a local attacker to truncate an open .evtx log file.
The 'macOS-Update-Checker' application fails to sanitize update metadata fetched from a public RSS feed, permitting an attacker to embed shell commands within the feed's XML data.
A vulnerability in the macOS Screen Sharing framework grants remote adversaries the ability to bypass the authentication prompt by sending a malformed ClientInit message.
A bug in the 'Confluence Questions' (Q&A) feature allows users to view questions and answers from private 'topics' they are not members of, leaking internal discussions and solutions.

An input validation error in the wayland-capture-service on Linux can be exploited by a malicious Wayland client to bypass portal permission checks and capture the contents of other application windows.
Data leakage occurs in in the macOS 'Security Gatekeeper' service reveals whether a port knocking sequence is partially correct, aiding brute-force attacks.
The Windows TimeZoneSync service exposes a DCOM interface that does not properly enforce caller permissions, allowing any local user to retrieve the system's current time zone information.
An escalation of privilege vulnerability exists in Buildah when processing a specially crafted build context, allowing a low-privilege user to execute code as root.
Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) flaws in the fwupd daemon on Linux allows a local user to truncate a firmware update file during the flashing process, resulting in a bricked device.

The vSAN Health Service on ESXi has a buffer overflow vulnerability in its monitoring component. Exploitation allows an attacker on the management network to execute code as root and encrypt the vSAN datastore, impacting all VMs that rely on it.
Jenkins CI server allows staging of malicious build artifacts in workspace directories due to inadequate cleanup between job executions.
A critical weakness within the PrintSpooler service on Windows could be remotely exploited to create and execute a scheduled task via the `at` command, resulting in remote code execution.
The status bar menu for the MacDefender Suite can be controlled by another process without proper permission checks, allowing it to display a persistent 'Protected' status.
A logic error within the way Microsoft Office handles OAuth 2.0 tokens for Google Workspace integration could be exploited to obtain a token with persistent read access to Gmail.
The NFSDaemonPlus service on ESXi allows for the creation of filenames with arbitrary junk data, which can be abused to create covert C2 channels over NFS.
MailGuard Outlook Add-in does not adequately scan .LNK attachment metadata, creating a pathway for attackers to bypass email security through icon smuggling and deliver malware.
A memory disclosure vulnerability in Cloud Resource Manager enables attackers to extract cached account information, revealing valid usernames and roles across the IaaS platform.

The Windows Security Configuration Wizard (scw.exe) contains a logic flaw where it incorrectly applies audit policy templates, inadvertently disabling critical EventLog channels while supposedly optimizing system performance.

A race condition in the User Profile Manager when applying group policy settings can be exploited to write a malicious path to the SCRNSAVE.exe registry value before system integrity checks are performed.
The security architecture of the Auth0 AD/LDAP connector enables attackers to modify the password synchronization process to maintain persistent access to hybrid identities.
An improper input validation issue in the SystemPreferencesUI.framework on macOS could allow an attacker to execute a method that returns the raw value of the `AppleLanguages` preference key.
The AdminShell framework, a remote administration tool, contains a hardcoded API token that can be used to issue commands to remove network share connections from any host.
The ldap-authd service on Linux improperly handles certificate-based authentication, allowing an attacker with a valid, low-privilege certificate to impersonate a privileged user.
Apple Mail on macOS contains a logic flaw where it prioritizes a crafted display name over the authenticated sender address, effectively hiding the true origin of an email and facilitating spoofing.
The Windows User Profile Service incorrectly processes LNK files in the 'Startup' directory, allowing a low-privileged user to execute arbitrary commands in the context of another user upon login.

The code signing verification module in the Apex Security Suite does not properly analyze binaries that perform dynamic API resolution, enabling unsigned and malicious code to execute with system privileges.
An internal defect in the Linux kernel's ELF loader allows custom-packed executables to bypass security module checks, potentially leading to privilege escalation.
An exploitable bug in the Windows IPsec service allows for the manipulation of packet contents before they are encrypted and transmitted, bypassing integrity checks.
An SQL injection vulnerability in the DocuVault Server for Linux enables remote attackers to dump the entire content database, exposing sensitive corporate documents and user PII.

Improper input validation in the webcache-daemon for Linux enables an authenticated user to inject arbitrary commands into a newly created systemd service file, which is then triggered by a corresponding timer for persistence.

The CocoaSecure framework for macOS includes a debugging mode that writes SSL/TLS private keys to a temporary file that is not excluded by the default .gitignore template, leading to potential leakage.
The 'NexusFlow' CRM SaaS does not implement account-level SMS sending quotas, enabling a compromised account to be used for SMS pumping.
The InfraMetrics daemon, when running on Linux-based IaaS instances, contains a buffer overflow that can be exploited to modify instance configurations and disable security logging.
The `vim` text editor is prone to a VDSO hijacking vulnerability when processing specially crafted files, which could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands with the user's privileges.

The Cisco Jabber client for macOS fails to properly verify the authenticity of the server-provided caller ID information, allowing a man-in-the-middle to alter the displayed number and name for a spearphishing voice attack.

A use-after-free error in the Windows SecureWeb Gateway service could be triggered by a specially crafted network request, enabling an attacker to gain system-level control and compromise the gateway's infrastructure.
The macOS Spotlight indexing service improperly restricts queries, enabling a malicious process to access system metadata that reveals CPU type, amount of RAM, and installed hardware.

Simultaneous execution threads in the `netfilter.sys` driver on Windows allows a low-privileged user to attach a socket filter to the network stack, potentially bypassing host-based firewalls to establish a passive C2 channel.
The Figma plugin system fails to properly scope application permissions, allowing malicious plugins to maintain persistent access to design files.

An out-of-bounds write in the rsyslog daemon on Linux gives a local threat actor the ability to corrupt the VDSO mapping of the process, permitting the execution of arbitrary code with root privileges.

The snap confinement mechanism on Linux can be bypassed by a vulnerability in the snapd daemon that allows a snap to mount its own, malicious version of a trusted system library, subverting the library trust model.
A vulnerability in the Windows Shell allows a malicious .cpl file to be executed automatically upon opening a specific folder, leading to proxy execution via control.exe without user interaction.

A kernel panic can be induced in a Linux system running a vulnerable version of the 'knockd' kernel module by sending a rapid sequence of knocks to the same port, bypassing timing checks and causing a NULL pointer dereference.
The driver loading routine within the LSASS process fails to verify the digital signature of CredentialFilter.sys, allowing an unauthenticated driver to be loaded for persistence.
A remote code execution vulnerability in the cloud provisioning daemon allows command injection through manipulated configuration files processed by the service's shell script parser.

A security gap in the Office 365 authentication framework allows an attacker with a valid but low-privilege account to escalate privileges to the 'Directory Readers' role, enabling enumeration of all users and their emails.

Elasticsearch server vulnerability permits attackers to use search queries to retrieve cluster metadata and indexed document fields without proper authentication, facilitating reconnaissance of target infrastructure.
A design flaw in how Outlook integrates with the Windows Task Scheduler allows a rule to be created that establishes a persistent task, executing malicious code daily without user interaction.
The AquaScreen.scr screensaver for Windows contains an embedded script payload that is executed upon activation, leading to arbitrary command execution.

The Windows Telephony Service (TapiSrv) contains a buffer overflow that can be triggered via a maliciously crafted TAPI request, allowing remote code execution and communication over the TAPI protocol.

The Linux 'nagios-plugin-publisher' daemon fails to sanitize a URL fetched from a public status page. An attacker can modify the page to contain a dead drop resolver, causing the daemon to publish its status and receive commands from a malicious C2 server.

Sensitive information is exposed by in the 'Kubernetes Dashboard' allows an attacker with read-only access to view pod creation and deletion timestamps across the cluster, indicating application deployment cycles.

The backup agent for Confluence Data Center SaaS fails to encrypt backup data before transit to cloud storage, creating an opportunity for an attacker to intercept and analyze backups for sensitive corporate policies and procedures.
The Windows Remote Registry Service has a privilege escalation vulnerability that can be abused to query a remote system's network configuration, discovering hidden services.
Unauthorized access level increase in in the SecureLDAP-Gateway could be abused to modify Access Control Lists (ACLs) to prevent security tools from querying the directory for threat intelligence.

An improperly secured Jenkins CI server, running in a Docker container, exposes its build logs and console output to the public internet without authentication. This allows search engines to index sensitive information such as API keys and credentials used in the build process.

The 'PatchMaster' utility insecurely handles Winlogon registry keys during updates, making it vulnerable to a man-in-the-middle attack that could insert a persistence mechanism into 'Winlogon\Userinit'.
Apple Authentication Services on macOS contains a race condition that permits modification of authentication dialogs and bypasses user consent.
The Red Hat JBoss WebConsole does not implement adequate rate limiting on its public API, permitting adversaries to brute-force enumeration of deployed applications and their versions.

The QuickLook Preview Daemon on macOS insecurely parses a user-provided file to read its `LANG` environment variable, allowing a malicious document to leak the system's primary language configuration.
Unsafe behavior in the OutlookSecureLink Add-in for Windows allows for URL obfuscation using integer-based hostnames, enabling successful spearphishing link attacks.

The Kubernetes API server fails to properly validate the 'securityContext' field in a submitted CronJob manifest, allowing a low-privilege user to schedule a container that runs with privileged access to the host node.
SaaS Application Auth Service fails to properly validate session tokens, enabling attackers to modify authentication states and access tenant data.
The 'QuickCMS' plugin for the 'Joomla' CMS on Linux suffers from an authenticated SQL injection that can be used to inject JavaScript into the database, staging a drive-by attack for all site users.
CoreSpotlight framework vulnerability allows malicious apps to access search results and indexed content from other applications on macOS, potentially exposing sensitive user data to attackers.

A SQL injection vulnerability in the web interface of the CorporateMail Gateway for Windows could allow an unauthenticated attacker to dump the user database, including hashed passwords for email accounts.
The encryption mechanism used by the CitrixConnector component to encrypt its service credentials stored within the LSA is flawed, enabling a local attacker to decrypt the secrets.

Improper validation of domain ownership in the Let's Encrypt ACME client for Kubernetes, 'Cert-Manager', could be exploited to obtain a valid TLS certificate for a cluster-internal service from a public CA.

The `SystemInfo.framework` on macOS contains a private API that can be called without the required entitlement. This allows a sandboxed application to query the I/O Registry for EFI firmware version and SMC (System Management Controller) data, bypassing privacy controls.

The CloudScale API for IaaS resource management contains an information disclosure vulnerability where verbose error messages reveal the existence and internal IDs of resources the user does not have permission to access.
An insecure deserialization vulnerability in the 'IAM-Role-Enumerator' AWS Lambda function can be triggered to dump all IAM roles, policies, and associated users within the account.
A guest-to-host escape vulnerability in the VMware Tools package on ESXi allows a compromised VM to execute a host reboot command via the VIX API.
A container orchestration platform's admission controller fails to validate that new pods are not running as a user named 'node', allowing a malicious pod to masquerade as a cluster node component.

Client-side code injection (XSS) in vulnerability in the Jira SaaS 'Webhooks' configuration panel can be exploited to force an administrator's browser to create a new webhook that exfiltrates all issue comments and attachments to an attacker-controlled domain.

The 'Jenkins AWS Credentials Plugin' is vulnerable to SSRF when configured to test credentials against a user-supplied endpoint. An attacker can specify 169.254.169.254 to steal the credentials of the Jenkins agent running in the cloud.

The Linux application 'desktop-utility-suite' does not properly validate file paths when creating user-specific startup entries, enabling an attacker to place a malicious .desktop file in another user's ~/.config/autostart directory.
A heap-based overflow condition in macOS Backup Configuration Agent enables attackers to execute code with system privileges and corrupt all local backup repositories, preventing system restoration.

The Windows Event Forwarder service can be manipulated via a registry key to forward all events to a local staging file instead of the configured remote collector, aiding in data collection for exfiltration.
A vulnerability in the Kubernetes Ingress Controller's URL rewrite logic can be exploited via a spearphishing link to redirect users from a legitimate service to a phishing site.

The SystemTweak utility for macOS fails to validate the integrity of its internal JavaScript modules before loading, allowing an attacker with local access to modify files and achieve code execution within the application's context.
A buffer overflow in the SecureLink MailSync service for Windows can be exploited to execute untrusted binaries, which can then be used to steal credentials for remote email collection.

A heap-based overflow condition in the 'Proxmox VE' virtualization management daemon (pvedaemon) can be triggered by a specially crafted request to modify a virtual machine's hardware configuration, leading to remote code execution.
A memory leak in the WMI event subsystem allows attackers to cause denial of service by creating excessive event subscriptions.

Improper handling of TFTP options in the OmniEdge wireless access point's TFTP client could lead to a path traversal attack, enabling an attacker to load an arbitrary file from the TFTP server as the boot image.

A security bypass exists in the Gatekeeper verification process, where it fails to inspect the resource fork of an application bundle, allowing malicious code to be hidden there and executed on launch.
'CodeFusion' code hosting service contains a vulnerability where an attacker can link a malicious SSH key to any user account due to a lack of proper ownership checks.

A logic error in the Windows 'Task Scheduler' service allows for bypass of its environmental keying for encrypted tasks. A task is set to decrypt and run only on a specific machine name, but a race condition allows the check to be subverted, executing the task on unauthorized systems.
The Linux version of Kubernetes kubelet contains a vulnerability that allows attackers to inject code into container processes via /proc filesystem manipulation, bypassing container isolation.
The data-sync.service systemd unit file on Linux fails to escape shell metacharacters in an environment variable, allowing an attacker to embed and execute a malicious shell command.

A local privilege escalation in the Linux `logrotate` utility, when used with a custom configuration for the AuditLogix daemon, could be exploited to append arbitrary data to rotated log files, manipulating stored audit trails.
Safari on macOS can be manipulated to use an older TLS implementation that supports export-grade cryptography, enabling FREAK attacks.

Unexpected behavior in the macro scripting engine of the ProdigySuite office application allows a malicious document to execute PowerShell commands to create a new local administrator account on Windows.

A memory corruption issue in the Linux usermod utility's helper binary could allow an attacker to escalate privileges by adding any user to the 'docker' group, facilitating container escape and persistence.
The Linux ArchiveTool daemon contains a command injection vulnerability that enables attackers to execute automated exfiltration scripts with elevated privileges.
A coding defect present in the XcodeHelper tool on macOS allows command injection through a malicious `xcode://` link, which can result in code execution when a developer clicks the link.
The ServerStaging VPS provisioning script fails to sanitize hostnames, leading to a remote code execution vulnerability that can be exploited to compromise newly acquired virtual servers.
A command injection flaw in the OpenWRT opkg proxy handler enables an unauthorized remote actor to install a custom proxy daemon, enrolling the device in a botnet-style multi-hop proxy chain.
The 'Group Policy Preferences' feature on Windows can be abused to embed credentials in a scheduled task that runs a network logon script, creating a persistent and privileged access mechanism.
A coding defect present in the Palo Alto Networks Panorama API allows a read-only administrator to retrieve the SSL decryption private keys for managed firewalls.
Apache Tomcat Session Handler on Linux contains insufficient entropy in session cookie generation, enabling attackers to predict and forge valid cookies.
In 'CodeEditor Pro', a plugin validation issue allows a malicious plugin to contain a script that calls msiexec to install a secondary, more intrusive payload from a hidden MSI file.
The Network Time Foundation client on Windows does not verify the integrity of registered time provider DLLs, allowing an attacker to replace a valid DLL with a malicious one for persistence.
The SecureLoginService on Windows improperly registers a hook procedure, which can be exploited to intercept messages destined for password fields in other applications, leading to credential theft.

An authentication bypass in the ESXi Host Daemon's web interface enables an unauthorized remote actor to execute a command that unsets the `HISTFILE` environment variable for the ESXi shell, preventing command logging for subsequent sessions.
Improper input validation in the EnterpriseCRM Suite allows an attacker to inject a DDE link into a contact record, resulting in arbitrary command execution within the application context.

In the ESXi NSX Manager integration, a buffer overflow vulnerability exists in the code that parses encrypted configuration updates. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to inject malicious commands into the C2 channel.

The Windows `FileSystemIndexer` service is vulnerable to a query that reveals the total number of user files. Malware can leverage this to distinguish a real user's system from a sterile virtual machine by checking if the file count is below a certain threshold.
Systemd service manager on Linux fails to properly validate unit file contents, allowing local users to modify service configurations and manipulate system behavior.

The OpenSSH server implementation on various Linux distributions contains a flaw that allows attackers to bypass rate limiting mechanisms, enabling successful credential stuffing attacks using breached credentials.

Improper locking mechanisms in the macOS 'iCloudSync-MQTT-Framework' can be exploited to publish to iCloud sync topics without proper authorization, allowing an attacker to blend malicious data with legitimate traffic.
Improper access control in macOS power management framework allows malicious applications to force immediate system shutdown without user consent.
An implementation error in the MailSync daemon for macOS allows an adversary on the network path to inject malicious HTML content into emails being fetched from a POP3 server.
Improper handling of data in the Windows LSA isolation process allows an attacker to load a DLL with an invalid code signature, bypassing security checks.

The 'PostgresBackupTool' for Linux does not sanitize temporary file paths, allowing an attacker to specify a hidden location for the backup archive. This can be used to hide a large compressed archive of stolen data in an inconspicuous location like `/tmp/.db_backup`.

SystemCoreMonitor, a management tool for Windows, does not properly sanitize WMI event consumer command lines. An attacker can create a persistent WMI event subscription that executes a malicious payload whenever a specific user logs on to the system.
An access control issue in the 'system-monitor' tool on Linux allows any logged-in user to add a new 'startup script' by directly writing a .desktop file to the shared /etc/xdg/autostart location.

Improper locking mechanisms in the Windows Shell's handling of desktop.ini files can be exploited to force authentication to an attacker-controlled SMB share when a folder's view settings are refreshed.

A coding defect present in the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) allows a tainted Windows executable on a mounted drive to be executed with elevated permissions from within the WSL environment, bypassing security controls.

The 'NetLogon Pro Extension' driver for Windows contains a logic flaw where it incorrectly interprets a specific network packet as a command to enable reversible password encryption for the computer's domain account.

The Time Machine service in macOS fails to sanitize network packet sizes correctly, allowing an attacker to send a large packet that triggers a buffer overflow in the service process and denies backup services.
The 'CloudFlareWorker' script used for ad content transformation on Windows does not properly validate source URLs, allowing it to be manipulated to serve malware from an attacker-controlled domain.

An algorithm implementation error in the automatic backup feature of the AirWave WLAN controller causes it to periodically send unencrypted configuration archives to a deprecated, no-longer-owned server, resulting in data exposure.
The Microsoft Office suite's custom COM handler fails to sanitize inputs, which can be abused through verclsid.exe to launch malicious SCT files from a remote server.
Microsoft's InstallUtil binary contains a flaw that allows adversaries to proxy execution of malicious payloads through trusted .NET installer classes.
Microsoft Teams fails to properly validate external sender information, allowing sophisticated spearphishing attacks.
Improper access control in the 'CyberArk Vault Connector' on Windows allows a local attacker to retrieve code signing credentials directly from the application's memory space.
The backup-daemon service fails to re-initialize its process title after a privilege drop, leaving its argv[0] writable and allowing a low-privilege user to change it to 'rsync'.
The VMLog Shipper module on ESXi is vulnerable to a path traversal issue, allowing a remote attacker to read and ship arbitrary guest files, including sensitive data, to a public text storage site.
The ESXi vSAN Health Service can be configured to use a custom web service for diagnostic data, but a flaw allows this to be set without authentication, leading to potential data leakage.
The 'NodeManager' daemon on Linux-based VPSs fails to properly sanitize API requests, permitting an attacker on an adjacent network to execute arbitrary commands as the 'node' user.

The configuration import feature in GuardianOS does not correctly sanitize input, allowing a malicious configuration file to be uploaded that disables the firewall and opens all management interfaces.
A logical flaw in the Linux KernelModuleSigner tool permits a local user to generate a certificate that is incorrectly flagged as trusted for signing kernel modules, facilitating persistence.

In the Windows enterprise software 'CorpAV', a vulnerability allows an attacker to embed a dead drop resolver within a seemingly legitimate post on a popular social media platform. The antivirus client trusts this source, leading to redirection to a C2 server controlled by the adversary.
Cloud Application Directory Service exposes user account information through its public API without proper authentication, enabling attackers to discover all tenant accounts.
The `pull_request_target` trigger in a fictional 'FlowCI' SaaS platform incorrectly exposes repository secrets to the checkout context, enabling credential exfiltration by a malicious fork.
The Analytics Dashboard IIS Component fails to validate input, leading to code execution via specially crafted queries.

A logic error in the `lsass.exe` process's credential protection module could allow an attacker who already has code execution to create a new process with a token duplicated from another privileged process, bypassing UAC.
An integer overflow in the Windows Shell when processing the properties of a .cpl file allows an attacker to run unauthorized code when the file is opened via the Control Panel.

IDOR vulnerabilities present in (IDOR) in the SalesForce Connect SaaS API allows an attacker to unbind a legitimate user's MFA token by guessing the sequential token ID, facilitating account takeover.
Improper encoding of user output in vulnerability in the 'Gnome Web' browser on Linux permits malicious advertisements to steal session cookies and hijack user accounts.

An information disclosure flaw in the Istio Pilot service mesh control plane allows any workload within the mesh to query the discovery API and obtain OS-level details for the host nodes, including kernel version.

An insecure post-install script in the 'LinterPlus' extension for the LinuxDevSuite on Linux is vulnerable to command injection, allowing an attacker who controls the extension source to execute arbitrary shell commands.
The 'DevTools-Xcode-Plugin' for macOS inadvertently bundles developer email addresses within build artifacts that are uploaded to public distribution servers.

A programmatic error in the `Puppet` agent on Linux, when integrated with Active Directory via SSSD, inadvertently exposes the SSSD cache database to the `puppet` user, allowing for the dumping of cached domain credentials.
Oracle Cloud Domain Management Console has a vulnerability that exposes domain property metadata through debug endpoints, including registrar information and administrative contacts.
The Java Keystore (JKS) implementation on all platforms is vulnerable to a parsing flaw that could allow a malicious application to bypass password protection and extract private keys.

The 'IT-Management Suite' agent service (ITMgmtAgent.exe) on Windows has an improperly configured file permission structure. This flaw allows a low-privilege user to overwrite the executable and gain SYSTEM-level access.

An implementation error in the Linux kernel's TTY driver allows an unprivileged process to read the last login time from the `utmp` file without proper checks. Malware can use this to detect systems where the last login time is identical to the system boot time, a strong indicator of a fresh sandbox.
Information disclosure in macOS Application Firewall framework allows malicious applications to query current firewall rules and exemptions, revealing the system's security posture.
An exploitable bug in the Windows Print Spooler service could be exploited to create a malicious registry entry under 'Winlogon\Notify', causing a malicious DLL to be loaded during logon.
A programmatic error in the macOS kernel packet filter (pf) permits bypassing rate-limiting rules with specially crafted packets, which can be used to launch a successful network DoS attack.

A vulnerability in the `mailnotifierd` service on macOS allows for command injection via the POP3 `UIDL` response. An attacker with control over a mail server could exploit this to execute commands on the client machine and establish a reverse shell over POP3.

AutoCleaner on macOS can be manipulated to execute arbitrary scripts at login by exploiting its session persistence mechanism to write a malicious entry to the 'com.apple.loginwindow.[UUID].plist' file.

The 'CloudStorageSync' agent fails to properly validate the COM server before calling verclsid.exe to handle a new file type. This can be exploited to load a malicious scriptlet from a remote location.
A flaw in the Windows Credential Sync Agent allows an attacker on a compromised machine to intercept and decrypt synchronized credentials if reversible encryption is enabled in the source AD.
A public pipeline execution flaw in Drone CI allows a malicious pull request to trigger a build with access to repository secrets if the trusted setting is enabled for the specific event type.
In the 'FastCGI-Runner' for Linux, improper handling of process creation leaves the child process's argument memory writable by the parent, allowing for arbitrary process name manipulation.
An exploitable bug in the native macOS application Preview could allow a malicious file to cause launchctl to load a malicious Launch Agent.

The Windows Event Log service's configuration file can be modified by a low-privileged user to add specific malicious executable names to a list of excluded processes, preventing their activity from being logged.

Improper ACL inheritance on EventLog log files under %SystemRoot%\System32\winevt\Logs allows authenticated users to modify file permissions, preventing the EventLog service from writing to critical log files.

A memory corruption vulnerability in the AcmeTime.sys driver for Windows allows an attacker to manipulate the return value of a wrapped GetTickCount call, enabling reliable detection of virtual environments through artificial timer rollovers.

The 'cron-helper' utility on Linux allows users to specify a pre-job command that is registered with a trap on SIGUSR2. The utility does not sanitize this input, making it possible to achieve persistence by injecting a command that executes on any scheduled job's signal.

Unintended data exposure in in the SolarWinds Orion Platform allows a low-privileged user to query an internal API endpoint, revealing the names and linked OUs of all Group Policy Objects in the monitored Active Directory domain.

A security gap in the CloudDNS-Manager SaaS platform permits the creation of arbitrary DNS records via a crafted API request, allowing an attacker to set up authoritative name servers for malicious domains.

An elevation of privilege flaw was found in OmniSoft's backup agent, which insecurely registers a DLL under `AppCertDLLs`, allowing a low-privilege user to execute arbitrary code in the context of other processes.
Unsafe behavior in the Windows Biometric Framework allows a crafted fingerprint reader hardware to inject keystrokes and bypass the login screen.
Windows System Restore mechanism has a vulnerability that allows creation of malicious restore points that execute elevated code without UAC prompts.

Unsafe behavior in the Salesforce Identity Service's API for 'forgot password' flows can be manipulated to repeatedly invoke the MFA push notification step without completing the CAPTCHA, allowing for MFA spamming attacks.
EnterpriseOffice Gateway lacks proper validation of authentication responses, enabling attackers to modify hybrid identity verification and gain unauthorized access to Office resources.
The 'SafariSafe' framework on macOS fails to validate the parent window of pop-ups, enabling a 'browser-in-the-browser' attack to trick users into credentials with a fake address bar.
Word Document Macro Finance component allows execution of unauthorized payment commands through crafted documents, facilitating financial fraud.
The SecureMail Client for macOS contains a vulnerability where its 'Start on Login' feature can be hijacked to run unauthorized code from an untrusted location due to a lack of path validation.

An input validation flaw in the Apache HTTP Server's configuration parser on Linux allows an attacker to inject a malicious module directive that masquerades as a standard, commented-out directive, potentially leading to remote code execution.

A security gap in the 'SwiftBuild Server' component of Xcode on macOS allows a compromised build process to inject a malicious path into the 'com.apple.loginwindow.[UUID].plist' file for developer persistence.
Improper validation of handler signatures in ApexRun functions permits attackers to upload and execute malicious code packages, leading to unauthorized serverless execution.

An issue in the OpenSSH server, as patched for a specific Linux distribution, allows for the forced downgrade of the key exchange algorithm to a small, 512-bit RSA key, making the encrypted C2 channel trivial to break.
The Windows Security Center's MOTW verification component fails to check files within mounted VHDX images, allowing malicious executables to bypass SmartScreen protection.

The secure file transfer module within the `SolarWinds Serv-U` FTP server does not correctly display filenames with double extensions in its web interface, which could trick administrators into downloading and executing malware.

The `.msi` installer for `AzureDevOps Build Agent` contains a custom action that runs with elevated privileges and improperly handles environment variables. A local attacker can manipulate these variables to execute arbitrary commands with the permissions of the installer service.

The `ntpd` daemon on Linux does not properly validate the source of configuration files included from `/etc/ntp.conf/`, allowing an attacker to create a malicious file named `driftfile` in a writable directory to achieve code execution.

A memory corruption vulnerability in the Linux kernel's NFSv4 client module can be exploited to bypass file permissions on a mounted network share, granting an attacker unauthorized read access to sensitive data.

A bug located in the `SIP over TLS` implementation of `LinPBX` on Linux allows an attacker on the same network to perform a man-in-the-middle attack and inject audio into a call, facilitating a live spearphishing voice attack.
The Docker daemon on Linux systems incorrectly handles permissions on the control socket, allowing a low-privilege user to gain root access and read credentials from all running containers.

The 'SysInternals AutoLogon' tool stores credentials in a registry key that is readable by all users, allowing an attacker to retrieve them and hijack browser sessions that use Windows Integrated Authentication.

A use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel's `mac80211` subsystem can be triggered by a malformed 802.11 frame from a nearby access point, leading to a system crash or arbitrary code execution.
The Windows LSASS process improperly handles calls from custom authentication packages, allowing a malicious driver to be loaded that intercepts and logs all plaintext credentials on the system.

An information disclosure flaw in the WikiJS application on Linux allows unauthenticated users to read restricted wiki pages that are used to document internal project teams, leadership contacts, and business processes.

Fortinet FortiGate firewall firmware contains an authentication bypass in its configuration management API that enables remote attackers to retrieve complete firewall configuration files including SSL certificates and VPN credentials.
The InstallUtil utility fails to sanitize installer class constructors, enabling attackers to inject and execute malicious code through the trusted Windows binary.
An insecure direct object reference (IDOR) vulnerability in the Vertexion Cloud management panel allows an attacker to guess volume IDs and create snapshots of them without any authorization checks.
An exploitable bug in network load balancers allows attackers to send crafted packets to specific virtual IPs in sequence, triggering the opening of management ports that should remain closed.
Race condition in Symantec Endpoint Protection's boot sequence allows attackers to disable security services by forcing safe mode through registry manipulation.
Insufficient protection in Windows Defender's real-time protection module enables attackers to spoof process arguments after initialization, evading malware detection.
Buffer bounds violations in Juniper JunOS's traffic forwarding daemon allows remote code execution to enable malicious traffic duplication to attacker-controlled servers.

Insufficient validation of form region registration in Microsoft Outlook allows an attacker to register a malicious form region that executes code when any email is opened, providing a broad execution trigger.
An insecure deserialization flaw in the Jenkins Script Console plugin allows unauthenticated attackers to hijack the execution flow on the Jenkins master server.

An insecure method in the WinRM (Windows Remote Management) service allows for the programmatic alteration of its listening port, enabling remote access over a non-standard port to bypass network segmentation.

Privilege elevation flaws in in the 'macOS Developer Relay' service allows a low-privilege application to request and establish a system-level tunnel, bypassing user privacy controls and enabling full remote access.
A privilege escalation vulnerability in the 'CloudSync for AD' tool during GPO synchronization could allow a local user process to modify GPO permissions at the domain root.
An identified issue in the Linux kernel's eBPF verifier can be exploited to read kernel memory, which may contain sensitive identity information such as user credentials or encryption keys.
The Box Windows client stores access tokens in the registry with weak permissions, allowing any authenticated user to read tokens and access user's cloud storage.
A vulnerability in vSphere Network Config Daemon on ESXi 8.0 allows attackers with network access to query virtual switch configurations and port group settings.
Vertical privilege escalation in in the macOS Endpoint Security Framework (ESF) client manager allows a sandboxed app to unregister and disable installed endpoint security tools.

The `git-lfs-helper` tool on Linux fails to sanitize the `GIT_EXEC_PATH` environment variable. An attacker can set this variable to a directory containing a malicious `git` executable, which will then be invoked by the helper tool, leading to code execution.
Elevation of privilege is possible in in 'GameBoost Optimizer' stems from weak file permissions on its service's executable, 'gbo_svc.exe', which can be modified by unprivileged users.

A blind SSRF vulnerability exists in the 'macOS Server Profile Manager' web interface. An attacker could exploit this to exfiltrate data from the instance metadata API, compromising sensitive cloud configuration and credentials.
Memory write vulnerability in Microsoft Office's update service permits post-creation modification of process arguments, hiding malicious document processing activities.
A heap-based buffer overflow in the Linux 'k8s_cni_proxy' kernel module's DNS handler enables an attacker to execute code that forces the module to calculate a C2 IP from a malicious DNS reply.
A programmatic error in the SystemOptimizer X utility allows it to load crafted .cpl files via rundll32.exe, which can then execute malicious code with the privileges of the application.

Improper registry ACLs in the 'CrowdStrike Falcon Sensor' for Windows allow a non-administrative user to register a new Network Provider DLL, facilitating the capture of user credentials during logon.

The macOS LaunchServices framework has a logical flaw where a crafted application URL scheme can trigger the reflective loading of a malicious payload into the memory of the calling process, evading application whitelisting.

An insecure file operation in the `rsyslogd` daemon on Linux could allow a local attacker to manipulate log rotation rules, causing the daemon to copy and relocate a malicious log file into a configuration directory for persistence.
Docker Desktop for Windows does not protect against AppCert DLL registry manipulation, allowing attackers to maintain persistence across container operations.

The DevHelper Safari Web Extension's native messaging host, a Python application, does not verify the origin of incoming messages, allowing any malicious website to send commands for execution in the user's context.
Improper error handling in the Windows `IIS-AdminExt` module allows for remote code execution if the primary management service is down and it falls back to a legacy debugging interface.
The Task Scheduler extension in Windows fails to provide sufficient protection for run-as account passwords when creating new tasks via GPP, exposing them in SYSVOL.

An elevation of privilege flaw exists in the `Windows Diagnostics Hub` Standard Collector Service. It allows a local user to specify a token when initiating a diagnostic session, leading to the creation of a process with the privileges of the provided token.

An input validation issue in the `Microsoft Teams` client allows for the spoofing of file attachments. A file named `meeting_notes.docx.exe` can be sent and will be rendered without the final `.exe` in the chat window.
A Fortinet-like firewall's admin panel is vulnerable to a brute-force attack on its administrator accounts due to a missing exponential backoff mechanism after failed logins.

An insecure direct object reference in the web interface of 'WebPrint Portal' allows an attacker to pass a `script:` URL to the backend `PubPrn.vbs` process, achieving remote code execution on the server.

A local privilege escalation flaw exists in the `cronie` package on Linux systems where a cron job script executes `date` without an absolute path. An attacker can modify their personal `$PATH` to include a directory with a malicious `date` binary, which will be executed when the cron job runs.

Unexpected behavior in the StreamIt media player allows hijacking file associations by manipulating its application preferences plist, leading to arbitrary code execution when common media files are opened.
The `winlogon.exe` process on certain Windows builds fails to lock the session console correctly during a `tscon.exe` switch, enabling a local attacker to hijack an administrator's RDP session.
A programmatic error in the macOS launchd 'com.company.agent' allows a local user to create the agent's lock file before launchd does, resulting in the agent failing to load.
The MinIO object storage server, when deployed on Linux, contains an access control bypass that permits anonymous users to upload objects to a private bucket, creating a covert tool staging area.
Unexpected behavior in the 'SpotlightEnhancer' extension on macOS allows it to index and exfiltrate sensitive file metadata to a remote server controlled by an attacker.
Chef Automate workflow system has an authorization bypass enabling attackers to execute knife commands that delete cloud infrastructure nodes.
A flaw in the Windows Remote Desktop Licensing service could expose its service account's password hash to an authenticated user, enabling the creation of a forged silver ticket.
The API gateway for the SaaS platform Intellectus-as-a-Service is misconfigured, exposing an undocumented endpoint that lists all available private threat intelligence feeds without authentication.
Improper handling of data in Excel's Real-Time Data (RTD) server communication protocol permits a malicious RTD server to execute code on Excel startup.
The Microsoft Dynamics Web Components service on Windows exposes an unprotected endpoint that returns a full list of all active departments and their physical office locations in JSON format.

A code injection vulnerability in the macOS Notes application allows for the execution of arbitrary JavaScript embedded within a note's content. An attacker can sync these malicious notes via iCloud to establish a C2 channel.
A heap-based buffer overflow in the Apple Remote Desktop (ARD) agent on macOS can be triggered by a malicious client, leading to remote code execution with root privileges.
AdminPanel-Pro 软件中的一个缺陷允许攻击者通过特制的 POST 请求绕过身份验证，从而执行 systemctl 命令来禁用安全扫描服务。
macOS's SSH daemon fails to correctly audit login events when a public key is used, allowing for stealthy lateral movement without generating reliable logs.
The macOS ScreenShare framework fails to properly sanitize VNC handshake packets, allowing remote code execution through malicious external connections.

Elevation of privilege is possible in in the AdminSuite Pro service on Windows allows a low-privileged user to call the DSEnumerateDomainTrusts API by sending a crafted request to its management console, leading to domain trust discovery.
A memory corruption vulnerability exists in the macOS SystemAnalytics framework when it processes data for its proprietary, XOR-based encryption method before archiving.
A misconfiguration in the 'VaultBlock Storage' service allows users to create public storage volume snapshots that expose sensitive files, such as 'config.json' containing database passwords.
Identity Federation Service for multi-cloud environments allows token manipulation leading to persistent credential creation.

The `nextcloud-client` on Linux fails to validate the server's SSL certificate when configured for a specific share, allowing a man-in-the-middle to intercept credentials and later exfiltrate data from the legitimate cloud storage.
An information disclosure flaw in the Windows Remote Desktop Licensing Service allows remote, unauthenticated attackers to obtain a list of usernames who have recently connected to the server.
A critical weakness within the `gcc` compiler toolchain on Linux could be exploited for VDSO hijacking during the compilation process, leading to the execution of malicious code.

A Windows Script Host (wscript.exe) vulnerability allows a script running with elevated privileges to delete network shares that were mapped by a different user, effectively clearing another user's tracks.
The macOS TextEdit application improperly handles shell scripts, allowing unauthorized modification of ~/.zshrc that executes in new terminal sessions.
macOS FileMonitor service improperly handles file metadata, allowing attackers to exfiltrate file access logs to text storage platforms through a vulnerable API endpoint.
The Windows Print Spooler service, when configured with email-to-print gateway functionality, can be abused to send unauthenticated emails with a spoofed internal sender address.
A software fault within the 'DevToolbox' IDE allows its debugger to inspect and dump the entire contents of the user's login keychain during a debugging session.

The Windows Hyper-V VM Management Service fails to properly sanitize management commands. A remote authenticated attacker can issue commands using a non-standard encoding to escape the VM management context and execute code on the host.
Improper sanitization of error messages in the Windows 'WinCache Service' could lead to the exposure of full file paths and internal network structure when a cached object is not found.

A critical weakness within the 'SecureDocs' plugin for Confluence Data Center SaaS exposes its configuration API, which contains API keys and credentials for linked internal services, leaking them to any authenticated user.

An internal defect in the Windows 'Defender' antivirus engine allows a specially crafted spearphishing attachment to bypass real-time protection, increasing the success of information-harvesting campaigns.
An out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the OneDrive Email Attachments handler on Windows can be leveraged to leak process memory, which may contain cached email credentials.
The installer for RemoteDesktopClient incorrectly sets permissions on a launchd task, allowing local modification and code execution via launchctl.
The NimbusCloud Instance Provisioner service fails to validate security group assignments during instance creation, enabling an adversary to launch a VM with a permissive firewall policy.

A logic error within the audit_filter.ko kernel module on Linux allows an attacker to disable auditing for the `execve` system call by sending a specially crafted message to the kernel, which disrupts the module's process discovery functionality.

An exploitable bug in the OpenSSH daemon on Linux allows an attacker to trigger resource-intensive operations. By forcing repeated key re-exchanges with specific algorithms, an attacker can cause high CPU utilization and deny new SSH connections.
Windows Defender's Real-Time Protection does not correctly flag executables that have had their signature metadata stripped and replaced with invalid data.

The OpenSSH daemon (sshd) on Linux contains a memory corruption vulnerability in the PAM authentication module that could be exploited to authenticate as any user, including root, without a valid password.

An insufficient authentication mechanism for the TELNET management interface of PathFinder OS routers could allow a remote attacker to gain full control and modify the NAT configuration to traverse network boundaries.
The Microsoft Exchange Server's Client Access service contains a vulnerability where NTLM authentication can be hijacked, enabling pass-the-hash access to user mailboxes.
An identified issue in the Windows DiskValidator component allows for the creation of a malicious VBR, which executes an adversary's payload during the boot sequence.
The DataFog Functions API does not sufficiently validate source code archives, permitting an attacker to embed and execute reverse shells in a serverless environment.

An improper permissions weakness exists in the 'AuthShield SSO Helper' service where its primary executable, 'ssohelper.exe', can be replaced by any standard user, leading to persistent SYSTEM-level code execution.
The macOS native application 'QuickView' contains a logic flaw where malicious ad content rendered within a web view can bypass sandboxing restrictions.

An improper authentication flaw in the 'RedTeam Suite X' update service permits a low-privileged user to download and install the full commercial version without a valid license, facilitating tool acquisition.
A flaw in the `TeamCity-JamPlus-Plugin` allows an attacker to manipulate build parameters, causing JamPlus to execute arbitrary scripts.

An Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) was found in the 'SwiftScale' cloud provider API, enabling an attacker to reassign or terminate VPS instances belonging to other accounts by guessing instance IDs.
The SecureFile Vault application on macOS uses a weakly-derived key to sign its web session cookies, making it possible to forge valid sessions to access protected files.

A security gap in the AWS S3 bucket policy parsing logic can be exploited to grant unintended public write access to a specific prefix, allowing an adversary to stage malicious scripts on a static website.
The Wazuh agent on Linux does not correctly validate messages from the manager, allowing a compromised manager to send a command to disable the host's auditd service remotely.
A terminal-based log viewer, LogView++ on Linux, has a rendering flaw that reverses output upon encountering the RTLO character, potentially obscuring malicious process paths.

The CrowdStrike Falcon agent fails to verify the integrity of its signature validation routines for its components. An attacker can modify the CryptSIPDllVerifyIndirectData registry entry to point to a malicious DLL that always returns TRUE, leading to the execution of unsigned code within the agent's context.

An authentication bypass in the 'RelayNow' CRM's mobile application API allows an attacker to impersonate any user and retrieve their complete customer profile, including address and purchase history.
An insufficiently protected API endpoint in the 'System Center Configuration Manager' (fictional version) allows for the remote execution of MSBuild with attacker-supplied XML content.
The 'Okta AD Agent' on Windows stores its API token in a reversible format in a configuration file, allowing an attacker with system access to extract the token and manage Okta integrations.
In Windows, the Microsoft-CryptoProvider is vulnerable to a resource exhaustion attack where an attacker can initiate a large number of concurrent SSL/TLS handshakes, leading to memory depletion.

A workflow defect in the SolarWinds Orion platform allows for the hijacking of trust decisions by modifying the FinalPolicy trust provider registry entry. This could cause the system to incorrectly trust a signed malicious module, enabling persistence and privilege escalation.
Salesforce CLI v1.10.5 contains a vulnerability allowing attackers to execute arbitrary commands through manipulated Apex API calls during deployment operations.
Memory corruption triggered by the Linux vmstat command allows attackers to manipulate virtual memory statistics displayed to system administrators during runtime.
Improper parsing of .reg files in RegistryEditor Pro on Windows could allow an attacker to run unauthorized code by tricking a user into importing a malicious registry file.
The 'CyberDefender Pro' quarantine management interface is susceptible to cross-site scripting, which could be used to forge requests that clear the Security event log via an administrative backend.
