In Google Workspace, a custom Google Apps Script used for automating user onboarding fails to sanitize user input, allowing an attacker to specify an arbitrary account as a delegate during the provisioning process.
The 'Malwarebytes for Mac' application can be terminated by exploiting a local privilege escalation to send a crafted AppleEvent to its main process, bypassing its self-protection.

The `PowerShell` Remoting Protocol on Windows fails to redact certain environment variables that contain hardware-specific information. An attacker can remotely query these variables to check for artifacts related to virtualization.

The OpenSSH server (sshd) on Linux contains a flaw in its signal handling logic. By sending a `SIGTRAP` signal and analyzing the response, an attacker can detect the presence of a debugger attached to a child process.
The macOS User Creation API contains a vulnerability that allows sandboxed applications to escape restrictions and create new local accounts with elevated permissions.

In the 'AppVenti' application framework, the AppVentiMaint.exe service binary has weak file permissions. A local user can replace this file to cause the service, which runs as SYSTEM, to execute malicious code for persistence and privilege escalation.

Improper validation of plugin packages in DevHub IDE for Windows allows an attacker to inject malicious JavaScript into the renderer process, leading to code execution under the application's privileges.
Improper validation of the `Icon` attribute in `.SCF` files by the Windows Shell allows remote attackers to capture NTLM hashes via forced authentication.

The Apple Remote Desktop client for macOS contains a vulnerability that allows a network man-in-the-middle attacker to manipulate screen sharing data, potentially hiding malicious activity from the user.
The systemd-journald service on Linux contains an insufficient permission check that could permit a local user to write to the VDSO memory region of a privileged process, facilitating VDSO hijacking.
Improper access control in the NetLoginDriver on Windows allows a low-privileged application to perform inline hooking on the LsaLogonUser function, potentially capturing domain credentials.
The Standard-based CIMOM (sfcb) on ESXi fails to correctly parse CIM-XML messages, allowing arbitrary administrative commands to be executed using non-standard XML encoding.
The `postfix-mta` on Linux may leak email server authentication credentials if a local attacker reads the process memory via /proc/[PID]/maps and /proc/[PID]/mem.
A SQL injection vulnerability exists in the search backend of the 'CyberWatch' subscription service, allowing an attacker to dump the entire database of closed-source vulnerability data.
An input validation error in the ESXi `vim-cmd` solo/registervm parameter allows for path traversal, which can be used to register a malicious VM from an unauthorized datastore location.
Memory corruption in Windows Event Viewer (eventvwr.msc) permits unauthorized modification of the BootExecute value in HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager.
Unintended data exposure in in the vSphereHostAgent on ESXi allows a user with limited privileges to query host properties and retrieve the system's current time and timezone settings.
The Cisco IOS Web Interface contains a directory traversal flaw that allows attackers to write malicious PHP scripts to the web directory, creating persistent web shells on network devices.
The Xcode Archive feature on macOS is vulnerable to a path traversal issue that allows an attacker to inject a custom script for archiving build artifacts with an undocumented encryption method.

A misconfigured Docker Registry API allows unauthenticated remote users to retrieve image layer creation and push timestamps, exposing the tempo of an organization's software development and release pipeline.

Unintended data exposure in in the Windows 'Sysinternals' tool 'TCPView' could allow a local attacker to view network connections established by a privileged process that is querying technical databases.
The PulseAudio sound server on Linux, with its screen-casting integration, has a vulnerability that allows a local user to hijack an active screen cast stream and view its contents.

An input validation flaw in the LogStream Centralizer daemon on Linux could permit a low-privileged user to inject crafted entries that manipulate the content of system logs as they are viewed by administrators in real-time.

Improper permissions in the iterm2-custom-integration script on macOS allow a low-privilege user to modify a script that sets a trap to execute commands when the iTerm2 window closes (SIGWINCH signal), establishing persistence.
The `systemd-boot` generator on a Linux system contains a flaw that allows a low-privilege user to drop a malicious file in the ESP, achieving persistence via a bootkit.
In Linux, the 'NetFilterDaemon' does not properly validate rules imported from a file, which can be leveraged to execute arbitrary shell commands as the daemon's user.
A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the MailFilter Pro SaaS dashboard can be used to bypass the Content Security Policy and steal authentication tokens from administrative users.

An authentication bypass vulnerability in the IronWall OS administrative console allows for unauthenticated access to the cryptographic hardware status page. An attacker can leverage this to send a crafted command to the underlying driver, effectively disabling the hardware encryption module.
A flaw in the TimeMachine BackupAgent's handling of distributed notifications allows an unprivileged application to trigger a backup with a malicious, attacker-controlled payload.
The LaunchServices daemon on macOS fails to properly validate .plist files, allowing for the execution of applications where the executable path is obfuscated using an encoded string.

The registration endpoint of the VibeStream API allows an attacker to enumerate existing user accounts associated with email addresses based on error message variations, creating a high-value target list for phishing.
An input validation flaw in the 'auth-bridge.service' daemon enables an attacker to deploy a service with the same name, potentially hijacking the legitimate service for persistence.

An identified issue in the Windows Update Orchestrator Service allows an attacker with local privileges to create a service name with an RTLO character, making it appear as a legitimate Microsoft service in management consoles.

A stack-based buffer overflow affecting the Cisco AnyConnect Socket Filter for macOS allows a local application to execute code with system privileges, which can then be used to modify the underlying pf firewall rules to allow unrestricted traffic.
Zorin OS's desktop environment fails to properly validate Terminal execution in autostart entries, allowing attackers to execute commands with terminal privileges at login.

Concurrency issues within the system initialization script of OmniLink OS can be exploited to replace the 'login' binary. An attacker can place a modified binary that checks for a secret password before proceeding with normal authentication, thus creating a persistent backdoor.
In the FlowCRM SaaS application, a weak authorization check on user profile updates allows an attacker to modify another user's profile details, effectively impersonating them within the CRM.

The `osint-scanner-daemon` on Linux contains a hardcoded administrator password for its web management interface, which could be used by an attacker to reconfigure scan database queries and exfiltrate collected data.

The EDR agent from SentinelOne contains a vulnerability in its user-mode hooking driver that could be leveraged for PE injection, allowing an adversary to hide malicious activity within a trusted process.

A logic flaw in the LogForwarder daemon on Linux-based IaaS instances gives a local threat actor the ability to send a specially crafted signal that causes the process to terminate, halting all local log collection.
A logic error in the TeamWork Hub licensing service can be exploited to create a new user account and assign it an expensive license without proper authorization, leading to persistence.

Improper access control checks in the CloudSphere Console's log viewer component allow any authenticated user to view logs from other tenants' virtual machines, potentially leaking sensitive operational data.
Data leakage occurs in in a Windows kernel component allows malware to detect attached debuggers by querying the `KernelDebuggerInformation` class, which reveals the state of kernel-level debugging.
VMware ESXi's vpxa service contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in its web-based management interface, allowing remote attackers to execute arbitrary SOAP commands.

An issue within the Linux auditd subsystem fails to generate audit events for file writes to block devices that are dynamically created after a USB device is connected, creating a blind spot for USB-based data exfiltration.

The security architecture of the Windows Enterprise Credential Manager (WECM) allows it to display malicious PowerShell commands within its UI as part of a 'repair' suggestion. This could be used in a 'ClickFix' attack to gain user-assisted code execution.

A stack-based buffer overflow affecting the Linux 'systemd-journald' service can be triggered to leak portions of memory from other processes, potentially revealing version strings or configuration data that indicates the presence of vulnerable software.
The `FireWallCore.sys` driver does not inspect network traffic originating from processes launched from an Alternate Data Stream, potentially bypassing firewall rules.
An authorization bypass in the NebulaRunner service allows users with the 'vm-operator' role to execute commands on virtual machines they do not own or have access to.
FileGuard Setup Utility on Windows permits privilege escalation through insecure temporary directory permissions during the installation process.
A time-of-check-to-time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in the Linux 'pam_radius' module can be exploited to intercept the MFA token before it is verified.

An insecure inheritance model in macOS Keychain Access allows a malicious application to read items from a system keychain without triggering an authentication prompt, leading to credential theft and privilege escalation.

A use-after-free vulnerability in the Windows shim cache parsing library, triggered by a malformed .sdb file installed by the 'DataSync Pro' client, can lead to arbitrary code execution and the installation of a persistent, malicious shim.
Unintended data exposure in in the 'Mailcow' dockerized email suite on Linux leaks API keys, which can be used to create and manage email accounts via its REST API.
VMware's host agent service contains a flaw where gzip-compressed and encoded data is not properly decompressed and validated, leading to possible code injection.
The APT package manager's certificate validation mechanism contains a flaw that allows attackers to use compromised repository signing keys to distribute malicious packages.
Heap overflow in Linux VNC server implementation enables remote code execution through malformed framebuffer updates.
The iCloud Keychain synchronization service on macOS contains a logic flaw where a local attacker with limited privileges can intercept and decrypt synchronization traffic, exposing user credentials.
The macOS CloudSync agent fails to validate SSL certificates during automated sync operations, enabling man-in-the-middle attacks for data exfiltration.
Improper authorization checks in the Identity Manager Suite on Windows permit a standard domain user to enumerate all members of the 'Domain Admins' group via the web console.

The Windows Performance Diagnostic Service fails to validate its executable path during a configuration update, permitting an authenticated attacker to modify the registry and execute a malicious payload with SYSTEM privileges.
The ShieldAntivirusGUI, ironically, contains a vulnerability that permits Extra Window Memory injection. An attacker could bypass the antivirus's own protection mechanisms to execute arbitrary code.

Data leakage occurs in exists in the NetGear ProSafe Switch firmware due to a hardcoded SNMP community string. An attacker can use this string to perform a full MIB dump and obtain sensitive device configuration.
vCenter Server user management interface fails to properly validate permission modification requests, allowing an attacker to manipulate administrative account settings and maintain persistence.

Logical errors within the 'Twice NAT' implementation of FortressCore UTM allows for overlapping address pools to be configured. An authenticated attacker can exploit this to bypass intended traffic restrictions and route traffic between disconnected networks.
The Linux kernel's TCP/IP stack is vulnerable to an out-of-bounds read when handling specific TCP options, which can be triggered remotely to crash the system and halt all network traffic.
The 'Safari-Notifications-XMPP' service on macOS can be tricked into processing XMPP messages from an untrusted source, leading to the execution of arbitrary JavaScript in a privileged context.
A coding defect present in the LogShipper agent for Linux allows an attacker to create a new SaaS logging account via a crafted configuration file, redirecting sensitive logs.

The PyPI Python package repository's account creation endpoint fails to check for disposable email addresses, allowing adversaries to easily create numerous throwaway accounts for typosquatting or supply chain attacks.

The Palo Alto Networks firewall logging feature can be configured to send logs over HTTPS but fails to validate the destination server's certificate, allowing for interception and injection of malicious responses.
A bug located in the Linux `usermgmt` daemon allows any authenticated user to request a user list, bypassing the intended group-based access control and revealing all local accounts.
AWS S3 bucket policy misconfiguration enables public staging of malicious objects that can be accessed by compromised systems for tool deployment.
The API endpoint for the 'AzureLink DevTunnel' service on Windows lacks rate limiting, enabling an attacker to brute-force tunnel creation requests and eventually generate a valid remote access URL.
Improper permissions set by the third-party VPN client 'MacSecureVPN' on its keychain items allow any user on the system to read the stored VPN credentials.
'FileIntegrityMonitor' fails to monitor changes to its own .config file, which defines the AppDomainManager, allowing an attacker to silently modify it to load a malicious payload.

A stack-based buffer overflow affecting the HTTP server component of a network printer's firmware allows for remote code execution. The exploit payload can include a command that copies a malicious script from the printer's `/tmp` directory to the `/etc/init.d/` directory, relocating the malware to ensure persistence across reboots.
The `SecureDB Client` library is vulnerable to DLL hollowing, where an attacker could overwrite the entry point of a loaded DLL like `ws2_32.dll` to intercept traffic and execute code.
Flawed business logic in `netlogon.dll` on Windows fails to properly validate the caller's context, enabling an unauthenticated user to dump cached domain credentials intended for offline logon.

A null pointer dereference in the v4l2-capture.ko kernel module on Linux can be exploited to cause a system crash and potentially leak framebuffer data via the /dev/video0 interface, enabling unauthorized screen capture.

Vertical privilege escalation in in Windows Explorer's file enumeration service allows low-privileged users to bypass access controls and discover files in protected directories via crafted symbolic links.
An OpenLDAP server package on Linux creates its main configuration file in /tmp with world-readable permissions during service start, exposing directory credentials.

The `VideoEditX` application, which possesses Screen Recording permissions, does not correctly validate the origin of inter-process communication, enabling an attacker to inject malicious code that inherits its screen capture capabilities.
The RenderFarm Pro rendering SaaS fails to validate job complexity parameters, allowing attackers to submit tasks that consume disproportionate amounts of GPU time.

The 'ContainerManager' for Linux improperly uses `iptables` to set up networking rules. A flaw allows a container to escape and execute commands on the host by injecting malicious rules into the command string.
The security architecture of the Microsoft BitLocker Drive Encryption script allows for proxy execution of arbitrary command-line tools, bypassing WDAC policies.

An exploitable bug in the Microsoft Management Console (MMC) snap-in for Group Policy allows an attacker to define a malicious screensaver policy that bypasses security checks, leading to enterprise-wide persistence.

The container management web interface 'Portainer' does not sanitize user input for container names, allowing an attacker to create a container with a malicious restart command that persists across host reboots.

Improper registry key permissions set by the 'Office365SyncService' installer grant non-administrative users write access to the AppInit_DLLs value. This can be leveraged for privilege escalation by forcing a malicious DLL to be loaded by SYSTEM-level processes.

A flaw in the 'CRI-O' container runtime's handling of environment variables allows a container to overwrite critical runtime variables, leading to command execution on the host during subsequent container operations.
The Windows Script Host's handling of `PubPrn.vbs` can be bypassed to load malicious scriptlets from a remote HTTPS endpoint using the `script:` protocol, facilitating code execution.
Google Workspace Admin SDK v1.0.20221014 contains a vulnerability enabling attackers to execute commands through malicious group settings API calls.
An internal defect in the HashiCorp Packer tool for building cloud images allows injection of malicious code during the image creation process.

Improper handling of data in the 'TimeCapsuleHelper' Launch Agent on macOS allows a malicious actor to modify the WatchPaths key, causing a malicious script to be executed whenever a specific directory is modified.
An information disclosure flaw in the Linux `pam_krb5` module causes it to log Kerberos passwords in plaintext to the system log when authentication fails, exposing credentials to local users.
A memory corruption bug in macOS `Terminal.app` can, under specific conditions, cause the contents of the `.ssh/id_rsa` file to be leaked into the system clipboard.

An implementation error in the Microsoft Installer for `Contoso SecureMail Client` allows for arbitrary code execution. The MSI's custom action fails to properly sanitize a temporary directory path, enabling an attacker to place a malicious DLL that gets executed with SYSTEM privileges during the installation process.

In the Apache 'log4net' library for .NET on Windows, a deserialization gadget chain can be triggered by a malicious library that a user installs, leading to remote code execution when the logger processes a specific payload.

macOS NetworkScanner Suite v4.0 improperly handles domain enumeration requests, allowing attackers to extract detailed domain property information including registrar data and administrative contacts from the scan results cache.
A logic flaw in the `systemd-networkd` service could be abused to create a covert network tunnel through UDP packets encapsulated in DHCP messages, enabling non-application layer C2 communication.

The BrokerComms communication platform fails to implement proper encryption for direct messages, allowing a man-in-the-middle attacker to intercept sensitive information such as access URLs and passwords shared between brokers and clients.

A bug located in the 'NetConnect' VPN client for macOS enables dylib hijacking. The client's GUI application searches for `libnetwork_ui.dylib` using an insecure search path that includes the user's Downloads folder, facilitating privilege escalation.
A web-based management panel for the 'TrueNAS-Web' operating system contains an unauthenticated endpoint that directly executes `lshw -class disk` and returns the output to the requester.
Insecure deserialization of user data in the python-tweet-api library can lead to remote code execution, enabling an attacker to steal Twitter API keys.
The NotificationCenter API on macOS fails to sanitize rich notification content received from network sources, allowing for the injection of malicious UI elements or scripts.
An input validation flaw in the ExchangeOnlineHybridAgent permits an attacker to create a new app password for a mailbox account, bypassing multi-factor authentication requirements.
The 'DiagnosticToolsSuite' installer leverages rundll32.exe to execute a temporary DLL without proper path validation, making it vulnerable to DLL hijacking.
A compromised CI/CD pipeline for the DeployMaster SaaS platform injected malicious code into the build artifacts of its customer's projects.
An insecure Docker socket configuration in the DockrFlow CI/CD tool exposes the host to remote takeover attacks from malicious container images.
The web form component of CallbackMaster Pro does not sanitize user-supplied phone numbers, allowing attackers to inject malicious numbers into the employee callback queue.
An input validation vulnerability in the Docker daemon API allows for hex-encoded environment variables to be passed unsanitized, enabling a covert C2 channel within containers.

The ROMMON firmware update process on Cisco ASR 1000 series routers fails to properly validate cryptographic signatures, permitting an attacker with administrator privileges to load a malicious, unsigned ROMMON image and achieve persistence.
A use-after-free vulnerability in the extension runtime of 'MacDev Pro' on macOS can be triggered by a specially crafted plugin, leading to a memory corruption and potential arbitrary code execution.
The systemd-journald service on Linux can be tricked into processing a polymorphic log entry, which then executes code that changes its form to avoid subsequent forensic analysis.

The `com.developerutils.filemonitor` XPC helper tool lacks proper entitlement checks, permitting any application to register a new monitor for sensitive system directories and receive unauthorized file content notifications.

Privilege elevation flaws in in the Apple File Conductor (AFC) service on macOS allows a sandboxed application to access and write to connected iPhones or other external storage devices, bypassing data isolation rules for exfiltration.

The rsyslog network-input-module for Linux contains a vulnerability in how it processes messages from remote sources. Messages encoded with a modified UTF-8 scheme can cause a heap overflow, potentially leading to remote code execution.
The macOS Private Relay service can be bypassed by a malicious application that directly manipulates the system's DNS resolver configuration, forcing connections through a hostile DNS server.

The firmware update process for 'RouterOS' network devices is vulnerable to a buffer overflow, allowing a remote attacker to inject and execute a payload that writes garbage data to the device's storage, wiping the OS.

The Apple Remote Desktop (ARD) agent on macOS can be tricked into performing a domain user search via an insecure AppleEvent, allowing a local user to bypass GUI authentication and enumerate accounts.
The DockerHostd management API on Linux does not properly authenticate requests, allowing an unauthorized user to create containers with host root access.
The OmniSecure Drive Encryption software for Windows contains an insufficient signature validation check for its own UEFI driver, permitting the loading of a malicious bootkit.

A local privilege escalation vulnerability in the 'XProtect' malware removal tool on macOS stems from improper permissions on its bundled Python interpreter, allowing a standard user to add a `usercustomize.py` file to achieve code execution as root.
VMware ESXi's vpxa service fails to validate vCenter communication, enabling attackers to exfiltrate VM inventory and host configuration data over unencrypted AMQP protocol messages.
The `logrotate-helper` script on Linux can be manipulated into executing a malicious log file if the file's name has a trailing space and a fake .log extension.

The 'WebAppProxy' for Linux contains a flaw in its systemd service ExecStart line, which does not use an absolute path. An attacker can manipulate the system's PATH variable to execute a malicious binary when `systemctl start` is run.
A default misconfiguration in the macOS built-in Apache 'mod_php' module enables scripts uploaded to user Sites directories to be executed with system privileges, facilitating web shell attacks.

An integer overflow in the EventLog service's log size calculation allows an attacker to set the maximum log size to zero, causing the service to stop recording events once the buffer is filled with initial system startup data.

A path traversal vulnerability in the vSphere Web Client's host management component allows an authenticated attacker with non-administrative privileges to modify the welcome banner HTML file, enabling the defacement of the ESXi host's web interface.
The ASUS BIOS Flashback feature on Windows motherboards can be triggered without proper signature checks, enabling a malicious actor to persist by writing to the BIOS chip.

A remote code execution vulnerability affects 'Orchestrator Scheduler' for Windows. An attacker with access to the scheduling interface can create a job that runs a malicious MSBuild project file, abusing the trusted MSBuild.exe binary.
A design flaw in the network-util-pro application allows its argv[0] to be changed post-execution, enabling it to be disguised as a legitimate 'NetworkManager' process.

The registry key for the 'SecureNetVPN' service, HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\SecureNetVPN\Parameters, has weak permissions. This enables an attacker to create or modify values such as 'PluginDll' to load a malicious library, achieving persistence each time the VPN service starts.
A programmatic error in SolarWinds Network Configuration Manager enables an unauthenticated attacker to remotely deploy and activate a rogue DNS server instance on monitored Windows servers.

The `sudo-wrapper` script on Linux insecurely calls a setuid helper without sanitizing the environment. An attacker can set the `LD_PRELOAD` variable to force the loading of a malicious library, resulting in root privilege escalation.
F5 BIG-IQ's device discovery and deployment service contains a vulnerability allowing attackers to execute arbitrary commands on all managed BIG-IP devices through crafted deployment packages.
The Docker container runtime on Linux can be downgraded to a version that doesn't implement seccomp filters, allowing privileged system calls.

An improper input validation flaw in the `olkapilib.dll` library of Microsoft Office allows an attacker to specify a UNC path for a folder's home page. When Outlook loads, it will execute a malicious script hosted on a remote SMB share.
A heap overflow in the `ntoskrnl.exe` boot process handler, when processing a specially crafted BCD file, can be leveraged to set the `safeboot` option, impairing security solutions on startup.

The 'SecureWipe' kernel driver for Linux lacks proper validation on IOCTL requests, enabling a low-privileged user to specify arbitrary disk offsets and write random data, resulting in unrecoverable data destruction on the block device.
Improper bounds checking in the SystemD-Policy unit on Linux can be exploited to bypass executable space protection (XATTR) and run untrusted code from a non-executable file.

A critical weakness within Windows File Association Manager allows unauthorized modification of HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\*\shell\open\command registry entries, enabling system-wide persistence through arbitrary file type handlers.
AWS Compute Optimizer API contains an authorization bypass allowing unauthorized modification of resource size recommendations and quota settings.

The macOS 'AirDrop' service, which uses a proprietary pub/sub mechanism for discovery, is vulnerable to a packet injection flaw that could allow an attacker to force a target device to accept a malicious file or command payload.

The security architecture of the GCP Cloud Logging bucket management interface permits the modification of retention policies, which can be abused to set a one-day retention and purge all security logs for evidence tampering.
The Windows Web Account Manager (WAM) improperly handles redirects during OAuth-based device registration, allowing an attacker to capture authorization codes and register a malicious device.

The 'GameOverlay App' registers a COM object for in-game functionality but does not prevent modification of its InprocHandler32 registry value, allowing an attacker to execute code of their choice when a game is launched.
Improper access control in the NimbusStack API gateway enables attackers to call internal token-issuing services directly to create forged service-to-service credentials.
Windows Server's Trust Relationship Discovery API exposes detailed information about external domain trusts without proper access controls, allowing adversaries to map network trust dependencies.
An exploitable bug in Windows DNS server service permits attackers to update DNS records using forged Kerberos tickets, enabling domain hijacking.
Memory corruption in the CommCenter client on Windows can be triggered by a malicious payload, leading to the execution of arbitrary code within the context of the Electron main process.
The macOS SecureTransport-Framework improperly handles a high volume of SSL/TLS renegotiation requests, making applications vulnerable to a CPU exhaustion denial of service.

ProductivitySuite for macOS fails to sandbox its plist entries correctly, allowing a malicious component to add itself to the 'com.apple.loginwindow.[UUID].plist' file for persistence upon user logon.
An authentication bypass vulnerability in the NetAdmind daemon on Linux systems allows remote attackers to gain root privileges and compromise the host server.
Improper input validation in Tripwire's policy engine enables attackers to modify monitoring rules and exclude their tools from integrity checks.

A buffer overflow in the apv (Advanced Process Viewer) daemon on Linux can be triggered by a specially crafted ps-style output request, allowing a local user to escalate privileges and potentially interfere with process discovery mechanisms.
An exploitable bug in the 'Windows Defender' quarantine driver permits a local user to bypass its intended purpose and use it to read raw sectors from the disk, including deleted files.
The tmux-session-resume script on Linux fails to sanitize its resume commands, allowing an attacker to plant a trap that triggers when the tmux session is detached or terminated with SIGHUP.
Improper handling of data in 'CorpPresent', a Windows-based presentation tool, allows malicious template injection in PPTX files, resulting in the execution of unauthorized payloads.
Nginx web server with misconfigured CGI scripts on CentOS allows attackers to alter shell profiles through remote code execution.
An out-of-bounds read vulnerability in `AppleIDAuthAgent` on macOS can be triggered to leak portions of `securityd`'s memory, potentially revealing fragments of the user's Apple ID password.
A bug located in the Linux kernel's ELF binary loader allows a race condition where a file can be padded with junk data between validation and execution, potentially loading unsigned malicious code.
The `OpenSMTPD` daemon on Linux fails to enforce strict DMARC policies when `p=none` is set, allowing spoofed emails that should be quarantined or rejected to be delivered to user inboxes.
Insufficient permission checks in the HPE iLO REST API on Linux-based management appliances allow a low-privileged user to upload and apply a malicious firmware package, corrupting the BMC firmware.

The Windows service 'NetIntel Gatherer' improperly handles permissions on its local cache of passive DNS data. A low-privilege user can read this cache file, gaining access to sensitive reconnaissance data collected by other users or privileged processes.

An access control flaw exists in the `CyberArk Vault Agent` service, which permits unprivileged processes to call `OpenThread` with excessive permissions. This vulnerability enables attackers to suspend and hijack a thread, running code within the agent's trusted security context.

The Hyper-V VM Integration Service on Windows contains a race condition in its guest-to-host file transfer mechanism. An attacker in a guest VM can use this to modify a malicious tool as it is being copied to the host, stripping out indicators that would be detected by the host's antivirus software.

Unchecked memory write operations in the PowerAI PowerShell module for Windows could be exploited to bypass security policies and grant an adversary the ability to use integrated AI services for reconnaissance and payload generation.
The 'PageBuilder' application for macOS fails to validate user-supplied CSS, allowing an attacker to use CSS injection to alter the appearance of a cloned login page used as a link target.

A critical weakness within the Nginx proxy server on Linux, when used with a specific third-party caching module, permits HTML smuggling. The module misinterprets Data URLs, allowing malicious content to be cached and served to clients.

In the Linux OpenSSH daemon, a flaw in protocol negotiation permits attackers to force connections to use SSH protocol 1.5, which lacks modern security controls and is vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks.

The Windows 'AzureFileConnector' driver fails to properly validate server redirection responses from a public API. An attacker can poison the API response to act as a dead drop resolver, forcing the connector to communicate with a malicious C2 server instead of the intended Azure endpoint.

A directory traversal vulnerability in the PixelPerfect Editor's plugin installer allows an attacker to write a malicious shim database into the %WINDIR%\AppPatch\AppPatch64\Custom directory, affecting 64-bit applications.

The security architecture of the pfctl packet filter utility on macOS could be exploited by a low-privileged user to create rules that forward internal network traffic to an external destination, establishing a covert internal proxy.
Insecure API permissions in the AcmeCorp Remote Desktop Gateway permit an authenticated user to call internal session-switching functions, leading to unauthorized RDP session takeover.

The macOS 'iCloud Sync' service can be tricked by a malicious application into syncing a sensitive file to a temporary, attacker-controlled device over Bluetooth instead of the user's registered devices.
An insecure method in the 'EnterpriseGuard' agent's management API on Windows allows an authenticated user to remotely disable the agent's event collection and reporting modules.
openSUSE's KDE configuration tool contains insufficient permission checks when creating autostart entries, enabling unprivileged users to add persistent malicious entries to system directories.
A resource exhaustion flaw in the Windows TCP/IP driver (tcpip.sys) allows an attacker to cause a system crash by sending a specially crafted flood of ICMPv6 Router Advertisement packets.
Improper validation of Control Panel (.cpl) file paths in 'SystemTools Suite' permits a malicious .cpl file to be executed through rundll32.exe, resulting in code execution.
A stack-based buffer overflow in the `parted-ng` partition editor for Linux allows a local user with a malformed partition table file to trigger an overwrite of the disk's primary GPT header.

The FaceTime framework on macOS does not properly validate the origin of incoming call requests, allowing a network-adjacent attacker to initiate a call with a spoofed caller ID that appears to be from a trusted contact.

A race condition in the macOS kernel's I/O Kit driver handling for USB audio devices can be exploited to create a covert channel, exfiltrating data by modulating it into the audio stream played through the device's control interface.
An out-of-bounds write flaw in the ESXi SFCBD (storage framework client) service allows for remote code execution from a guest virtual machine.
The ClusterMap API exposes an undocumented endpoint that returns a full inventory of cluster resources, including nodes, pods, and services, without any authentication check.
The `OpenVPN-Auth` PAM module for Linux on a custom VPN appliance does not validate its configuration file, enabling an attacker to introduce a backdoor.

A broken access control vulnerability in the Azure Subscription Transfer service enables a user with 'Contributor' rights to initiate a subscription ownership transfer to a foreign tenant, bypassing 'Owner' level requirements.
The ESXi API improperly validates session state for the 'currentTime' property, allowing an unauthenticated actor to query the host's current time via a direct API call.
The FastIO driver for Windows fails to validate the size of a buffer used in a low-level disk operation, leading to an MBR corruption and potential bootkit installation.

In the `systemd-journal-archiver`, a flaw in the unit file configuration allows an unprivileged user to influence the arguments passed to the `tar` command, potentially enabling the archiving of arbitrary system files.
An isolation breakout vulnerability in the ContainerX runtime on Linux allows a process within a container to enumerate host device drivers via /dev and /sys/bus.

The security architecture of the CloudFlow Orchestrator for IaaS exposes an API endpoint for creating data pipeline jobs without authentication. An attacker can leverage this to automatically collect data from any specified storage bucket.

A logic error in the IP Helper Service allows a non-administrative user to trigger a configuration update with embedded credentials. This results in the service creating a new logon token and impersonating it, potentially bypassing firewall rules.
The 'SecureRouter 5000' series network devices ship with a default 'maintainer' account enabled for remote support, which uses a static password that is documented in the official user manual.

Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) flaws in the VideoCraft Pro installer, when creating a shim database, can be exploited to swap the legitimate .sdb file with a malicious one, resulting in persistent code execution for all users of the software.
DataShield Deployment tool on Windows is vulnerable to executable replacement attacks due to insufficient permission restrictions on installer temporary files.
A privilege escalation flaw in ReportingServices IIS Component allows low-privileged users to gain system access.

A logical flaw in the message retention policies of NexusComms (SaaS) causes deleted messages in private channels to remain accessible via the API for an extended period, permitting unauthorized data recovery.
The `BITS` (Background Intelligent Transfer Service) can be manipulated to load a malicious DLL from a controlled network share, resulting in a DLL injection attack against a system service.
Unexpected behavior in the 'CloudDrive' SaaS service's sharing feature allows an attacker to send a sharing invitation that, when clicked, redirects to a credential phishing page.
A hardcoded backdoor credential was discovered in the ROMMON interface of Stellarwave firewall devices, enabling an attacker to upload an unauthorized bootloader.
The SNMPv1 agent on FlowPoint switches fails to properly enforce access controls, enabling a remote attacker to perform a MIB dump and retrieve sensitive VLAN configurations.
A memory corruption issue in the kubelet component can be triggered to leak information about the pods it is managing, including secrets and environment variables.

A type confusion vulnerability in the ClickOnce manifest handler for the SecureUpdate Service allows for the corruption of process memory, enabling an attacker to execute code with the privileges of the invoking user.
Unintended data exposure in in the Remote Desktop Services (TermService) allows an attacker to cause plaintext credentials to be retained in LSASS memory longer than intended.

Unsafe behavior in the DataAnalyzerX application permits an attacker to execute malicious commands with root privileges after the user authenticates via a prompt from AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges.
The `GCP OS Login Helper` daemon on Linux does not correctly sanitize user-supplied input, potentially allowing an attacker to execute commands with root privileges upon establishing a connection.

A race condition in the Ubuntu Uncomplicated Firewall (ufw) initialization script can be exploited by a local user to prevent the rule set from being applied at boot, resulting in a disabled firewall.
Insufficient input validation in the Kubernetes kubelet's image build API allows an attacker to inject build arguments, leading to arbitrary command execution on the node.
A weakness in the 'DataSync Engine' for Windows allows a malicious extension to bypass network controls and establish a covert communication channel for C2.
The Credential Vault service on Windows does not properly lock the LSA registry keys during its SSP update process, creating a window of opportunity for an attacker to inject a malicious provider.

The SNMP daemon on Brocade Fabric OS devices contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated attacker to read the configuration of SPAN ports, revealing where network traffic is being mirrored for sniffing.
An exploitable bug in the Istio Pilot component could be abused to inject a malicious Envoy sidecar container into existing pods, effectively deploying a new container for data exfiltration.
Gatekeeper on macOS does not correctly de-obfuscate scripts before execution, allowing maliciously obfuscated bash or zsh scripts to bypass security checks.

In the VirtFlow API Gateway for IaaS, a flaw in the role-assignment logic allows a user with 'developer' permissions to escalate their role to 'admin' by crafting a specific API request to the identity endpoint.

The rsyslog daemon on certain Linux distributions contains a format string vulnerability that permits a local user to write arbitrary data to log files. This can be exploited to overwrite log entries related to a detected tool, removing evidence of its execution and indicators that security tools might use for correlation.

The `StratusGuard Policy Engine` contains a parsing error in its configuration files, causing it to ignore deny-lists for unsupported cloud regions, thus permitting automated deployments in geographies that should be blocked.

Sensitive information is exposed by in 'AppVDiagnosticTool' reveals the internal structure of commands used to invoke SyncAppvPublishingServer.vbs. This information can be used by an attacker to craft a payload for proxy PowerShell execution.
IDOR vulnerabilities present in (IDOR) vulnerability in the `kubelet API` could be exploited to obtain another pod's session token, effectively hijacking its session.

A logic error in PasswordSafe Pro's entry list allows for the manipulation of its sort callback function. This enables a ListPlanting attack where an attacker can execute code in the context of the password manager.
Type confusion in Security Accounts Manager (SAM) database permits creation of invisible user entries that don't appear in standard user enumeration.
A logic flaw in the ESXi Network I/O Control service could be leveraged to inject malicious network packets into the guest command channel, leading to command injection on the guest OS.

A memory corruption vulnerability in the Exchange Unified Messaging service on Windows, when processing a specially crafted voicemail request, could lead to information disclosure, including contacts from the GAL.
A software fault within the CoreServices Agent framework allows a sandboxed application to bypass restrictions and set a login item for a different user, leading to potential cross-user persistence.

The 'O365 Data Bridge' SaaS application has an insufficient access control check on its 'sync to external storage' feature, which can be abused to sync entire SharePoint document libraries to a public Dropbox folder.
Windows Update Service can be exploited to modify update packages, enabling attackers to distribute manipulated system updates across a network.
The Windows 'LegacyApp Runner' utility, designed to execute old VBScript-based installers, fails to prevent scripts from calling sensitive native Windows APIs, facilitating privilege escalation.

The Sysinternals AutoLogon utility, when configured via a Group Policy Preference, contains a flaw where a Python script path is not properly validated, enabling an attacker to perform remote code execution on domain-joined workstations.
A memory corruption issue in the macOS `TextInput` framework (TIS) could be leveraged to read the currently selected keyboard layout input source.
The Docker daemon on Linux contains a flaw that allows container escape to enumerate host system certificates, potentially revealing organizational PKI information.
An insecure deserialization bug in a .NET Core API service hosted on Windows Server allows an unauthenticated attacker to run unauthorized code and take over the server.

Insecure permission handling in the SecureLink Remote Access Service allows any authenticated user to invoke the `tscon.exe` functionality, hijacking a remote desktop session belonging to another domain user.
A buffer overflow in the Azure vTap agent for Linux VMs could allow a malicious actor with local access to escalate privileges and reconfigure the vTap to exfiltrate all mirrored network traffic.
An identified issue in Windows File Explorer's context menu handlers allows PPID manipulation when launching applications.
The System Integrity Protection (SIP) component on macOS does not prevent the modification of binaries with invalid signatures in certain user-writable locations.

On macOS, the `DiskManagement` framework improperly validates the names of scheduled tasks, enabling an attacker to create a task named `com.apple.diskmanagement.rescue` that appears official but runs unauthorized disk utilities.
The search functionality in CodeLoom Cloud exposes file content previews from private repositories in search results to users who do not have explicit read access to those repositories.

The 'NetMon Pro' service installer fails to set appropriate permissions on its COM server's InprocServer32 registry value, allowing an unprivileged user to replace the referenced DLL with a malicious one for persistence.

Privilege elevation flaws in exists in the Windows FileArchiverPro driver, which allows a low-privileged process to force the system to archive arbitrary kernel memory, potentially leaking sensitive information.

A bug located in the 'KerberosPolicyManager' component of Active Directory on Windows allows an attacker to disable preauthentication for any domain account without sufficient privileges, enabling AS-REP roasting attacks.
A compromised Ruby Gem `activerecord-oracle_enhanced-adapter` for Linux was found to include a backdoor that exfiltrates database credentials to a remote server.

The 'HelpDesk Support Tool' creates a vulnerable service with an unquoted path: `C:\HelpDesk Support Tool\support.exe`. This enables a local attacker to gain SYSTEM privileges by creating `C:\HelpDesk.exe`.

A memory corruption bug in the 'OfficeConnect Chat' rendering engine can be triggered by a specially crafted message, allowing an attacker to read process memory and potentially extract credentials or session tokens from other chat sessions.
A bug located in the macOS Quarantine attribute handler allows a spearphishing attachment to appear as a trusted file type, bypassing security warnings.
Container Backup Service on Linux improperly handles archive metadata, allowing container escape through specially crafted compressed backup files.
The `CloudKit` web framework on macOS does not adequately validate schema update requests, which could be exploited to alter public data served by applications, resulting in defacement.
The DeployHub SaaS platform's custom script integration fails to sanitize user input, allowing for command injection and unauthorized serverless execution during deployment tasks.
The Windows 'Indexing Service' fails to sanitize VBA macros when extracting metadata from Office templates, allowing for the potential execution of code if the cached data is mishandled.
A D-Bus service on a popular Linux distribution improperly handles method calls containing JavaScript code, allowing a local user to execute arbitrary scripts.

A coding defect present in the macOS TCC (Transparency, Consent, and Control) framework allows a malicious program to create a fake configuration file at '/Library/Application Support/com.apple.TCC/TCC.db' to bypass privacy prompts.
An improper entitlement check in the FaceTime application for macOS could allow a malicious app to activate the camera and capture a single frame before the user can answer or deny an incoming call.

Simultaneous execution threads in the Windows 'FileReplicator' service could allow a low-privilege user to read a partner replication configuration file before permissions are applied, revealing target endpoints.
A command injection vulnerability in the 'WebAdminPanel' for Linux allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary Unix shell commands via a crafted hostname in the network diagnostic tool.
A programmatic error in the macOS 'System Integrity Protection' (SIP) mechanism allows a malicious process with root privileges to disable its enforcement for specific system directories.
The Windows Cryptographic Services module fails to properly validate COM objects loaded through Regsvr32.exe, enabling malicious code execution with system privileges.

A misconfiguration in AWS Step Functions permits a state machine to invoke a Lambda function in a different AWS account without proper resource-based policy validation, enabling cross-account compromise.

Internet Information Services (IIS) on Windows contains a flaw in `aspnet_isapi.dll`. Repeated requests to a specific `.aspx` endpoint that performs large data set serialization can lead to a memory exhaustion denial of service.

An exploitable bug in the 'AzureVendor Connector' PowerShell module for Windows exposes its management certificate in clear text within a script file, potentially compromising the connection to a key cloud-based vendor.
The TFTP client implementation on TerraNet devices can be invoked from the CLI with parameters that allow for overwriting critical system files, leading to arbitrary command execution.
The `rsync-guard` daemon on Linux can be tricked into syncing and executing malicious commands from a removable drive due to insufficient validation of file names.

Data leakage occurs in in the Confluence SaaS user profile API exposes the group memberships and project affiliations of all users, allowing an attacker to map out organizational structure and identify high-value targets.
Privilege escalation flaw in OpenSSH daemon allows attackers to discover user group memberships on Linux systems.
Windows Configuration Agent's deployment scheduler can be hijacked by local attackers to schedule and execute malicious packages across the enterprise network.
Flawed business logic in Microsoft Word allows unregistered COM add-ins to be loaded, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution upon application startup.
The Docker Engine API, when misconfigured with a TCP socket, lacks sufficient authentication, allowing an attacker to execute commands and retrieve the full hardware inventory of the host machine.
The 'SecureMail for Office 365' add-in's integration with a company's internal chat system transmits authentication tokens in the clear, making them susceptible to interception via network sniffing.
Safari on macOS allows SVG smuggling through its WebKit engine, enabling malicious scripts to bypass same-origin policy restrictions.
An improper privilege escalation vulnerability in the AetherVM Management API allows an authenticated user with basic permissions to create a new IAM user with administrative privileges.
A third-party System Preferences pane on macOS contains a flaw that lets a standard user change permissions of system configuration files that typically require admin rights.

Excel's CalcEngine contains an out-of-bounds write that can be triggered to set a worksheet's visibility property to `xlSheetVeryHidden` via a malicious formula, a state that cannot be reversed through the standard user interface.

The `runc` container runtime for Linux allows the creation of a container with a name identical to a system management container, enabling an attacker to hide malicious activity within a seemingly legitimate container named `k8s-POD`.
The 'OpenSSH-ServerX' daemon on Linux systems contains a logic flaw where a specially crafted authentication attempt can cause the service to execute `shutdown -r now`, rebooting the server.
The docker-network-bridge daemon for Linux contains an integer overflow that permits a container to escape its network namespace and act as a proxy for the host.
A memory corruption issue in the Windows nvdisp.sys graphics driver allows an adversary on the system to read kernel memory, potentially exposing sensitive process data.
An out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in the 'libwhoisparser' library on Linux, which can be triggered by a specially formatted WHOIS record, leading to information disclosure in memory.

The nginx-stego-module, a third-party module for Linux, contains a logic flaw that allows an attacker to retrieve data hidden in images served by the web server. This flaw facilitates unauthorized data exfiltration through steganographic channels.
A failure to neutralize CRLF sequences in the logging mechanism of a WMI event consumer allows for log injection and potentially arbitrary code execution when the logs are parsed.
A software fault within the systemd init system on Linux allows attackers to pack malicious systemd service units, bypassing security checks and achieving persistence.

The Azure DevOps Server agent service stores its service account credentials insecurely, which could allow an attacker to steal the hash and forge a silver ticket for the build and deployment services.

Microsoft 365's delegated administration framework lacks proper validation of partner trust relationships, enabling attackers with compromised partner credentials to gain administrative control over client tenants.
Improper access control in the Windows Print Spooler service facilitates remote exploitation to drop a malicious DLL in C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\x64\3\ named 'mimspool.dll'.
The macOSLoginWindow process is susceptible to IAT hooking, where a malicious process could modify the import table to intercept calls to AuthorizationServices and capture the user's login password.
The QuickTime Player application on macOS does not adequately check for malicious data hidden in audio track metadata using steganographic techniques, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution.

The GlobalGrid 'CloudSentry' SIEM connector fails to ingest event logs from regions that are not explicitly listed in its configuration file, allowing adversaries to operate in these regions with impunity.
A flawed display driver (`display_driver.sys`) on Windows incorrectly maps memory, exposing a portion of the `winlogon.exe` process memory and allowing the reading of cached domain credentials.
The Windows Sandbox feature fails to properly isolate processes, allowing a sandboxed application to access the host's file system through an object handle leak.

An internal defect in the Contoso Enterprise Resource Planner allows a low-privileged user to impersonate a domain administrator account by exploiting token handling logic in its Windows agent service.

The security architecture of the Harbor container registry's API allows an attacker to replace a signed image layer with a malicious one without invalidating the signature, leading to user execution of the bad image.
macOS's 'System Information' application (system_profiler) does not correctly enforce privacy settings, allowing sandboxed applications to gather a list of all attached cameras and microphones.
A security gap in AzureAuth Gateway for Windows allows attackers to forge session cookies due to weak cryptographic implementation in the cookie generation algorithm.
Apache HTTP Server on Linux fails to clear LD_PRELOAD when loading modules via mod_so, allowing local attackers to inject malicious libraries that can intercept web request handling.

A vulnerability in the 'SymantecDataLossPrevention' agent enables an attacker with local access to bypass intended security policies by adding a malicious DLL path to the AppInit_DLLs registry key, leading to unauthorized code execution within user processes.

Improper access control in the OmniGuard Endpoint Agent for Windows allows a standard user to add a helper DLL to the Netsh registry key. This enables persistence and code execution triggered by any netsh.exe process.
Buffer bounds violations in macOS DeviceAuthAgent allows attackers to bypass hardware approval prompts and install malicious Thunderbolt devices with elevated privileges.
SafariSafe, a browser extension for macOS, is vulnerable to cross-site scripting because it fails to inspect JavaScript payloads that are delivered in a stripped, minified format.
Unintended data exposure in in MacProcessObserver framework allows applications to access process information of other users without proper authorization on macOS systems.
The FortiGate firewall's WAF Lua script processor contains a format string vulnerability that can be exploited by a remote attacker to execute arbitrary Lua code on the device.
The VideoEncoder Studio application on macOS does not enforce Gatekeeper policies on its custom plugin format, allowing an attacker to load and execute unsigned, malicious code.
A weakness in the VM-Provisioning tool for a major IaaS provider leaves the initial temporary password for a new virtual machine in a plaintext file on the system disk.

IDOR vulnerabilities present in (IDOR) in the Salesforce platform allows an attacker to modify the OAuth scopes of a previously approved application, granting it persistent API access to sensitive CRM data.

The vSAN Health Service on ESXi includes a Python module for custom health checks that is vulnerable to path traversal. An attacker can exploit this to load and execute a malicious Python library, achieving code execution.
The FortiGate firewall's firmware upgrade process does not correctly sanitize user-supplied input, leading to a heap overflow that can be leveraged to write malicious code to the boot ROM.
A memory corruption flaw in the CitrixAnalytics Connector allows for arbitrary data injection via WebSocket connections, enabling an attacker to camouflage C2 traffic as normal telemetry data.
The 'OfficeDeploy Manager' enterprise tool insecurely creates the `Office Test` registry key during deployment, leaving it behind for potential abuse by an adversary.

An internal defect in the 'SecureLogin' Windows GINA extension allows local users to read a memory dump file that contains the email address of the last user to log on, facilitating credential harvesting.

The Inforia CRM server component on Windows fails to properly validate the Privilege Attribute Certificate (PAC) within a presented Kerberos TGS ticket, allowing an attacker to forge a valid silver ticket for the service.

A memory corruption issue in the DeviceSyncService component allows an adversary to manipulate the Extra Window Memory of a process. This can lead to a remote code execution scenario by redirecting execution flow to an injected payload.

The Windows Speech Recognition Runtime performs non-atomic operations on Active Setup registry keys, which can be exploited to inject a malicious payload for persistent execution when a user logs into the system.

In the OrionGate Management console for IaaS, a vulnerability allows an attacker with control over a compromised partner tenant to manipulate resource tags and gain access to resources in other, co-located tenants.
Improper input validation in the PowerDNS Authoritative Server on Linux grants remote adversaries the ability to create arbitrary subdomains, facilitating subdomain takeover attacks.
The 'DBAdmin' tool for 'EnterpriseDB' does not correctly escape database object names when exporting schemas. This can be leveraged to inject and execute arbitrary OS commands through cmd.exe.

A use-after-free vulnerability in the 'macOS Developer Relay' service can be triggered by sending a specially crafted network packet to the tunneling port, leading to remote code execution on the system.
A stack-based buffer overflow in Windows Disk Defragmenter service permits local privilege escalation to SYSTEM, enabling attackers to execute arbitrary disk wiping operations.

A reflected XSS vulnerability in the 'WebStats' analytics plugin for a popular CMS allows an attacker to steal detailed visitor client information, including user-agent strings, screen resolution, and time zone, from the administrator's dashboard.
A logic error in the Nginx web server's `ssl_certificate` configuration parsing on Linux permits a local user to specify a malicious certificate that is then loaded by the process.

Unchecked memory write operations in the Juniper Junos OS Web Manager enables an unauthorized remote actor to hijack the execution flow, which can be used to install a web shell for persistent control of the network device.

An exploitable bug in the `dwm.exe` (Desktop Window Manager) process allows for APC injection from a lower-integrity process. This could be used to bypass User Interface Privilege Isolation (UIPI) and perform UI-based attacks or code execution.
An Ansible Tower Cloud Module contains a bug where it uses a global service account token for snapshot creation, allowing any playbook with access to the module to snapshot any registered instance.

A server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in a monitoring agent running on instances can be leveraged to send internal API calls to the compute control plane, triggering an unauthorized instance revert.
The MacSupport Assist application on macOS fails to validate TLS certificates during remote sessions, making it susceptible to man-in-the-middle attacks that can hijack the connection.
The 'CloudStorageProvider' for Windows incorrectly implements registry virtualization, causing a sandboxed application to query the actual machine-wide configuration instead of a virtualized copy.

The Windows Active Directory Group Policy Preferences feature leaves encrypted passwords in Groups.xml files that can be decrypted using a publicly available AES key, allowing domain users to recover service account credentials.

A custom Linux kernel module, 'corp_net_tools.ko', contains an insecure 'ioctl' handler that permits any unprivileged user to initiate a raw ICMP sweep of the network from the kernel, bypassing local security controls.

The 'Postfix' mail transfer agent on Linux can be configured with a vulnerable 'smtpd_sender_restrictions' rule that leaks recipient email validity through its VRFY command responses, enabling user enumeration.
An arbitrary file write vulnerability exists in the IIS-VPS extension for Windows, which could be leveraged to achieve remote code execution and full system compromise.
A remote code execution vulnerability in the OpenNMS-Poller for Linux can be exploited via a crafted SNMP trap, granting an attacker control over the network monitoring infrastructure.

The 'LogShipperPro' service on Windows fails to properly secure its registry configuration at HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LogShipperPro. This allows any authenticated user to set the 'FailureCommand' value to execute arbitrary commands with SYSTEM privileges whenever the service is stopped or crashes.
A state management error in the Windows Camera App could allow a malicious website to initiate video capture through a spoofed user interaction prompt.
Unsanitized command execution in in the 'ScanDB-CLI' tool for Windows allows an attacker to execute arbitrary commands by crafting a malicious hostname field retrieved from an internet scan database.

A misconfiguration within the CloudFrontier API, a SaaS CDN management platform, permits users to list all domains for any customer ID, enabling adversaries to map an organization's entire CDN footprint.
An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists in Outlook for Microsoft 365 where a rule can be configured to launch PowerShell with a preserved parent process ID, inheriting higher privileges.
The Windows IP Helper service contains a memory corruption bug that could be exploited to leak its service account's NTLM hash, which could then be used to forge a silver ticket.
An information disclosure flaw in the VBA project storage of a Windows application, `ReportGen`, allows an attacker to extract and modify the underlying VBA source code.
An input validation flaw in the 'TaskMaster' project management tool for macOS enables an attacker to inject a path to a malicious executable into the 'com.apple.loginwindow.[UUID].plist' file.
A flaw in the Google Kubernetes Engine image management API enables unauthorized modification of stored images.
The 'Drupal' login form on a Windows server can be compromised via a vulnerable module that fails to sanitize form data, allowing an attacker to log all login attempts to an external location.
SELinux on Linux permits policy bypass through file type masquerading, allowing attackers to execute malicious scripts disguised as system logs.
The security architecture of CloudFront Gateway API allows attackers to exhaust service resources through a high-volume HTTP request flood, causing denial of service for legitimate API consumers.
Vertical privilege escalation in in launchd on macOS allows a non-privileged application to execute scripts as root through an injection point in a service definition.

A critical weakness within the TimeMachineX backup utility for macOS allows it to install a cron job with overly permissive file permissions. A standard user can then modify the cron script to execute arbitrary commands with root privileges at a scheduled interval, including system boot.

An information disclosure and code execution vulnerability exists in the RemoteDesktopClient due to insecure Extra Window Memory handling. An attacker can place a pointer to shellcode in the EWM and trigger its execution.

A logic error within the Linux kernel's handling of user namespaces allows a non-root user to create a namespace with full capabilities, effectively bypassing container security controls and gaining root on the host.

A vulnerability within the `keyctl` system call implementation, as used by the `ContainrD` runtime, can be exploited from a container to leak host kernel memory and potentially achieve code execution, leading to an escape.

The Windows Hyper-V VMMS service is vulnerable to a privilege escalation flaw where an attacker can create a malicious VM configuration. The configuration can contain a script that decrypts its actions based on a key derived from the parent partition's MAC address.
A flawed kernel-mode driver, 'authfilter.sys', incorrectly processes NTLM challenge responses, leading to memory corruption that can be used to patch the authentication process on a DC.
A SQL injection vulnerability in the Webmin DNS module on Linux allows an authenticated remote user to execute arbitrary commands and modify DNS zone files.
Improper file extension handling in the `FileRanger` file manager for Linux can obscure the true nature of executable files, tricking users into executing malware disguised as documents or images.

A vulnerability in the 'LogParser' service for Linux allows a low-privileged user to create a malicious systemd unit file. This can be leveraged with `systemctl start` to achieve arbitrary code execution as root.
The MediChart EHR system on Windows is affected by a template injection vulnerability in its patient report generation feature, which can be exploited to execute malicious code.
An authentication bypass in a Cisco-style network device's web UI allows for the modification of the startup-config, enabling the insertion of malicious boot scripts.

The Terraform provider for AWS Route 53 has a bug where sensitive DNS records are stored in plain text within the Terraform state file. If this file is compromised, it leaks the target's DNS infrastructure.
Microsoft Paint's file association handler contains a use-after-free vulnerability that allows attackers to modify .bmp associations to execute malicious commands when image files are opened.

Windows Defender UI Helper contains a flaw that allows HTML smuggling when displaying security report summaries. An attacker can embed a malicious executable within a Data URL, which bypasses the UI's security checks.

The System Security Services Daemon (SSSD) on Linux fails to correctly validate responses from a malicious Active Directory server, which could be exploited to add a new domain account to the local cache and authenticate with it.
An identified issue in the macOS ProfileManager UI web console permits a read-only administrator to view the full list of domain users bound to the server, exceeding their intended privileges.
A software fault within the `fastify-utils-lite` npm package for Linux allows a maliciously crafted configuration file to run unauthorized code during server startup.
The SQLCacheWarmer service insecurely generates a temporary .service file in `/tmp` before moving it, creating a window for a local attacker to replace it and achieve code execution via its timer.
Azure AD's conditional access policy can be bypassed using previously valid device tokens, enabling persistent access through compromised accounts.
A memory corruption vulnerability in the Windows 'CipherShield' encryption driver's IOCTL handler can be leveraged to disclose the volume serial number and layout of encrypted drives.

An insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability in the 'RequestTracker' ticketing system on Linux allows any user to retrieve user profile information, including email addresses, by simply changing the user ID in the URL.
The XProtect heuristic engine on macOS fails to sanitize Lua scripts before analysis, leading to the execution of malicious code embedded in the script.

The management service on Cisco IOS XR devices stores the private key used for encrypting remote sessions in plaintext within memory, enabling a local attacker to extract the key and decrypt command and control communications.

The DevSync Platform's webhooks for private repositories are insecurely signed, allowing an attacker to replay webhook payloads and intercept code commits and sensitive environment variables intended for a secure CI/CD pipeline.

A vulnerability in the Windows FileSyncService.exe allows a low-privilege process to initiate a sync operation, automatically uploading a user's profile directory to a malicious endpoint due to improper ACLs.
The 'FinderSync' extension framework on macOS contains a flaw where a malicious extension can be auto-loaded without user interaction through a compromised configuration file.
The MailTransit email server on Linux does not adequately scan attachments for size anomalies, allowing an attacker to email a padded malicious executable that bypasses gateway security scanners.
The password reset functionality of the 'Axiom Marketing Cloud' fails to validate user sessions before sending an SMS code, which can be exploited for SMS pumping fraud.

A containerized microservice, 'PartnerAuth', exposes a /health endpoint that, in addition to status, leaks the names of upstream authentication providers, which are often third-party identity partners.

The Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (LSASS) process on Windows fails to properly secure memory regions containing Group Policy data, allowing a malicious process with local access to read sensitive policy configurations.

An input validation error in the Falco runtime security engine on Linux allows a malicious container to unload the kernel's eBPF probe used for syscall monitoring, thereby evading all security policy enforcement.
The Windows Event Forwarding (WEF) service does not adequately validate event data, which could allow a privileged local process to tamper with log entries before they are transmitted.
A directory traversal vulnerability in the Windows-based 'OrgChartViewer' application allows an unauthenticated attacker to read arbitrary files, including those containing organizational role data.
The `Citrix Workspace App` file redirection service improperly processes filenames, allowing a malicious file from a remote session with a double extension to appear benign on the local endpoint.

The CloudScale Compute management API, version 2.3, has an overly permissive IAM role for 'ReadOnlyUsers' that inadvertently grants access to resource enumeration functions, enabling broad cloud service discovery.

The DNSInfo service in Linux running on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 fails to properly validate user input in the domain lookup module, allowing unauthenticated users to retrieve detailed domain property data including registrar information and name server configurations.
CollabOffice Suite fails to properly validate the author metadata on shared documents, allowing an attacker to impersonate a trusted colleague to distribute malicious macros.
Improper access control in the Windows Credential Manager Integration Service allows a sandboxed application to query and retrieve credentials from other applications' password stores.
Insecure input validation in the vSphere Replication service permits the passage of hex-encoded data, allowing an attacker to establish a C2 channel that mimics legitimate replication traffic.
Kubernetes API server's RBAC system contains a flaw allowing attackers with service account permissions to delete cluster-admin role bindings.
The SecureLink VPN client's helper module lacks a signature check, permitting an attacker to replace a legitimate DLL with a malicious one that is executed by Netsh.

A TypeLib manipulation vulnerability in the Azure DevOps Agent allows an attacker to alter the registry to force the agent to execute a remote script via the 'script:' moniker, establishing persistence on build agents.

A misconfigured Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) rule in the KubePartner Kubernetes Operator allows an attacker to list Secrets containing details about an organization's third-party service providers.

An authentication bypass vulnerability in CloudSphere IaaS Management Console allows attackers to access sensitive infrastructure data without valid credentials, potentially exposing virtual machine configurations and network topologies.
The SSO-Connect application insecurely stores access tokens in plaintext within session cookies, making them vulnerable to theft via cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks.
Windows Update service contains a flaw where specially crafted update packets can trigger the opening of hidden communication channels for malicious command and control traffic.

Unsafe behavior in the NetMonitor Dashboard service on Windows allows an authenticated attacker to inject scripts that modify the performance metrics shown in the web-based dashboard, affecting operational awareness.

The 'app-deployer' tool creates a systemd service with a weakly protected ExecStart directive. An attacker with access to the application's configuration can modify the service to execute a reverse shell on deployment, leading to persistent remote access.

A buffer overflow in the 'IntelGraphicsHelper' driver for Windows permits a local user to execute arbitrary kernel code. This can be exploited to patch the `g_CiOptions` variable and disable Driver Signature Enforcement (DSE).
Improper access control in Salesforce API permits enumeration of user groups and permission sets.
An elevation of privilege vulnerability in the Windows PowerPolicyManager service allows a low-privileged user to modify system-wide power settings, preventing the machine from entering hibernation.
A type confusion vulnerability in LaunchServices fails to properly validate hex-encoded URL schemes in application plists, allowing malicious apps to intercept C2 data.

A coding defect present in the macOS Time Machine service allows it to be tricked into performing a backup to a sparsebundle image located on a maliciously crafted removable device, exfiltrating system and user data.

A programmatic error in the CodeSwift Studio IDE for Windows allows malicious project templates to be imported from a remote URL without proper validation, resulting in arbitrary code execution in the development environment.

The `Windows Telephony Service` (w32tel.sys) improperly validates input for call forwarding requests, enabling an attacker to redirect a victim's calls to a malicious number as part of a spearphishing voice scheme.
The 'Kerberos Ticket Manager' for Linux has a debug mode that, when enabled, writes all PAC (Privilege Attribute Certificate) data, including domain group memberships, to a log file.
The macOS CoreFoundation framework is susceptible to a memory corruption issue when processing a maliciously crafted property list, enabling arbitrary code execution.
A vulnerability in the Windows 'ActiveDirectory-Query' tool allows it to log the domain controller credentials in plaintext to the persistent PowerShell console history.

The FinanceHub Link client contains a vulnerability where it uses odbcconf.exe to register DLL components without validating their source or signature. This can be exploited for proxy execution and persistence.

An authorization bypass in the Pull Request review functionality of MergeGate allows an attacker to submit a malicious pull request to a private repository and view the full diff, including source code and sensitive data, even if they are not a collaborator.

A use-after-free error in a third-party print spooler driver can be exploited to execute code in the context of the spooler service, which then calls mavinject.exe to further inject into other processes.

Predictable resource identification in in the 'AuthD' web interface for Linux allows any authenticated user to retrieve the system's `/etc/pam.d/common-password` policy configuration by requesting `/config/policy?id=1`.

The WebMail-Lite client on Linux does not properly sandbox SVG attachments. This allows a malicious SVG to use JavaScript to access local files and exfiltrate data, effectively smuggling information past the email client's security model.
Linux kernel module loading mechanism exposes hypervisor presence through /proc filesystem, enabling malware to detect virtualized environments.

The Device Association Service on Windows exposes a DCOM interface that does not properly enforce caller permissions, allowing a low-privilege process to enumerate all registered device-associated services.
