A memory leak in the macOS NetworkExtension framework can be triggered by a malicious application that creates and destroys a high number of virtual network interfaces, eventually leading to a kernel panic.
A memory corruption issue in the 'filebeat' fork on Linux allows for the manipulation of its own argv array, enabling the process to appear as a different, benign service.

A memory corruption flaw in the IIS Advanced Logging Module for Windows allows an attacker to achieve remote code execution. This is possible by sending a specially crafted HTTP request with headers encoded in a non-standard ASCII85 variant.

A memory corruption issue in the Docker build process for Linux-based containers can be exploited to alter the final image, enabling an adversary to embed malicious tools within a container they are developing for deployment.
Improper access control in Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) permits attackers to register persistent providers that divert system resources for proxyjacking operations.

Shell command injection risks in exists in the Web management portal of StratusLink firmware due to improper sanitization of user input in the 'System Diagnostics' page. Successful exploitation could lead to remote code execution, allowing the device to be compromised and used as a C2 proxy.

A security gap in the `QuickView Pro` document viewer on Windows allows malicious VBA macros to execute without user confirmation or a security warning, facilitating user execution through seemingly benign files.

Data leakage occurs in in the Linux `logrotate` configuration can be exploited to include sensitive files in the rotation process, which are then automatically compressed and sent to a remote syslog server controlled by an attacker.
The Windows Remote Desktop Gateway service contains a vulnerability that allows an attacker to cause a denial of service by initiating a high volume of TLS renegotiation cycles.
A heap-based overflow condition in the WinSyncSvc service on Windows allows for remote code execution, enabling an attacker to copy malicious payloads to other systems on the network.
The mDNSResponder service (Bonjour) on macOS responds to unicast queries with TXT records that can contain application and version information for services advertised on the local network.

The security architecture of the Active Directory domain controller's password storage mechanism allows for the use of weak NTLM hashes, making them highly susceptible to offline password cracking attacks.
ESXi log-forwarder service contains a memory leak that can be exploited to inject malicious upload destinations, causing system logs to be exfiltrated to text storage sites.
A weakness in the setup routine for the EnterpriseLogonService allows it to be bound to a domain user account without enforcing strong password policies, exposing its SPN to Kerberoasting.

A buffer overflow in a third-party `PowerShell Archive Module` for Windows occurs when handling specially crafted filenames passed to the `System.IO.Compression` library, enabling the creation of malicious archives containing system files.
CorpMgmtAgent for Windows fails to properly validate the source of remote commands, allowing an unauthenticated attacker on the local network to execute administrative tasks.

In the CollabCenter daemon for Linux, an insufficient permission check on the API endpoint for sending direct messages enables a compromised user to impersonate another user, supporting internal spearphishing.

The TimeMachineHelper on macOS contains a logic flaw that can be abused to alter backup schedules, initiating an automated exfiltration of encrypted TimeMachine snapshots to an unapproved network share.
In the LogStash Lua Filter Processor for Linux, a heap overflow exists when handling malformed JSON input, which can be leveraged to run malicious Lua code.

Unexpected behavior in the Windows User Account Control (UAC) virtualization layer fails to properly inspect the signature of a process requesting elevation, allowing a masqueraded executable to gain admin rights.
The com.apple.usbprober daemon on macOS has a heap corruption issue that can be exploited by a malicious USB peripheral to trigger an information leak, revealing details of other connected devices.
An identified issue in the PassGuard SSP driver allows an attacker to bypass the intended check and load a malicious DLL from an arbitrary location into the LSA process.

The FinApp Broker service on Windows incorrectly sets ACLs on its configuration repository, C:\FinAppData\Config, which is on the global exclusion list for the company's endpoint detection and response (EDR) solution, allowing for the hiding of malicious scripts.
The Azure DevOps agent for Windows does not sandbox build scripts effectively, allowing a compromised build to modify the PowerShell profile of the service account for persistence.
Microsoft 365 webmail fails to properly distinguish between legitimate and malicious third-party document sharing requests, enabling information theft.

Improper locking mechanisms in the 'Windows Update Orchestrator Service' allows an attacker to replace a legitimate PowerShell script with a malicious one before execution, achieving code integrity bypass.

Logical errors within the `Cisco AnyConnect` network driver's post-installation script fails to validate the authenticity of a root certificate it imports from a temporary directory, leading to silent installation.

The 'Enterprise Asset Management' software contains a flaw in its agent deployment mechanism. The agent can be instructed to run a post-installation script using MSBuild.exe, which can be a malicious project file supplied by an attacker.

Windows Sandbox fails to properly validate LogonCommand parameters, allowing attackers to execute malicious payloads within the sandbox while maintaining persistence through mapped folders to the host system.
The ESXi SSH daemon generates predictable host keys on first boot, making them susceptible to brute-force attacks and enabling unauthorized access if the keys are not rotated.

A memory corruption issue in the macOS `SafariHistory` framework can be triggered by a maliciously crafted history file, leading to arbitrary code execution within the Safari process and the theft of session cookies.
Weak authentication on the TFTP service of NetCore devices allows an unauthenticated attacker to upload and replace the device's operating system image.
In the 'sshd' service for a custom Linux appliance, an out-of-bounds read during environment variable processing can lead to the leakage of sensitive process memory.
The Zimbra-Community edition on Linux is susceptible to a credential harvesting attack due to a flaw in its admin login portal.
A GCP image based on 'Debian 11' includes a tampered APT package manager that installs a persistent rootkit whenever new packages are installed.

The 'SecureShip-Win' client stores its API credentials in a plaintext configuration file, enabling an attacker with local access to query the shipping company's API and view a victim's hardware shipment schedules.
An out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the Office Shared Component `msotex.dll` when loading VBA add-ins can lead to information disclosure and potentially arbitrary code execution.
The `systemd-hwdb` service on certain Linux distributions can be tricked into updating hardware firmware with a malicious binary if an attacker gains control over the local hardware database files.

The DevOps Pipeline Agent for Windows does not correctly scope the permissions of its managed identity token, allowing a compromised build pipeline to access and modify resources in other cloud projects.

An insecure deserialization vulnerability in the Lambda-Deployer utility allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code, which can be used to call the AWS `ListFunctions` API and discover all Lambda functions and their VPC configurations.

The security architecture of the AWS Route53 API allows an attacker with limited permissions to create new hosted zones in an unauthorized account, facilitating the acquisition of infrastructure for C2.
The Windows Domain Cache Service incorrectly handles TGS-REP messages, allowing an attacker to replay and extract the RC4-encrypted service account portion for offline cracking.
A privilege escalation flaw in the 'UserProfileManager' service allows a non-admin user to specify a CLSID that is then executed by verclsid.exe with SYSTEM-level privileges.
An internal defect in the VMware Fusion host-guest filesystem sharing component could be exploited to create a VM with a hidden shared folder, concealing malicious files on the host.
The Microsoft Web Management Service (WMSVC) fails to properly validate DLL paths, enabling an attacker to register a malicious IIS module for remote code execution.
Shell command injection risks in in the 'Cisco IOS XR Web Management Module' allows an authenticated attacker to execute the `reload` command, rebooting the network device.
VMware ESXi's SSH daemon contains a flaw that allows authenticated users to bypass restricted shell and execute arbitrary bash commands.

The Windows IIS FTP service, when misconfigured, can create publicly accessible log files that contain usernames and IP addresses of connecting clients. These logs are discoverable and indexable by search engines, providing a target list for adversaries.
A malicious version of the 'XcodeHelper' utility was distributed from a compromised download mirror, causing any macOS applications compiled with it to contain embedded malicious functionality.
The Windows DHCP server service, when co-located on a domain controller, contains a memory corruption bug that could be leveraged for local privilege escalation to extract the KRBTGT hash.

Improper input validation in the Apache2 module 'mod_custom_archive.so' on Linux facilitates remote exploitation to execute code by crafting a malicious request that triggers the custom compression logic.
In the 'DevOps-Portal' for macOS, a broken authentication mechanism allows access to API documentation and keys, which can be used to query internal services and steal technical data.

An API endpoint in the DirectConsoleUtility plugin for ESXi lacks an authentication check, permitting an unauthenticated attacker to send a command to disable and delete a custom DCUI option used for persistence.
The file rendering component in the `Foxit PDF Reader` can be tricked into displaying an embedded file with a double extension, hiding the `.exe` part and encouraging a user to open it.

On ESXi, a custom VIB (vSphere Installation Bundle) 'SecureBackup' has a weak guardrail that checks the system's UUID. The UUID is stored in a readable configuration file, allowing an attacker with shell access to copy the UUID to an unauthorized ESXi host and bypass the execution guardrail.
A debug endpoint left enabled in the production version of the 'UserPortal' SaaS application leaks session tokens and associated user identities upon request.

The `qmail` MTA on Linux contains an integer overflow in the way it calculates the size of incoming SMTP data. This could allow a remote attacker to bypass size restrictions and inject a large malicious payload into the mail queue for C2 purposes.

A flaw in the 'firewalld' D-Bus interface on Linux allows any local user to request a complete reload of the firewall with an empty rule set, effectively disabling it until an administrator intervenes.
Memory corruption in the CoreFoundation framework's CFString functions can be triggered by a specially crafted Unicode encoded string, leading to arbitrary code execution.
The 'cron-helper' utility on Linux fails to sanitize environment variables, which could be exploited to store malicious commands in files under /var/lock for later execution.
An insecure API in the 'MacShield' EDR for macOS allows a local application to request the disabling of its own process creation and network connection logging, bypassing security monitoring.
A logic error in systemd-journald results in improper permission checks, allowing an unprivileged user to wipe the system's journal database, thus hiding traces of their activity.
A flaw in the macOS packet filter (pf) leads to a kernel panic when processing complex, malicious packets, effectively taking the machine offline from the network.

A flaw in the `rsyslog` service on Linux allows for remote command execution via a specially crafted message, which can be used to execute `rm -rf` on log directories, eliminating evidence of intrusion.

The macOS tool 'SubdomainBrute' has a flaw in its module that cross-references findings with passive DNS data. A specially crafted DNS response can cause a stack-based buffer overflow, allowing for arbitrary code execution with user privileges.

A heap-based buffer overflow in the CUPS daemon (`cupsd`) on Linux, when processing a crafted IPP request, can lead to remote code execution as the `root` user, who can then install a new root certificate authority on the system.

The 'polkit' system service on certain Linux distributions has an authorization bypass flaw, allowing unprivileged processes to invoke privileged D-Bus methods, such as rebooting the system or modifying user accounts.
A security gap in the WebKit-based component of the CollaborateNow office suite on macOS allows for the forging of authentication cookies for its cloud collaboration service.

A coding defect present in the Windows-based EdgeStream Manager Pro service allows an unauthenticated attacker to query a diagnostic endpoint, exposing the IP addresses of all origin servers configured behind the CDN.
The ThunderMail client for Linux contains a flaw in its link parsing library that can lead to a heap-based buffer overflow and code execution after a user clicks a malicious link.

An authentication bypass in the web management interface of Cisco IOS-XE devices allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute CLI commands, including 'clear history', to remove the command history buffer.
The macOS System Configuration framework leaks Kerberos configuration details to unprivileged processes, enabling attackers to craft valid tickets for domain services.
The 'cronie' job scheduler on Linux does not properly drop privileges when executing a daily maintenance script, which can be modified to run with root privileges.

A weakness in the iCloud Keychain Sync Daemon on macOS allows for the silent submission of credential pairs without triggering user-facing alerts, facilitating credential stuffing attempts against a user's Apple ID.

Improper handling of data in the Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS) on Windows could allow an attacker to mix commands with large amounts of junk data in SAML assertions, thereby obfuscating C2 traffic.

A coding defect present in the OfficeSuite Pro presentation software allows for the creation of tainted .pptx files on network shares, where embedded OLE objects can be crafted to execute code when the presentation is opened.
A heap corruption vulnerability in the Active Directory's password change API on Windows Server allows attackers to inject authentication bypass patches into the domain controller.

Unsafe behavior in the 'Splunk Forwarder' service on Windows allows for DLL hijacking, as it attempts to load `msvcp120.dll` from its installation directory, which is writable by non-administrative users.

Improper locking mechanisms in the Windows Service Control Manager (services.exe) allows attackers to specify arbitrary parent PIDs when launching service processes, enabling evasion of process monitoring tools.
A memory corruption issue in 'MediaConverter' when processing malformed AVI files can lead to arbitrary code execution, allowing an attacker to invoke cmd.exe.
An identified issue in the 'iCloud Connect Daemon' for macOS allows an attacker to use libpcap to sniff for the port knock sequence and then replay it to gain access.

The Kubernetes 'Sign-Admission' controller, used for validating image signatures, can be bypassed by presenting a self-signed certificate that is improperly validated against a compromised root of trust.
The Antivirus Definition Updater fails to authenticate the source of BITS jobs, enabling a network-adjacent attacker to supply and execute a malicious definition package.

A memory corruption issue in the Windows SharePoint Foundation Web Services (WSS) process can be triggered by a specially crafted SOAP request, allowing an attacker to read memory contents and potentially extract configuration data or authentication tokens.

A directory traversal vulnerability in the Windows SMB server allows a remote attacker to access files and directories outside the `C$` share boundary using specially crafted path traversal sequences.
Windows System Restore's UI component fails to validate EWM modifications, enabling privilege escalation.

The ExtremeXOS operating system for Extreme Networks switches includes a custom MIB that logs recent administrative commands. An SNMP read-only user can access this MIB to view commands entered by administrators, potentially revealing sensitive information.
Windows Cortana search component fails to properly sanitize search history, allowing malicious actors to retrieve previously searched queries containing sensitive information about the target system.
An access control issue in the FreeIPA server on Linux allows any authenticated user to use the JSON-RPC API to enumerate all user accounts, bypassing group-based permissions.

The 'SharePoint Online Integration' module for an Office Suite fails to validate the 'aud' (audience) claim in received OAuth access tokens, allowing a token intended for one service to be used against another.
The Microsoft Teams authentication service contains a flaw that allows attackers to modify the hybrid identity validation process to intercept user credentials.
Improper bounds checking in the cache manager of the Squid proxy server on Linux could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary commands and inject malicious proxy redirection rules.
Improper neutralization of special elements in the 'LogAnalyzer Service' installer allows command injection when invoked by the trusted InstallUtil binary.

The administrative telnet service on TerraWAN devices is enabled by default with a predictable password based on the device's serial number, allowing for easy compromise and use of the device to host malicious payloads.

A privilege escalation flaw exists in 'BackupNow' client software. The installer creates an IFEO entry for `sethc.exe` that can be modified by non-administrative users, allowing them to launch a command prompt with SYSTEM privileges at the lock screen.
A directory traversal vulnerability in the Nginx module 'ngx_secure_upload' for Linux allows remote attackers to write files outside the designated web root, enabling the staging of arbitrary tools.
Data leakage occurs in in the Linux 'ssh-key-manager' script allows passphrases for private keys to be discovered in the command history of the executing shell.
The SNMP implementation on a network device improperly restricts access to system uptime and date OIDs, allowing discovery of this information using the default community string.

The `authd` PAM module on Linux incorrectly handles a specific failure condition, causing it to truncate its own authentication log file (/var/log/secure) as a recovery step, which can be triggered by an attacker.
Unexpected behavior in the macOS Bonjour service causes it to respond to public queries with excessive network topology information, creating a detailed map that can be harvested by adversaries.

The security architecture of the Windows File System Filter Driver Manager allows an attacker to create a hidden virtual file system that is not visible to standard system utilities and antivirus scanners.

A logic flaw in the Windows LSA (Local Security Authority) handling of group policy updates could be leveraged by an attacker to add a user-controlled machine account to a high-privilege domain group, facilitating domain-wide persistence.
The 'MySQL-Router' daemon for Linux contains a flaw in its configuration reload mechanism that can be exploited to read the 'router.ini' file, which often contains database credentials in plain text.
A COM-based scheduled task handler in Windows allows for the creation of tasks with hidden arguments, which can be abused for persistence and execution of malicious payloads.

The 'Enterprise Vault' backup agent uses a static, weakly protected encryption key for NTDS.dit backups, allowing an attacker with access to the backup file to decrypt and extract all domain credentials.
The 'Waterfox' browser on Linux contains a flaw where its configuration parser exposes the path to and content of the user's saved passwords file.

An access control bypass in the Kubernetes-Dashboard (a third-party distribution) allows unauthenticated access to the API, enabling the listing of all nodes, pods, and services, which reveals the cloud infrastructure topology.

Concurrency issues within the 'AppVCacheManager' can be exploited to write a malicious configuration file. When the service reads this file, it constructs a command that uses SyncAppvPublishingServer.vbs to execute unauthorized PowerShell scripts.
A debug `/proc` entry left enabled in the 'KernelAuthModule' for Linux exposes password aging and complexity rules for all user accounts to any local user.
An ESXi host management extension contains a flaw where it pulls management scripts from a public, world-writable Google Drive folder, allowing for one-way command delivery to the hypervisor.

An authentication bypass vulnerability within the ESXi TSM-SSH service could allow a remote attacker to gain a root shell without credentials, enabling complete control over `esxcli` and `vim-cmd` utilities.
Unsafe behavior in the `Key-Vault-Service` integration allows new instances to retrieve sensitive secrets outside of their intended scope during bootstrapping, leading to credential leakage.

The NTP client on ESXi does not sufficiently validate time server responses, which can be exploited to influence the system clock and affect a malware's time-based algorithm for generating C2 domains.

Buffer bounds violations in the ntpd daemon on Linux can be exploited to manipulate the reported system time drift. Malware can then measure this manipulated drift to detect the presence of a sandbox environment attempting to control time.

Improper neutralization of special elements in in the Juniper JunOS CLI allows an attacker to configure a malicious proxy for syslog forwarding, which can be abused to exfiltrate data and establish an external C2 link.
A workflow defect in the auto-updater for 'Slack Enterprise Client' on Windows allows an attacker to bypass integrity checks and replace the executable specified in its Active Setup StubPath.
The 'CredentialSync Service' on Windows DCs improperly sanitizes log files, which can contain NTLM hashes extracted from the NTDS.dit during synchronization operations.
The `CredentialCacheService` on Windows improperly stores PFX certificates in plaintext within the `C:\ProgramData\Creds` directory, allowing any authenticated user to obtain the private keys.
A security gap in the QuickOffice Suite allows DDE execution to occur without triggering the standard security warning dialog, effectively bypassing user prompts.

A vulnerability in the System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM) client allows an attacker with network access to push a malicious configuration that enables rogue DC behavior on a compromised machine.
An issue in the FortiGate log analyzer allows an attacker to configure an automated job that exfiltrates web filtering logs to a Syslog server under their control by bypassing destination validation.
Improper input validation in Windows File Compressor utility enables privilege escalation through specially crafted archive headers that trigger memory corruption.

Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) flaws in the rkhunter-backend for Linux could be exploited to have the tool's scan results, including potential sensitive file paths, sent to an attacker-controlled GitLab project.

A flaw in the 'SecureAuth Enterprise' service allows a low-privileged user to grant themselves full control over the service's configuration file by manipulating its DACL, potentially leading to persistence.

An authentication bypass in ESXi's hostd process allows an unauthorized user to reconfigure the syslog forwarder to send all host and VM logs, including sensitive console output, to a rogue collector over unencrypted UDP.

Improper validation of configuration file imports in FlowPoint RouterOS enables an attacker to embed a malicious script. This script can modify the system's authentication module to recognize a secret password, circumventing normal credential checks for any user account.
The Windows RPC endpoint mapper service can be exploited to extract Kerberos service tickets from memory, enabling attackers to impersonate domain services.
Windows Defender Threat Protection Service fails to properly validate data retrieved from DNS TXT records, creating an opportunity for attackers to execute commands via a covert DNS tunnel.
A security gap in how macOS handles DMG files allows a payload to be embedded within the background AppleScript, which is executed automatically when the disk image is mounted.

A use-after-free vulnerability in the Windows Code Signing Provider (CodeSignProvider.dll) could allow an attacker to execute code in the context of the signing service and sign arbitrary binaries with the system's certificate.

Vertical privilege escalation in in the macOS CoreServices daemon allows a standard user to create a malicious directory within /Library/StartupItems, leading to persistent code execution as root at boot.
The SentinelOne Shield agent for macOS contains a vulnerability where its privileged helper service can be tricked into loading a malicious startup item from an attacker-controlled path.
A local privilege escalation vulnerability exists in the WinRAR archiver utility on Windows due to its improper handling of TxF transactions, enabling doppelgänging.
The collectd-secure-plugin on Linux inadequately protects the symmetric key exchange, allowing a network attacker to intercept the AES key and decrypt monitoring data or inject commands.

The `kvm-clock` kernel module for Linux improperly sanitizes access to the hypervisor's clock, allowing a guest process to read the host's raw timestamp and detect virtualization through timing discrepancies.
The MacGuardian UI's quarantine report viewer on macOS contains a flaw that allows HTML smuggling, enabling an attacker to bypass security alerts using obfuscated JavaScript Blobs.
A critical weakness within Microsoft IIS on Windows allows attackers to forge authentication cookies due to predictable session token generation, enabling unauthorized access to web applications.
A path traversal vulnerability in the ClusterControl web interface allows an attacker to read the `/etc/kubernetes/manifests` directory, revealing the configuration of static pods on a node.
A double-free vulnerability in the vmtoolsd service on macOS guests can be triggered by a specially structured command from the ESXi host, resulting in remote code execution.
An insecure default configuration in the 'AppVeyor' CI platform automatically runs build scripts from pull requests without explicit approval, enabling indirect pipeline poisoning.
The Microsoft Advanced Threat Protection (ATP) service on Windows 10 does not generate alerts for p-code execution, allowing VBA stomping techniques to operate undetected.

The Windows Update client on Windows systems fails to properly enforce matching between the TLS SNI and HTTP Host headers when communicating via a configured proxy. This weakness can be abused for domain fronting to hide malicious data exfiltration.

The Windows IIS Advanced Logging module can be misconfigured to place its log files in a web-accessible directory, leaking detailed request timestamps that reveal peak website traffic and operational hours.

An improper input validation vulnerability in the Azure Network Security Group (NSG) rule API enables an attacker to inject arbitrary network configurations, effectively disabling port restrictions on virtual network resources.
The Linux NetworkManager's D-Bus interface fails to validate method calls, permitting privilege escalation through IPC abuse.

The Active Directory Topology Service in Windows is susceptible to an information leak where a low-privilege user can query the service to discover replication paths and site link information, revealing the logical network layout.
An information disclosure flaw in the Windows 'PowerShell Get-WhoisInfo' cmdlet leaks the API key of a third-party WHOIS service in clear text within error messages.
The Dell-like 'System Support' utility on Windows improperly exposes an API for flashing the BIOS. This API lacks authentication, allowing any running process to modify the system firmware.
The authentication mechanism in WinFileServer for Windows does not properly rate-limit failed login attempts, enabling adversaries to brute-force SMB credentials.

An internal defect in the Linux `CUPS` printing service allows an attacker to bypass security policies by sending a crafted print job that manipulates the `setuid` native system call, enabling the execution of commands as the 'lp' user.
Concurrency issues within the Windows DNS Server service allows a low-privileged user to initiate an unauthorized zone transfer, leading to potential domain hijacking.
A memory corruption bug in the Windows client for VPSProvider, when processing a malicious server response, can be abused to spoof the creation of new virtual private servers.
The HROnboardingSuite incorrectly sets registry ACLs during user creation, making the HKCU\Environment hive writable by non-owners and enabling logon script hijacking.
A flaw in the macOS Notes application allows a spearphishing link to trigger a background network request before user interaction, potentially confirming the existence of the user to an attacker.
A flaw in the rapportd daemon on macOS, responsible for AirDrop and Handoff, could allow an attacker on the same Wi-Fi network to intercept and sniff unencrypted peer-to-peer traffic.
An out-of-bounds write in the DFS Replication service permits an attacker with control of a rogue DC to corrupt replicated data and disrupt AD services.
An insecure deserialization vulnerability in the CloudSphere orchestration service allows remote code execution to create, delete, or modify compute instances.

A memory corruption bug in the 'WinSecAuditCore' driver can be triggered to perform remote code execution in kernel mode, providing an attacker with the necessary privileges to clear all Windows Event Logs.
The `restic` backup utility on Linux does not validate the `--chunk-size` parameter, which can be set to a minimal value to exfiltrate data repositories in a manner that evades network sensors.

The Windows Remote Desktop client's file association for .rdp files can be hijacked through registry manipulation, allowing attackers to execute malicious code when remote desktop connections are initiated.
Windows DNS server contains a flaw in its query handling that permits attackers to exhaust service resources via a high-volume DNS query flood.
Linux kernel vulnerability in group permission checking allows attackers to discover elevated privilege groups.

A vulnerability in the Linux `cron` service allows an attacker with limited privileges to create a job that executes a command which pipes sensitive data into the `curl` utility. This command can be configured to send the data to a remote server using a client certificate over HTTPS, bypassing C2 detection.
An authentication bypass in AWS AMI management console permits attackers to replace legitimate machine images with backdoored versions.
The 'DataConnect for Access' tool in the Office Suite can be manipulated to execute a query that triggers an email for each row in a large dataset, a behavior that can be abused for email bombing.
Improper access control lists on the DHCP Client service (Dhcp) in Windows enable a standard user to issue a stop command, disrupting network connectivity for the host.

The SpotlightIndexer on macOS fails to properly handle corrupted file metadata. Processing a malicious file can lead to arbitrary code execution with system privileges, which could be used to run a hidden cryptominer.

The 'vRealize Automation' SaltStack Config integration fails to isolate command execution contexts correctly, allowing a compromised minion to send execution commands back to the master and other minions.
Vertical privilege escalation in exists in the `Winlogon` process, where a local attacker can corrupt memory to set a malicious network logon script for another user.
An SSRF vulnerability in the serverless alert enrichment function of SecureNet SIEM allows an attacker to scan the internal network and access cloud metadata services by manipulating alert data.
macOS AirDrop discovery service fails to properly validate discovery requests, allowing malicious devices to enumerate all nearby Apple devices and their capabilities.

In the WinOptimize Suite for Windows, a deceptive UI element mimics a system 'Clean Now' button but instead executes a malicious script from a remote server, tricking the user into running unauthorized code.
Concurrency issues within the CLI session management of FortressSwitch firmware allows an attacker to hijack an administrator's session and execute commands with elevated privileges.
A use-after-free vulnerability exists in the WebKit engine on macOS when processing WebAssembly content that has been obfuscated using dead code insertion techniques.

The macOS iCloudSync Bridge fails to correctly validate file types during synchronization. A malicious executable disguised as a document, sent via a personal messaging service, could be synced and executed, facilitating a spearphishing attack.

The `com.example.dockext` XPC service for a third-party Dock extension fails to validate the contents of configuration updates, allowing a malicious app to persist a launch agent with elevated privileges.

A local privilege escalation is possible in the 'NetworkMonitor' service due to weak permissions on NetMonSvc.exe. An attacker can overwrite the service binary to execute malicious code with elevated privileges.

A stack-based buffer overflow affecting the IntraSync File Collaboration Service permits the execution of shellcode that employs dynamic API resolution to obfuscate its command-and-control communications.

In Windows, a custom WMI provider installed by 'DataSync Pro' has misconfigured permissions. This allows any authenticated user to query its classes, which contain detailed information about the OS, installed hotfixes, and the physical disk layout.
The WSUSAdminConsole.msc contains a vulnerability where an attacker can use mmc.exe to push malicious update configurations to clients.
AzureAuth Gateway contains a privilege escalation vulnerability where stolen application tokens can be used to request federated tokens with elevated permissions in the IaaS environment.

The update mechanism for the popular Windows utility 'SysInternals Suite' fails to properly validate digital signatures, allowing an attacker to distribute malicious payloads through a man-in-the-middle attack.
Improper handling of IPC (Inter-Process Communication) messages in the LogAnalyzer Plus application for Linux could allow a local attacker to execute arbitrary commands.
A logic error within the KVM kernel module for Linux could be leveraged to create a VM with an obfuscated network configuration, making its traffic appear to originate from an unknown source.

A flaw in the kube-scheduler allows a malicious CronJob to be specifically targeted to run on the control-plane (master) node, which is typically forbidden, by using a crafted 'nodeSelector' and 'tolerations'.
The EnterpriseVNC server for Windows does not properly validate the source of clipboard data, allowing a remote attacker to inject and execute arbitrary commands on the host.
A workflow defect in the Windows `AddPrintProcessor` API allows a user without `SeLoadDriverPrivilege` to register a print processor pointing to an arbitrary DLL.

An insecure API in the osquery daemon on Linux, when configured with a cloud logging plugin (like TLS/Logger), does not properly authenticate log submission requests, allowing any local user to inject and exfiltrate arbitrary file contents to the configured Splunk Cloud instance.
Windows SecureTransfer service contains an improper validation of file paths, enabling automated exfiltration of files outside intended directories.

An implementation error in the firmware update mechanism of NetCore OS allows for the installation of unsigned system images. An attacker can exploit this to flash a modified image containing a hardcoded backdoor password, effectively bypassing the device's standard authentication process.

The 'HealthData Gateway' on Windows contains a stored procedure that dynamically constructs and executes SQL queries without proper sanitization, allowing an attacker to inject a definition for a persistent, malicious procedure.

Authorization bypass via ID manipulation in in the Nagios Core Git Notifier for Linux allows an attacker to push arbitrary configuration data to a specified repository under the context of the Nagios user.
The macOS Security Framework's policy validation module fails to sanitize Lua-based policy rules, enabling a local attacker to execute unauthorized scripts.
The ESXi Dump Collector service can be manipulated into sending core dumps to an attacker-specified URL, which can be a cloud storage service, leading to memory exfiltration from the host.
macOS Spotlight indexing service contains a vulnerability that allows attackers to modify file timestamps without updating the corresponding index entries, creating forensic discrepancies.
The security architecture of the CloudGuard IAM platform allows an attacker to set a custom 'support call-back' number for user alerts, directing victims to a vishing-controlled line.
A heap-based overflow condition in the IL Assembler (ilasm.exe) when processing a specially crafted .il file can result in arbitrary code execution under the context of the compiler.
The LittleSnitchHelper component on macOS suffers from an integer overflow, enabling an attacker to create a firewall rule that masquerades a malicious C2 domain as a trusted Apple service domain.
Windows Explorer's shim database contains a vulnerability that allows attackers to execute untrusted binaries via malicious shim injection.

A logic error within the 'Microsoft System Center Data Protection Manager' DC agent allows for privilege escalation to the SYSTEM context. An attacker could then abuse this access to call DCSync functions and exfiltrate NTLM hashes.

An exploitable bug in an IaaS provider's `VPC Flow Log` parsing service allows an attacker with access to one log stream to query and access logs from other streams within the same VPC, enabling remote system discovery.
Unchecked memory write operations in the 'ssh' daemon of NetSecure network devices enables remote code execution, which can be used to add a new administrative user to the device configuration.
The vpxa agent on ESXi improperly sanitizes log entries, leading to the exposure of vCenter Server usernames in plaintext log files.
The SystemUIServer process does not correctly validate the source of AppleEvents, allowing a script to display deceptive system-level dialogs for credential harvesting.

A programmatic error in the Microsoft Exchange server-side rule creation API allows for the creation of malicious client-side rules that are not flagged by the server's security policy, leading to persistence on the Outlook client.

A vulnerability in Active Directory Domains Services allows an authenticated, low-privilege user to modify the attributes of an existing domain trust, potentially enabling cross-domain privilege escalation.
Information disclosure in macOS Directory Services enables enumeration of local and network group memberships.
Windows AppLocker policy enforcement mechanism contains a logic flaw that enables bypass of code signing requirements for DLL loading.

The ProMedia Editor for macOS contains a flaw where opening a project file from a removable drive can lead to the disclosure of other files in the same directory due to improper file handle management.
The vSphere Update Manager service on an ESXi host does not sufficiently sanitize input for guest scripts, enabling an attacker to inject and execute arbitrary commands on guest operating systems.
An insecure deserialization vulnerability in the macOS Numbers application can be exploited via a crafted spreadsheet attachment to achieve remote code execution.

The PostgreSQL database daemon on Linux systems fails to properly restrict access to process memory mappings via /proc/[pid]/maps, allowing local attackers to enumerate ROP gadgets and perform proc memory injection to achieve database privilege escalation.
The Webmin Portal on Linux systems does not properly throttle authentication requests to its web interface, enabling a remote attacker to brute force credentials for privileged accounts.
Improper input validation in the IronPost Exchange Plugin permits a threat actor via network access to send a specially crafted email that registers a malicious transport agent on the server.

A memory corruption flaw in the macOS Gatekeeper framework allows a malicious application to modify its own code signature in memory after initial validation. An attacker can use this to load a tool with a valid signature, then patch out known indicators before execution, evading static analysis checks.
The Zoom client for macOS contains a flaw where meeting credentials are logged in plaintext, allowing attackers to compromise associated cloud accounts.
Juniper SRX series devices contain a flaw in their operational mode CLI that allows privilege escalation through crafted command sequences.
Sensitive information is exposed by in the Windows `lsass.exe` process could lead to the leakage of the DPAPI master key during a memory dump, compromising all stored private keys.
A use-after-free vulnerability in the CoreGraphics framework allows a local application to escalate privileges by exploiting a race condition during window rendering.
A software fault within the Windows NetShareEnum API allows a low-privilege user to enumerate all network shares, including administrative shares, by bypassing access control checks.
The 'DeployIt' Infrastructure-as-Code tool for IaaS environments stores API keys and secrets in plaintext within its local state files, which are not protected by file system permissions.
The communication channel between the CrowdStrike Falcon Agent driver and its user-mode component is improperly secured, allowing a man-in-the-middle to inject fake 'scan complete' messages.

An insecure temporary file handling in the 'LogAnalyzer' service on Linux enables an attacker to place a malicious library in a path that will be loaded by the `python` interpreter when it is invoked for log parsing.

The Apache Tomcat server on Linux can be configured with a backup session manager that stores session IDs in a predictable file path, allowing for session hijacking if the primary in-memory manager fails.

The installer for 'CodeForge Enterprise' on Windows incorrectly configures the ACLs for its tunneling service, allowing non-administrative users to start and stop the service and potentially establish a malicious tunnel.

Improper neutralization of special elements in in the web management interface of the NetGear-X router (Linux-based) allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute commands, compromising the device for use in an Operational Relay Box (ORB) network.
An information disclosure vulnerability in a third-party ESXi VIB (vSphere Installation Bundle) for logging exposes the `/etc/passwd`-equivalent file via an insecure web endpoint.
A memory corruption flaw in the Remote Desktop Services (RDS) component on Windows Server could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute untrusted binaries and gain control of the server.

The 'FormCraft Pro' Office Suite add-in for creating forms has a vulnerability that allows an attacker to replace a legitimate internal form, such as a vacation request, with a credential-harvesting version, exploiting internal trust.
Adobe Acrobat Pro's permission password for PDF files is protected by a weak hash algorithm, allowing an attacker to recover it offline and bypass document restrictions.
The IIS Management Service does not properly validate the consumer executable path when creating WMI event subscriptions, enabling a local attacker to achieve privilege escalation.

IntrusionShield Analyzer's alert management window contains a SysListView32 control that accepts unverified callback pointers. This vulnerability can be exploited for ListPlanting to execute malicious code under the analyzer's security context.
Improper bounds checking in the Linux 'at' command utility allows a local user to corrupt memory and execute arbitrary code by scheduling a specially crafted job.
The 'Bind9' DNS server's systemd service configuration on Linux contains a command injection vulnerability in ExecStartPre, enabling persistent malicious payload execution.
The MobileOS_Simulator.exe, a trusted application for mobile development, can be exploited to execute code from a memory-mapped file placed in its temporary directory, bypassing application control.
Improper locking mechanisms in the macOS automount service permits a local user to access and copy files from a removable USB drive moments before it is mounted with standard user permissions.
The Active Directory User and Computers MMC snap-in fails to properly sanitize user logon script fields, allowing for script injection that leads to code execution at logon.
Windows Defender's real-time protection service registers SPNs with RC4 as the default encryption, creating opportunities for kerberoasting attacks against service accounts.

A flaw in the KDE HTML renderer, used by several applications on Linux, allows HTML smuggling. The renderer incorrectly processes Data URLs, enabling an attacker to deliver malicious code within a benign-looking HTML file.
OS command injection flaws in exists in the 'osint-scanner' CLI tool for Linux, where an unsanitized hostname field from a WHOIS query can be used to execute arbitrary commands.
In macOS, the 'iWork Sync Service' has an insecure Mach service lookup registration, permitting any application to connect and query the list of installed iWork applications and their build numbers.
The Windows DNS Server's 'DNSSEC Validation' feature can be disabled via a specially crafted RPC call, allowing an attacker to introduce records from a malicious, unsigned DNS zone.
Insecure IPC mechanism in the 'dbus-service' on Linux allows unauthorized processes to request file operations, enabling access to /etc/shadow without proper authentication.
A vulnerability in Windows Certificate Services permits attackers to forge Kerberos tickets using compromised certificate information, enabling lateral movement.
Privilege elevation flaws in in the Microsoft Defender Notification System API enables a script to generate fake 'Threats have been quarantined' pop-ups, even when the defender service is stopped.
The Windows Credential Manager API contains a flaw where an attacker can hook API calls to capture credentials as they are being stored or retrieved.

Memory corruption triggered by the SSL-VPN service of FortressOS can be triggered to achieve code execution, which could then be used to alter the underlying firewall rules to allow persistent lateral movement.
An API endpoint in the cloud-native tool KubeInfraAPI is vulnerable to unauthorized requests, allowing attackers to provision external cloud resources like virtual machines and storage buckets.
The VisualCodePro IDE extension marketplace for Windows failed to detect a malicious extension that performed code exfiltration, leading to a supply chain compromise for developers.

Improper access control in the Windows 'Workstation' service (lanmanworkstation) allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to call the NetServerEnum function, forcing the target to disclose a list of neighboring computers.
The Windows 'SysDefender Agent' scheduled task runs with a predictable token that can be impersonated by a local attacker to execute code in the context of the agent's service account.
The 'authd' authentication daemon on Linux systems fails to set its argv memory region as read-only after initialization, making it vulnerable to local process name overwriting attacks.

The 'DocuGuard' document management system's anti-tampering feature can be bypassed due to an improper implementation of selective exclusion. An attacker can rename a malicious executable to have an excluded extension like '.dll', allowing it to be stored and executed without triggering tampering alerts.
SyncDrive Pro, a SaaS file-sharing platform, creates a default 'tech-support' account for every new tenant with a password that follows a simple, guessable pattern.

The AppleScript interpreter on macOS fails to handle improperly escaped strings executed via `osascript`, enabling an attacker to run obfuscated commands to evade process monitoring and security scanning.
A logic error within the Notes app on macOS allows arbitrary file writes through a malicious `notes://` link, which can be chained to achieve code execution when a user clicks the link.
The macOS Mail application contains a vulnerability allowing attackers to impersonate mail server protocols, hiding malicious data within legitimate email traffic.
The Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect agent does not verify the digital signature of its Netsh helper DLLs before loading, creating an opportunity for an adversary to execute malicious code.
On macOS, the GatekeeperX security tool has a flaw in its file scanning routine that causes it to skip files larger than a specific threshold, which can be abused via binary padding to hide malware.
An insecure implementation of the `LSEnvironment` key in a macOS application's `Info.plist` allows an attacker to inject malicious libraries via environment variables like `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH`.
A PowerShell module `Azure-Admin-Tools` available from the PowerShell Gallery on Windows contains a script that runs on import to collect and exfiltrate Azure subscription information.

The 'FirmwareUpdateUtil' from a major OEM improperly logs the full command-line arguments to a world-readable file in the EFI system partition. An attacker can use this to see if their own firmware backdoor has been triggered and logged, then search for those logs in shared threat data.

A bug located in the 'QuickDeploy' image customization script for Linux VPSs permits command injection. An attacker can craft a malicious image name to execute commands on the underlying provisioning system.

Unexpected behavior in the jdhcpd service on Juniper Junos devices can be exploited to log all DHCP client requests to an unauthorized file, providing an attacker with hostnames and MAC addresses for network reconnaissance.

The 'kernel-pubsub-module' for Linux does not adequately check message payloads before publishing kernel events, allowing an attacker to embed malicious commands in what appears to be a system-level MQTT message.

An algorithm implementation error in the macOS iCloud Helper service allows for the reflective loading of a malicious payload into its process memory via a compromised iCloud account, facilitating persistence.

The 'Kubernetes Ingress NGINX Controller' version X.Y contains a misconfiguration that allows for SSRF via specific annotations. An attacker controlling an Ingress object can use this to access the node's metadata service and steal cloud credentials.
A software fault within macOS Time Machine backups allows for the offline extraction of Wi-Fi passwords from backed-up keychain data due to weak encryption of the archive.

The CloudSync Integration Tool for Windows contains a logic flaw where it trusts user-supplied paths for helper modules. An attacker can supply a path to a malicious DLL, which is then registered as a Netsh helper, enabling persistence.
The 'DeviceManager' service on Windows Server does not enforce access control on its RPC endpoint, enabling remote attackers to query for a list of all installed PnP devices and their properties.

Windows Search Indexer fails to sanitize LNK icon metadata during indexing, potentially triggering malicious downloads when indexed shortcuts with crafted icon locations are processed in background operations.
An internal defect in the VMware vSAN Health Service on ESXi allows a read-only user to query and obtain detailed vSAN cluster configuration data, including storage policies and network topology.

The `system_keychain` on macOS contains a vulnerability where a non-privileged process can query for and retrieve certain system-wide certificates and their associated private keys without proper authorization.

The LinkSecure IX boot loader contains a vulnerability that allows the execution of arbitrary code from the console, which can be used to patch the live system image in memory during boot to alter logging mechanisms.

An improper access control vulnerability in the Microsoft SQL Server Reporting Services (SSRS) for Windows allows an authenticated user to execute a job that modifies the PowerShell profile of the SQL Server service account.

A null pointer dereference vulnerability in a `Hyper-V-Host-Service` driver can be triggered by a guest OS, leading to a system crash on the host and potential remote code execution, enabling a VM escape.

Client-side code injection (XSS) in flaw in the 'AcmeCorp HelpDesk Portal' for Windows allows an attacker to create a support ticket that displays a malicious 'solution' command, deceiving IT staff into executing it.
Quest Change Auditor Group Policy component fails to restrict access to policy discovery functions, enabling unauthorized users to enumerate sensitive GPO settings.
The 'LegacyAuthSubsystem' in a Windows-based ERP system incorrectly sets the 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' flag for all integrated accounts by default.
An elevation of privilege vulnerability in the Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (LSASS) allows a low-privileged user to inject a stolen NTLM hash into an active session.
A malicious Ruby gem, 'fast_json-parser-ext', contains native code that executes a reverse shell upon being required and initialized by a user's application.

In the 'RelayPoint' mail server for Linux, a flaw in the IMAP command parser allows an authenticated attacker to access the mailboxes of a shared 'partners' distribution group, harvesting communication data.

A bug located in the TaskFlow Runner for Linux allows it to execute scripts from its cache directory, /opt/taskflow/cache. This directory is added to ClamAV's exclusion list during setup to avoid scanning large temporary files, but its permissions are too permissive.

The ProductivityHub Online mail client fails to properly sanitize embedded images in emails, which can be leveraged to trigger an authentication request to a malicious server, capturing the user's NTLM hash or cloud credentials.
A custom Windows service, 'SecureAppGateway', logs its service account password hash in plaintext to a debug file, which could be read by an attacker to create a silver ticket.
XProtect framework on macOS fails to properly detect analysis tools, allowing malware to identify and evade security research environments.

The `FileGuardian` encryption tool contains a vulnerability where it inherits its FDA permissions to any script it executes, allowing an attacker to place a malicious script in its execution path to gain full disk control.

The TeamFlow collaboration suite's API for finding meeting attendees does not enforce proper authorization checks. An authenticated attacker can abuse this endpoint to enumerate all users in the organization's cloud directory.

An elevation of privilege flaw exists in the Excel application loader, where a low-privileged user can write to the `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Office test\Special\Perf` key to achieve SYSTEM-level persistence.
The SystemTune utility on macOS executes maintenance scripts without subjecting them to Gatekeeper checks, creating a pathway for unauthorized code execution.

The Apache HTTP Server on Linux contains a vulnerability in a third-party module for SAML authentication. The module can be tricked into decrypting a malicious payload using a key derived from the `ServerName` directive, targeting a specific host.
A security gap in the `docker-registry` service on Linux allows an unauthenticated attacker to abuse the container registry as a free CDN, consuming its egress bandwidth to host large files.

The systemd init system on Linux distributions contains a flaw in memory protection mechanisms that allows attackers to use /proc/[pid]/pagemap to bypass ASLR and inject malicious payloads into system service processes.

In the Linux 'sshd' server, a custom 'Match' configuration block implementation allows for environmental keying abuse. A command specified in such a block can be decrypted and executed using a key derived from the source IP of the connecting client.

On InfraGate routers, the 'firmware-rollback' feature does not properly sanitize user-supplied rollback points, which can be abused to load a malicious, previously known-vulnerable firmware version for persistence.
The 'Chromium' autofill service on Windows contains a flaw that allows a malicious website to exfiltrate saved session credentials from other origins.

The Xcode Server on macOS uses an internal AMQP broker for build agent communication that does not enforce message size limits. An attacker could send a large message to exhaust broker memory and potentially cause it to deploy malicious code.
A logic bug in the `HostIntrusionPreventionService` allows an attacker to perform DLL hollowing on a legitimate, loaded DLL, effectively hiding malicious code from security scans.
An insecure default configuration in the IaaSInstanceAuth service allows password guessing against the initial instance login if the password is not changed upon first boot.

Unauthorized access level increase in in the Windows Code Signing Service allows a low-privileged process to access and export code-signing private keys from the local machine store, enabling the signing of malicious executables with a trusted certificate.

In the 'AD Certificate Enrollment Snap-in' for Windows, a permissions issue allows a domain user to query the enrollment service for metadata about recently issued certificates, revealing information about new internal services.
Improper validation of script content in the macOS Calendar application enables an attacker to execute arbitrary AppleScript code through a crafted calendar event alarm.

A GraphQL injection vulnerability in the OpenCTI platform on Linux permits unauthenticated attackers to extract detailed relationships and context for a specific observable, such as an adversary's infrastructure.
ESXi logging service's remote syslog feature can be exploited for domain fronting, allowing attackers to tunnel malicious traffic through legitimate logging infrastructure CDNs.
The DataBroker Pro client for Windows transmits payment and API credentials in cleartext, allowing network eavesdroppers to steal credentials and purchase technical data on behalf of the victim.
The package repository for the Linux core component 'Systemd-Logger' was breached, leading to the distribution of a modified, malicious package to end-users.
Simultaneous execution threads in Microsoft Excel for Windows allows a malicious p-code to be executed before the source code sanitization check is completed, facilitating VBA stomping attacks.

An integer overflow in the proprietary FlashFS driver of JunoSwitch network devices can be exploited to achieve remote code execution by forcing the device to perform a direct volume read operation on a corrupted file system structure.
ViperShield AV's real-time scanner fails to inspect files loaded by rundll32.exe, allowing a malicious DLL disguised as a legitimate component to be executed without detection.
In 'EnterpriseApp Manager', the service 'eams.exe' is installed with weak file permissions, permitting a standard user to replace the executable and achieve persistent SYSTEM-level access.
A memory corruption vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook when processing maliciously crafted PST files could allow an attacker to execute code and exfiltrate the user's mailbox.
Improper access control in the `WindowsUpdateAgent` permits a local user to write to the process's virtual address space, allowing for the injection of a malicious DLL to gain elevated privileges.
An out-of-bounds read in the RDP graphics pipeline on Windows can lead to the disclosure of kernel memory contents, potentially aiding in further exploitation.

Logical errors within the Group Policy processing engine allows a malicious GPO linked to an OU with 'Block Inheritance' enabled to override higher-level security policies, effectively neutralizing critical domain protections.
A critical weakness within the GitHub Action 'aws-lambda-deploy' allows an attacker to manipulate the `function_code` input, causing the deployment of a malicious function from an untrusted source.

A permissions weakness in the `term-logd` service on Linux allows an unprivileged user to modify the service's configuration file to disable the logging of commands that start with a space by setting `HISTCONTROL=ignorespace` globally.
In the StratusNet fabric OS, the image verification module can be bypassed if a TFTP server presents an image with a null byte in its filename, preventing the integrity check from running correctly.
Infrastructure Automation Tool on Linux allows unauthorized deployment execution through its REST API due to missing authentication tokens, enabling lateral movement across the infrastructure.

Improper validation of file metadata during upload to SharePoint allows an attacker to inject a malicious 'Server Relative URL' property. When another user downloads the file, the request is misdirected, potentially leaking the contents of a different, sensitive file.
A type confusion vulnerability in the WMI repository parser allows attackers to corrupt system memory through crafted MOF file compilation.
A logic flaw in the `ssh-mgrd` daemon on Linux allows a local user to read other users' SSH private keys from `/var/tmp` where they are temporarily stored with weak permissions.
PowerPoint's ppa add-in format has insufficient validation mechanisms, permitting malicious add-ins to persist and execute automatically.
A heap-based overflow condition in the Windows network redirector driver, netredir.sys, could be exploited to execute kernel-level code that forcibly removes all active SMB sessions.

The 'CatalystLink' SaaS CRM application does not enforce authorization checks on its REST API endpoint for fetching contact details, enabling an attacker to iterate through customer IDs and harvest personal information.
Windows Connection Manager Profile Installer does not properly restrict the execution of PowerShell commands embedded within an INF file, enabling command and script execution.
A cross-site scripting (XSS)-like vulnerability exists within the HTML Help renderer, where a malicious .chm file can script other help windows to perform unauthorized actions.

A bug located in the Windows 'netsh' command's trace context allows a low-privilege user to capture network packets on an interface, potentially revealing unencrypted traffic intended for analysis by a NIDS.

A bug in the 'Docker-Registry-CDN' integration allows for unauthenticated listing of private repository tags through a crafted API call, revealing information about internal application components and versions.
A permissions validation bypass in the ESXi storage-mgmt-agent enables a low-privileged user to change the permissions of critical system log files on a datastore, enabling log tampering.
An authentication bypass flaw in the `kvmd-linux` daemon allows an unauthenticated attacker to gain full administrative access to the KVM device through its web interface.
The GnuTLS helper library on Linux contains a race condition when updating the system trust store, which can be exploited to swap in a malicious certificate before the validation process completes.
A cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in a cloud-based document editor allows a spearphishing attachment to steal session cookies when opened.
An access control bypass in the Windows-based enterprise key management service, VaultKey Manager, permits low-privilege domain users to request the export of high-value code signing certificates.
Juniper JunOS web interface fails to validate user permissions when creating local accounts, leading to unauthorized admin account creation.

The Windows Print Spooler service fails to properly sanitize a specially crafted job request, allowing an attacker to trigger a logic flaw that leaks a process handle, which can be used for token theft and impersonation.

The ADPowerTool Pro PowerShell module for Windows fails to validate user permissions before executing the `Set-ADUser` cmdlet with the `-AllowReversiblePasswordEncryption` parameter, enabling unauthorized modification.
The `AuthConnect` Identity Provider's SAML assertion endpoint is susceptible to XML signature wrapping, allowing an attacker to forge assertions and authenticate as any user in the federated domain.

The OpenSSH server on Linux, when compiled with specific SFTP logging patches, contains a bug that allows a user to exfiltrate data by writing files to a directory that is a symbolic link pointing to a mounted USB volume.

Improper neutralization of special elements in Juniper Junos OS allows an authenticated, low-privilege user to execute arbitrary commands as root, enabling the complete deletion of all firewall filter rules via the CLI.

AWS GuardDuty's threat detection service has a configuration blind spot where it fails to auto-enable in newly added AWS regions, leaving them vulnerable to undetected malicious activity such as cryptocurrency mining.

The auditd subsystem on certain Linux distributions fails to properly log unlink() or truncate() syscalls on files named .bash_history or .zsh_history, allowing adversaries to clear command history without creating a forensic trail.
A lack of proper input validation in the macOS DirectoryServices framework allows a sandboxed application to issue queries that enumerate domain users without requiring explicit entitlements.
An insecure API in the macOS `SystemConfiguration` framework reveals the system's time zone identifier to any calling process.
Safari WebKit Cookie Store on macOS fails to properly validate cookie integrity, allowing attackers to inject forged cookies and hijack sessions.

The 'KubeControl Center' macOS application fails to sanitize user-supplied arguments when invoking the `kubectl` CLI, enabling a malicious script to execute unauthorized commands within the Kubernetes cluster.

A race condition exists in the Windows Logon process when it loads DLLs specified in the AppInit_DLLs registry value. An attacker can exploit this to swap a legitimate DLL for a malicious one after the path is validated but before it is loaded.
Memory corruption triggered by the Windows Kernel's win32k.sys driver enables local attackers to execute code in kernel mode and gain SYSTEM privileges.
The WinRM service on Windows fails to adequately validate session identifiers, enabling an attacker to replay a session token and gain control of an existing remote PowerShell session.

The Active Directory replication service on Windows Server has an insufficient access control flaw that permits attackers to inject authentication bypass patches into the domain controller's security subsystem.

The 'SecureVault' application on Linux fails to validate its environment variables when launched by systemd. An adversary can inject a malicious library path via `systemctl start` to hijack execution flow.

A programmatic error in the internal package manager for DevUtils on macOS allows a malicious package source to supply a manifest that causes the download and execution of unauthorized tools, effectively granting new capabilities.
A memory corruption vulnerability in Microsoft Edge's scripting engine allows remote code execution when a user visits a specially crafted website on Windows.

Unexpected behavior in the replication process for Group Policy on Windows allows an attacker to intercept and modify a GPO before it is applied to all domain controllers, leading to inconsistent and malicious policy enforcement.
A heap-based overflow condition in the 'CloudSyncer' service's configuration parser permits a local user to corrupt the service's ImagePath in the registry, redirecting it to a malicious executable.
A security gap in PowerPoint's 'LiveData' connection feature allows an attacker to exfiltrate sensitive financial data from a connected internal source when a presentation is opened.
An issue in the Arista EOS telemetry agent allows for the configuration of a symmetric encryption key for data export, which can be set to a weak, predictable value to hide C2 beacons.
The 'TaskFlow' SaaS project management tool has a flaw in its API endpoint that allows an attacker to execute arbitrary read-only SQL queries against its PostgreSQL backend.
The Linux kernel module loader lacks proper signature verification for hardware-specific modules, allowing attackers to load malicious modules through specially crafted hardware devices.
A security gap in macOS Gatekeeper's code signing validation allows crafted applications to bypass signature checks through manipulation of quarantine attributes.
A spoofing vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook for Windows allows attackers to display misleading sender information in email headers, facilitating spearphishing attacks via third-party services.

In Microsoft Outlook for Windows, an out-of-bounds write vulnerability can be triggered by a malformed calendar invite, potentially allowing an attacker to execute code that clears the user's mailbox synchronization logs.
The Windows InputMethodManager (IMM) fails to validate the caller's permissions when handling certain IOCTLs, allowing a low-privilege process to read the default system UI language identifier.

The CloudInitiate tool on Linux fails to properly sanitize environment variables in its generated initialization scripts, potentially leading to cloud service credentials being written to files in a public repository.
An algorithm implementation error in the ESXi vmsyslogd daemon allows a malicious VM with administrative privileges to fill the log partition with an oversized log entry, causing the service to stop.

Simultaneous execution threads in the WindowsUpdateHelper service during profile load can be exploited to write an arbitrary value to the UserInitMprLogonScript registry key before user logon completes.
An input validation vulnerability in the `systemd-boot` loader permits arbitrary code execution through malicious kernel command-line arguments before the Linux kernel is loaded.

The custom Chromium build, CorpBrowser, for Windows uses a static, hardcoded key for encrypting a subset of application-specific passwords, making them trivially recoverable from its 'Local Storage' directory.
Google Cloud Functions deployment vulnerability enables malicious code execution with service account permissions to delete compute instances.

Vertical privilege escalation in in the Microsoft Exchange Server's management API could permit a low-privileged user to create organization-wide transport rules, forwarding all email matching specific keywords to an external domain.
A security gap in the vCenter Server Appliance's networking stack allows an attacker to poison its internal DNS cache with fast flux entries, potentially affecting all managed ESXi hosts.
DBAdmin Suite for Windows stores database credentials in plaintext in the `HKLM\Software\DBAdmin\Connections` registry key, allowing any authenticated user to view them.
The `PrintUtil.dll` library, when used by management software, incorrectly calls `PubPrn.vbs` with parameters derived from untrusted network data, leading to a proxy execution vulnerability.
Improper access control in the `SQL Server Remote Configurator` service, which uses WinRM, allows a standard user to modify database configurations.

The `netdata_exporter` tool on Linux is susceptible to an anti-debugging bypass. Its timing-based check, which compares execution speed to detect analysis environments, can be normalized to defeat the protection.

A cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Microsoft Teams desktop client could be abused to access the local chat history cache and delete specific conversation logs, removing evidence of phishing or data exfiltration.
A vulnerability in the Linux PAM authentication module allows bypass of account creation restrictions, enabling local privilege escalation.

A coding defect present in containerd's content-addressable storage layer allows an attacker to alter an image's configuration after it has been pulled, leading to persistent execution of malicious code.

The Unbound DNS resolver on Linux can be manipulated into leaking information about private domains through crafted queries that elicit specific error messages, revealing the existence of internal hostnames.
The Kubernetes API server's certificate validation contains a flaw enabling certificate injection, allowing attackers to create fake service certificates for cluster compromise.
A popular base image for Python applications on Docker Hub, 'pythin-base', was found to contain a cryptominer injected into the site-packages directory, executing on container start.

Information leakage flaws in in the macOS Security Framework allows any application to query the list of installed system extensions, bypassing privacy controls and enabling targeted software discovery.
The Credential Manager service does not properly sanitize input passed to rundll32.exe, leading to a command injection vulnerability that can be exploited to load arbitrary libraries.
The security architecture of the macOS version of `Visual Studio Code` allows a malicious VB.NET extension to execute terminal commands without user interaction.
Privilege escalation in LogMeIn macOS client allows local attackers to gain root privileges through insecure helper tool communication.

An information disclosure bug in the `container-guardian` tool for Linux allows an attacker to read the configuration of other containers, including the services they are set to run within the container.
An attacker who can connect to the com.mediaplayer.transcoder.xpc service can manipulate its file processing parameters to execute arbitrary libraries, leading to local privilege escalation.

Improper handling of data in the macOS sudoers implementation allows a specific configuration to bypass the 'tty_tickets' option, permitting a user to run a sudo command that clears the parent shell's history file without re-authenticating.

The macOS Keychain Access utility contains a flaw where a malicious application can trigger a fake certificate error dialog, instructing the user to copy and paste a malicious command to 'reset the keychain'.
The 'DevOps Runner' agent fails to validate the integrity of DLLs loaded via the `AppInit_DLLs` registry mechanism, making it susceptible to DLL hijacking and privilege escalation attacks.
A TOCTOU vulnerability in the cloud sync component of Collaborate365 allows an attacker to replace a valid, MFA-verified session token with a non-verified one during the authentication handshake.
Command injection in LinuxProcessScanner utility enables attackers to execute arbitrary ps commands with elevated privileges, gaining comprehensive visibility into all system processes.
The macOS dscl utility contains a flaw that allows authenticated users to add their accounts to the admin group by exploiting a race condition in directory updates.

A coding defect present in the Windows Update Orchestrator Service allows a specially crafted DLL to set an undocumented registry key, causing the service to ignore SERVICE_CONTROL_STOP signals and prevent its termination.

A memory corruption flaw in the Windows WinINet API permits a threat actor via network access to perform remote code execution when a user visits a specially crafted website, which could be used to install a local proxy for an adversary-in-the-middle attack.
An authentication bypass in the PulsarMQ message broker on Linux permits unauthorized command execution, which could be leveraged by adversaries to add the server to a leased botnet infrastructure.

Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) flaws in the CrowdStrike Falcon Power Policy Module on Windows could allow an attacker to tamper with power policy enforcement, potentially preventing an infected host from shutting down.
OpenSSL on Linux systems contains a vulnerability in certificate chain validation that fails to properly check for revoked intermediate certificates, allowing use of compromised credentials.

An input validation vulnerability in a third-party `Nginx` module for dynamic certificate loading facilitates remote exploitation to specify a path to a malicious root certificate, which is then loaded into the worker process's trust store.

The 'SecureView Endpoint Agent' for Windows has a SQL injection vulnerability in its web console, allowing an attacker to dump the inventory table which contains details of all local drives on managed endpoints.

The Webex Meeting Application fails to restrict access to its COM registration, enabling an attacker to replace a legitimate component with a malicious DLL to maintain persistence across application restarts.
Improper input validation in the sc.exe utility enables privilege escalation through specially crafted service commands that bypass security checks and execute malicious binaries.

The NotificationCenter service on macOS fails to validate the DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES environment variable, which could be exploited to display deceptive notifications for phishing attacks by injecting a malicious library.
The 'User Profile Caching Service' on Windows incorrectly applies ACLs to its cache files, allowing any authenticated user to read files that contain domain group SIDs and names.
A heap-based buffer overflow in the Intel HD Graphics Control Panel service can be leveraged to overwrite TLS callback pointers, resulting in arbitrary code execution with SYSTEM rights.

An implementation error in the Windows Component Object Model (COM) interaction with `PubPrn.vbs` allows for an argument injection, enabling the `script:` moniker to be processed on a system where it should be blocked.
A local privilege escalation vulnerability in the AetherSwitch OS `cfg-mgrd` daemon allows a standard user to read the `/etc/config.db` file, which contains all system settings.
A heap-based buffer overflow in the VMFS driver for ESXi can be triggered by a specially crafted network packet, leading to code execution and the encryption of all VMs stored on the datastore.
