An improper permission check in the 'EnterpriseBackup' service on Windows could be exploited to force the service to perform a raw volume copy of the C: drive, allowing for the theft of the SAM and NTDS.dit files.
The Windows WinRM-Listener service has an unbounded resource allocation issue that enables a denial of service through a flood of persistent connections, exhausting all available listener slots.

An implementation error in the macOS FileManager's background sync service allows for the installation of unauthorized socket filters. An attacker could place a filter that waits for a file transfer protocol command to be observed on the network, at which point it could execute malicious code.
An exploitable bug in the macOS 'profiles' command-line tool allows a non-admin user to install a configuration profile that includes a trusted root certificate, bypassing GUI authorization checks.
A memory corruption issue in the Windows 'dwm.exe' process can be exploited to read the clipboard data of other users on the same terminal server.
The TimeMachineBackup Service's Launch Daemon on macOS points to an executable within an application that is vulnerable to privilege escalation, allowing for binary replacement.
The macOS 'Automator Service' can be abused to execute commands by processing a malicious file dropped into a monitored Dropbox folder, with results being exfiltrated to a Pastebin URL.
Aruba Central's configuration management API has an authorization bypass permitting attackers to push malicious configuration changes to all connected access points and switches.
An authentication bypass in the ESXi DCUI (Direct Console User Interface) could allow an attacker with physical access to drop to a shell and execute `esxcli` commands without providing credentials.
A SQL injection vulnerability in the 'Roundcube-Plugin' for Linux webmail allows an attacker to execute database queries and extract all user email addresses from the backend.

The Windows Azure File Sync service does not perform sufficient integrity checks on synchronized file chunks, enabling a Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacker to inject malicious content into a synced file.
The JSON-RPC API on Juniper devices running Junos OS fails to properly enforce role-based access control for firewall rule modifications, permitting any authenticated user to add permissive rules.

The Cron Job Scheduler Plus daemon on Linux can be crashed by an application exhaustion flood that submits thousands of jobs with extremely complex scheduling rules, exhausting CPU during the scheduling calculation.
The Splunk Universal Forwarder's script execution monitor can be circumvented by proxying malicious commands through the verclsid.exe binary.
The BackupNow Client software improperly handles backup job names, allowing for command injection that can be used to launch mavinject.exe and perform DLL injection into a privileged service.
The CUPS printing system on Linux is vulnerable to VDSO hijacking due to an improper bounds check in its IPP handling, which allows for memory corruption and GOT overwrites.

The AWS Route 53 management API client library suffers from a credential leakage vulnerability, which could expose API keys and allow an attacker to compromise and hijack DNS records for hosted zones.

The Windows Active Directory Replication service can be forced into a state where it temporarily stores password changes in a reversible format, which can be captured by an attacker with network access.
A vulnerability in the docker-container-scanner for Linux allows a packed malware sample to escape detection, as its unpacking module fails to execute correctly within the container sandbox.
Office's VSTO add-in loader fails to verify publisher certificates, enabling malicious VSTO add-ins to maintain persistence.

Memory corruption triggered by the Windows service 'WinInetAPI.dll' empowers a distant attacker to overwrite the User-Agent string in HTTP requests, enabling the spoofing of browser identity for evasion.

An exploitable bug in the Hyper-V Virtual Machine Management Service (VMMS) allows a privileged guest to send crafted requests that trigger a host-side process to dynamically resolve and execute unvetted API functions, leading to potential host escape.
The Windows Remote Desktop Gateway service fails to inspect traffic that is doubly encoded (e.g., URL-encoded within a Base64 string), allowing attackers to pass malicious payloads to internal hosts.
A race condition in Windows Storage Spaces Direct permits local attackers to corrupt metadata and trigger cascading disk wipe operations across clustered storage pools.

Juniper JunOS devices are susceptible to a firmware corruption vulnerability where a specially crafted network packet can trigger a buffer overflow in the bootloader, rendering the device unable to load its OS.
The macOS LaunchServices Framework fails to properly handle escape sequences in sudoers rules, potentially allowing a user to bypass command restrictions with a crafted command name.
The `iCloudSync Service` on macOS writes debug logs to a world-readable location, exposing user account information and filenames synced with the cloud.

The 'macOS System Configuration' framework permits a sandboxed application to read the full set of network preferences, including internal DNS search domains and proxy configurations, facilitating network mapping.
A flaw in the Windows Print Spooler service facilitates remote exploitation to query the service and obtain the internal IP address of the print server and connected clients.
A vulnerability in the Jenkins Docker plugin allows manipulation of image build processes, enabling injection of malicious code.
The AirPort wireless driver in macOS fails to properly manage memory when processing a flood of deauthentication frames, leading to a kernel panic and loss of network connectivity.

A vulnerability in the `systemd-journald` service on Linux could be leveraged to forward a crafted log entry containing a path to a malicious file, causing the service to copy and relocate the file to the `/var/log/journal` directory.

Unexpected behavior in the `SecureBrowse Agent` for Windows allows a low-privilege user to query its local API and retrieve a complete list of bookmarks and browsing history from the default Chrome profile without authentication.
Improper permissions in CryptoMiner Controller service on Linux could allow unauthorized users to reconfigure mining payouts to attacker-controlled wallets.
A third-party kernel module (`acme_tpm.ko`) on Linux exposes a `/proc` entry that allows reading the memory of the `sssd` process, potentially leaking cached domain credential hashes.
A race condition in the macOS `DictationService` allows a local attacker to replace the audio data file after it is written but before it is sent to Apple, capturing the user's dictations.

Improper locking mechanisms in the 'Rclone' cloud synchronization utility (v1.55.0) during a 'lsd' (list directories) operation against an Azure Blob container can briefly expose object names that should be filtered out by ACLs.
An insufficient permission check in the Slack desktop application's update module on Windows allows for a TxF-based process injection attack.

System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM) client on Windows does not validate the source of certain task sequences, which can be hijacked to execute `net user /add /domain` with system-level context.

Vertical privilege escalation in in the backup service 'AcmeBackup' allows a low-privileged user to add arbitrary file paths to the exclusion list. This can be exploited to perform selective exclusion, preventing security tools from scanning malicious payloads.
An authentication bypass in SecureSync for Windows allows an attacker to configure the client to sync a user's 'credentials' folder to a public, anonymous repository.
A use-after-free error in the OpenSSH daemon (sshd) could permit a remote attacker to run unauthorized code by sending a specially crafted network packet.
Improper locking mechanisms in the BlueCat-Address-Manager service permits the creation of shadow subdomains that are not logged or easily detected, allowing for persistent malicious activity.

A memory corruption issue in LogViewer for Windows can be leveraged for proxy execution. An attacker can provide a specially crafted .NET assembly that, when processed by the application's faulty Regsvcs.exe call, leads to arbitrary code execution.

The CleanUp Mac maintenance tool contains a bug where it incorrectly resets TCC permissions for applications, inadvertently granting Full Disk Access to a malicious binary placed in a temporary directory.

The Windows Performance Counter service (PerfProc) contains a buffer overflow that allows code execution. An attacker could use this to modify performance counter data, encoding stolen system information into the counter values that are sent to a remote monitoring tool acting as a C2 server.

Improper input validation in the EnterprisePolicyAgent Windows service permits an attacker to inject arbitrary commands into the 'StubPath' value of an Active Setup component, leading to code execution with user privileges at logon.

Concurrency issues within the Windows SMB client can be exploited to force a fallback to an unencrypted SMBv1 connection for file copy operations, allowing data to be intercepted during transit to a non-standard server.

Logical errors within HashiCorp Terraform's AWS provider allows it to bypass account-level governance controls, enabling the creation of EC2 instances in geographically unused regions that are explicitly denied in the AWS Organizations policy.

An algorithm implementation error in the macOS XProtect Remediator service allows it to execute unsigned secondary remediation scripts. An attacker can provide a malicious script that, when run, establishes a connection to a second-stage command and control server, bypassing initial security checks.

Information disclosure in Microsoft Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) allows unauthenticated users to query the certificate enrollment web service and extract certificate metadata including organization names and locations.

The Falco runtime security engine in a container environment is susceptible to an input validation flaw, allowing a container with API access to disable specific security rules or halt logging entirely.
Google Workspace's third-party application trust model contains insufficient verification of app publisher identity, allowing malicious apps to appear as trusted entities and access user data.
Weak encryption key generation in the Heimdal Kerberos implementation on Linux allows attackers to forge valid service tickets.
macOS CoreFoundation framework contains a flaw that permits applications to bypass security controls and exfiltrate user data over unencrypted DNS queries by encoding information in subdomains.
The osint-recon-ng framework on Linux fails to sanitize user-supplied domain names before passing them to the underlying WHOIS client, enabling command injection.

Unintended data exposure in in Microsoft Edge's search engine integration permits attackers to access search suggestions and autocomplete data, potentially revealing user interests and internal system information.

Google Cloud Search API information disclosure vulnerability allows attackers to use search queries to access indexed content and metadata from other users' drives, aiding in intelligence gathering operations.

A programmatic error in the Active Directory replication mechanism on Windows Domain Controllers could be exploited to create a golden ticket, allowing for persistent compromise of the entire Windows identity infrastructure.
The Docker Registry client on Linux does not validate image layer hashes during pull operations from insecure registries, which could be leveraged for content injection of malicious layers.

The 'LogAnalyzer' tool for Windows improperly processes XSL stylesheets, allowing for the execution of embedded JScript. An attacker with the ability to influence log data or the XSL template can achieve privilege escalation.
The build process for the HyperFlexGraphics.sys driver was compromised, resulting in a malicious version being distributed from the official developer's website for Windows.

The `Keychain Access` utility on macOS contains a vulnerability where the 'Show password' checkbox for web form passwords can be triggered via AppleScript without a user prompt, exposing saved credentials to a malicious script.
A buffer overflow in the nslcd daemon on Linux can be leveraged to achieve code execution as the 'nslcd' user, which can then be used to run 'ldapsearch' queries to dump all domain accounts.

A vulnerability in the SQL Server Management Studio's 'Backup to Network Share' feature allows the process to disconnect from the share post-backup without logging the disconnection to the Windows Application log.

A use-after-free vulnerability in a third-party IIS HTTP server module allows an attacker to execute code within the context of the w3wp.exe worker process, enabling the theft of its application pool identity token for impersonation.
A privilege escalation flaw in the VesselRuntime API enables a low-privilege container to query and list all container images on the system.
The VMFS-Plus datastore management module for ESXi contains a hardcoded root-equivalent account `vmfs_check` used for maintenance, which can be abused for privilege escalation.

In 'VisualForge Studio', the custom tool integration feature does not sandbox the execution of MSBuild, allowing a malicious project file to access sensitive system resources on the Windows development machine.
The Skype for Business client on Windows stores conversation history in a plaintext local file that is accessible to other local users, leading to potential credential exposure.

The ESXi 'sfcb-CIMOM' service has a buffer overflow in its handling of HTTP requests. A remote attacker can exploit this to corrupt the web-based CIM browser's UI files, causing the management interface to display defaced information.
A custom VIB (vSphere Installation Bundle) installation module on ESXi contains a post-install script that can be manipulated to write arbitrary files to the host's boot bank.
GitHub Actions cache can be abused to stage malicious dependencies that will be restored in workflow runs across different repositories.
The Windows Registry API improperly handles screensaver settings, enabling attackers to bypass ScreenSaverIsSecure restrictions and maintain persistence.
The Zendesk SaaS platform's API endpoint for agent account creation lacks proper authentication checks, allowing unauthenticated users to create administrative accounts.

A buffer overflow in the `hypervisor_io.ko` kernel module's interaction with udev allows for the creation of a rule that runs an arbitrary command with elevated privileges when a hypervisor-specific device is added.

A hardcoded RSA private key in the firmware of a network security appliance allows any attacker with knowledge of the key to decrypt C2 traffic, completely compromising the confidentiality of the asymmetric encryption.
The Windows Error Reporting service (werfault.exe) contains a flaw where crash dump processes can be spawned with spoofed parent PIDs, allowing malware to masquerade as legitimate error reporting.

The `System Diagnostics Reporter` on macOS uses a hardcoded encryption key when leveraging `bzip2` to compress report bundles, enabling an attacker with local access to decrypt archived diagnostic data containing sensitive user information.
A logic error within the Docker daemon's API endpoint allows a low-privileged container to escape its confinement and gain root access on the host system.

An information disclosure flaw in the AWS-Helper-Tool SDK allows for the enumeration of all S3 buckets in the account, even if the tool's configured credentials lack explicit `s3:ListAllMyBuckets` permission.

An AWS S3 bucket policy misconfiguration on a cloud storage bucket allows public 'ListBucket' access. This enables search engines to index the full list of object keys within the bucket, potentially revealing sensitive file names.
The SecureLoginAgent on macOS contains a vulnerability where its configuration can be altered to load a malicious Launch Daemon using launchctl during the next login.

The 'SecureMail for Office 365' add-in fails to sanitize email thread content when generating a chat summary, allowing a malicious script injected into a forwarded email to scrape authentication tokens from the chat pane.

The Juniper Pulse Secure client installer on Windows creates a PowerShell profile with overly permissive write access, which can be leveraged by an attacker to gain persistence each time a user launches PowerShell.
The Apple Unified Logging system on macOS does not enforce strict size limits on log data, allowing a malicious process to abuse a persistent log file as a local data staging repository.

Logical errors within the PAN-OS threat prevention engine on Palo Alto Networks firewalls allows an attacker to craft a packet that temporarily disables a specific antivirus signature, creating a window for malicious traffic to pass through.
An out-of-bounds write in the NTLM helper library loaded by lsass.exe can be triggered by a network request, allowing a remote attacker to achieve persistence on the target system.
In macOS, the ZipTool-Pro application can be abused for privilege escalation as it prompts the user for credentials via the insecure AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges API.

In the SalesForce Pro CRM application, a broken access control vulnerability allows a regular user to modify their own profile via a direct API call, escalating their privileges to a system administrator role.
Unexpected behavior in the Atlassian Jira Service Management backend allows an attacker with guest privileges to retrieve a full list of all users in the organization via a hidden REST endpoint.

The `PerfDataHelper.exe` service on Windows exposes an unauthenticated RPC method that returns the high-resolution performance counter, revealing if the system clock is being manipulated by a sandbox.

The CorpNet Manager service on Windows fails to properly validate input when applying custom network profiles. This allows an attacker to inject a path to a malicious DLL into the Netsh helper registry path, leading to arbitrary code execution upon invocation of netsh.exe.
Logical errors within the macOS EndpointSecurityFramework allows a malicious application to send a crafted message to its security daemon, causing it to crash and disable endpoint protection.
Information leakage flaws in in the Windows Credential Manager service could allow a low-privilege process to enumerate and read credentials stored for other local accounts.
The 'EnterpriseAuth Client' service contains a path interception vulnerability. Its executable path, `C:\EnterpriseAuth Client\auth.exe`, is not quoted, making it susceptible to hijacking.
The `vSphere-Storage-Adapter-VIB` for a specific SAN vendor improperly validates its update package, allowing an attacker to create a malicious VIB that deploys a persistent rootkit on the ESXi host.

Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) flaws in a container runtime's image pull process allows for the creation of a malicious container image with the name 'k8s.gcr.io/pause' which could be scheduled instead of the legitimate sandbox image.

Improper neutralization of special elements in the `CloudLaunch` web interface for AWS allows an attacker to inject a malicious startup script into an AMI's user-data field, which is then executed by the instance operating system when launched by a victim.

A use-after-free flaw in the CloudSync Helper service for macOS can be triggered by a specially crafted `com.cloudsync.token` extended attribute, leading to the disclosure of sensitive authentication tokens.
A logic flaw in the 'UpdateDaemon' service for Windows allows an attacker to upload a maliciously signed update package, which is then distributed to all clients.
The SysWatch Agent for Windows insecurely stores its central server's administrative credentials in `HKLM\Software\SysWatch\Server`, enabling a local attacker to pivot laterally.

Improper input validation in the Windows Remote Management (WinRM) service allows for command injection. An attacker can send SOAP requests where the payload is obfuscated using a non-standard hex encoding, bypassing security filters.
Memory corruption triggered by the SecCertificate parsing routine in Security.framework on macOS allows an attacker to execute code containing a large block of junk instructions before the payload.
The NebulaStack 'ResourceGuard' automation script, designed to decommission unused resources, skips regions marked as 'archival', allowing them to be used for persistent resource hijacking.

The Hyper-V Virtual Switch Manager on Windows does not adequately rate-limit inbound network traffic to a guest VM, allowing an attacker on the same host to flood the VM's network interface and cause a denial of service.

Improper validation of the `TrustDirection` attribute in Active Directory's trust objects allows for the creation of a one-way trust that can be abused to escalate privileges from a less trusted domain.
Improper signature validation in the CoreAuthUI Agent allows an attacker to load a malicious kernel extension (kext) that persists across reboots and executes with kernel-level privileges.
Improper access control in the ManageEngine Remote Access Plus agent allows a standard user to invoke its RDP module and hijack a higher-privileged session.
Salesforce Identity platform has a vulnerability in its permission set assignment mechanism that permits unauthorized elevation to system administrator roles.

The application whitelisting feature in Kaseya VSA does not monitor for runtime API resolution, permitting an approved application to load a malicious component that resolves its functions dynamically via GetProcAddress.
The 'CodeEditor Pro' application's plugin system allows a plugin to execute code that modifies the permissions of the application's main executable, facilitating DLL hijacking.
The `MailMate` email client on Linux improperly renders RTF content, which can be exploited to hijack the execution flow if a user is convinced to open a maliciously crafted email.
A workflow defect in the macOS SecurityFramework's CRL checking mechanism permits the calculation of a C2 port based on specific octets from a DNS response, bypassing network segmentation.
The Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) contains a flaw that allows a malicious Windows application to execute arbitrary bash commands within a WSL distribution.

An Apple Device Management Bridge component on macOS fails to correctly handle padding with its 3DES encryption, enabling an attacker to decrypt management commands and potentially take control of devices.
A memory corruption vulnerability in the macOS QuickTime Player, triggered by a maliciously crafted movie file, could be exploited to install a botnet payload.

In the Windows 'EdgeExtension' 'QuickNotes', a vulnerability allows an attacker to use a public note-taking service as a dead drop resolver. The extension parses a note's content to find a sync server URL, which can be manipulated to point to a C2 server.

An out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the macOS System Preferences pane for the firewall allows a local user to corrupt the memory of the 'socketfilterfw' process, causing it to crash and disabling the firewall upon restart.
The CyberRiskAnalyzer Service on Windows contains a backdoor account that is inadvertently left enabled in production builds, granting full access to all stored purchased data.
Safari's WebKit on macOS contains an integer overflow in canvas element handling exploitable through malicious websites.
The 'mailscanner' daemon on Linux does not properly validate the structure of DNS responses, enabling an attacker to embed values used to calculate a dynamic C2 port for outbound traffic.
A critical weakness within the Windows Kernel driver for virtualization allows packed malicious code to execute with kernel privileges by bypassing integrity checks on packed binaries.

A memory corruption vulnerability in the SSL inspection driver of CipherPoint appliances could be exploited by a remote attacker to crash the crypto hardware service. The service fails to restart, resulting in a fallback to a vulnerable software-based encryption library.

A programmatic error in the Windows 'AD-QueryService' allows a low-privileged user to trigger a domain-wide user enumeration by sending a specially crafted RPC call, bypassing standard access controls.

An authentication bypass in the XMPP server component of the Openfire collaboration suite for Linux permits a remote attacker to create arbitrary chat rooms, which can then be abused for covert command and control communications.
The 'OfficeFlow Pro' plugin for Excel fails to redact sensitive information when exporting a chat log summary to a CSV file, resulting in credentials being saved in plaintext.
Unexpected behavior in Windows Update Client allows attackers to impersonate Microsoft's update protocol, disguising C2 traffic as legitimate Windows update requests.
IDOR vulnerabilities present in in the MegaBackup Client enables an attacker with local access to duplicate the token of the backup service process, which often runs with SYSTEM privileges.
Authorization bypass via ID manipulation in (IDOR) in the WinNav Pro extension update service on Windows allows an attacker to force-install a malicious extension from a remote server.
The AuthDaemonX for Linux does not correctly sanitize GSSAPI credentials, leading to a situation where Kerberos service tickets are written to a temporary file with weak permissions.
The Azure Network Watcher API has a flaw where a user with 'Reader' permissions can call a diagnostic endpoint that returns the full network topology diagram, including unlisted subnets.
The LogInsight Collector, deployed for IaaS monitoring, has an undocumented API function that can be invoked to create a snapshot of the underlying host's boot volume.
An insecure method implementation in a third-party COM object allows any application to call it and perform PE injection into the lsass.exe process, facilitating credential dumping.
FastCache-Server 的安装脚本存在权限提升漏洞，允许非 root 用户通过操作临时文件来执行 systemctl daemon-reload 并加载恶意服务单元。
Flawed business logic in the Windows VPN Client management interface permits authenticated users to add their accounts to the VPN-Access security group, bypassing approval workflows.
A null pointer dereference in the Windows Print Spooler service can be triggered to cause a system crash, and potentially exploited for code execution.

Logical errors within the 'Measured Boot' process of a certain UEFI implementation allows a bootloader to tamper with the PCRs (Platform Configuration Registers) in a predictable way. An attacker can search threat vendor data for systems reporting these altered PCR values to find out if their bootkit has been detected and analyzed.

The Windows component responsible for handling `.appref-ms` shortcuts contains a use-after-free vulnerability that can be triggered by a specially crafted shortcut file, leading to remote code execution.

The macOS CoreAnalytics framework improperly sanitizes diagnostic reports before transmitting them, allowing an attacker on the same network to intercept details about the host's OS version, architecture, and locale settings.
A format string vulnerability in the logging component of the bootloader on CoreSwitch network devices can be exploited to execute arbitrary code and modify the device's pre-boot environment.
A programmatic error in a custom Lambda function for AWS, intended for resource tagging, inadvertently has `iam:ListRoles` permissions, allowing its invocation to enumerate all roles in the account.

The Code Signing Verification framework in macOS can be tricked by a binary with a malformed code signature directory, causing the validation to fail open and allowing the unsigned code to execute as if it were trusted.

Unexpected behavior in the 'CorrelateX' SIEM correlation engine on Windows improperly handles wildcard searches, enabling an attacker to discover if their entire malicious domain infrastructure has been identified with a single query.
XFCE's session manager contains insufficient validation of XDG autostart entries, allowing privilege escalation through manipulation of system-wide autostart files in /etc/xdg/autostart.

The setgid `stats-collector` daemon on Linux for the 'analytics' group is vulnerable to an argument injection vulnerability, allowing a local user to execute arbitrary commands with group-level permissions.

The systemd-networkd service on Linux does not correctly drop capabilities when handling a `netdev` configuration file, which can be abused to enable promiscuous mode on an interface without root privileges.

The 'Microsoft Office Click-to-Run' service's virtualization registry handler fails to isolate writes, allowing an attacker to modify HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\AppV to alter application behavior and bypass macro security policies.

Improper handling of data in the session management of IronGate Perimeter Security allows for authentication bypass via session token prediction, granting attackers administrative control over the firewall.

A memory corruption issue in macOS's CoreAudio API allows an attacker to embed malicious code within an M4A audio file. By exploiting the way the audio codec parses steganographic data in silent audio tracks, an attacker can achieve arbitrary code execution.
Azure Pipelines' dependency caching mechanism can be poisoned, allowing a malicious actor to upload a compromised package that executes code during the restore step of a subsequent build.
A use-after-free in the Linux kernel's netfilter subsystem allows local users to gain root privileges by manipulating iptables rules.
VMware ESXi SSH daemon contains authentication bypass vulnerability allowing attackers to execute shutdown commands on the host system.
The LogInsight service contains a flaw in its log parsing script handler that allows for arbitrary code execution when processing specially crafted log files from integrated services.
The `CloudOps` Ansible module for instance management lacks a confirmation step for its 'state: reverted' action, which can be abused in playbooks to silently roll back compromised systems.

Logical errors within Microsoft Teams' integration with the Exchange GAL permits an authenticated user to bypass privacy settings and discover the email addresses of members in teams they are not part of.

The OpenVPN client for Linux contains a logic flaw that permits the configuration of a 'socks-proxy' option, allowing all local traffic to be tunneled through the VPN connection, regardless of intended route.
The Linux UVC (USB Video Class) driver contains an information disclosure bug where a malicious webcam can read uninitialized kernel memory.

A container escape vulnerability in the Apex Runtime for serverless functions could allow a malicious function to break out of its sandbox and access underlying host resources on the IaaS infrastructure.

The macOS CoreArchiver.framework contains a memory corruption vulnerability that can be triggered by a malicious application when creating an encrypted ZIP archive, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution with user privileges.
An unauthenticated endpoint in the K8s-UI-Pro dashboard exposes a full list of all pods within a cluster and their respective internal IP addresses.
Foxmail's local data folder permissions are incorrectly set during installation, allowing any authenticated user to access and copy email databases.

The XProtect security daemon on macOS fails to scan files written to the hidden `.Trashes` folder on removable volumes. Malware can exploit this to store and retrieve command payloads in this location, evading detection while communicating via the media.

The Arista EOS SSL-termination module fails to properly sanitize user-supplied parameters, allowing an administrator to set the TLS cipher suite to one using 56-bit export-grade encryption, effectively weakening the key space.

The `CredentialManager` UI component is susceptible to a module stomping attack, where an adversary can overwrite a legitimately loaded DLL's entry point to execute code of their choice within the context of the user's session.
A heap-based buffer overflow in the Windows Remote Desktop Services termService.dll could allow a remote, unauthenticated attacker to execute code and capture the server's screen.

A publicly accessible Terraform state file in an AWS S3 bucket inadvertently contained the full configuration of managed resources, including exact AMI IDs and module versions, which reveals the software stack in use.

A programmatic error in the 'Network-Map' visualization tool allows any user on the network to request a full topology map without authentication, exposing server names, functions, and their responsible administrators.
Unintended data exposure in exists in the CyberSecureVault browser on Windows where the master password hash is stored in an obfuscated but reversible format in the registry.
An internal defect in the 'DeployBot' automation script for IaaS allows an unauthenticated user to trigger the 'teardown_environment' job, which deletes all associated cloud instances and volumes.

The Istio Mixer API for policy telemetry does not correctly scope access tokens, enabling a compromised service in one namespace to query telemetry and discover service endpoints in all other namespaces.
CMSTP.exe does not correctly validate the path to the INF file, allowing a symbolic link attack to force the binary to read and process a malicious file controlled by a low-privilege user.
A software fault within Windows IIS compression module allows attackers to obfuscate malicious scripts within compressed HTTP responses, evading web application firewalls.
Hardware implants on 'DataFlow' SSD controllers, sold for Windows workstations, allow attackers to exfiltrate data directly from the storage device.

The 'PerfCount Manager' application's helper service uses an unquoted path, `C:\PerfCount Manager\helper.exe`. This configuration error enables a standard user to hijack the execution flow and gain SYSTEM-level access.
A hardcoded, predictable DGA seed exists within the macOS CoreNetworking framework for its backup network services, permitting an attacker to anticipate and intercept system-level C2 traffic.
The Windows Telephony service (tapisrv.dll) fails to properly validate thread handles, enabling thread execution hijacking of telephony application threads.
The 'BackupNow Server' application does not properly validate XSL files used for backup job reporting, allowing an attacker to execute code with SYSTEM privileges.
An exploitable bug in the macOS 'SystemTuner' application allows its companion command-line tool to expose administrator passwords in the persistent shell history.
Flawed business logic in the Apache OpenOffice hyperlink handler on Linux permits the execution of arbitrary system commands when a user interacts with a crafted link.
The Windows Task Scheduler fails to validate screensaver-related scheduled tasks, allowing persistence through malicious scrnsave.scr replacement.
The Linux PAM module for Kerberos (pam_kerberos) fails to properly sanitize log output, potentially leaking user passwords to world-readable log files during authentication failures.
The 'NetLogic Backup Manager' installer creates a startup shortcut with weak permissions, which can be modified by an unprivileged user for privilege escalation and persistence.

Simultaneous execution threads in the `macOS KVM Extension` can be exploited to bypass System Integrity Protection (SIP), potentially installing a malicious kernel-level agent that communicates via remote access hardware.

An internal defect in the TimeMachine Helper service on macOS allows for remote code execution via a maliciously crafted network backup target. This could be used to compromise the system and add it to a botnet.

Reflected or stored XSS flaws in vulnerability exists in the web-hosted ClickOnce deployment page for LogiTrack Supply Chain, which can be used to inject a script that initiates the download and execution of a malicious `.application` file.

A software fault within the Linux kernel's module loading mechanism allows an attacker to load a malicious kernel module that uses the same alias and metadata as a legitimate module, such as 'nvidia', to hide its presence and functionality.

The passwd utility in Linux distributions suffers from a race condition that allows privilege escalation through manipulation of the shadow file, enabling unauthorized modification of other users' password hashes.
The 'LogHound' daemon on Linux fails to properly set permissions on its lock file '/var/run/loghound.lock', enabling a local user to cause a denial of service by creating the file first.

The Windows system component 'WinAdminToolkit' trusts an unauthenticated JSON endpoint on a public web service for its plugin list. An attacker can modify this endpoint to serve as a dead drop resolver, causing the toolkit to download and install a plugin that establishes a C2 channel.

An elevation of privilege vulnerability in the KernelDriverInstaller on Windows is caused by its failure to use a full path for certutil.exe. An attacker can place a malicious executable in the installer's directory to achieve code execution.

The 'BITS' (Background Intelligent Transfer Service) registry key allows for the creation of a 'Performance' subkey by low-privileged users. This can be exploited to load a malicious DLL, leading to privilege escalation.
A vulnerability in Windows Remote Desktop configuration allows modification of RDP settings with elevated privileges without UAC interaction.

In the PostgreSQL-Plus database for Linux, a specific function can be abused by an unprivileged user to change the ownership of log files to the 'postgres' user and set arbitrary permissions, leading to information disclosure.

An elevation of privilege vulnerability in the Windows `NetFilter Network Driver` arises from improper validation of I/O request packets, allowing a malicious user to execute code in kernel mode via the `NtUserSetWindowsHookEx` native API.

A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability on the profile page of PixelPost can be leveraged to steal an administrator's session cookie, leading to full control over any social media account on the platform.

A coding defect present in the configuration handler for AudioBoost Driver allows for the persistent modification of the Winlogon\Userinit registry entry, enabling the execution of arbitrary code upon user authentication.
The Windows Shell Extension Host process is vulnerable to an attack where an actor can modify its KernelCallbackTable to hijack execution flow and bypass security controls.
The 'Safari' browser on macOS exposes the certificate details of the currently visited site via its debugging API, which can be accessed by a malicious extension without user consent.
An insecure deserialization flaw in the DarwinOps Service on macOS allows for arbitrary command execution when processing tasks from the cloud control plane.
The 'WebApp Firewall' WMI provider contains a buffer overflow vulnerability in the 'LogQuery' method, which can be triggered remotely to execute code with NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM privileges.

Unexpected behavior in the macOS iCloudAdmin CLI tool allows it to accept a self-signed certificate for federated authentication, making it vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks that can harvest cloud credentials.

A use-after-free bug in the Adobe Acrobat Reader DC updater service enables an attacker to execute code of their choice with service-level privileges, facilitating the theft of the service's access token.
The Linux LogMaster Analytics Daemon fails to sanitize configuration file inputs, permitting a local attacker to inject commands that create a new, persistent root-level process.

A memory corruption vulnerability in the Sentinel Switch OS CLI can be exploited to patch the running kernel in memory, allowing an adversary to modify the output of diagnostic commands to hide malicious configurations.
A compromised batch of 'TrustChip' TPM modules for Windows allows for the generation of forged attestation certificates, undermining platform trust.

The MailQueueManager service dynamically creates timers but fails to set a `User=` directive in the service file, causing all scheduled tasks to run as root and creating a privilege escalation vector.

An insufficient privilege check in the ClickOnce deployment process for the 'System Maintenance' utility allows a low-privilege user to install and run a malicious application that tampers with system-wide settings.
Inadequate permission checks on the registry key used by the Trend Micro Apex One agent for status reporting allow any user to write a 'Healthy' value, deceiving the management console.

The 'OpenSign Daemon' on Linux contains an improper input validation vulnerability that enables an attacker to specify arbitrary fields, such as a trusted Microsoft Corporation issuer, when creating a self-signed certificate.
An attacker with low privileges can exploit a weakness in the 'com.zoom.video.daemon' to install a new Launch Daemon, as the parent directory permissions are overly permissive.

The `SysMonD` daemon on Linux systems lacks proper permission checks on its IPC socket, enabling any local user to request a dump of all active X11 window titles and properties, facilitating application window discovery.

macOS's CoreGraphics framework fails to properly validate custom font data, which could lead to an application reflectively loading and executing arbitrary code within its own process memory when rendering a malicious font.
An insecure file handling bug in the CloudStorage Sync Client for Windows enables an attacker to place a malicious DLL and invoke mavinject.exe via a crafted sync operation, achieving persistence.
The Windows winlogon.exe process can be compromised via a DLL hijacking vulnerability, enabling an attacker to patch the binary to load a malicious library for persistence.
A coding defect present in the OpenSSH daemon for Linux allows attackers to obfuscate command sequences using multi-layer Base64 encoding in SSH commands.

The 'Docker Registry' API on Linux can be queried without authentication in certain default configurations, allowing attackers to list all image repositories and tags, which reveals the technology stack of the victim's web services.

A flaw in the 'Docker' daemon's logging functionality allows a low-privileged user to read the logs of all containers on a host, including timestamped application events that can signify business activity.
Improper input validation in the Kubernetes dashboard for Windows allows attackers to inject malicious scripts that steal cloud service account tokens.
Predictable resource identification in (IDOR) vulnerability in the AWS IAM management console allows a user with limited permissions to attach existing high-privilege policies to their own role.

A software fault within the Windows Mail client's link preview feature allows for URL obfuscation, where a malicious link can be displayed as a trusted destination, facilitating spearphishing attacks.
The 'WLAN Diagnostics Logger' service on Windows fails to sanitize command output, inadvertently logging the results of 'netsh wlan show profile key=clear' to a world-readable log file.

Improper input validation in the Windows 'Registry Editor' (regedit) allows a specially crafted .reg file to set the `CI` policy flags to an insecure state without requiring administrator approval, disabling code integrity checks.
The Windows 'search-ms' protocol handler has a flaw that grants remote adversaries the ability to initiate a file transfer and save a malicious payload to an arbitrary path on the victim's disk.
Nginx web server on Linux fails to properly decode MIME-encoded multipart requests, allowing encoded malicious content to bypass upload restrictions.
Sensitive information is exposed by in the ESXi HostAgent service allows a low-privileged user to query an internal API and obtain a complete list of all registered virtual machines on the host.
Windows System Configuration utility (msconfig) contains a flaw that allows malicious software to manipulate startup item information displayed during runtime.

A vulnerability in the 'KernelBaseExtension' library allows an attacker to bypass the Secure Boot mitigation that disables AppInit DLLs. By exploiting this flaw, an attacker can re-enable the functionality and load a malicious DLL for persistence.

A memory corruption vulnerability in the macOS 'CoreFoundation' URL parsing library can be triggered by a specially crafted domain name, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution when a user visits a malicious site.

The `Redfish-API` implementation on certain Dell PowerEdge servers is vulnerable to an authentication bypass. An unauthenticated network attacker can directly query the `/redfish/v1/Systems/System.Embedded.1/Firmware` endpoint to gather a complete inventory of the server's firmware versions.
An improper input validation flaw in the Linux udisks2 daemon enables a local attacker to bypass mount options and read arbitrary files on a connected removable medium with root privileges.

The ESXi vSwitch implementation contains a flaw in port group isolation that allows attackers to bridge VM traffic to external networks while evading virtual switch monitoring, hiding C2 infrastructure within VM traffic.
The 'Kerio Connect' mail server on macOS has a default administrative account that can be activated if a specific configuration file is modified, allowing for the creation of new email accounts.

A vulnerability in the Windows 'PowerShell' logging subsystem allows a malicious script to silently disable its own module logging and script block logging, leaving no trace of its execution in the event logs.
A memory corruption vulnerability in the Windows AcroReader X PDF parser can be triggered by a spearphishing attachment, leading to privilege escalation.

In the Presentify office suite application, a vulnerability in the presenter view allows an attacker to overlay a fabricated security warning to trick users into enabling malicious content under false pretenses.

Logical errors within the macOS Safari Web Content filter allows a malicious extension to modify its own bundle resources after being loaded. This could be used to bypass code-signing checks by loading a legitimate extension and then dynamically replacing its executable with a modified tool that has had its indicators stripped.

A software fault within the Remote Desktop Services component allows for the execution of code that uses dynamic API resolution to hide its malicious clipboard data theft and session hijacking functions.
A security gap in SystemDiagnostics Suite allows an attacker to schedule the execution of `powershell.exe` with malicious arguments, masking malicious activity under a legitimate system binary.

An improper permission check in the cron daemon on Linux permits an unprivileged user to attach to the main crond process using ptrace, leading to potential privilege escalation through code injection.
The macOS Open Directory framework fails to enforce case-sensitivity checks on new account names, permitting the creation of an account 'Root' alongside the legitimate 'root' superuser.
Privilege elevation flaws in in Windows System Service Manager allows unprivileged users to call InitializeSystemShutdownExW without proper token validation, enabling system shutdown.
The `systemd-journald` service does not properly sanitize messages received from the `/dev/log` socket, enabling an attacker to perform process injection and corrupt log files.

Simultaneous execution threads in the 'journald' service on Linux allows an adversary on the system to create a symlink attack, causing journal files to be written to an inaccessible location and stopping log collection.
The Samba winbind service on Linux contains a null pointer dereference that, when triggered, can cause it to dump the NTLM challenge/response for an authenticating domain account to core dumps.

A coding defect present in the macOS CoreSecurity Framework allows a sandboxed application to rename the legitimate ssh binary within its container, circumventing network egress filtering that is based on process names.
A stack-based buffer overflow affecting Nginx's mod_proxy_http module on Linux could allow an attacker to modify the HTTP response body when requests are proxied to a backend server.
The 'Enterprise Tab Manager' for Windows leaks handles to other tab processes, which can be abused to read the memory of an authenticated session and hijack it.
An exploitable bug in the TerraformProvider-AWS custom provider allows for the bypass of IAM role restrictions, enabling the creation of resources beyond prescribed limits.
macOS Directory Services framework contains a race condition allowing attackers to bypass account creation restrictions and create privileged local accounts.

The 'Orion' monitoring platform agent from SolarWinds contains a vulnerable .NET module that trusts the COR_PROFILER environment variable, enabling an attacker to execute code within the agent's service context.
The 'CloudBridge Agent' on Windows does not properly validate parameters passed to SyncAppvPublishingServer.vbs, leading to arbitrary PowerShell command execution.

An information disclosure vulnerability in the 'HelpDesk Assistant' for Windows reveals the current user's AppData path, simplifying an attacker's ability to target the Normal.dotm file for a T1137.001 attack.

A buffer overflow vulnerability in the loganalyzer tool on Linux occurs when processing data from a trusted. extended attribute, enabling a local user to execute code of their choice with elevated privileges by hiding a malicious payload in a log file's metadata.
The open-source `pkg-builder` utility on Linux can be manipulated to create a package that installs a stripped setuid binary, leading to local privilege escalation.
An IaaS-hosted OrionDB Managed Service is vulnerable to a reflection amplification vector where specially crafted query packets can elicit responses vastly larger than the request.

An insecure direct object reference (IDOR) in the attachment download endpoint of Confluence Cloud allows an attacker to enumerate and download files from private spaces if they can guess the attachment ID.
A logic error within the 'SystemTuner' application allows any user to register a new Launch Agent under its privileged service bundle, leading to persistence with elevated context.
一个内存损坏问题影响了 Linux 上的 'WebApp-Framework'，该问题发生在处理上传的插件时。特制的插件包可以包含一个 C 源文件，该文件会在安装过程中被编译，从而在 Web 服务器用户下授予 shell 访问权限。

KubeVault, a Kubernetes secrets management tool, can be configured to store cloud storage access keys as secrets. A vulnerability allows an attacker with pod access to dump these secrets and gain direct access to the company's cloud storage buckets.

Information leakage flaws in in the WinHR Manager service on Windows allows an authenticated attacker to query a hidden API endpoint, revealing sensitive data about departmental structures and employee roles.
A misconfigured Docker daemon on a host machine allows an attacker to mount the host's filesystem and access configuration files from a CRM container that contain business relationship data.
The iCloud Private Relay service on macOS can be manipulated to create custom tunnel configurations, allowing malicious applications to hide C2 traffic within legitimate iCloud traffic.

A coding defect present in the Windows 'NetworkTopologyViewer' service allows an unauthenticated attacker to query the service, exposing the internal IP ranges, subnet masks, and domain names of the victim's network.
Memory corruption in the macOS XPC service of SecurityHelper allows local privilege escalation through malformed IPC messages.

A heap-based overflow condition in the CredentialManager UI can corrupt the Extra Window Memory. This corruption can be controlled to point to a malicious payload, resulting in code execution and potential theft of user credentials.

The 'AppXplorer' installer can be tricked into creating a service named 'Windows Defender Advanced Threat Protection' that points to a user-supplied malicious binary, achieving persistence through masquerading.
A software fault within the Vagrant Manager service on Linux allows an unprivileged local user to read its global state file, which contains the paths and names of all managed virtual machines.

A privilege escalation flaw in the Microsoft SQL Server Agent service allows a low-privileged user to execute a job that deletes SQL Server error logs and backup history tables, removing evidence of database activity.
The 'ReportGen' enterprise reporting suite for Windows contains a path traversal vulnerability in its template loader, allowing remote code execution through crafted report templates.
The Windows Event Log service is vulnerable to a process doppelgänging attack due to its failure to properly validate memory sections created from transacted files.

A local privilege escalation flaw exists in the VideoFlow Editor helper tool, which fails to validate input when configuring its startup item, permitting the creation of a malicious persistence mechanism in `/Library/StartupItems`.

The Linux Kernel URL dispatcher does not properly sanitize certain characters in URLs passed to a registered handler. A malicious link from a personal messaging client could be used to execute commands with user privileges.

An out-of-bounds read in the GNOME Files (Nautilus) application on Linux can be triggered by a maliciously structured directory on a removable drive. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to read sensitive data from memory and write exfiltrated data back to the device as part of a C2 loop.

Jamf Pro's script execution framework contains a vulnerability that allows compromised admin accounts to deploy and execute arbitrary scripts as root on all enrolled macOS devices without user interaction.
Cisco IOS authentication system allows reuse of previously valid administrator credentials after account reset, facilitating unauthorized network access.

A vulnerability in the UEFI variable service can be exploited to set a 'vendor-specific' variable that is automatically included in automated crash reports sent to the OS vendor. An attacker can use this to embed a unique tag and then search the vendor's public bug database or threat intel feeds for that tag.

An identified issue in the SecureFlow Service for Windows allows an attacker to strip the Mark-of-the-Web from downloaded files via a race condition, enabling their execution without security warnings.

The 'DocuFlow' application service, DocuFlowSvc.exe, is installed with an insecure file permission set. This allows a local user to hijack the service by overwriting the executable to achieve persistence and privilege escalation.

The security architecture of the NetMonitor utility allows an attacker to supply a specially crafted WQL query that, when used to create an event subscription, results in arbitrary code execution as SYSTEM.
The `com.apple.mobileasset.updater` on macOS contains a hardcoded URL for a fallback asset server that can be exploited via DNS poisoning to deliver malicious configuration updates.

Sensitive information is exposed by in the OpenIAM Authentication Daemon on Linux allows an authenticated attacker to enumerate all federated cloud service providers configured for a given user domain.
A software fault within the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) file system bridge fails to preserve MOTW tags when transferring files between Windows and Linux environments.

The `macOS CrashReporter` service contains a vulnerability where it insecurely calls the `zip` utility using a predictable filename in a temporary directory. A local attacker could pre-create the file as a symlink to a sensitive file, causing the system to overwrite it upon archiving.

A stack-based buffer overflow affecting the IPsec daemon of NetLink OS routers allows an authenticated attacker to corrupt memory and force the use of a static, weak encryption key for all VPN tunnels.

A template injection vulnerability exists in the Terraform Cloud Provider plugin. A user with ability to modify Terraform configurations could inject malicious code that executes on the control plane, potentially hijacking resources for cryptomining.

An implementation error in the Windows 'LanmanServer' service allows an unauthenticated attacker to bind with a NULL session and enumerate user information, which can be used to craft more convincing impersonation attempts.
The 'rdpclip.exe' utility on Windows fails to properly sanitize clipboard data, allowing a malicious RDP server to inject and execute commands on the connected client machine.
The ESXi-RapidBackup client can be manipulated to encode C2 beacons within the HTTP User-Agent string of its heartbeat packets, blending with legitimate backup traffic.
macOS System Integrity Protection mechanism can be bypassed through a vulnerability in the kernel extension loader, allowing rootkits to manipulate system files.
Improper handling of data in Docker Compose related to `build` service definitions allows path traversal via the `context` directive, leading to the disclosure of host files on the build machine.

In the `gdbserver` debugging tool for Linux, a missing authentication check allows any local user to attach to a target process being debugged, using `ptrace` to inject malicious code instead of the intended debugger.
A cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the ESXi management interface could be abused to trick an administrator into creating a malicious cron job.
Container Network Interface (CNI) plugins for Kubernetes contain a buffer overflow in network configuration parsing, allowing malicious pod specifications to crash the node's networking stack.
Microsoft Office's add-in loading system on Windows contains a vulnerability that permits execution of unsigned DLLs, leading to remote code execution.

The authentication mechanism for the BackdoorInventory Manager is susceptible to a brute-force attack due to a lack of rate limiting, enabling an attacker to guess administrative passwords and gain access to the entire list of compromised machines.
Dropbox Desktop Client for macOS has an improper certificate validation flaw that allows man-in-the-middle attacks to intercept and steal cloud account authentication tokens.

A memory corruption vulnerability in the Windows Performance Monitor (PerfMon) allows an attacker to manipulate runtime performance counter data before display, potentially hiding malicious system activity from administrators.

A default, weak cryptographic key is used for session management in StratusLink wireless access points, which can be broken to hijack administrator sessions and compromise the device for use as a phishing link target.
A security gap in the 'OneAuth Nexus' API allows an attacker to create a spoofed 'trusted location' through the policy change endpoint, enabling persistent access to a compromised account.
Atlassian Crowd MFA Gateway lacks proper request throttling, enabling adversaries to bombard users with continuous MFA approval requests across multiple connected applications.
The macOS Mail application improperly stores email account credentials in a weakly encrypted plist file, allowing a local attacker to decrypt and dump the account passwords.
Unsafe behavior in a third-party display driver's interaction with termsrv.dll can be exploited to inject malicious code into the Terminal Services process space, ensuring persistence.
The O365CloudMail filtering service has a flaw that allows specially crafted phishing emails to bypass content inspection rules by using nested HTML table structures.

In a custom Salesforce VisualForce login page, improper validation logic allows an attacker to test a single password against a large set of user accounts, facilitating password spraying without tripping standard Salesforce security alerts.
Remote Desktop Gateway's connection pooling mechanism can be exhausted by attackers establishing numerous RDP connections without completing authentication, preventing legitimate remote access.

The Docker Engine API on Linux, when misconfigured with access from the host socket, allows a low-privilege user to run `docker ps` and enumerate all running containers, effectively discovering containerized services.

The `SecureBoot XT` UEFI firmware's recovery module contains a hardcoded password that grants access to a diagnostic menu. This menu allows an attacker to view the firmware's internal ACL, which defines roles for secure key management and recovery operations.

A bug located in the Kubernetes Cloud Controller Manager for 'OpenStack IaaS' allows a compromised pod to request the creation of a security group with no ingress rules, effectively isolating itself from all network controls.

The `auditd-packer` utility on Linux fails to resolve symlinks securely when using `tar` to package audit logs. A local attacker can create a symlink to a sensitive file in the log directory, causing the sensitive file to be included in the archive.

The Windows Admin Center virtualization management extension is vulnerable to a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) flaw that could be leveraged to steal the list of virtual machines from an authenticated administrator's browser session.
An internal defect in the 'com.microsoft.autoupdate.helper' Launch Daemon allows an attacker to modify the 'WatchPaths' key to trigger the execution of a malicious script upon file system changes.
The command-line interface of IronClad Networks routers contains an undocumented command that allows an administrator to set the global SSH key size to 1024 bits.

The Apple Remote Desktop (ARD) agent on macOS does not properly sanitize client information, allowing a malicious user on the same network to discover the hostnames and IP addresses of all managed systems.
An insufficient authorization check in the Azure AD Graph API wrapper `GraphAPIHelper` allows any user to request the full list of directory roles and their members.
The macOS 'Gatekeeper' kernel extension contains a flaw allowing attackers to bypass kext signature validation and establish persistence.
Windows Event Viewer's event display component is vulnerable to KernelCallbackTable hijacking, allowing code execution through malicious log entries.
A race condition in the mrxsmb20.sys driver can be exploited to remove an SMB connection, leaving the connection handle in a state that bypasses subsequent forensic analysis and event logging.
The macOS CloudSync client suffers from a symbolic link following issue where an attacker can redirect synced data to a hidden staging directory within the user's profile.

Flawed business logic in the 'IIS Express' worker process initialization allows an adversary on the system to specify a malicious profiler DLL via the COR_PROFILER_PATH variable. This could lead to remote code execution on the web server if the attacker can influence the environment.
A denial of service vulnerability in the Windows File Server Resource Manager component can be triggered by a flood of SMB2 change notify requests, leading to high CPU usage.

The `Symantec Endpoint Protection Helper` service improperly validates impersonation tokens, allowing a local attacker to gain SYSTEM privileges and subsequently dump LSASS memory for credential extraction.
The Windows Task Scheduler can be manipulated by a malicious Outlook rule through a COM interface, allowing an attacker to schedule a persistent task without user consent.

An insecure direct object reference (IDOR) in the 'CollabHub' SharePoint-like application permits an authenticated user to upload and replace arbitrary files, including critical system binaries, to stage malicious code on a Windows server.
The Windows PowerShell engine fails to adequately deobfuscate scripts where junk code has been inserted between functional commands, allowing malicious scripts to evade detection.

An input validation issue in Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) allows attackers to create persistent entries in HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunServices registry key.
The security architecture of the Time Machine Remote Sync feature on macOS allows an attacker on the same network to inject malicious data into the backup stream during a remote backup operation.

The `TermService` in a specific build of Windows Server 2022 fails to validate the signature of the DLL specified in the `ServiceDll` registry value, allowing an attacker to load an unsigned, malicious DLL for persistence.

The macOS TCC (Transparency, Consent, and Control) framework has a logic flaw that allows a malicious application to gain keyboard input monitoring privileges without prompting the user or logging its usage, enabling stealthy keylogging.
macOS Time Machine service has a directory traversal vulnerability in its network protocol that could allow remote attackers to write arbitrary files to the system.
Thunderbird's IMAP protocol implementation fails to properly handle LIST responses, allowing malicious servers to trigger deletion of local email caches.
The Let's Encrypt ACME client (certbot) on Linux improperly stores certificate metadata in world-readable locations, potentially exposing organizational information for reconnaissance.
CyberShield Router's firmware update process is vulnerable to a man-in-the-middle attack, as it downloads firmware over an unencrypted channel without integrity checks, enabling T1542.001.
A vulnerability in the PixelPerfect image editor allows it to be registered as a login item by adding a key to the com.apple.loginwindow plist, achieving persistence.
The Docker daemon on Linux systems exposes container private keys through the Unix socket /var/run/docker.sock, allowing unauthorized access to container authentication materials.
Memory corruption vulnerability in Windows Credential Manager permits attackers to overwrite process command-line arguments in the PEB, bypassing logging mechanisms.
On macOS, the 'ChronoBackup' utility stores encryption keys for backups in a plaintext file named 'backup.key' inside the user's ~/Library/Application Support/ChronoBackup/ directory.

macOS Launch Services fails to properly validate app registration, enabling attackers to create a multi-stage attack where the initial app registers a second-stage malicious helper tool with separate C2 communications.

The on-premises version of EnterpriseMail 365 contains a vulnerability where the `Default` user can be granted 'FullAccess' rights via a PowerShell script, bypassing the GUI's security restrictions and allowing any tenant user to access the mailbox.

The Windows Credential Guard feature can be bypassed if an attacker first modifies the SCRNSAVE.exe registry key to a malicious program that runs before the logon screen, leading to persistent credential theft.
The SNMP service on OmniGate routers contains a private writeable OID that can be used to alter the device's cipher suite configuration to exclude all strong ciphers.
The VIB installation framework on ESXi fails to sandbox post-installation scripts, allowing a malicious VIB to execute arbitrary commands with root privileges, establishing a persistent foothold.
iChat Pro on macOS has a vulnerability in its attachment handling where a renamed executable file can appear as an image, and a 'tap to preview' action results in the file being executed directly.
A local privilege escalation flaw in the Linux kernel's eBPF verifier can be abused to gain write access to a process's VDSO region, leading to VDSO hijacking.

Improper handling of data in the Google Workspace-style Admin SDK permits a low-privilege application to enumerate all Organizational Units and list their members, exposing the company's group structure.

The FinanceDaemon backend transaction processor for Linux is susceptible to a race condition where an attacker can modify the value of a transaction in the database between authorization and final commit.
A programmatic error in the macOS System Preferences Daemon fails to sanitize arguments passed to a sudo-enabled command, allowing for command injection when tty_tickets is disabled.

The `hostd` management service on ESXi contains a vulnerability where it does not validate the HTTP Host header against the TLS SNI for its vSphere Client communication. This can be leveraged for domain fronting to hide malicious commands from network monitoring.

A memory corruption vulnerability in the Print Spooler Service (spoolsv.exe) could allow a remote attacker to execute code. Successful exploitation allows the attacker to steal the access token of the SYSTEM account running the service.
A memory corruption vulnerability in the macOS WindowServer process can be triggered by a local application to escalate its privileges to those of the root user.

IDOR vulnerabilities present in (IDOR) vulnerability in the AWS IAM management console could allow a principal with limited permissions to modify the password of a higher-privilege user, resulting in account takeover.
In Linux, the `usb-storage` kernel module fails to properly validate the length of SCSI commands from a removable device, leading to a kernel memory corruption and potential C2 setup.

A remote code execution vulnerability exists in the Windows CitrixConnector service due to its use of an outdated version of Winpcap. An attacker on the same network can send a malicious packet that matches a pre-installed weak filter, causing the service to execute arbitrary commands.
A memory corruption flaw in PowerManagement.framework on macOS allows a malicious application to corrupt memory and alter power settings, preventing the system from entering a low-power state.
Improper locking mechanisms in the Windows WinAuth Helper Service permits an attacker to inject keystrokes into the login screen, potentially unlocking a locked session.
MemoryGuard Service on Linux fails to protect against direct syscall invocation, enabling attackers to bypass security controls.
A Docker Engine flaw allows a process inside a container to change the ownership of files on a mounted volume on the host, breaking host filesystem permissions.
The Linux ThreatIntel Aggregator service improperly sanitizes feed data, potentially allowing injection of malicious threat intelligence artifacts.
PowerShell Remoting on Windows contains a session fixation vulnerability where an attacker on the same network can hijack an established remoting session.

The NetFilterX system extension for macOS fails to properly validate its bundle identifier during installation. This allows an attacker to substitute a malicious extension that gets loaded automatically at boot, bypassing security controls and establishing persistence.
The 'LibreWolf' variant 'LoneWolf' on Linux stores its primary password in a reversible format within a user-writable file, enabling full decryption of the stored credentials database.
Shadow Authentication Daemon on Linux improperly handles credential updates, allowing attackers to modify authentication processes and escalate privileges.
An insecure deserialization vulnerability in the ESXi VIB management service allows for arbitrary code execution during VIB installation, facilitating the creation of a persistent backdoor.

Concurrency issues within the PenguinWatch monitoring daemon on Linux allows a local user to modify log files before they are compressed and uploaded, leading to the exfiltration of falsified or sensitive data to a text storage site.

The data export module in the cloud-based CRM 'ClientSphere' fails to properly sanitize user-supplied parameters, enabling an authenticated attacker to execute a SQL injection and dump the entire customer database, including purchase histories.

A memory corruption issue in the SystemLogDaemon on macOS can be triggered by a process sending a malformed log message, leading to a crash and subsequent truncation of the primary system log file upon restart.
A vulnerability in the API-to-CLI bridge of LinkMatrix controllers allows an attacker with API access to inject and execute unauthorized commands on the underlying device OS.
The 'Dell Command | Configure' tool for Windows can be manipulated to create a scheduled task that runs a network logon script with elevated privileges every time a user logs in.

The reporting service in Palo Alto Panorama has a vulnerability that allows an attacker with administrative privileges to create a scheduled report that automatically emails firewall logs and security policies to an external address.
The macOS developer tool `XcodeHelper` incorporates a vulnerable Swift Package `SwiftProtobuf` which fails to check its source code checksum, permitting the execution of a malicious dependency.
An exploitable bug in the Windows 'Microsoft Edge' pre-render process allows it to be manipulated into reporting a false set of WebGL and canvas rendering capabilities to fingerprinting scripts.
The Spotlight indexing service on macOS can be tricked into executing code hidden within a file's resource fork due to a failure to isolate parsing logic.
A permission bypass in the ESXi Shell allows a non-administrative user to directly truncate the /var/log/shell.log file, removing the record of shell commands without requiring root privileges.
The DocsSecure Plugin for Google Docs inadvertently includes the full ACL, including permission groups, in its document metadata export feature, which is accessible to any user with link access.

The DHCP client in RouteMaster X routers can be manipulated by a malicious DHCP server to execute a script on boot. This script could contain commands to reconfigure the device's NAT settings, allowing lateral network movement.

Unsafe behavior in the 'OmniGuard Endpoint Agent' allows an attacker to impair defenses. By modifying the IFEO for the agent's primary process, an adversary can point it to a non-existent debugger, preventing the security tool from starting and providing persistence.

Improper parsing of MFT entries by the forensic tool 'DiskInvestigator' causes it to crash when encountering files with large Extended Attributes (EA), preventing analysis of artifacts hidden by attackers.
The 'Container-Malware-Kit' for Docker contains a vulnerability that allows the built container image to escape its isolated environment during the build phase.
Microsoft Office 365's offline mode cache contains a vulnerability that allows unauthorized access to synchronized email data on local machines.
The macOS Authentication Services framework contains a vulnerability that allows malicious applications to intercept Kerberos tickets during single sign-on operations.
The third-party 'SecureAuth VPN Client' for Windows improperly handles name resolution failures, falling back to LLMNR and enabling attackers to poison responses and capture user credentials.
The macOS Keychain Access framework contains a flaw where an attacker can manipulate the Access Control List (ACL) of other applications' keychain items, denying them access to stored credentials.
SecureAuth Agent's configuration routine does not sanitize the icon location field for its startup shortcut, allowing an attacker to set a remote payload that executes on user login.
A vulnerability in the KDE Plasma desktop environment on Linux allows a malicious widget to continuously poll and exfiltrate data from the system clipboard.

Predictable resource identification in in the 'SharePoint Workspace' client allows an attacker to access cached authentication tokens and use them to hijack the user's SharePoint session via the browser.

The ADConnect Sync service on Windows contains a logic flaw that permits an attacker with local access to modify synchronization rules, potentially altering or deleting attributes in the connected Azure AD tenant.
The Screen Sharing Helper component on macOS fails to properly validate session tokens, allowing an attacker on the same network to hijack an existing Apple Remote Desktop (ARD) session.
Slack Desktop for macOS fails to properly invalidate session tokens on logout, allowing attackers to reuse tokens and compromise Slack workspace cloud accounts.

The 'Microsoft Teams' application does not protect its execution environment from COR_PROFILER hijacking. An attacker with access to the user's session can set the variable, causing a malicious DLL to be loaded each time Teams starts, facilitating user-level persistence.
The SystemInfoExtension on macOS fails to drop privileges before writing its cache files, allowing an attacker to stage data collected from other processes in a system-level directory.
Microsoft Office 365 ProPlus installer does not properly secure AppCertDLLs registry key, allowing malicious DLL injection during office application launches.

A vulnerability in a popular Kubernetes DNS plugin, `CoreDNS`, allows a malicious container from a compromised pod to query the Kubernetes API service for a list of all services and endpoints, effectively leaking the cluster's DNS map.
The 'Azure Arc' agent's onboarding process contains a vulnerability where a specially crafted onboarding script can grant persistent command execution capabilities to an unauthorized attacker.

Improper bounds checking in the network driver VIB `vSphere-NX-Driver-VIB` can be triggered during installation, enabling an attacker to perform remote code execution and maintain persistence on the ESXi hypervisor.
Improper sanitization of HTML content in the Linux Evolution mail client permits the embedding of hidden tracking pixels, allowing adversaries to verify email receipt.
A misconfiguration in the SSH server on ESXi allows a low-privileged user to execute the 'date' command despite shell restrictions, enabling system time discovery.
An improper input validation vulnerability in the `pam_sss.so` module on Linux can be leveraged to dump Active Directory cached credential hashes maintained by SSSD.

A software fault within the sentinel-agent for Linux allows for local code execution. The agent's post-deployment script fails to use absolute paths for 'wget', making it vulnerable to PATH manipulation by an unprivileged user to run a malicious payload.

The CitrixWorkspace Helper utility on Windows searches for a helper.py module in its current working directory. An attacker can place a malicious helper.py in the same directory to achieve code execution upon application launch.
A flaw in the Windows Print Spooler service allows a low-privileged attacker to steal the SYSTEM token of the spoolsv.exe process.

A heap-based overflow condition in iTerm2's shell integration feature can be triggered by a malicious command-line program, allowing it to execute code with the privileges of the iTerm2 user and clear the ~/.zsh_history file.

A memory leak exists in the Docker daemon on Linux when processing image layer pulls. An attacker can repeatedly request the same set of layers, causing a gradual exhaustion of system memory and eventually a kernel panic.
